items.title: V2X World
items.text:
A connected-vehicle simulator with a real US SCMS.

V2X World is a deterministic, discrete-event simulator of connected-vehicle (V2X) systems, written in Rust. One run models the road traffic, the radio channel, the network and message layers, the IEEE 1609.2 security envelope, the credential system that issues and revokes certificates (the US SCMS or the ETSI ITS PKI), the attackers, and the misbehaviour detectors and authority. The same scenario, seed and build give the same bytes out on every supported platform. It is built for research on V2X security and privacy: what credential management costs in bytes, queueing and latency; how long a misbehaving vehicle stays believed; what a roadside eavesdropper learns across pseudonym changes; and what post-quantum signatures cost on the air.

flowchart LR
  S[scenario.yaml] --> L[load, merge, validate]
  L --> B[build: world, models, nodes, backend]
  B --> R[event loop]
  R --> M[(recording.mcap)]
  R --> X[metrics.json]
  M --> V[v2xw info / Studio / Python]
  X --> C[v2xw compare / experiment tables]

Layer Modelled Page World OpenStreetMap, SUMO net.xml and OpenDRIVE imports, procedural grid, radial and random networks, buildings, DEM terrain, vegetation Worlds and maps Traffic IDM, EIDM, Krauss, Gipps, Wiedemann 99, ACC/CACC; MOBIL and sublane lane change; HCM gap acceptance; fixed-time, actuated and NEMA signals; pedestrians and cyclists; a mesoscopic tier; demand from Poisson arrivals, OD matrices, counts, GTFS and assignment Traffic and mobility, Traffic demand Radio and network IEEE 802.11p, LTE-V2X and NR-V2X sidelinks, cellular Uu; path loss, fading, obstruction; ETSI and SAE congestion control; WSMP and GeoNetworking; fragmentation Radio and network Messages BSM, CAM, DENM, CPM, VAM, SPaT, MAP and others, with real encodings where the code has them Messages Security IEEE 1609.2 / ETSI TS 103 097 envelopes, real or modelled ECDSA, post-quantum and hybrid schemes as cost models, verification policies, P2PCD Security and crypto Credentials the CAMP SCMS (enrolment, butterfly keys, linkage values, reports, revocation, CRLs) and the ETSI TS 102 941 PKI SCMS and credentials Threats and detection position, timing, identity and credential attacks, jammers, an eavesdropper; local detector suites; misbehaviour-authority pipelines Threats and detection Measurement MCAP recordings that replay byte for byte, metrics with sample counts and intervals, exports, sweeps, comparison, sensitivity Metrics and outputs

Every model ships a model card: its equations, every parameter with a unit, default and cited source, its assumptions, what it ignores and how it was validated (model parameters).

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
Rust comes from rust-toolchain.toml through rustup; the Studio needs Node 22+ and pnpm 10. Full prerequisites: Install and build.

git clone https://github.com/ak3zaidan/V2X-World.git && cd V2X-World
cargo build --release -p v2xw-cli                       # target/release/v2xw and v2xw-server
./target/release/v2xw validate scenarios/highway-congestion.yaml
./target/release/v2xw run scenarios/highway-congestion.yaml --out runs/highway
./target/release/v2xw info runs/highway/recording.mcap

worlds/fetch.sh manhattan                               # the OpenStreetMap extract (ODbL, git-ignored)
./target/release/v2xw run scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --out runs/midtown

./run-sim.sh                                            # engine on :8787, paused
pnpm --dir ui install && pnpm --dir ui --filter @vwp/studio dev   # http://127.0.0.1:5173

highway-congestion.yaml builds its own road network and needs no download. The command reference is Command-line tool.

items.title: How to cite
items.text: Cite the software as described in CITATION.cff (GitHub's "Cite this repository" button reads it); the BibTeX entries for the software and the paper are on Citation and licence. Name the engine build and the scenario hash a result came from: both are in every run's manifest.json, and together with the seed they reproduce the run. The code is Apache-2.0 and the V2X-World dataset is CC BY 4.0; the licences of the third-party ASN.1 modules and the map data are on the same page. The standards and papers the models implement: Standards and references.

items.title: Layers
items.text:
interfaces   v2xw-cli (v2xw, v2xw-server)   v2xw-server (VWP + JSON-RPC)   v2xw-py   v2xw-wasm   ui/
                         |                              |
 orchestration        v2xw-experiment  v2xw-engine (scenario, event loop, wiring, manifest)
                         |
 runtime              v2xw-node (OBU/RSU/VRU device runtimes)   v2xw-proto (credential protocols)
                         |
 models               v2xw-world  v2xw-mobility  v2xw-demand  v2xw-radio  v2xw-net  v2xw-msg
                      v2xw-sec  v2xw-threat  v2xw-energy  v2xw-interop
                         |
 measurement          v2xw-metrics   v2xw-record
                         |
 contract             v2xw-core (kernel, RNG, registry, model cards, manifest, math)

Each model crate owns one domain and does not reach into another's: mobility never touches radio or security, radio treats a frame as a length, MCS and access category, metrics read recorded events and never engine state. v2xw-engine is where the model crates are composed into a run. Exact dependency edges: crates.md.

items.title: A run
items.text:
1. Load. Scenario::load (crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/) parses YAML or JSON, migrates the schema, merges meta.base overlays on the untyped document, deserialises and validates, returning every error with its dotted field (scenarios.md).
  2. Build. Engine::build(scenario, build_utc) imports or generates the world (v2xw-world), registers every selected model with its card in the v2xw_core::Registry, spawns nodes and backend entities (wiring.rs, phase2.rs) and assembles the manifest.
  3. Run. Engine::run(&mut recorder) drives one event heap until the end sentinel. Every record goes to a Recorder (MemoryRecorder, or the MCAP writer in v2xw-record) and to the metric providers.
  4. Finish. The CLI writes the recording, the resolved scenario, metrics, the run report and the manifest, then reads the recording back to verify it (recording-and-metrics.md; on-disk format: dev/recording-format.md).

items.title: The event loop
items.text:
crates/v2xw-engine/src/run.rs. One single-threaded loop pops events in the total order (time, priority, seq): priority is fixed per event class, seq is assigned at schedule time, so ties resolve by rule. A few event classes are phases: pure maps over actors, receivers or nodes that may run on a thread pool, merged in id order.

pop (time, priority, seq)
  Control       scenario timeline: weather, outages, demand, parameter changes
  MobilityStep  phase over actors; publish gt.kinematics and a VWP Keyframe/Delta, advance
                the world by dt, rebuild the snapshot, spawn and retire nodes
  PhyEnd        phase over one frame's receivers: link budget, SINR, reception outcome
  PhyStart      one frame goes on the air
  NodePhase     phase over nodes: generation, signing, verification, stores, detectors;
                node-local queues drain inside the map and never reach the heap
  Observe       metric flush and the end-of-run sentinel

Mobility is periodic (time.mobility_step_ms). A radio event strictly inside a step reads positions by the published extrapolation rule pos(t') = pos(t) + vel(t) (t' - t) (v2xw_core::kinematics::Kinematics::extrapolate, applied only in Engine::position_at). Each mobility step is a Jacobi update: every decision reads a frozen start-of-step snapshot, so actor visiting order cannot change the result.

Time dilation and fast-forward. A scenario may declare windows (time.fast_forward) in which traffic is frozen and no radio event is generated, and the engine jumps between credential-system events (top-ups, shuffles, CRL publication and fetches, re-enrolment) on the mobility-step grid. Weeks of PKI behaviour fit in a short run; every window is recorded in the manifest.

items.title: Fidelity tiers
items.text: Each model family has abstract, medium and high tiers (v2xw_core::card::Tier): closed-form or probabilistic stand-ins for very large runs, the literature-standard models, and frame-level detail. A scenario picks tiers per family (radio.tiers) and may name a specific model by id (radio.models). The validator refuses combinations that cannot compose, for example phy: high with mac: medium. At city scale (scale), a microscopic focus region runs inside a mesoscopic queue network (mobility/tiered/meso-micro) with the radio matched to it.

items.title: Plug-in seams
items.text: Every model family is a trait (for example v2xw_radio::traits::Propagation, v2xw_mobility::traits::CarFollowing, v2xw_threat::Detector, v2xw_metrics::MetricProvider) plus a model card. Models reach the engine only through a narrowed context (v2xw_core::ctx::Ctx, implemented once in crates/v2xw-engine/src/ctx.rs, narrowed per family in adapters.rs), which supplies the clock, keyed RNG streams and the reads that family is allowed. Models run in process: Rust models link into the engine (the registry refuses a copyleft licence in process), and Python models sit behind the same traits through the adapters in v2xw-py. extending.md walks through each seam.

items.title: Determinism contract
items.text:
Same scenario file + seed + engine build + plug-in set gives byte-identical outputs on macOS, Linux and Windows, x86-64 and arm64, native or WebAssembly, any thread count. The mechanisms, all in v2xw-core:

Mechanism Where counter-based RNG: each stream keyed by SHA-256(master_seed, domain, entity), samplers with fixed draw counts rng.rs pure-Rust transcendentals (libm); platform f64 functions are not used math.rs fixed event priorities and monotonic sequence numbers event.rs dense, totally ordered ids; reductions sorted by id ids.rs writer-side quantisation of every recorded float to its declared grid math::quantize_to, v2xw-world/src/quant.rs, v2xw-record/src/grid.rs

No component below the transport reads the wall clock; ordered collections are used wherever iteration order reaches an output. The run manifest (v2xw_core::manifest, assembled in crates/v2xw-engine/src/manifest.rs) pins the engine version, a build hash over compiler, platform, git commit and dirty state, every registered model with its card hash, the world hash, the scenario hash over canonical JSON, the master seed and the crypto mode. Runtime diagnostics (wall time, memory) are excluded from every digest by construction (v2xw_metrics::summary::DigestSet).

items.title: Belief and ground truth
items.text:
The simulator separates what is true from what a device could know:

  • A node (v2xw-node) holds its own GNSS fix, its own drifting clock, what it received and what is in its stores. It sees the world through v2xw_core::nodeview, never through actor state.
  • Detectors and the MA pipeline consume v2xw_threat::obs::ObservedMessage and the receiver's own belief. Attackers receive an AttackerView with no world, no actor index and no actor ids; every action that changes bytes on the air is logged host-side on a ground-truth channel with the true actor id, which is what labels a dataset.
  • Entities in the credential system talk only through modelled links that charge for bytes and compute (v2xw_proto::kernel); an end entity reads no backend state.
  • Recording channels carry a visibility class; NODE-only recordings and datasets refuse ground-truth records.

Source scans in crates/v2xw-node/tests/firewall_sentinel.rs and the conformance kit's firewall suite enforce these boundaries.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Every setting is a scenario field (scenarios.md). There are no configuration files or environment variables that change a run's results; the only environment variables read are for optional tooling (SUMO location, the assistant's provider keys, test switches).

How to read the generated reference, and the status vocabulary in full: Configuration overview. Adding a setting: Extending: settings.

items.title: Where a setting lives
items.text:
All under crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/:

File Role schema.rs the typed scenario: every field, its type, its documented default and unit; deny_unknown_fields, so a misspelt key is an error validate.rs BOUNDS (numeric ranges), CHOICES (closed value sets), KEY_STATUS (implementation status of every key), and the cross-field rules options.rs labels and one-line explanations for each value of a closed set; named presets for numbers; the model ids a slot accepts, taken from the registry guide.rs a basic/advanced level per field, a plain-language description and recommended range for basic fields, the Studio's quick settings and study starting points publish.rs the published settings surface, generated from the above and from the registry's model cards module_keys.rs fallback for keys whose tables live beside the engine module that implements them (for example ma_policy.rs, scms_topology.rs)

Model parameters are not scenario fields of their own: a slot holds a ModelChoice { id, params } (for example security.protocol, net.uu, entries of radio.models), and the parameters a model accepts, with units, defaults, ranges and sources, come from its model card.

items.title: Implementation status
items.text:
KEY_STATUS classifies every key, and the published surface tags every field with it (x-status), so it is always visible whether editing a field changes a run:

Status Meaning wired the engine reads it and it changes the run partial the engine acts on part of it, or only under conditions the row's note states not-implemented validated and hashed, read by nothing refused the loader rejects every value this build cannot act on; only implemented values load descriptive describes the scenario (name, tags) and by design changes nothing computed

A test (every_leaf_has_a_status) requires every published leaf to match a row.

items.title: The published surface
items.text:
v2xw_engine::scenario::publish::surface() returns, as JSON:

Key Contents schema JSON Schema 2020-12 over the whole scenario, with unit, default, x-status, x-path per node fields the same tree flattened to one row per editable leaf groups the sections in display order slots every place the scenario selects a model, with the selectable ids models every registered model's card and parameters statuses the status vocabulary

The server returns it from the scenario.get and scenario.schema RPCs; the Studio's settings window and the assistant are generated from it rather than hand-written. Tests require that every key in every shipped scenario is described, that a document built from the published defaults loads, and that no unclassified field is offered.

items.title: Validation rules worth knowing
items.text:
• Tier combinations must compose (phy: high needs mac: high; abstract propagation needs an abstract PHY).
  • time.mobility_step_ms is bounded to the range the mobility models are calibrated for.
  • An attacker population names exactly one of fraction, count or actor_ids.
  • security.crypto_mode: real narrows security.signature to the schemes with a real implementation (ecdsa-p256).
  • security.protocol and actors.backend.protocol must name the same credential protocol.
  • A shorter credential i-period than the deployment's needs time.calendar: compressed, which every output then labels.

The same validator runs in the CLI (v2xw validate), behind the scenario.validate RPC, and when a run is built.

items.title: Extending the simulator
items.text:
Every extension keeps the same rules: a model card, keyed randomness, v2xw_core::math for transcendentals, no wall clock, no ground truth in node-side code, quantised outputs (Conventions; the invariants are also in AGENTS.md). The conformance kit's plug-in suite checks them. Each section below is a summary; the linked page is the step-by-step recipe.

To add Where it plugs in Recipe a model in any family the family trait, a ModelCard, Registry::register_model, a slot builder in the engine Models a misbehaviour detector v2xw_threat::detect::Detector, a suite in phase2.rs Detectors a metric v2xw_metrics::MetricProvider, MetricDef, register_all Metrics a scenario setting schema.rs, validate.rs, options.rs, guide.rs Settings a shipped scenario or a city scenarios/, worlds/cities.yaml Scenarios and cities a signature or KEM scheme, a threshold protocol, a Python model, an out-of-tree crate v2xw_sec::scheme, v2xw_proto::threshold, v2xw.plugins, examples/ Plugins

items.title: A model (any family)
items.text:
Implement the family trait (v2xw_radio::traits::Propagation, v2xw_mobility::traits::CarFollowing, ... ; the full table is on Models), build its card with a unit, default, range and source for every parameter (or todo-calibrate with a calibration plan), draw randomness only through ctx.rng(domain, entity), test it including a test shown to fail, run v2xw_conformance::plugin::run_suite, and make it selectable where the engine builds the slot: radio models in crates/v2xw-engine/src/wiring.rs (radio.models), car-following in v2xw_mobility::carfollowing::library::FACTORIES (actors.vehicles.driving), detectors, attackers and MA pipelines in phase2.rs, metrics through v2xw_metrics::register_all.

examples/ is an out-of-tree cargo workspace with one worked plug-in per interface: propagation-log-distance, carfollowing-constant-time-gap, detector-heading-rate (including the conformance suite) and metric-detector-load (cd examples && cargo test).

items.title: A detector
items.text: Implement v2xw_threat::detect::Detector; on_message receives an obs::ObservedMessage, the receiver's SelfBelief and its map store, and nothing that identifies the true sender. Quantise before comparing against a threshold; leave a check whose input the receiver does not have out of the verdict rather than scoring it zero. detection.local accepts the suites compiled into phase2.rs. See Detectors.

items.title: A metric
items.text: Implement MetricProvider over recorded channels, never engine state, and declare each metric with a MetricDef (unit, dimensions, grid, minimum samples, source, what it does not account for). Use stats::Proportion (Wilson interval), ratio_of_sums and Distribution; accumulate counts and bytes as integers. Register it in register_all or behind an opt-in group in wiring::build_metrics_for, and give a headline metric a direction and health band (polarity.rs, health.rs). See Metrics.

items.title: A setting
items.text: Add the field to crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/schema.rs (unit in the name, default documented, skip-serialised at its default), a range in validate::BOUNDS or a set in validate::CHOICES, a KEY_STATUS row, labels and presets in scenario::options, and a level and guidance in scenario::guide; read it where the engine builds the affected model, test that it changes a same-seed run, and run just docs-gen. The publish tests require it to be described, loadable at its default and classified. See Settings.

items.title: A scenario
items.text: Copy the closest file in scenarios/, or write a short overlay on scenarios/base/ with meta.base. State what it measures and what it does not, justify each non-default number, and use city-independent forms (rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km, rsu_placement, target: auto). v2xw validate must pass; add it to scenarios/ready-made.txt to offer it in the Studio. See Scenarios and cities and Scenarios.

items.title: A city
items.text: Add an entry to worlds/cities.yaml, fetch it with worlds/fetch.sh <id>, and check it with cargo run -p v2xw-cli --bin city_audit -- <scenario.yaml> --only <id>. See Scenarios and cities.

items.title: A signature or KEM scheme
items.text: Copy crates/v2xw-sec/src/scheme/template.rs, fill in the id, the parts in wire order with their primitives and hardware-profile operations, and add one line to SIGNATURE_SCHEMES or KEM_SCHEMES; hybrid_mldsa65.rs is a worked example. See Plugins.

items.title: A model in Python
items.text: python/v2xw/plugins.py puts a Python object behind an engine trait: CarFollowing (abstract tier, per vehicle per step) and Detector (once per window with an Arrow record batch), both callable and conformance-checked through v2xw.conformance, and MaPolicy, which runs inside a run started with v2xw.run(..., ma_policy=...). A Python plug-in draws no randomness of its own, reads no clock, uses v2xw.math instead of math, and keeps hashed iteration order out of its results. Example: python/examples/python_idm.py. See Plugins.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Need For Notes Rust via rustup everything rust-toolchain.toml pins the compiler (1.98.1) and installs rustfmt, clippy and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target on first use just optional task runner just --list; every recipe is a plain cargo or pnpm command Node 22+, pnpm 10 the Studio ui/package.json pins pnpm@10.15.0 (corepack can provide it) Python 3.9+, maturin the Python package cd python && maturin develop (Python) SUMO optional co-simulation (mobility.provider: sumo), export-sumo with netconvert, cross-validation; found through SUMO_HOME or V2XW_SUMO_VENV (SUMO co-simulation) OSM extracts real-city scenarios worlds/fetch.sh <city-id> writes worlds/cache/<id>.osm.xml (git-ignored, ODbL) (Worlds and maps) A WebAssembly-capable clang optional: replaying recordings in the browser with no engine Apple's clang has no wasm32 back end; Homebrew's llvm does (Studio tour)

just setup fetches the Rust, Python and UI dependencies in one step.

items.title: Get the code
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/ak3zaidan/V2X-World.git && cd V2X-World

Every command on these pages runs from the repository root.

items.title: Build
items.text:
cargo build --release -p v2xw-cli      # target/release/v2xw and target/release/v2xw-server
cargo build --release -p v2xw-demand-cli   # target/release/v2xw-demand (demand and route tools)
cargo build --workspace                # everything, debug

Third-party crates are optimised even in debug and test profiles (Cargo.toml [profile.dev.package."*"]), because the engine runs real P-256 and P-384 arithmetic. On a machine with little memory, build with -j 1 (as just build-cli and just build-server do).

items.title: Check the install
items.text:
./target/release/v2xw --version
./target/release/v2xw validate scenarios/highway-congestion.yaml   # procedural road, no download
./target/release/v2xw run scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml --out runs/phase1
./target/release/v2xw info runs/phase1/recording.mcap

phase1-grid.yaml is one minute of a Midtown-shaped procedural grid with signed BSMs; it finishes in about a minute of wall time. Then follow Your first simulation.

items.title: The Studio
items.text:
pnpm --dir ui install
./run-sim.sh                                   # engine on :8787, paused (terminal 1)
pnpm --dir ui --filter @vwp/studio dev         # http://127.0.0.1:5173 (terminal 2)

Studio tour walks through it; Studio describes its packages and checks.

items.title: Recording, metrics and exports
items.text: Code: crates/v2xw-record (container, encoder, reader, exporters, datasets), crates/v2xw-metrics (providers, statistics, invariants, summary), the output step in crates/v2xw-cli/src/run.rs, and crates/v2xw-experiment for sweeps.

items.title: What v2xw run writes
items.text:
File Contents Reproducible recording.mcap every record, the manifest metadata, the resolved scenario as an attachment the data section is; the file hash is not (see below) scenario.resolved.yaml the scenario after migration, base merge and defaults: what actually ran yes metrics.json every metric.sample the run emitted yes run-report.json event, frame and record counts per channel; content_digest yes manifest.json v2xw_core::manifest::Manifest: build, models and card hashes, world, scenario and seed, crypto mode, the files above digested all but build_utc and the recording's file hash progress.jsonl, checkpoint.json progress lines; a resumable checkpoint (--checkpoint-every)

The digest to compare is content_digest: SHA-256 over every message's topic, log_time and bytes in stored order (v2xw_record::Reader::content_digest). The MCAP writer emits its summary-section records from a hash map, so the file's own SHA-256 can differ between two identical runs; the summary is an index and does not change content. --digest with --no-recording streams the same kind of hash without writing a file, for comparing scaling runs at different thread counts. A run resumed from a checkpoint must produce the same digest as the uninterrupted run.

--record-level trades detail for size: full (scene and every record), receptions (no scene), events (no per-reception records), metrics (metric samples and summaries only, for runs of days). --node-only records the NODE-only profile, which refuses every ground-truth record.

items.title: The container
items.text:
MCAP (readable with standard MCAP tools and Foxglove). Two namespaces, never mixed on one topic:

  • vwp/...: the VWP binary frames (Keyframe, Delta, and others) stored verbatim, so a replayed stream is byte-identical to the live one (VWP §7.2; crates/v2xw-record/tests/byte_identity.rs);
  • record/...: serde records for events, telemetry and metrics.

The reader (reader::Reader) verifies chunk checksums, seeks by index, replays frames and treats malformed input as an error, never a panic. v2xw info prints the manifest, channels and verification report. The same reader runs in the browser through crates/v2xw-wasm.

items.title: Channels
items.text:
crates/v2xw-record/src/channels.rs lists every channel with its visibility class (v2xw_core::ctx::Visibility). Main groups:

Visibility Channels gt gt.kinematics, gt.spawn, gt.despawn, gt.attack.action, gt.subject, gt.device_exposure, phy.prr, net.reassembly node node.tx, node.verify, node.drop, node.neighbor, node.security, node.credentials, node.telemetry, mac.cbr, net.bytes, net.frag, sec.cert, sec.pseudonym, proto.msg, det.observation, ma.report, ma.received, ma.case, ma.decision, app.warning, app.advice, privacy.link, privacy.track, pki.case, pki.flow node-and-gt node.rx, phy.rx, msg.latency, app.outcome, pki.knowledge, pki.report_fate public proto.revocation, backend.state, pki.state, signal.priority, traffic.control, scenario.event derived metric.sample mixed snapshot.keyframe, snapshot.delta

A node-and-gt record carries node-visible fields beside ground-truth ones; NODE-only exports project the ground-truth fields out. The table in channels.rs is authoritative for each channel's class.

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
A MetricProvider reads recorded events and reduces them; it never touches engine state. Each metric's MetricDef declares its name, unit, dimensions, aggregation, visibility, definition, source, grid, the minimum sample count below which it reports insufficiency, and what it does not account for (which validation refuses to leave empty). Select with metrics: [all] or a list of metric names; a provider is installed when the list names all or one of its metrics. The metric catalogue lists every metric with its unit, aggregation, visibility, definition and source; it is generated from the definitions.

Family Module Metrics communication comms pdr by distance bin, pdr_all_pairs, per, pdr_by_cause, cbr, pir, goodput, bytes_air, bytes_uu_ul, bytes_uu_dl, bytes_backhaul, bytes_backend, bytes_total, airtime_per_node latency latency e2e_latency (p50, p95, p99) per flow and message type, latency_stage, latency_stage_share, latency_trace_rejected awareness awareness aoi, aoi_peak, nar, delivery_ratio load load channel_occupancy, channel_load, offered_load, carried_load, loss_rate, collision_rate, half_duplex_rate, mac_queue_depth, mac_drops, mac_access_delay overhead overhead security_overhead, net_header_overhead, link_overhead, cert_bytes_share, air_bytes_per_payload_byte, bytes_per_vehicle_hour fragmentation frag frag_sdu_loss, frag_sdu_loss_predicted, frag_sdu_loss_independent, frag_fragment_loss, frag_content_loss, frag_content_loss_predicted security security verify_rate, verify_cost, verify_wait, verify_queue_depth, unverified_ratio, full_cert_share, p2pcd_requests, digest_misses, envelope_overhead, revocation_latency_stage, crl_entries, crl_bytes signing overhead signing (opt-in: metrics: [all, signing]) sig_*: what the signature scheme costs on the air, in devices and in the backend detection detection the confusion matrix (det_tp, det_fp, det_tn, det_fn) and det_recall, det_fpr, det_precision, det_f1, det_accuracy, time_to_detect, time_to_decision, false_accusations detection scores detection (opt-in: metrics: [all, detection-scores]) det_mcc, det_informedness, det_markedness, det_kappa, and the per-message matrix det_message_tp, det_message_fp, det_message_fn, det_message_tn mobility and safety safety ttc_min, ttc_conflicts, pet, drac, headway_time, headway_distance, Edie flow/density/mean_speed, speed, acceleration; time.warmup_s suppresses samples for windows that end inside the warm-up period.

items.title: Statistics
items.text:
Enforced by the types in stats.rs:

  1. every aggregate carries its sample count;
  2. a proportion carries a Wilson score interval; a ratio of sums (bytes over bytes) carries none and says so;
  3. too few samples report insufficiency, never a point estimate;
  4. percentiles state their interpolation rule (type 7, linear);
  5. a zero denominator is insufficiency, not NaN.

Counts, bytes and airtime accumulate as integers; float reductions sort into IEEE-754 total order before summing; binning is on integer grid indices, so a value on a bin edge lands in the same bin on every platform. invariants.rs turns each stated invariant (for example byte conservation) into a runnable check that names what failed and by how much. health.rs and polarity.rs give each headline metric a direction and health bands, used by v2xw compare.

items.title: Exporters (exporters)
items.text:
Exporters run after the run, over the recording, and write into <out>/<id>/.

Id Output recording keeps the MCAP recording jsonl, parquet, arrow one table per recorded channel with a schema.json of declared grids; opts.profile: node drops ground truth veremi per-receiver traces and a ground-truth log in the VeReMi format (codebook: veremi-ext, the F2MD attack enumeration 0-19, or veremi-1, VeReMi 1.0 bit codes; --veremi on v2xw run) sumo-fcd, sumo-tripinfo, sumo-edgedata, sumo-lanedata, sumo-summary, sumo-e1, sumo-e2 SUMO output formats, for tools written against SUMO

Options and file layouts: Datasets and exports. Dataset profiles, the datasheet and the leakage linter that keeps identity and labels out of node-visible features are in crates/v2xw-record/src/dataset/; the release schema is dataset/schema.md.

items.title: Across runs
items.text:
• v2xw experiment run: one results table per sweep, with replication counts, sample counts and intervals; a row with one usable replication carries no interval. figures.rs turns a results table into Plotly JSON.
  • v2xw compare a b: the settings that differ and every headline metric's change, better or worse by its health direction (v2xw/run-comparison/1; JSON, Markdown or CSV).
  • v2xw sensitivity: one-at-a-time perturbations on one seed with expected directions (Sensitivity analysis).

Guides: Running and recording, Comparing runs, Experiments and sweeps.

items.title: Scenarios
items.text:
A scenario file is the whole input of a run: world, fleet, radio, network, messages, security, credential system, threats, detection, metrics and, optionally, a parameter sweep. Apart from output paths and the explicit CLI overrides (which are recorded), there is no configuration outside it, so a run is reproducible from one file and a seed.

Schema: crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/schema.rs (Scenario), current version v2xw/scenario/1. Settings, ranges and their status: configuration.md; every field: the generated reference.

items.title: Loading pipeline
items.text:
bytes -> parse (YAML or JSON) -> migrate to the current schema -> merge meta.base -> deserialise -> validate

Modules under crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/: migrate.rs (one migrator per schema step), merge.rs, validate.rs. The loader reads files only (no environment, clock or network), so two loads of one file give the same Scenario, and Scenario::content_hash over its canonical JSON is the scenario hash in the manifest. validate returns every problem at once, each as a dotted field plus the conflict, for example radio.tiers.phy: 'high' requires mac 'high' (mac is 'medium').

items.title: Overlays (meta.base)
items.text:
A scenario may name a base file, resolved relative to the including file. The merge runs on the untyped document, so "not written" stays distinct from "written as the default":

  • mappings merge key by key, recursively;
  • anything else, including a sequence, is replaced by the overlay;
  • null deletes the base's key.

Most shipped scenarios are short overlays on scenarios/base/city.yaml (a downtown at midday: connected fleet, the US SCMS, eight roadside units at the busiest signalised intersections, detection on every vehicle) or scenarios/base/radio-faceoff.yaml.

items.title: Top-level sections
items.text:
Section Configures schema, meta version; name, description, tags, base seed the master seed; every RNG stream derives from it (hex or decimal) time t0, duration_s, mobility_step_ms, des_resolution, warmup_s, credential calendar (real weekly i-periods from the US epoch, or compressed), fast_forward windows city, world a city of the library, or an explicit world source (kind: osm-xml, sumo-net or procedural with a grid, radial or random generator), buildings, terrain actors vehicles (demand, equipped fraction, driving models, classes), VRUs, roadside units and their placement and roles, the backend deployment weather initial condition and intensity; fronts arrive through events radio rat (dsrc-80211p, lte-v2x-pc5, nr-v2x-pc5, hybrid), tiers per family, model choices, region, channel, MAC and DCC settings net layer (wsmp, gn-btp), GeoNetworking forwarding, fragmenter, backhaul, cellular Uu, backend network, channel access messages sets (bsm, cam, denm, spat, map, srm, ssm, psm, vam, cpm), codec_tier (uper, size-model), rates and intervals security envelope (ieee1609.2, etsi103097), signature, kem, crypto_mode (modeled, real), verification_policy, signer-id policy, pseudonym_change, protocol and its parameters, scms options nodes hardware profiles for OBUs, RSUs and backend entities; compute tiers threats attackers, jammers, compromised_rsus and their attack, eavesdropper detection local detector suites and the MA pipeline metrics metric ids, or [all] exporters output exporters (Datasets and exports) events the timeline apps V2X applications: fcw, eebl, ima, lta, bsw, pcw, rlvw, glosa energy emission, fuel and EV energy models and fleet mobility provider: native (default) or sumo (TraCI) traffic junction and jam behaviour (right turn on red, rerouting, keep-clear, gridlock), signal control (fixed-time, actuated, NEMA, green wave) perception sensor suites for CPM senders and the occlusion rule scale city scale: a microscopic focus region in a mesoscopic city experiment sweep (dotted path to list of values), seeds, replications

Every optional section, and every optional field at its default, serialises as absent, so adding a field to the schema does not move existing scenario hashes.

items.title: The timeline (events)
items.text:
Each item has t, optional until, a type and its parameters; an item may instead fire on a ground-truth condition (when, max_fires, cooldown_s). Types: demand.multiplier, weather.front, attack.wave, outage, param.change, closure, safety.hard-brake, safety.breakdown, safety.cut-in.

events:
  - {t: 60.0, until: 240.0, type: demand.multiplier, value: 1.3}
  - {t: 90.0, until: 270.0, type: safety.breakdown, target: auto}
  - {t: 0.0, type: closure, target: auto}

items.title: Cities
items.text:
A scenario says what happens; a city says where. worlds/cities.yaml (compiled into the binary; v2xw cities lists it) names each city's extract, downtown box and jurisdiction (speed preset, right turn on red and similar rules, v2xw_world::jurisdiction). v2xw run <scenario> --city <id>, the server's run.start/scenario.load and the Studio's city picker replace the scenario's world with the city's. City-independent forms make that work (crates/v2xw-engine/src/city.rs):

  • actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km: demand as a density, multiplied by the imported network's driving-lane length;
  • actors.rsu_placement: {count, roles}: units at the busiest signalised intersections;
  • target: auto on a closure or breakdown; at: busiest-junction on a jammer;
  • the clock keeps its local time of day.

Extracts are fetched with worlds/fetch.sh <id> (Overpass API) into worlds/cache/. More: Worlds and maps.

items.title: Sweeps (experiment)
items.text:
experiment:
  sweep:
    security.protocol.id: [protocol/scms/camp, protocol/etsi/ts102941]
    actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h: [1500.0, 15000.0]
  seeds: [1, 2, 3]
  replications: 2

The plan (v2xw_experiment::plan) is the cross product of the swept values, seed slots and replications in a fixed order, each run's seed derived by hashing from the master seed; the same seed is reused across cells (common random numbers). A swept path must already exist in the serialised scenario, so set an optional field in the base before sweeping it. v2xw experiment run|status|resume executes, journals and aggregates; runs are serial by default (Experiments and sweeps).

The folders:

Folder Holds scenarios/base/ the bases other files overlay: city.yaml, midtown.yaml, radio-faceoff.yaml scenarios/edge/ boundary cases: clock skew, long offline periods, CRL Generator outages, holidays, a 10,000-entry standing CRL, no coverage scenarios/scale/ a scaling ladder (2, 10, 100, 1,000 and 10,000 vehicles) scenarios/real-world/ the realistic SCMS benchmarks on Midtown (DSRC, LTE-V2X and a quarter-fleet version) and Portland, the Midtown realism check, Portland on its measured terrain scenarios/interop/ SUMO interoperation: a SUMO network and a .rou.xml demand (SUMO co-simulation) scenarios/benchmark/ the VeReMi Extension-style legacy-attack export on three seeds (Datasets and exports) scenarios/sensitivity/ the family files and the catalogue the sensitivity sweep runs (Sensitivity analysis) scenarios/platform/ sensitivity specs for platform checks: BSM inter-transmission time, the CBR window, J2945/1 congestion control, RSU application rates, and seed spread scenarios/tests/ fixtures the Rust integration tests and the Studio's end-to-end specs load

Scenarios with a procedural world (for example highway-congestion.yaml, connected-intersections.yaml, credential-lifecycle.yaml, pdr-vs-distance.yaml) run without any download.

items.title: The Studio (browser UI)
items.text:
ui/ is a pnpm workspace (Node 22+, pnpm 10). The Studio adds nothing to the wire: every engine interaction is a VWP v1 frame or JSON-RPC method of protocol/vwp-v1.md. A walk-through of the page for users is the Studio tour; this page is the developer's view.

Package What it is packages/protocol (@vwp/protocol) VWP v1 client: framing, binary decoders, pose dequantisation, slot model, vwp-world/1 parser, typed JSON-RPC client, VwpClient, Web Worker transport; no runtime dependencies packages/viewer (@vwp/viewer) framework-free Three.js viewer: one scene for 2D and 3D, instanced actors, per-tile world geometry, signals, overlays, cameras, picking packages/mock-server (@vwp/mock-server) a Node server speaking the server side of VWP v1 over a synthetic world, for UI development and tests apps/studio (@vwp/studio) the React shell (React, Zustand, uPlot)

items.title: Running
items.text:
pnpm --dir ui install
# engine (any one of these) on :8787
./run-sim.sh
v2xw-server --scenario scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --port 8787
v2xw-server --actors 200 --port 8787                     # synthetic fixture, no map
# page
pnpm --dir ui --filter @vwp/studio dev                   # http://127.0.0.1:5173

VWP_ENGINE (default http://127.0.0.1:8787) sets the engine the dev server proxies /vwp/v1, /rpc, /world and /agent to; VWP_STUDIO_PORT sets the page's port. The endpoints are relative, so the page is same-origin with the engine.

items.title: Structure (ui/apps/studio/src/)
items.text:
Area Where What shell shell/Header.tsx, shell/panels.tsx, shell/route.ts run state, scenario and city picker, clock, panels mirrored in the URL hash viewport components/Viewport.tsx, components/TimeControls.tsx the canvas, overlays and cameras, transport and scrub bar inspector components/Inspector.tsx, components/ObuHud.tsx, components/pki/ a selected node's state, messages, provenance ("why"), log; the OBU HUD; credential-system views settings settings/SettingsWindow.tsx, settings/QuickSettings.tsx every scenario setting, generated from the engine's published surface (scenario.get), validated with scenario.validate, applied with scenario.set metrics metrics/ (Dashboard.tsx, Chart.tsx) live MetricSample series and breakdowns runs components/RunBrowser.tsx, components/ComparisonView.tsx, components/RunDetails.tsx past runs and same-seed comparison assistant components/AgentPanel.tsx, components/CopilotPanel.tsx the optional assistant (/agent/*) state state/engine.ts, state/store.ts the hot path and the React projection

state/engine.ts owns the VwpClient, the Viewer, the decoded world, the provenance dictionary, telemetry rings and metric history. React sees a projection refreshed at 5 Hz (state/store.ts); poses, interpolation and instance writes never pass through React.

Protocol behaviours the UI relies on:

  • view.follow is the telemetry subscription: selecting an actor follows it and Telemetry frames for that node start arriving.
  • Channels start unsubscribed; the app subscribes to the event channels its overlays and markers need at connect.
  • Values carrying a prov_id resolve their provenance with no round trip; others offer the explain method.
  • Sentinel values (0xFFFF, u64::MAX, NaN) mean "not modelled at this tier" and render as n/a.

Replay without an engine. src/lib/replay.ts loads the v2xw-wasm reader and feeds recorded Keyframe/Delta frames, byte for byte as the engine produced them, through the same decoders and pose buffer as the live socket path.

items.text:
pnpm --dir ui typecheck

items.title: Testing and validation
items.text: A check is only trusted if it has been seen to fail. The validation suites and the conformance kit therefore run each check against a deliberately broken input or model as well as the shipped one, and report a check that the fault did not turn red as unproven.

items.title: Where tests live
items.text:
Kind Location Run unit tests #[cfg(test)] modules beside the code cargo test -p <crate> --lib integration tests crates/<crate>/tests/*.rs cargo test -p <crate> --test <name> conformance kit tests/conformance (v2xw-conformance) cargo test -p v2xw-conformance network validation crates/v2xw-netval cargo run --release -p v2xw-netval --bin netval-report traffic validation crates/v2xw-trafficval cargo run --release -p v2xw-trafficval --bin traffic_validation SUMO cross-validation crates/v2xw-interop, crates/v2xw-cli/src/bin/cross_validate.rs just cross-validate (needs SUMO) Python python/tests/ pytest python/tests after maturin develop UI ui/**/test, ui/apps/studio/e2e* pnpm --dir ui test (studio.md)

The whole Rust suite (cargo test --workspace, just test) runs real P-256/P-384 arithmetic and many full engine runs and is long; scope with -p and --test while iterating. Some engine and validation tests import worlds/cache/manhattan.osm.xml (fetch with worlds/fetch.sh manhattan).

items.text: Crate Tests What they establish v2xw-sec official_vectors.rs, cavp.rs, ieee1609_2a_d6.rs, crl_ctl_vectors.rs, ecqv_certs.rs butterfly and linkage values against CAMP and OpenSCMS vectors; NIST CAVP samples for ECDSA P-384, SHA-384 and AES-128-CCM; IEEE 1609.2a Annex D.6 KDF2/MAC1 vectors v2xw-sec equivalence.rs, overhead.rs real and modelled backends give identical outcomes and sizes; envelope overhead equals its derivation byte for byte v2xw-sec real_artefacts.rs the published US SCMS trust lists and chain files decode and verify, when the local cache (not redistributable) is present; V2XW_SCMS_ARTEFACTS=1 makes absence a failure v2xw-record byte_identity.rs, overflow.rs replayed frames equal live frames; malformed input is an error in debug and release v2xw-proto flows.rs, wire_sizes.rs every flow emits exactly its declared stages; every message size has a provenance v2xw-node firewall_sentinel.rs node code cannot reach ground truth (source scan, proven with injected faults) v2xw-engine scenario.rs, sensitivity_expectations.rs, ... loader and validator behaviour; expectation rows load and are consistent v2xw-cli cli.rs, longrun.rs two runs agree on content_digest; a resumed run equals the uninterrupted one

items.title: The conformance kit (tests/conformance)
items.text:
cargo test -p v2xw-conformance                     # everything
cargo test -p v2xw-conformance --test vwp          # the VWP v1 wire checklist, one test per item
cargo test -p v2xw-conformance --test kit          # plug-in suite, golden digests, firewall
cargo run  -p v2xw-conformance --bin v2xw-golden-digest

Paths are relative to tests/conformance/.

Part Library What wire checklist src/checklist.rs, tests/vwp/ each item of protocol/vwp-v1.md §10, named after its id; items owned by another crate are delegated and the pointer is checked; items that cannot be established in process are recorded with the reason plug-in suite src/plugin.rs for a contributor's model: no private RNG, no wall clock, no ground truth, valid card with a source for every default, determinism under reordering and thread count, quantised outputs, declared RNG domains match the ones used golden determinism src/golden.rs, golden/*.json scenario hash, world hash, record digest and per-channel counts of fixed scenarios, no floats, paths or timestamps; a missing record fails; re-bless with V2XW_CONFORMANCE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p v2xw-conformance --test kit golden only for an intended output change interface firewall src/firewall.rs the node firewall, generalised to other crates

items.title: Validation suites
items.text:
v2xw-netval holds each network layer to a reference from outside the crate that implements it: the PHY to its published equations and receiver tables, the MAC to IEEE 802.11 / EN 302 663, DCC to TS 102 687 and SAE J2945/1, the sidelink to the 3GPP procedures, headers and messages to their tables and to an independent decoder, the security envelope to OpenSSL, and whole runs to conservation, metamorphic and determinism properties. Each Check runs in Mode::Honest (must pass) and Mode::Faulted with a named realistic fault (must fail), on every invocation. Faults are injected at the model-check boundary, so no rebuild per fault is needed.

v2xw-trafficval groups its checks as model (IDM, MOBIL, gap acceptance and social force against their papers; ring-road fundamental diagram; string stability; the Sugiyama ring), calibration (saturation flow, start-up lost time, speeds and accelerations, turning, critical gaps, pedestrians, motorcycles against published measurements), safety (TTC and PET distributions, SSAM thresholds, conflict rates), invariants (no red entry, no conflicting greens under NEMA, no jumps at closures) and city imports. The traffic_calibration study compares fundamental diagrams (Greenshields and triangular fits, capacity against the HCM), stop-and-go wave speed, headway distributions, string stability and the Sugiyama ring with theory and with SUMO's default driver, and exits non-zero when a held figure leaves its band.

just validation-report runs both suites and writes target/validation/network.md and target/validation/traffic.md; just cross-validate compares traffic with SUMO on a grid and on Midtown and the radio with Veins and OpenCV2X results, writing target/validation/cross-validation.md. v2xw check-traffic <run> audits any finished run.

What each suite and the Python cross-check tools prove, and how to run them: Validation and conformance tools. CI gates and the contribution workflow: Contributing.

items.title: Continuous integration
items.text: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs, on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace. A determinism job imports tests/fixtures/midtown-6block.osm.xml on each platform and publishes the world and VWP payload digests; a final job fails unless all three platforms agree (just world-hash prints this machine's value).

items.title: How to cite
items.text:
V2X World is written by Ahmed Zaidan (ORCID 0009-0009-4590-7996). The repository's CITATION.cff is the citation record (GitHub's "Cite this repository" button reads it). Its current values:

Field Value title V2X World author Ahmed Zaidan (0009-0009-4590-7996) version 0.1.0 licence Apache-2.0 type software keywords V2X, connected vehicles, SCMS, IEEE 1609.2, misbehavior detection, misbehavior authority, vehicular PKI, simulation repository https://github.com/ak3zaidan/V2X-World website https://ak3zaidan.github.io/V2X-World/

To cite the software:

@software{zaidan_v2xworld,
  title   = {{V2X World}},
  author  = {Zaidan, Ahmed},
  version = {0.1.0},
  year    = {2026},
  license = {Apache-2.0},
  url     = {https://github.com/ak3zaidan/V2X-World}
}

A paper describing the simulator is in preparation (arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX, a placeholder); the entry below will be filled in when it is available:

@misc{zaidan_v2xworld_paper,
  title         = {TODO: paper title},
  author        = {Zaidan, Ahmed},
  year          = {TODO},
  eprint        = {XXXX.XXXXX},
  archivePrefix = {arXiv},
  url           = {https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX}
}

The V2X-World dataset on Hugging Face is licensed CC BY 4.0, which requires attribution: cite it with the software entry above (or the paper, once it is out) and name the dataset release you used.

For a result, also report what makes the run reproducible: the scenario file (or its scenario_hash), the seed, the engine's build_hash and git_commit, and the content_digest of the recording, all in the run's manifest.json and run-report.json (Recording format). Cite the models' sources as their cards give them (Standards and references).

items.title: Standards and references
items.text:
The standards, specifications and papers the engine's code cites, with the sections it cites most and the modules that implement or calibrate against them. The list is built from the citations in crates/ (doc comments and model cards); a document the code does not cite is not listed. The per-parameter source of every model default is on its card, published on the Model parameters page.

Licensed text

Several of these documents (SAE, IEEE, ETSI before publication, 3GPP drafts) are licensed. The engine reproduces field names, identifiers, constants and table values needed for interoperability, never the text. Test vectors transcribed from licensed documents carry their citation and the source file's hash (tools/oracle/transcribe).

items.title: Python API
items.text: The v2xw package (python/v2xw/) drives the engine from Python: load and validate a scenario, run it, read its metrics and its recording, and write plug-ins. It is a binding, not a second implementation: every call delegates to the native module v2xw._v2xw, built from crates/v2xw-py. Typed stubs ship in _v2xw.pyi; python/tests/test_stubs.py holds them equal to the module. A walkthrough is on Python.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install maturin
cd python && maturin develop                 # editable, into the active virtualenv
cd python && maturin build --release         # a wheel in ../target/wheels
pip install 'v2xw[arrow]'                    # optional pyarrow for the zero-copy table paths

requires-python >= 3.9. Without pyarrow, every table still crosses as Arrow IPC bytes.

import v2xw

scenario = v2xw.Scenario.load("scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml")
run = v2xw.run(scenario, recording="run.mcap", build_utc="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")
pdr = run.metrics.series("pdr")
rec = v2xw.Recording.open("run.mcap")
table = rec.arrow("node.tx")

items.title: Module v2xw
items.text:
Name Signature Meaning run run(scenario, *, build_utc=None, recording=None, metrics=True, metric_window_s=1.0, ma_policy=None) -> Run runs a Scenario (or a path to one). build_utc is the manifest timestamp; left out, it is read here, the package's only wall-clock read, and excluded from every digest. recording is the MCAP path, or None for no file. metrics registers the metric providers. metric_window_s is the aggregation window (0: one sample per metric). ma_policy is a MaPolicy for every provider MA that would run the deployment-wide rule run_twice run_twice(scenario, *, build_utc, ma_policy_factory=None) -> (str, str) runs twice and returns both record-stream digests: the determinism gate. ma_policy_factory builds a fresh policy per run read_ipc read_ipc(buffer: bytes) -> pyarrow.Table reads an Arrow IPC stream buffer (from Metrics.ipc or Recording.table); raises ImportError naming the extra if pyarrow is missing math class of static functions the engine's deterministic transcendentals (below) plugins, conformance modules the plug-in seam and its checks __version__ str the package version

Errors: V2xwError (base), ScenarioError (the scenario will not build or validate), RecordingError (a recording cannot be written or read), MetricError (a provider refused its definition), DeterminismError (a determinism or conformance check failed).

items.title: Module v2xw.conformance
items.text:
The plug-in checks, split between the engine's call path and Python-side facts.

Name Signature Meaning check check(model, *, quantum=1e-3) -> Report the whole suite over a car-following plug-in (an instance or an attached handle): native_checks, a purity sweep under purity_guard, and scan_source native_checks native_checks(model, *, quantum=1e-3) -> list[Check] through the engine's call path: determinism, thread-count independence, dyn-compatibility, finiteness, quantisation to quantum, card validation and completeness purity_guard context manager yielding a list replaces random.random, time.time, datetime.now and relatives with functions that raise, recording each call scan_source scan_source(obj) -> Check advisory: imports of banned modules in the plug-in's source, read with ast Check frozen dataclass (check, passed, detail, advisory=False) one check's outcome Report frozen dataclass (checks) properties passed (no non-advisory failure), failures, warnings; raise_for_failures() raises DeterminismError or returns self

Passing the suite is necessary, not sufficient: hidden state between calls is caught only by comparing two real runs (v2xw.run_twice).

items.title: Configuration overview
items.text:
Every setting that changes a run is a field of the scenario file. There is no other configuration file and no environment variable that changes results; see How settings work for where each setting is defined in the code and the validation rules worth knowing.

This section has three parts:

Part What it is Source Generated reference one page per top-level scenario section, every editable leaf with its type, unit, default, range or choices, level and status; plus model parameters generated from the engine How settings work the files a setting is defined in, the published surface, the validator hand-written Curated tables settings grouped by research question, per-domain parameter inventories, SCMS constants, sensitivity results hand-written, see below

items.title: How the generated reference is produced
items.text:
The reference is produced from the same data the Studio's settings window and the assistant read, so it cannot describe a field the engine does not have or miss one it does.

flowchart LR
    S["schema.rs<br/>(reflected at build time)"] --> P["scenario::publish::surface()"]
    V["validate.rs<br/>BOUNDS, CHOICES, KEY_STATUS"] --> P
    O["options.rs<br/>labels, presets, slot ids"] --> P
    G["guide.rs<br/>level, explanation, recommended"] --> P
    R["Registry<br/>model cards"] --> P
    P --> D["dump_settings example<br/>target/docs-settings.json"]
    D --> Y["tools/docs/gen_config_reference.py"]
    Y --> M["docs/configuration/reference/*.md"]
    P --> RPC["scenario.get / scenario.schema RPC"]
    RPC --> UI["Studio settings window"]
just docs-gen
# which runs:
cargo run -q -p v2xw-engine --example dump_settings -- --out target/docs-settings.json
python3 tools/docs/gen_config_reference.py target/docs-settings.json
cargo run -q -p v2xw-engine --example dump_metrics -- --out target/docs-metrics.json
python3 tools/docs/gen_metric_catalogue.py target/docs-metrics.json

The last two lines generate the metric catalogue the same way, from the MetricDef of every provider the engine can install.

The generator names no scenario field itself: sections, subsections, units, defaults, ranges, choices, statuses and descriptions all come from its input. It fails if a published field lands on no page or on two, and if a generated page is missing from the nav of mkdocs.yml.

The engine's own tests hold the input honest (crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/publish.rs):

Test Guarantees every_shipped_scenario_is_described every key in every file under scenarios/ is in the published schema the_published_defaults_load a document built from the published defaults passes the loader, whose deny_unknown_fields rejects an invented key every_leaf_has_a_status every leaf matches a KEY_STATUS row every_number_publishes_a_unit every numeric leaf has a unit, read off its name or declared

Do not edit docs/configuration/reference/ by hand

Change the engine (see Extending: settings) and run just docs-gen.

items.title: How to read a row
items.text:
Each section page opens with its group and blurb, then one table per subsection:

Column Meaning Comes from Setting the dotted path. [] is a list element (actors.rsus[].profile), * a map key (nodes.per_class.*). Each row has an anchor, #s-<path-with-dashes> schema.rs field names after serde renames Type the JSON type; optional when the field may be absent or null; the Rust type in brackets where the JSON type alone is ambiguous schema.rs Unit the unit. Field names carry their unit as a suffix (_s, _ms, _us, _ns, _m, _km, _mps, _mps2, _hz, _db, _dbm, _dbi, _deg, _kbps, _mbps, _veh_per_h); the few numeric leaves whose name does not carry one declare it in publish.rs publish.rs UNIT_SUFFIXES Default the value the loader uses when the field is absent. Blank means absent is meaningful (the row's description says what happens) Scenario::minimal() serialised Range or choices [lo, hi] or (lo, hi] for a numeric bound (no upper value means unbounded); a list of values for a closed set; "(or another value)" for an open set; "narrowed by x when y" when another field restricts the set; "recommended ..." advice for basic fields validate::BOUNDS, validate::CHOICES, options, guide Level basic for the fields that decide what a run models; advanced for model internals, fidelity tiers and developer switches guide::level_of Status whether editing the field changes the run (vocabulary below) validate::KEY_STATUS Description the field's doc comment and its plain-language explanation; for a model slot, the family and a link to its parameters; for a conditional field, when it applies; for a status other than wired, the status note schema.rs, guide, KEY_STATUS

A closed set whose values have labels gets a second table under the row with each value, its label and its meaning (from scenario::options).

items.title: Status vocabulary
items.text:
Status Label Meaning wired Active The engine reads it and it changes the run. partial Partly active The engine reads part of it, or acts on it only under the conditions the field's own note states. Editing it may do less than it appears to. not-implemented Not yet implemented Validated and part of the scenario digest, and read by nothing. Editing it changes the scenario hash and nothing else. refused Only its implemented values load The loader rejects every value this build cannot act on, so the field exists but its choices are narrower than the schema's. descriptive Description Describes the scenario (name, tags, notes); kept in the run's record and by design changes nothing computed. unknown Unclassified No KEY_STATUS row matches. The every_leaf_has_a_status test keeps this out of a build.

KEY_STATUS entries are path prefixes and the longest match wins, so a section is classified once and exceptions are stated beneath it. The vocabulary itself is published (statuses in the surface), so the Studio and the generator render it without hard-coding the words. The reference index counts the settings per status.

items.title: Scenario fields and model parameters
items.text:
A scenario field is a typed leaf of the scenario, checked by the loader against BOUNDS and CHOICES. A slot is a field that selects a model; its value is a ModelChoice:

radio:
  models:
    propagation:
      id: propagation/winner-plus-b1       # the model's registry id
      params: { heights: effective }       # overrides of the card's defaults

The parameters a model accepts are not scenario fields of their own. They live on the model's card (v2xw_core::card::ModelCard), each with a unit, default, range and source, and are listed on the generated Model parameters page, which also lists every slot with its family and selectable ids. Anything not named in params keeps the card's value, so a parameter set is content-addressable from the id and the overrides. Some slots take a bare id instead of { id, params }; the slot table on the models page says which.

A few model parameters are also published as typed fields so the settings window needs no JSON for them (for example the Misbehaviour Authority's detection.ma.params.*); they appear on their section page with a range and status like any other leaf.

Parameters marked todo-calibrate

A card parameter with no published source is marked todo-calibrate with a calibration plan rather than given an invented value. The models page shows each card's list.

items.title: By status
items.text: Status Settings wired 612 descriptive 4 refused 4 partial 64 Status Label Meaning wired Active The engine reads this and it changes the run. partial Partly active The engine reads part of this, or acts on it only under the conditions the field's own note states. not-implemented Not yet implemented Validated and recorded in the scenario digest, and read by nothing. Editing it does not change the run. refused Only its implemented values load The loader refuses any value this build cannot act on, so the field is real but its choices are narrower than the schema's. descriptive Description Describes the scenario: shown in the page and kept in the run's record. By design it changes nothing the run computes. unknown Unclassified This build does not say whether the engine acts on it.
