items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description actors.vehicles.demand.kind string mobility/demand/none mobility/demand/poisson, mobility/demand/tr36885-drop, mobility/demand/none, mobility/demand/sumo-rou, mobility/demand/routes, mobility/demand/trips, mobility/demand/od-matrix, mobility/demand/counts, mobility/demand/gtfs, mobility/demand/purposes, mobility/demand/composite advanced wired The demand model's id, e.g. mobility/demand/poisson. Model slot: family mobility, see model parameters. actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h number veh/h [0, 100000000]recommended 500 (night) to 4,500 (rush hour) on a city extract. basic wired Vehicles per hour offered to the network, when the model takes a rate. How many vehicles drive into the map each hour. More vehicles means more radios sharing one channel, which is what makes V2X congest. actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km number km [0, 1000] advanced wired Vehicles per hour per kilometre of driving lane: the arrival rate stated so that it fits any city. Once the world is built it becomes rate_veh_per_h (the rate times the network's driving-lane length), and it wins over a rate_veh_per_h the file also gives. Midtown's 119 km of driving lane at 25 veh/h/km is 3,000 veh/h. actors.vehicles.demand.fleet_size integer vehicles [1, 50000]recommended 2 to 50 to watch individual vehicles; 100 to 300 for channel load on this machine. basic wired Hold exactly this many vehicles on the road for the whole run: every trip that ends is replaced by a new one, and a trip that cannot enter or has no route is redrawn. The arrival rate is then not used. Absent runs the arrival process. Keeps exactly this many vehicles driving for the whole run: when one finishes its trip a new one sets off, as in a field trial with a fixed test fleet. Leave it empty to let vehicles arrive at the hourly rate instead. actors.vehicles.demand.params json (serde_json::Value) null advanced wired The model's own parameters, in the shape its parameter struct deserialises. actors.vehicles.classes.*.fraction number [0, 1] advanced wired Its share of the fleet, 0..=1. The shares across classes must sum to 1. actors.vehicles.classes.*.obu string obu/cohda-mk5, obu/cohda-mk6c-qualcomm-9150, obu/generic-automotive-soc-no-hsm, obu/pq-capable-hypothetical, obu/unex-obu-301-craton2, obu/unex-obu-301-craton2-software advanced wired The hardware profile its OBU runs, or null for an unequipped class. actors.vehicles.equipped_fraction number 1.0 [0, 1]recommended 0.05 (early deployment) to 1 (every vehicle). basic wired What fraction of vehicles carry an OBU. 0.0 is a legal scenario: a pure traffic run with no radio. The share of vehicles that carry a V2X radio. Today's deployments are a few percent; a mandate would equip every new vehicle. actors.vehicles.driving json (v2xw_mobility::carfollowing::library::DrivingSpec) advanced wired Driving actors.vehicles.drivers.realism string calibrated, identical, heterogeneous, humanrecommended Calibrated for city runs; human for congestion and shockwave studies; identical to test a model in isolation. basic wired The driver population: calibrated (the default), identical, heterogeneous or human. How human the drivers are. Real drivers differ from one another, react late and misjudge gaps, which is what turns dense traffic into stop-and-go waves (Treiber, Kesting & Helbing 2006). actors.vehicles.drivers.parameter_spread number [0, 2] advanced wired Overrides how far drivers differ in time gap, acceleration, braking and standstill gap: a multiplier on the per-class spread (0 none, 1 as fitted to real drivers). actors.vehicles.drivers.reaction_time_s number s [0, 2]recommended 0.6 to 1.2 s; leave unset to use the realism preset's. basic wired Overrides the drivers' reaction time in car following, seconds (0 reacts at once). How long a driver takes to respond to the car ahead. 0.7 s is a prepared driver's brake reaction, 1.25 s a surprised one's (Green 2000). actors.vehicles.drivers.perception_error number [0, 3] advanced wired Overrides how badly drivers misjudge the gap and the closing speed: a multiplier on the Human Driver Model's estimation errors (0 none, 1 as published). actors.vehicles.drivers.truck_lane_restriction boolean advanced wired Keeps trucks out of the leftmost lane of a motorway with three or more lanes. actors.vehicles.drivers.motorcycle_filtering boolean advanced wired Overrides the jurisdiction's rule on motorcycles filtering between stopped cars; true turns on the sub-lane model if the scenario has none. actors.vehicles.drivers.distraction boolean recommended Off (today); on for safety-benefit studies of FCW and EEBL, with realism human. basic wired Drivers look away from the road: on-path dwells and off-path glances drawn from the naturalistic fits of Morando, Victor & Dozza 2019, the vehicle ahead seen as last seen while the eyes are off, and an FCW or EEBL warning from the vehicle's own unit bringing them back (v2xw_mobility::drivers §6). Unset is off. Whether drivers look away from the road now and then, as real drivers do about 800 times an hour (mirrors, instruments, a phone). While they look away they do not see the car ahead brake; a forward-collision or brake-light warning from their own V2X unit makes them look back. actors.vehicles.drivers.max_accel_mps2 number m/s² [0.3, 5]recommended 1.0 to 2.0 m/s². advanced wired The passenger car's comfortable maximum acceleration a (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000), m/s². Replaces the model's calibration for cars; every driver still gets their own style and spread around it. Unset is the model's (1.4 m/s² for the urban IDM). How hard a car driver accelerates when the road ahead is clear. actors.vehicles.drivers.comfort_decel_mps2 number m/s² [0.5, 6]recommended 1.5 to 3.0 m/s². advanced wired The passenger car's comfortable deceleration b, m/s². Unset is the model's (2.0 m/s²). How hard a car driver brakes in normal driving (emergency braking is harder). actors.vehicles.drivers.time_headway_s number s [0.3, 4]recommended 1.0 s (aggressive) to 2.0 s (cautious); about 1.5 s typical. basic wired The passenger car's desired time gap to the vehicle ahead T, s. Shorter gaps raise road capacity and shorten the time a warning has to act. Unset is the model's (about 1.2 to 1.5 s). The time gap drivers keep to the car ahead. Shorter gaps fit more cars on the road and leave less time to react to a warning. actors.vehicles.drivers.min_gap_m number m [0.5, 10]recommended 1.5 to 3 m. advanced wired The gap a passenger car keeps to a stopped vehicle s0, m. Unset is the model's (2 m). The distance drivers leave to the car in front when queued at a light. actors.vehicles.drivers.politeness number [0, 1]recommended 0.2 to 0.5. advanced wired MOBIL's politeness factor p (Kesting, Treiber and Helbing 2007): 0 is a selfish driver who changes lane whenever it helps them, 1 weighs the followers' loss as much as their own gain. Unset is 0.5 (Kesting 2007 reports 0.2 to 0.5 as realistic). Applies to every class. How much drivers care about the cars behind them when changing lanes: 0 is selfish, 1 fully considerate. actors.vehicles.drivers.lane_change_threshold_mps2 number m/s² [0, 2]recommended 0.1 to 0.3 m/s². advanced wired MOBIL's lane-change threshold Δa_th, m/s²: the least advantage worth changing lane for. Unset is 0.1 m/s² (ibid.). The least advantage a lane change must bring before a driver bothers. actors.vehicles.drivers.speed_factor number [0.5, 1.5]recommended 1.0 (SUMO's default) to 1.1; 0.9 for cautious traffic. basic wired How fast drivers choose to drive on a free road, as a multiple of the posted limit: the population mean of SUMO's speedFactor. Unset is 1.0 (SUMO's default). How fast drivers go on an empty street compared with the speed limit: 1.1 means the average driver goes 10 % over. actors.vehicles.drivers.speed_spread number [0, 3]recommended 1 (SUMO's spread, about ±10 % for cars); 0 to 2. advanced wired How far drivers differ in that chosen speed: a multiplier on each class's deviation (SUMO speedDev, 0.1 for a car). 0 gives everyone the mean. Unset is 1. How much drivers differ in the speed they choose: 0 makes everyone drive the same speed. actors.vehicles.drivers.red_runner_share number [0, 1]recommended 0 (the default); 0.05 to 0.2 to study red-light-violation warnings. Field studies count roughly 1 to 5 red entries per 1,000 vehicles at urban signals (Bonneson, Zimmerman & Brewer, TTI 0-4027, 2002, as FHWA's red-light-running guidance quotes it). advanced wired The share of drivers who run reds: they go on an amber inside their threshold without checking they reach the line before the red. Unset is 0. The share of drivers who keep going on amber even when they will reach the line after it turns red, as red-light runners do; 0 makes every driver clear on amber. actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.enabled boolean advanced wired Whether drivers commit violations at all. Unset is false. actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.red_run_share number [0, 1]recommended 0.6 (the default) with the 0.6 s mean tolerance reproduces 1.0 red-light violation per 10,000 vehicle-cycles and 3 to 6 per 1,000 vehicles (Bonneson, Zimmerman & Quiroga, TTI 0-4196-P1, Table 1); 0 for none. advanced wired The share of drivers who enter on red within their tolerance. Unset is 0.6, calibrated so that the run reproduces 1.0 violation per 10,000 vehicle-cycles (Bonneson et al., TTI 0-4196-P1, Table 1, Texas). With violations enabled, the share of drivers who will still enter after the light turns red, each up to their own lateness (exponential, mean red_run_tolerance_mean_s). actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.red_run_tolerance_mean_s number s [0, 4] advanced wired The mean of a runner's tolerance after the red onset, seconds (exponential). Unset is 0.6 s: a median entry 0.42 s into red (TTI 0-4196-P1 Figure 4: under 0.5 s). actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.red_run_tolerance_max_s number s [0, 16] advanced wired The longest tolerance, seconds. Unset is 4.0 s (98 % of violations within 4.0 s, TTI 0-4196-P1 Table 3). actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.amber_tail_max_s number s [5.5, 12] advanced wired The longest amber threshold drawn, seconds: the Zegeer & Deen 1978 logistic's tail beyond the dilemma zone's far edge. Unset is 8 s; 5.5 keeps the clamp. actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.fail_to_yield_share number [0, 1] advanced wired The probability that a driver fails to yield at a junction where they must give way (SUMO jmIgnoreFoeProb). Unset is 0 (todo-calibrate: no field rate was read). actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.ignore_foe_speed_mps number m/s [0, 40] advanced wired The fastest foe a failing driver ignores, m/s (SUMO jmIgnoreFoeSpeed). Unset is 5. actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.crashes boolean advanced wired Whether a collision resolves to a crash state. Unset is true. actors.vehicles.drivers.violations.crash_clearance_s number s [0, 86400] advanced wired How long a crashed vehicle stands before it is cleared, seconds. Unset is 900 s (a choice, todo-calibrate). actors.vehicles.drivers.start_reaction_s number s [0.3, 3]recommended 1.08 s (Bonneson 1992, a 1.22 s mean); 0.8 to 1.5 s. advanced wired The median time a driver takes to move off when the light turns green or a crosswalk clears, seconds. Unset is 1.08 s (Bonneson 1992's 1.22 s mean start-response, lognormal σ 0.5). How long the first driver in line takes to react when the light turns green. actors.vehicles.drivers.queue_start_delay_s number s [0.05, 3]recommended 0.5 s (calibrated to measured discharge headways); 0.3 to 1.0 s. basic wired The median delay before a queued driver moves off after the car in front does, seconds: what sets the start-up lost time and the saturation flow at a light. Unset is 0.5 s (calibrated to Greenshields 1947 discharge headways). How long each driver in a queue waits after the car in front moves before moving off. It decides how many cars get through each green. actors.vehicles.drivers.truck.max_accel_mps2 number m/s² [0.3, 5]recommended 0.5 to 1.3 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable maximum acceleration a, m/s². How hard truck drivers accelerate when the road ahead is clear. actors.vehicles.drivers.truck.comfort_decel_mps2 number m/s² [0.5, 6]recommended 1.5 to 4 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable deceleration b, m/s². How hard truck drivers brake in normal driving. actors.vehicles.drivers.truck.time_headway_s number s [0.3, 4]recommended 1.5 to 2.5 s. advanced wired Desired time gap to the vehicle ahead T, s. The time gap truck drivers keep to the vehicle in front. actors.vehicles.drivers.truck.min_gap_m number m [0.3, 10]recommended 2.5 to 4 m. advanced wired Gap kept to a stopped vehicle s0, m. The distance truck drivers leave to the vehicle in front when queued. actors.vehicles.drivers.bus.max_accel_mps2 number m/s² [0.3, 5]recommended 0.5 to 1.2 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable maximum acceleration a, m/s². How hard bus drivers accelerate when the road ahead is clear. actors.vehicles.drivers.bus.comfort_decel_mps2 number m/s² [0.5, 6]recommended 1.5 to 4 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable deceleration b, m/s². How hard bus drivers brake in normal driving. actors.vehicles.drivers.bus.time_headway_s number s [0.3, 4]recommended 1.5 to 2.5 s. advanced wired Desired time gap to the vehicle ahead T, s. The time gap bus drivers keep to the vehicle in front. actors.vehicles.drivers.bus.min_gap_m number m [0.3, 10]recommended 2.5 to 4 m. advanced wired Gap kept to a stopped vehicle s0, m. The distance bus drivers leave to the vehicle in front when queued. actors.vehicles.drivers.motorcycle.max_accel_mps2 number m/s² [0.3, 5]recommended 2 to 5 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable maximum acceleration a, m/s². How hard motorcyclists accelerate when the road ahead is clear. actors.vehicles.drivers.motorcycle.comfort_decel_mps2 number m/s² [0.5, 6]recommended 2.5 to 4 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable deceleration b, m/s². How hard motorcyclists brake in normal driving. actors.vehicles.drivers.motorcycle.time_headway_s number s [0.3, 4]recommended 0.8 to 1.5 s. advanced wired Desired time gap to the vehicle ahead T, s. The time gap motorcyclists keep to the vehicle in front. actors.vehicles.drivers.motorcycle.min_gap_m number m [0.3, 10]recommended 1 to 2 m. advanced wired Gap kept to a stopped vehicle s0, m. The distance motorcyclists leave to the vehicle in front when queued. actors.vehicles.drivers.bicycle.max_accel_mps2 number m/s² [0.3, 5]recommended 0.8 to 1.5 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable maximum acceleration a, m/s². How hard cyclists accelerate when the road ahead is clear. actors.vehicles.drivers.bicycle.comfort_decel_mps2 number m/s² [0.5, 6]recommended 1.5 to 3 m/s². advanced wired Comfortable deceleration b, m/s². How hard cyclists brake in normal driving. actors.vehicles.drivers.bicycle.time_headway_s number s [0.3, 4]recommended 1 to 2 s. advanced wired Desired time gap to the vehicle ahead T, s. The time gap cyclists keep to the vehicle in front. actors.vehicles.drivers.bicycle.min_gap_m number m [0.3, 10]recommended 0.5 to 1.5 m. advanced wired Gap kept to a stopped vehicle s0, m. The distance cyclists leave to the vehicle in front when queued. actors.vehicles.gnss.quality string reid-2019 reid-2019, j2945-1, rtkrecommended reid-2019 (the default: city streets are not the open sky J2945/1 tests in); j2945-1 to study a certified device at its test accuracy. basic wired The receiver's quality: reid-2019, the measured production receiver (3.07 m horizontal at 68 %, Reid et al. 2019), unless set; j2945-1, a receiver that meets SAE J2945/1's open-sky accuracies (1.5 m horizontal, 3 m vertical at 68 %; heading noise and the low-speed heading latch); rtk, an RTK-corrected one (0.26 m). The urban classes degrade each the same way (J10, 11 §5; 09 §5 keeps the measured receiver the default). How good the vehicles' GPS receivers are: the measured production receiver (about 3 m), one that meets the SAE J2945/1 open-sky accuracies (1.5 m), or RTK (about 0.3 m). Every safety message carries this position. actors.vehicles.gnss.rtk boolean recommended Off for today's fleet; on to study what precise positioning buys. basic wired An RTK-corrected receiver (Reid 2019's OxTS RT3000 rows: 0.26 m at the 68th percentile) rather than a standard one (about 1.5 m). Unset is standard. Whether vehicles position themselves with survey-grade corrected GPS (about 0.3 m) instead of an ordinary receiver (about 1.5 m). Every safety message carries this position. actors.vehicles.gnss.outlier_rate_hz number Hz [0, 0.5]recommended 0.01 per second (default); 0 for clean positions. advanced wired How often a fix jumps by an outlier, per second. Unset is 0.01. How often a vehicle's GPS fix jumps away for a moment. actors.vehicles.gnss.outlier_magnitude_m number m [1, 200]recommended 5 to 30 m. advanced wired How far an outlier puts the fix, metres. Unset is 12 m. How far such a jump puts the reported position. actors.vehicles.gnss.burst_rate_hz number Hz [0, 0.5]recommended 0.006 per second (default); higher for a dense downtown. advanced wired How often a degraded burst (multipath, an urban canyon) starts, per second. Unset is 0.006. How often a stretch of poor positioning starts, as among tall buildings. actors.vehicles.gnss.outage_probability number [0, 1]recommended 0 (default) to 0.05. advanced wired The chance each fix is lost entirely. Unset is 0. The chance each position fix is lost altogether, as in a tunnel. actors.vehicles.gnss.smoothing_tau_s number s [0, 600]recommended 100 s (the US real-world presets, RTCA DO-229's smoothing constant); 0 for raw fixes. advanced wired The receiver's position-smoothing time constant, seconds: the receiver propagates its solution with its own Doppler velocity and blends each raw fix in at this time constant, as deployed receivers do (gnss/error/gauss-markov module docs). Unset or 0 outputs every raw fix, whose white noise makes consecutive 10 Hz BSMs disagree by metres (R-USFP). How slowly the GPS receiver blends new fixes into the position it reports, steering by its own measured speed in between, as real receivers do. 0 reports every raw fix, which jumps by metres between messages. actors.vehicles.gnss.static_hold_mps number m/s [0, 1.5]recommended 0.3 m/s (the US real-world presets); 0 for off. advanced wired The receiver's static-hold threshold, m/s: below this measured speed it holds its position and reports zero velocity. Unset or 0 is off; read only with smoothing_tau_s. Below this speed the GPS receiver treats the vehicle as stopped: it holds the position and reports zero speed. Needs the smoothing. actors.vehicles.gnss.velocity_noise_mps number m/s [0, 0.5]recommended Unset (default) to compare with earlier runs; 0 with the BSM timing model on, whose fitted output noise then carries the message-level speed and heading noise. advanced wired The receiver's velocity output noise, m/s per horizontal axis, drawn afresh at every fix. Unset is the GPS SPS committed velocity accuracy (0.2 m/s at 95 %, σ 0.102 m/s), which as a white 10 Hz noise makes consecutive BSMs' speeds differ by sd 0.14 m/s, where CV-pilot locked devices' differ by 0.045 m/s. 0 leaves the BSM-level speed and heading noise to bsm_timing's fitted output_noise. How much the GPS receiver's reported speed jitters from one fix to the next. Unset uses the GPS service's 95 % accuracy figure, which makes consecutive messages' speeds differ about three times more than real CV-pilot units' do. actors.vehicles.gnss.stated_sigma_m number m [0, 12.7]recommended Unset (default) to compare with earlier runs; 0.3 m (Tampa CV pilot) or 2.0 m (Orem) to match a deployment. advanced wired The one-sigma horizontal accuracy the receiver states in each BSM's J2735 PositionalAccuracy.semiMajor, metres (the median over devices). Unset or 0 states the model's own honest 95 % radius (about 6.5 m with raw fixes, 5.1 m smoothed). Deployed OBUs state far less than their real error: the CV-pilot medians are 0.30 m Tampa, 0.40 m NYC, 0.50 m Wyoming and a constant 2.00 m Orem (detect-fix3, measured with tools/realdata). The position accuracy each car's radio claims in its messages (one standard deviation). Unset claims the receiver's true error statistics; real deployed units claim much less than their real error, which makes detectors that trust the claim stricter. actors.vehicles.gnss.stated_sigma_log_sd number [0, 3]recommended 0.81 with 0.3 m (Tampa's spread); 0 with 2.0 m (Orem's units all claim the same). advanced wired The per-device spread of that stated accuracy: a lognormal's log-sd, drawn once per receiver. Unset or 0 states the median on every device; Tampa's per-device medians give 0.81. How much the claimed accuracy differs from one car to the next. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.enabled boolean recommended Off (default) to compare with earlier runs; on for honest-trigger studies. advanced wired Turns the model on. Unset or false is off (every existing run unchanged). Gives each car's radio its own message timing, as real units have: some stamp each message with the instant of the GPS fix (locked), others do not (free), and those now and then send a position one fix too old or too new, or the last one again. Real CV-pilot data shows that is what makes honest cars trip the US position-consistency check. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.calibration string recommended data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot.yaml when present; unset uses provisional built-in values. advanced wired A v2xw.bsm_timing.v1 calibration file (YAML), as the real-data pipeline writes it (data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot.yaml). Unset is the built-in values, which are PROVISIONAL (CV-pilot sample statistics, research/synthesis/check-realdata-and-vesnos.md §2.2-2.4). A timing calibration file fitted to real CV-pilot messages. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.locked_share number [0, 1]recommended 0.25 (Tampa CV pilot, built in); sweep 0 to 1. advanced wired The share of OBUs in the locked class (secMark on the GNSS fix epoch), 0 to 1; the other classes share the rest in proportion. Unset is the calibration's own share (0.25 built in: Tampa's 48 locked of 190 classified IDs). The share of cars whose message time is locked to the GPS fix. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.enabled boolean recommended Off (default) keeps earlier runs; on for the most realistic locked-unit timing (CV-pilot Tampa and Wyoming units). advanced wired Turns the chain on. Unset or false is off. Locked units report the position of the GPS fix itself and stamp the message on the fix or one millisecond early, switching between the two as real units do; when a unit switches to early its position often takes a small lasting step. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.profile string tampa_locked, wyoming_obu, tampa_chainrecommended tampa_chain with data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot-chain-device.yaml for the closest out-of-sample match to Wyoming; tampa_locked is the default. advanced wired The rate set: tampa_locked (default; Tampa's locked IDs, a fit set), wyoming_obu (the one Wyoming OBU, P1-E4's held-out source) or tampa_chain (Tampa's chain devices alone, steps out of state 0 only; use it with data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot-chain-device.yaml). Which real units' switching rates to use: Tampa's locked units (stamped early on about 10 % of messages), the Wyoming unit (46 %), or Tampa's switching units alone (tampa_chain, 26 %, whose positions step only while stamped on the fix; use it with the chain-device timing file). actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.stay_minus1 number [0, 1]recommended Unset (the profile's: 0.235 Tampa, 0.566 Wyoming). advanced wired P(the next BSM is stamped 1 ms early | this one is); unset is the profile's. The chance that a message stamped early is followed by another early one. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.stay_zero number [0, 1]recommended Unset (the profile's: 0.918 Tampa, 0.630 Wyoming). advanced wired P(the next BSM is stamped on the epoch | this one is); unset is the profile's. The chance that a message stamped on the fix is followed by another on the fix. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.steps boolean recommended On (default) with the chain. advanced wired Lasting position steps at 0 -> -1 transitions, at the profile's rate and size. Unset is true. Whether a switch to early stamping can carry a lasting position step of a few centimetres, as the real units' positioning filter does. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.speed_per_m number m/s per m [-5, 5]recommended Unset (no speed change; it barely moves the position check but matters for speed-consistency detectors); 0.499 for Tampa's switching units. advanced wired The reported speed's change with a step, m/s per m of along-track step. Unset is no speed change; set, it turns the change on (Tampa's chain devices: 0.499). How much the reported speed jumps, in m/s per metre, when a unit's position takes a step; the jump then fades. Real units' speed steps with their position. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.speed_tau_s number s (0, 60]recommended Unset (Tampa's 0.357 s). advanced wired The speed change's decay time, s; unset is Tampa's 0.357 (needs speed_per_m). How quickly the speed jump that comes with a step fades. actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.position_follows number [0, 1]recommended Unset (Tampa's 0.759). advanced wired The share of the speed change the reported position moves with, 0 to 1; unset is Tampa's 0.759 (needs speed_per_m). How much of the speed jump the reported position follows: 1 moves the position with the reported speed, 0 leaves it on the old speed.

items.title: vru
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description actors.vru.pedestrians integer people 0 recommended 0 to 400 at once. basic partial How many pedestrians. People walking on the sidewalks and crossings. Those with a phone or wearable can broadcast their own safety messages (PSM). Status: Pedestrians walk sidewalks and cross streets on crosswalk lanes (social-force model), and away from them: with the default 'observed' behaviour they walk at speeds by age group (Knoblauch et al. 1996), step off after a start-up time when walk comes on, cross against flashing or steady don't-walk when they are among the share who do and the gap passes the HCM critical headway (calibrated to Midtown counts, Basch et al. 2015), walk in groups, and cross mid-block (jaywalk, straight or diagonal) where blocks are long, more often beside stopped traffic, with a lane-by-lane gap. Vehicles yield to anyone on a crosswalk, stop for anyone in or about to enter their lane mid-block, a few yield to a pedestrian waiting at the kerb, and never stop inside a crosswalk. Signalised crosswalks get MUTCD walk, flashing don't-walk (3.5 ft/s clearance) and don't-walk intervals. Cyclists ride the lanes that admit bicycles at naturalistic speeds (conventional and e-bike, Schleinitz et al. 2017). Partial because: crossing nodes with no crossing way get no crosswalk, the grid has no separate cycle lanes, and a cyclist rides the lane centre. actors.vru.cyclists integer people 0 recommended 0 to 150 at once. basic partial How many cyclists. People riding bicycles and e-bikes among the traffic. Status: Pedestrians walk sidewalks and cross streets on crosswalk lanes (social-force model), and away from them: with the default 'observed' behaviour they walk at speeds by age group (Knoblauch et al. 1996), step off after a start-up time when walk comes on, cross against flashing or steady don't-walk when they are among the share who do and the gap passes the HCM critical headway (calibrated to Midtown counts, Basch et al. 2015), walk in groups, and cross mid-block (jaywalk, straight or diagonal) where blocks are long, more often beside stopped traffic, with a lane-by-lane gap. Vehicles yield to anyone on a crosswalk, stop for anyone in or about to enter their lane mid-block, a few yield to a pedestrian waiting at the kerb, and never stop inside a crosswalk. Signalised crosswalks get MUTCD walk, flashing don't-walk (3.5 ft/s clearance) and don't-walk intervals. Cyclists ride the lanes that admit bicycles at naturalistic speeds (conventional and e-bike, Schleinitz et al. 2017). Partial because: crossing nodes with no crossing way get no crosswalk, the grid has no separate cycle lanes, and a cyclist rides the lane centre. actors.vru.device_fraction number 0.0 [0, 1]recommended 0 to 0.5; few phones broadcast V2X today. basic wired What fraction of them carry a device that transmits. The share of pedestrians and cyclists carrying a device that sends V2X messages. actors.vru.behaviour string observed observed, document advanced wired How the pedestrians behave: observed (the default — walking speeds by age group, start-up at walk, a share who cross against the signal into a gap, groups, and mid-block crossing) or document (the 1995 social-force defaults: one speed law, everyone waits for walk, nobody crosses mid-block). actors.vru.midblock_rate_per_100m number per 100 m [0, 100] advanced wired Overrides the observed behaviour's mid-block crossing rate, decisions per 100 m of eligible sidewalk walked; 0 turns mid-block crossing off. actors.vru.red_crossing_share number [0, 1] advanced wired Overrides the observed behaviour's share of pedestrians who cross against the signal when the traffic leaves a gap. actors.vru.ebike_share number [0, 1] advanced wired Overrides the share of cyclists on e-bikes. actors.vru.crossing_gap_margin_s number s [0.5, 6] advanced wired Overrides the median time a pedestrian wants a traffic gap to leave beyond the time to walk across (the HCM's start-up and clearance time), seconds. actors.vru.walking_speed_mps number m/s [0.5, 2.5]recommended 1.51 m/s (Knoblauch 1996 crosswalk study); 1.2 to 1.6 m/s. advanced wired Overrides the mean walking speed of pedestrians under 65, m/s. Under observed the 65-and-over mean scales with it (keeping Knoblauch et al. 1996's ratio, 1.25 against 1.51 m/s); under document it is the one Gaussian's mean (1.34 m/s). How fast pedestrians under 65 walk on average; older walkers are slower in proportion. Slower walkers need longer gaps and longer crossing time.

items.title: rsu_placement
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description actors.rsu_placement.count integer roadside units [0, 256]recommended 0 to 20 on a city extract. basic wired How many units, at most: one per signalised intersection, the intersections with the most approach lanes first, no two closer than min_spacing_m. items.title: Deployment
items.text:
Which certificate system runs and how it is laid out: the providers on the trust list, the electors who sign that list, and the parts of the design the US does not deploy. Leave it on "US system (2025)" for the real deployment. Any change the US does not make is marked not US and recorded in the run's manifest.

The credential system the backend runs; it must match the one the vehicles use. Model slot: family protocol, see model parameters.

items.title: Failures & servers
items.text:
Servers that go down, slow down or lie during the run, and each server's hardware, capacity and links.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description actors.backend.entities.*.profile string backend/cloud-vm-x86, backend/hsm-appliance-luna7, bs/lte-macro-genericrecommended The backend's default profile. advanced partial Its hardware profile id. The hardware one backend server runs on, which prices its cryptography. Model slot: family hardware-profile, see model parameters. Status: Keyed by CAMP SCMS role (ra, pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, lop, crl_store, crl_broadcast, eca, dcm). 'profile' sets the hardware the entity's cryptography is costed on and 'service_model' its queue ('service/mmc', the default M/M/c, or 'service/mm1'). 'net' is not read: every entity sits on net.backend_net. actors.backend.entities.*.service_model string service/mmc, service/mm1recommended service/mmc. advanced partial Its service model id. One backend server's queue: its workers in parallel, or one at a time. Model slot: family service-model, see model parameters. Status: Keyed by CAMP SCMS role (ra, pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, lop, crl_store, crl_broadcast, eca, dcm). 'profile' sets the hardware the entity's cryptography is costed on and 'service_model' its queue ('service/mmc', the default M/M/c, or 'service/mm1'). 'net' is not read: every entity sits on net.backend_net. actors.backend.entities.*.net string backend-net/fixedrecommended Leave unset. advanced partial Its network model id. Not read: every backend server sits on the backend network. Model slot: family backend-net, see model parameters. Status: Keyed by CAMP SCMS role (ra, pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, lop, crl_store, crl_broadcast, eca, dcm). 'profile' sets the hardware the entity's cryptography is costed on and 'service_model' its queue ('service/mmc', the default M/M/c, or 'service/mm1'). 'net' is not read: every entity sits on net.backend_net. actors.backend.entities.*.availability.model string always-up, two-staterecommended Unset (the backend-wide setting). advanced wired always-up (the default) or two-state. This role's own outage model, over the backend-wide one: for example the RA alone failing at random. actors.backend.entities.*.availability.mtbf_h number h [1, 87600]recommended Unset (the backend-wide setting, else 720 h). advanced wired Mean time between failures, hours (720 unless set). This role's mean time between failures, in hours, over the backend-wide one. Applies when actors.backend.entities.*.availability.model is two-state, null. actors.backend.entities.*.availability.mttr_min number min [1, 10080]recommended Unset (the backend-wide setting, else 30 min). advanced wired Mean time to repair, minutes (30 unless set). This role's mean time to repair, in minutes, over the backend-wide one. Applies when actors.backend.entities.*.availability.model is two-state, null. actors.backend.entities.*.service_time.model string deterministic, log-normalrecommended Unset (the backend-wide setting). advanced wired deterministic (the default) or log-normal. This role's own service-time model, over the backend-wide one. actors.backend.entities.*.service_time.cv number σ/mean [0, 3]recommended Unset (the backend-wide setting, else 0.25). advanced wired The multiplier's coefficient of variation (0.25 unless set). This role's service-time spread, over the backend-wide one. Applies when actors.backend.entities.*.service_time.model is log-normal, null. actors.backend.links[].from string ra, pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, lop, crl_store, crl_broadcast, eca, dcmrecommended A server role. advanced wired The entity the link starts at. One end of a backend link whose latency or capacity you override. actors.backend.links[].to string ra, pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, lop, crl_store, crl_broadcast, eca, dcmrecommended A server role. advanced wired The entity it ends at. The other end of the link. actors.backend.links[].latency_ms number ms [0, ∞)recommended 10 ms (the engine's default backend link). advanced wired One-way latency, milliseconds. The link's one-way latency. actors.backend.links[].capacity_mbps number Mbit/s (0, ∞)recommended 1,000 Mbit/s (the engine's default backend link). advanced wired Capacity, megabits per second. The link's capacity. actors.backend.failures[].node string ra, pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, lop, crl_store, crl_broadcast, eca, dcm (or another value)recommended Pick the provider, then the server. advanced wired The server: a role (pca, la1, la2, ma, crlg, ra, …) or a committee member, <role>-member-<k> (pca-member-0, linkage-member-2, crl-member-1); the home provider's, unless qualified by its provider, <provider>/<role> (provider-b/crlg). The server that fails: a role of the home provider, another provider's (provider-b/crlg), or a committee member. actors.backend.failures[].mode string offline, slow, maliciousrecommended offline for an outage study. advanced wired offline, slow or malicious. How it fails: down (messages dropped), slow (extra time per message) or lying (invalid committee shares). actors.backend.failures[].from_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Inside the run. advanced wired When it starts, s. When the failure starts, in seconds into the run. actors.backend.failures[].to_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset, or after from_s. advanced wired When it ends, s; absent for the rest of the run. When the server recovers; unset means it stays failed to the end. actors.backend.failures[].extra_ms number ms (0, 600000]recommended 10 to 1,000 ms. advanced wired For slow: the extra service time per message, ms. Under slow, the extra service time each message takes. actors.backend.availability.model string always-up always-up, two-staterecommended Always up; random outages to study how the SCMS rides out failures (a sensitivity sweep, not a measured figure). advanced wired always-up (the default) or two-state. Whether every backend server fails at random: its up times and repair times are drawn at random (exponential), and while down it is offline, so devices retry their requests. actors.backend.availability.mtbf_h number h 720.0 [1, 87600]recommended 720 h (a month; an assumption: no provider publishes its availability). advanced wired Mean time between failures, hours (720 unless set). The mean time a backend server runs between two random failures, in hours. Applies when actors.backend.availability.model is two-state. actors.backend.availability.mttr_min number min 30.0 [1, 10080]recommended 30 min (an assumption). advanced wired Mean time to repair, minutes (30 unless set). The mean time a failed backend server takes to come back, in minutes. Applies when actors.backend.availability.model is two-state. actors.backend.service_time.model string deterministic deterministic, log-normalrecommended Fixed; variable to see how service-time spread moves latency percentiles. advanced wired deterministic (the default) or log-normal. Whether each backend request takes the same time every time (the cost table) or a time that varies at random around it (log-normal, median the fixed time). actors.backend.service_time.cv number σ/mean 0.25 [0, 3]recommended 0.25 (an assumption: no provider publishes it). advanced wired The multiplier's coefficient of variation (0.25 unless set). How widely backend service times spread: the coefficient of variation of the log-normal multiplier (0 is fixed, 1 as wide as an exponential). Applies when actors.backend.service_time.model is log-normal.

for radio benchmarks. mobility/demand/none No vehicles No vehicle demand: pedestrians, roadside units and the backend only. mobility/demand/sumo-rou SUMO route file (.rou.xml) Every vehicle, flow and vehicle type of a SUMO route file, each driven by its own type. mobility/demand/routes Saved routes (v2xw/routes/1) The trips and chosen routes a traffic assignment saved, run again as they are. mobility/demand/trips Trip list A list of trips, each with its own departure, origin and destination. mobility/demand/od-matrix Origin-destination matrix Trips drawn from a zone-to-zone matrix, as SUMO's od2trips draws them. mobility/demand/counts Traffic counts Routes and trips sampled to reproduce observed counts, as SUMO's routeSampler does. mobility/demand/gtfs Transit timetable (GTFS) Buses and trams on their scheduled routes, from a GTFS feed. mobility/demand/purposes Trips by purpose A day of home-based tours and other trips, each departing on its purpose's profile. mobility/demand/composite Several demand models together The trips of several demand models at once, for example commuters plus transit. actors.vehicles.classes.*.obu Value Label Meaning obu/cohda-mk5 Cohda mk5 obu/cohda-mk6c-qualcomm-9150 Cohda mk6c qualcomm 9150 obu/generic-automotive-soc-no-hsm Generic automotive soc no hsm obu/pq-capable-hypothetical Pq capable hypothetical obu/unex-obu-301-craton2 Unex OBU 301 craton2 obu/unex-obu-301-craton2-software Unex OBU 301 craton2 software actors.vehicles.drivers.realism Value Label Meaning calibrated Calibrated city drivers Each driver their own free speed, reaction at a green and following style; with a 0.8 s reaction and misjudged gaps: dense traffic forms stop-and-go waves. actors.vehicles.gnss.quality Value Label Meaning reid-2019 Production receiver, measured (3.07 m at 68 %) Reid et al. that meets J2945/1's open-sky accuracies: 1.5 m horizontal and 3 m vertical at 68 %, speed 0.28 m/s, heading 2-3°, the heading held below 1.10 m/s. rtk RTK (0.26 m) An RTK-corrected receiver, 0.26 m at 68 % (Reid 2019's OxTS RT3000 rows). actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.profile Value Label Meaning tampa_locked Tampa locked wyoming_obu Wyoming obu tampa_chain Tampa chain actors.vru.behaviour Value Label Meaning observed As observed in Midtown Walking speeds by age, crossing against the signal and mid-block as field studies measured. document Textbook (everyone obeys) One walking speed, everyone waits for WALK, nobody crosses mid-block. actors.rsus[].roles[] Value Label Meaning report-forward Relay misbehaviour reports Forwards vehicles' reports to the backend when they have no cellular link. crl Broadcast the revocation list Repeats the certificate revocation list on the air. provisioning-proxy Deliver certificate top-ups Carries pseudonym-certificate downloads for vehicles without cellular. spat Signal timing (SPaT) and priority Broadcasts the junction's signal state and answers emergency-vehicle requests. map Intersection map (MAP) Broadcasts the junction's lane geometry. spat-map Signal timing and map Both of the above. cpm Infrastructure collective perception (CPM) Its own cameras or radars watch the junction and it broadcasts what they see. actors.rsus[].profile Value Label Meaning rsu/cohda-mk5-rsu Cohda mk5 RSU Roadside unit (Cohda MK5 RSU). rsu/commsignia-its-rs4 Commsignia its rs4 Roadside unit (Commsignia ITS-RS4), the most complete public RSU datasheet in the hardware sheet. actors.rsus[].backhaul Value Label Meaning backhaul/fixed Fixed line A wired link with a set latency and capacity. backhaul/fibre Fibre Metro fibre to the backend: 1 Gbit/s and well under a millisecond. backhaul/dsl DSL (copper) A VDSL2 phone line: 20 Mbit/s up, 80 down, about 9 ms each way. backhaul/microwave Microwave A point-to-point radio hop: 400 items.title: apps
items.text:
Group: Applications. The V2X applications vehicles run on what they hear, and how drivers follow their advice.

7 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see how to read these tables. Paths use [] for a list element and * for a map key.

Status Meaning wired

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description apps.enabled[] string fcw, eebl, ima, lta, bsw, pcw, rlvw, glosa advanced wired Enabled[] apps.glosa_compliance number 0.0 [0, 1]recommended 0 (advice shown, not followed: no field rate is published); 0.25 to 1 to study the benefit. advanced wired The fraction of equipped drivers who follow GLOSA's speed advice, 0..=1. The share of drivers who slow down to the speed a green-light advisory tells them, so they arrive on green instead of stopping at red. apps.fcw_ttc_s number s 2.4 (0, 30]recommended 2.4 s (NHTSA's FCW confirmation test); 2.0 to 3.0 s. advanced wired FCW's time-to-collision threshold, seconds. How many seconds before a rear-end collision the forward collision warning sounds: earlier warns sooner but more often for nothing. apps.ima_tti_s number s 4.0 (0, 30]recommended 4 s (this build's choice); 3 to 6 s. advanced wired IMA's look-ahead to the conflict point, seconds. How far ahead, in seconds of driving, the intersection movement assist looks for a crossing vehicle that would reach the same point. apps.lta_gap_s number s 4.1 (0, 30]recommended 4.1 s (HCM 6th ed. Exhibit 20-11 critical gap); 3.5 to 5.5 s. advanced wired LTA's critical gap, seconds. The gap in oncoming traffic the left-turn assist requires before it stays quiet: a smaller gap means fewer warnings. apps.pcw_ttc_s number s 3.0 (0, 30]recommended 3 s (this build's choice); 2 to 4 s. advanced wired PCW's time threshold, seconds. How many seconds before a pedestrian or cyclist would be in the vehicle's path the pedestrian collision warning sounds. apps.rlvw_decel_mps2 number m/s² 3.4 (0, 30]recommended 3.4 m/s² (AASHTO Green Book comfortable deceleration); 2.5 to 4.5 m/s². advanced wired RLVW's comfortable-stop deceleration, m/s². The braking a driver can do comfortably: the red-light violation warning sounds once stopping for the red would need harder braking than this.

items.title: Choices
items.text:
The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

apps.enabled[] Value Label Meaning fcw Forward collision warning Warns when the car ahead is closing at a time to collision of 2.4 s or less. eebl Emergency electronic brake light Warns when a vehicle ahead brakes harder than 0.4 g. ima Intersection movement assist Warns of a crossing vehicle about to reach the same conflict point. lta Left turn assist Warns a left turner when the oncoming gap is too short. bsw Blind spot warning Warns of a vehicle in the blind spot before a lane change. pcw Pedestrian collision warning Warns when a pedestrian or cyclist will be in the path within 3 s. rlvw Red light violation warning Warns when the driver can no longer stop comfortably for a red. glosa Green light speed advisory Advises the speed that arrives on green; drivers follow it at the compliance share.

items.title: Misbehaviour authority
items.text:
How reports of bad messages reach the MA and how the MA decides. Covers what a vehicle stores and uploads, how the RA shuffles reports, the MA's decision rule, and whether a person reviews each case. The US pilots used manual review.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description detection.ma.id string threat/ma/corroborated threat/ma/corroborated, threat/ma/legacy-windowrecommended Corroborated, which needs reports from several vehicles. basic wired The model's registry id. The misbehaviour authority: the backend service that reads reports and decides whom to revoke. detection.ma.params json (serde_json::Value) recommended Use the fields. advanced wired Overrides for its card's defaults. Anything not named here keeps the card's value, which is what makes the parameter set content-addressable. The Misbehaviour Authority's parameters, each shown as its own field above; this block is their JSON spelling. detection.ma.params.event_window_s number s 5.0 (0, 3600]recommended 5 s (F2MD); 1 to 30 s. advanced wired Reports about one vehicle that arrive within this long of the first are one event, however many there are (F2MD DELTA_REPORT_TIME). Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated. detection.ma.params.event_min_reporters integer reporters 2 [1, 1000]recommended 2; 1 trusts a single reporter. advanced wired How many different trusted vehicles must report an event before it counts as evidence. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated. detection.ma.params.min_events integer events 3 [1, 1000]recommended 3; 1 to 10. advanced wired How many corroborated events inside the window it takes to revoke, so one bad moment is not enough. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated. detection.ma.params.window_s number s 60.0 (0, 86400]recommended 60 s; 10 to 600 s. advanced wired The sliding window the events must fall in. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated. detection.ma.params.min_reporters integer reporters 3 [1, 1000]recommended 3; 1 to 10. advanced wired How many different trusted vehicles must have reported across the counted events (the legacy k). Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated. detection.ma.params.defence boolean true recommended On. advanced wired Counts only reporters the authority still trusts, so attackers cannot report honest vehicles off the road. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated, threat/ma/legacy-window. detection.ma.params.reputation_max integer reports 40 [0, 1000000]recommended 40 (the legacy engine's PipelineConfig). advanced wired A reporter that is itself reported this many times in the window is no longer trusted. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated, threat/ma/legacy-window. detection.ma.params.report_budget integer reports 30 [0, 1000000]recommended 30 (the legacy engine's PipelineConfig). advanced wired A reporter filing more than this many reports in the window is rate-limited. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/corroborated, threat/ma/legacy-window. detection.ma.params.report_threshold_k integer reporters [1, 1000]recommended 3 (PipelineConfig.report_threshold_k). advanced wired The legacy authority: how many trusted reporters it takes to revoke. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/legacy-window. detection.ma.params.revoke_min_seconds integer s [1, 3600]recommended 4 (PipelineConfig.revoke_min_seconds). advanced wired The legacy authority: the evidence must fall in at least this many different whole seconds. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/legacy-window. detection.ma.params.revoke_persist_s number s [0, 3600]recommended 3 s (PipelineConfig.revoke_persist_s). advanced wired The legacy authority: how long the evidence must persist before it revokes. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/legacy-window. detection.ma.params.revoke_window_s number s [0, 86400]recommended 15 s (PipelineConfig.revoke_window_s). advanced wired The legacy authority: the sliding window the evidence must be sustained in. Applies when detection.ma.id is threat/ma/legacy-window.

items.title: messages
items.text:
Group: Messages. Which V2X messages are generated and how they are encoded.

15 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see how to read these tables. Paths use [] for a list element and * for a map key.

Status Meaning wired partial

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description messages.sets[] string bsm, cam, denm, spat, map, srm, ssm, psm, vam, cpm advanced partial Sets[] Status: Which message sets are generated, each by the station that sends it in a deployment. bsm and cam: every equipped vehicle; a BSM carries J2945/1 path history and path prediction, and its event flags and lights when set; a CAM its low-frequency container every 500 ms. denm (needs gn-btp), at the C2C-CC triggering conditions: a vehicle whose emergency stop signal comes on (6 m/s2, UN R48) raises an emergency-brake-light DENM updated every 100 ms while it stays on, and a broken-down vehicle with its hazards on, once it has stood 10 s, a stationary-vehicle DENM repeated every second, updated every 15 s and cancelled (the cancellation repeated for 15 s) when the hazards go out. spat and map: roadside units with that role, from the signal plan the drivers obey (min, max and likely end times) and the junction's own lanes, at 10 Hz and 1 Hz. srm and ssm (need codec_tier size-model): emergency vehicles ask the junction whose MAP they heard for priority, its unit answers, and its controller extends or ends greens for it (NTCIP 1211, signal.priority). cpm (needs gn-btp): each vehicle's radar and camera perception, shared at the TS 103 324 rules. psm and vam: VRU devices. messages.codec_tier string uper uper, size-model advanced wired Which codec tier: real uper bytes or the validated size-model. messages.rate_hz number Hz [1, 50]recommended Unset; 10 Hz to match ns-3 and Veins; 1 to 20 Hz to study load. basic wired A fixed awareness-message rate, messages per second: every BSM and every CAM goes out on this period instead of J2945/1's 10 Hz and the ETSI CAM triggers (heading 4°, position 4 m, speed 0.5 m/s, EN 302 637-2 §6.1.3), the way ns-3's BsmApplication and Veins' beaconInterval send. Congestion control may still stretch it. Unset keeps the standards' generation rules. How many awareness messages each vehicle sends per second, at a fixed rate. Unset, vehicles follow the standards: 10 per second in the US, and in Europe as often as their motion changes. messages.spat_interval_ms integer ms [100, 10000]recommended 100 ms (10 Hz, CTI 4501). advanced wired The SPaT broadcast interval of a roadside unit running spat, ms: CTI 4501's 10 Hz (100 ms) unless set. How often a traffic light's roadside unit broadcasts its signal phase and timing. messages.map_interval_ms integer ms [100, 60000]recommended 1,000 ms (1 Hz, CTI 4501). advanced wired The MAP broadcast interval of a roadside unit running map, ms: CTI 4501's 1 Hz (1 000 ms) unless set. How often a roadside unit broadcasts the intersection's lane map. messages.cpm_interval_ms integer ms [100, 1000]recommended 100 ms (ETSI TS 103 324) to 1,000 ms. advanced wired T_GenCpm, ms: how often a vehicle running cpm checks whether a CPM is due (ETSI TS 103 324 §6.1.2.3, 100 ms unless set; at most T_GenCpmMax, 1 000 ms). How often a vehicle checks whether to share what its sensors see; a longer interval means fewer, larger collective perception messages. messages.cpm_dcc_limited boolean recommended Off (today); on for a realistic CPM load in dense traffic (ETSI TS 103 324). advanced wired Whether T_GenCpm follows the congestion control: the DCC's minimum gap between transmissions, clamped to [T_GenCpmMin, T_GenCpmMax] = [100, 1 000] ms (ETSI TS 103 324 V2.1.1 §6.1.2.1, Annex D; Off unless set. Whether vehicles send collective perception messages less often when the channel is congested, following the congestion control as the standard says, instead of at their own rate whatever the load. messages.cpm_quality_threshold integer rating (0-15) [0, 15]recommended Empty (not applied, today); 3 as ETSI TS 103 324 recommends. advanced wired ObjectPerceptionQualityThreshold, 0 to 15: a CPM carries only objects whose §7.1.8.6 quality exceeds it, and states that quality (TS 103 324 §6.1.2.3, Table F.1 recommends 3; Not applied unless set. The lowest perception quality (0 to 15) an object must exceed to be shared in a collective perception message; tracks the sensors have lost for a while fall below it. messages.cpm_max_objects integer objects [1, 255]recommended Empty (255, the format's limit); lower to study a size budget. advanced wired The most perceived objects one CPM carries, 1 to 255: the selection is ordered by the §6.1.3.2 object utility and the lowest-utility objects beyond it wait for the next event. The ASN.1 bound 255, in perception order, unless set. The most objects one collective perception message carries; when more are due, the most informative go first and the rest wait for the next message. messages.denm_traffic_condition boolean recommended Off (today); on for highway studies (C2C-CC triggering conditions). advanced wired Whether a vehicle running denm raises the C2C-CC traffic-condition DENMs (sudden speed drop / dangerous end of queue, local slow down / traffic jam ahead; RS 2007 R1.6.10; Off unless set. Whether vehicles warn the traffic behind them of the end of a queue and of slow or stopped traffic ahead, on non-urban roads, as deployed C-ITS cars do. messages.denm_traction_loss boolean recommended Off (today); on for winter-weather studies (C2C-CC triggering conditions). advanced wired Whether a vehicle running denm raises the C2C-CC traction-loss DENM (adverse weather, RS 2002 R1.6.10 §3.3; Off unless set. Whether a vehicle whose anti-lock brakes find a slippery road (ice, snow) warns the vehicles around it. messages.path_history_points integer points [0, 23]recommended 15 (SAE J2945/1); 0 to 23 (the J2735 limit). advanced wired The most path-history points a BSM's Part II (and a CAM's low-frequency container) carries: J2945/1's 15 unless set, at most J2735's 23; 0 sends none. The points are the Part II's bulk, about 8 to 9 bytes each. How many points of its recent track a vehicle puts in each safety message; more points let receivers follow its path but make every message bigger.

items.title: bsm
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description messages.bsm.path_history_on_change string keep keep, clearrecommended keep (SAE J2945/1, the default for a vehicle sending BSMs; a CAM-only ETSI station clears unless this is set); clear to study what clearing buys for privacy. advanced wired What a pseudonym change does to the vehicle's path history. Unset follows the node's standard: keep on a node that sends BSMs (SAE J2945/1; J5), and clear on a station without the BSM service (an ETSI CAM station, as before J5). A set value holds for every node. Whether a vehicle keeps its recent track in its safety messages when it changes pseudonym, or starts it again so the new pseudonym's messages do not show where the old one drove.

items.title: Choices
items.text:
The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

messages.sets[] Value Label Meaning bsm BSM: Basic Safety Message Every equipped vehicle's position, speed and heading, ten times a second (SAE J2735/J2945/1). cam CAM: Cooperative Awareness Message The European counterpart of the BSM, sent on change of position, speed or heading (ETSI EN 302 637-2). denm DENM: hazard warning An event message raised by a hazard such as hard braking or a breakdown (ETSI EN 302 637-3). spat SPaT: signal phase and timing Roadside units broadcast each signal's state and time to change (needs units with the spat role). map MAP: intersection geometry Roadside units broadcast the lanes and stop lines of their junction (needs the map role). srm SRM: signal request (emergency priority) Emergency vehicles ask the junction for a green; needs SPaT and MAP and the size-model codec. ssm SSM: signal status The junction's answer to a signal request. psm PSM: Personal Safety Message Pedestrians' and cyclists' devices send it (SAE J2735) when actors.vru.device_fraction is above 0; it is not a set to list here. vam VAM: vulnerable road user awareness The European PSM (ETSI TS 103 300-3): VRU devices send it on the ETSI stack when actors.vru.device_fraction is above 0; it is not a set to list here. cpm CPM: collective perception Vehicles share what their sensors detect (ETSI TS 103 324). messages.codec_tier Value Label Meaning uper Uper size-model Size model messages.generator.id Value Label Meaning generator/bsm-j2945-1 BSM timing (SAE J2945/1) Tunes when Basic Safety Messages are sent. generator/cam-en302637-2 CAM triggering (ETSI EN 302 637-2) Tunes the CAM triggering intervals and thresholds. messages.bsm.path_history_on_change Value Label Meaning keep Keep (SAE J2945/1 6.3.6.16) The path history carries on under the new pseudonym: J2945/1 has no clearing rule and asks for 200 m of history (DATAACC-039). clear Clear at each pseudonym change (privacy research) The history starts again at each change, so the new pseudonym's first messages do not show the old one's track; not a J2945/1 rule.

items.title: attacker/jammer/constant
items.text:
A constant wideband jammer: continuous OFDM-like noise in the channel, entering every receiver's noise term for as long as it is on.

version 1.0.0; tiers medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source tx_power_dbm dBm 16.75 paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two. channel - 180 standard: : single-channel operation on the ITS-G5A control channel is the default

Equations.

  • noise rise: N' = N + Σ_j P_j, with P_j the jammer's received power at this receiver in mW The same sum the aggregate-interference term goes through, ordered by node id.

Assumptions.

  • The jammer is on for the whole window it is asked about: it has no protocol and nothing to wait for.
  • Its received power at a victim is computed by the engine with the same link budget a frame gets, so obstacles and shadowing bound its reach the way says they do.

Limitations.

  • The measured anchors are blind areas, not powers: about 250 m in open space and 167 m at a dense urban crossroad, reproduced only with the study's own 17.58 dBm victim transmitter.

Ignores.

  • Subcarrier selectivity: a jammer here is wideband over the 10 MHz channel, so attacker/jammer/constant-pilot is not shipped (see the module docs).
  • The jammer's own antenna pattern and its own duty-cycle-dependent power amplifier behaviour: the declared power is constant while it is on.
  • GNSS jamming and spoofing, which are 's models and not this family's.

Sources.

  • paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two.
  • standard: (PHY jamming and flooding: constant, reactive, random duty cycle, modelled as an interferer in the SINR sums) and

items.title: attacker/jammer/pulsed
items.text:
A duty-cycle jammer: wideband noise for a fraction of a fixed period, with a per-jammer phase drawn from the Attack stream.

version 1.0.0; tiers medium, high; hosting in-process; draws random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source tx_power_dbm dBm 16.75 paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two. period_ns ns 100000000 todo-calibrate: names a 'random duty cycle' jammer but neither it nor prints a period; the default is one T_CBR so that the duty cycle is visible in the CBR a receiver reports (calibration pending) duty - 0.5 [0.0, 1.0] todo-calibrate: no cited duty cycle exists for a V2X jammer; 0.5 is a design choice at the midpoint of the sweep (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • emission windows: on over [phase + k·T, phase + k·T + d·T) for every integer k, phase ~ U{0, …, T−1} ns The phase is drawn once per jammer from (Attack, Node) and cached, so the window list is a pure function of (seed, node, T, d).

Assumptions.

  • The period is a constant, not a random variable: the randomness is in the phase, which is what makes two jammers in one run independent without making one jammer's schedule depend on how often it was polled.

Limitations.

  • Neither the period nor the duty is cited (both todo-calibrate), so a number produced with this model rests on a design choice and the registry reports it.

Ignores.

  • Subcarrier selectivity: a jammer here is wideband over the 10 MHz channel, so attacker/jammer/constant-pilot is not shipped (see the module docs).
  • The jammer's own antenna pattern and its own duty-cycle-dependent power amplifier behaviour: the declared power is constant while it is on.
  • GNSS jamming and spoofing, which are 's models and not this family's.

Sources.

  • paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two.
  • standard: (PHY jamming and flooding: constant, reactive, random duty cycle, modelled as an interferer in the SINR sums) and

items.title: attacker/jammer/reactive
items.text:
A reactive jammer: wideband noise only while energy above a trigger threshold is sensed, which is the profile whose losses are uncorrelated with SINR dips.

version 1.0.0; tiers medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source tx_power_dbm dBm 16.75 paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two. trigger_dbm dBm -75.0 paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two. reaction_delay_ns ns 40000 todo-calibrate: the study prints the trigger threshold but no reaction latency; the default is the standard's own preamble plus SIGNAL field (32 µs + 8 µs), which is a lower bound on when detection can have happened, not a measurement (calibration pending) tail_ns ns 0 paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two.

Equations.

  • emission windows: on over [s.from + δ, s.to + τ) for every sensed interval s with s.energy ≥ trigger; overlapping windows merge δ is the reaction delay and τ the hold-over tail; τ = 0 by default because the study describes emission only while energy is sensed.

Assumptions.

  • The engine supplies what the jammer heard (SensedInterval); this model does not compute the jammer's own link budget, for the same reason the PHY does not compute a hidden terminal's.
  • A sensed interval below the trigger produces no emission at all, so a reactive jammer in a quiet region is silent and costs nothing.

Limitations.

  • The cited anchors are a 170 m open-space blind area and delivery down to 0.6 in dense urban with the transmitter near the jammer; the study also reports low impact with reduced line of sight, which this model reproduces only through the engine's own obstacle stack.

Ignores.

  • Subcarrier selectivity: a jammer here is wideband over the 10 MHz channel, so attacker/jammer/constant-pilot is not shipped (see the module docs).
  • The jammer's own antenna pattern and its own duty-cycle-dependent power amplifier behaviour: the declared power is constant while it is on.
  • GNSS jamming and spoofing, which are 's models and not this family's.

Sources.

  • paper: Puñal, Aguiar and Gross, 'In VANEX There is No Such Thing as Jamming' (2012). The study's own receiver noise floor is −86 dBm; this crate keeps its own −98 dBm kTB-plus-noise-figure floor and does not mix the two.
  • standard: (PHY jamming and flooding: constant, reactive, random duty cycle, modelled as an interferer in the SINR sums) and

items.title: backhaul/dsl
items.text:
A VDSL2 telephone line: asymmetric rate and an interleaving delay of milliseconds.

version 1.0.0; tiers high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source rate_mbps Mbit/s 20.0 [0.1, 100000.0] datasheet: Openreach FTTC 80/20 tier: 20 Mbit/s upstream down_mbps Mbit/s 80.0 [0.1, 100000.0] datasheet: Openreach FTTC 80/20 tier: 80 Mbit/s downstream distance_km km 5.0 [0.0, 5000.0] todo-calibrate: a metro-scale route from the roadside to the backend (calibration pending) hops - 7.0 [0.0, 64.0] todo-calibrate: router hops of a metro access network (calibration pending) loss - 0.0 [0.0, 0.5] todo-calibrate: per-packet loss of the medium (calibration pending) latency_ms ms 8.3245 [0.0, 2000.0] standard: derived: distance × propagation (ITU-T G.652 fibre 4.9 µs/km; c in air) + hops × per-hop delay

Equations.

  • FIFO per direction: arrival = max(offer, line free) + bytes·8 / rate(dir) + distance·us_per_km + hops·per_hop

Assumptions.

  • One FIFO per direction per roadside unit: the messages of every vehicle it relays queue behind each other on the line.
  • latency_ms, when given, replaces the distance and hop delay as the fixed one-way part.

items.title: backhaul/fixed
items.text:
Fixed-latency roadside backhaul (abstract tier), configured as fibre: one-way latency plus an optional serialisation term.

version 0.1.0; tiers abstract; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source latency_ns ns 402000 paper: Coll-Perales 2022 Table VI, transport network with the MEC at the gNB: 0.402 ms mean, 0.422 ms at the 99.99th percentile takes fibre and microwave from these figures (0.4-2.4 ms mean) bandwidth_bps bit/s null todo-calibrate: no published figure gives the capacity of a roadside unit's fibre or Ethernet drop (calibration pending) degraded_multiplier - 10 todo-calibrate: specifies the degraded state as a 'backhaul latency multiplier' and gives no multiplier (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • one-way delay: d = latencymultiplier + bytes8/bandwidth, the serialisation term omitted when no capacity is modelled; the multiplier is 1 except in the degraded state

Assumptions.

  • One latency for the link, in both directions, with no queueing: the abstract tier. The measured transport-network chain (backhaul/measured-tn, the Coll-Perales M/M/1 model) is the medium and high tier and is not this model.

Limitations.

  • No queueing, no loss, no jitter and no availability model, so the 99.99th percentile a study of an undersized link needs is not reachable here — that is exactly what says backhaul/measured-tn is for.

Sources.

  • paper: Coll-Perales et al., 'End-to-end V2X latency modeling and analysis in 5G networks', IEEE TVT 2022, arXiv:2201.06082
  • paper: Narayanan et al., 'A first look at commercial 5G performance on smartphones', WWW'20
