items.title: safety-app/eebl-vsca
items.text:
Emergency electronic brake light, receiving half: estimates a peer's deceleration from its claimed speeds, applies the TS 103 759 plausibility window and the forward-collision geometry, and warns when a relevant peer ahead is braking at or above 0.4 g.

version 0.1.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source decel_threshold_mps2 m/s2 3.92 standard: SAE J2945/1 BSM Part II emergency-brake event flag at 0.4 g = 3.92 m/s² [ and §11, both VERIFIED] estimate_window_ms ms 500 standard: ETSI TS 103 759 V2.2.1: the EEBL plausibility gate requires the preceding vehicle's deceleration to be positive within 500 ms before the claimed detectionTime [] hold_ms ms 500 todo-calibrate: no source gives how long a brake-event warning stands after the last supporting claim (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • deceleration estimate: a = (v(t₁) − v(t₂)) / (t₂ − t₁) over two consecutive claims, with 0 < t₂ − t₁ ≤ estimate_window_ms and both times the sender's own

Assumptions.

  • A receiver at this fidelity has no brake-event flag: BSM Part II is not encoded ( marks its cadence UNVERIFIED) and a CAM's basic vehicle container carries none, so the deceleration is differentiated from claimed speeds.
  • The interval is measured between the two claimed generation times, so a peer with a drifting clock produces a wrong deceleration — which is the real consequence and the one a clock attack should have.

Limitations.

  • A two-point difference of a quantised speed is noisy: a CAM's speed is reported to 0.01 m/s and a 100 ms interval turns one quantum into 0.1 m/s², so the estimate is usable at the 0.4 g threshold and not below it.
  • The host-side half — broadcasting a self-generated brake event — is the generator's, not this application's.

Sources.

  • paper: CAMP VSC-A final report, DOT HS 811 492A (application definition)
  • standard: ETSI TS 103 759 V2.2.1 §4-7

items.title: safety-app/fcw-vsca
items.text:
Forward-collision warning over the neighbour table: warns of an impending rear-end collision with a peer ahead in the same direction, and emits the belief-side time to collision and required deceleration.

version 0.1.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source ttc_warn_s s 1.5 todo-calibrate: marks the FCW time-to-collision threshold UNVERIFIED (calibration pending) ttc_imminent_s s 0.75 todo-calibrate: no source gives the boundary between a warning and an imminent-collision alert (calibration pending) corridor_half_width_m m 0.9 todo-calibrate: marks the VSC-A zone geometry TODO: calibrate (calibration pending) heading_tolerance_rad rad 0.7853981633974483 todo-calibrate: no source gives the heading agreement that makes a peer 'same direction' (calibration pending) range_m m 150.0 todo-calibrate: the evaluation horizon is an implementation choice, not a published one (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • time to collision: ttc = gap / (v_ego − v_peer·cos(Δheading)), evaluated only while closing
  • required deceleration: a_req = closing² / (2·gap) — the rate the ego would need, not the rate the peer was observed to apply
  • same-direction corridor: |(p_peer − p_ego)·l̂| ≤ corridor_half_width_m and |Δheading| ≤ heading_tolerance_rad, with l̂ the ego's lateral unit vector

Assumptions.

  • A peer's lane is unknown to a receiver, so 'same lane' is a corridor in the ego's own heading frame.
  • Closing speed uses the peer's claimed speed projected onto the ego's heading; the peer's own acceleration is not in a CAM's or a BSM's mandatory content at this tier.

Limitations.

  • Gaps are between reported reference points, so vehicle length is not accounted for and every time to collision is correspondingly optimistic — the same limitation v2xw-metrics records for the ground-truth ttc_min.
  • required_decel_mps2 is the deceleration the ego would need, not FHWA-HRT-08-051's DRAC, which is the deceleration the second vehicle was observed to apply. The two are not interchangeable and the field name says which this is.
  • Every numeric trigger is uncalibrated: 's FCW row has no verified number in it.

Sources.

  • paper: CAMP VSC-A final report, DOT HS 811 492A (application definition)
  • paper: FHWA-HRT-08-051, Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (time to collision, 1.5 s conflict threshold)

items.title: safety-app/ima-vsca
items.text:
Intersection movement assist over the neighbour table: extrapolates both paths at constant velocity, warns when the ego and a crossing peer reach the conflict point together, and emits the belief-side post-encroachment time.

version 0.1.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source tti_warn_s s 4.0 todo-calibrate: marks the IMA time-to-intersection threshold UNVERIFIED and notes it is 'not in the accessible report' (calibration pending) pet_warn_s s 1.5 todo-calibrate: no source gives the post-encroachment time at which an intersection application should warn records the PET threshold itself as UNVERIFIED (calibration pending) pet_conflict_s s 5.0 todo-calibrate: records the PET threshold as UNVERIFIED (calibration pending) moving_threshold_mps m/s 0.5 todo-calibrate: no source gives the speed below which a crossing path is undefined (calibration pending) range_m m 150.0 todo-calibrate: the evaluation horizon is an implementation choice (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • conflict point: solve p_ego + t·v_ego = p_peer + s·v_peer by Cramer's rule; a determinant below 1e-9 is treated as parallel
  • post-encroachment time: pet = |t_ego − t_peer|, the interval between one road user leaving the conflict point and the other arriving

Assumptions.

  • Both paths are straight and both speeds constant over the prediction horizon, which is the constant-velocity extrapolation VSC-A's own IMA description assumes for a stop-sign-controlled or uncontrolled intersection.
  • The intersection's geometry is not read: the conflict point is where the two reported paths cross, which needs no map and therefore works on a node that has none.

Limitations.

  • Road users are points: neither vehicle's extent beyond the conflict point is accounted for, so the post-encroachment time is an over-estimate of the safety margin in exactly the way v2xw-metrics records for its cell-based pet.
  • A curving approach is a straight line here, so a vehicle turning into the ego's path is seen late.
  • Every numeric trigger is uncalibrated: 's IMA row has no verified number in it.

Sources.

  • paper: CAMP VSC-A final report, DOT HS 811 492A (application definition)
  • paper: FHWA-HRT-08-051, Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (post-encroachment time)

items.title: verification-policy/on-demand
items.text:
Verify only the messages a safety application marks relevant; deliver the rest to the applications flagged as unverified.

version 0.1.0; tiers medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source relevance_threshold ratio 0.5 [0.0, 1.0] todo-calibrate: the relevance score above which a message is verified (calibration pending)

Limitations.

  • A message delivered unverified is delivered: an application acting on it is acting on an unauthenticated claim, and the unverified_ratio telemetry field is what makes that visible.

Sources.

  • paper: Krishnan & Weimerskirch, 'Verify-on-Demand', SAE Int. J. Passenger Cars - Mech. Syst. 4:536-546, 2011 [, cited via ePrint 2022/133 ref. 7]

items.title: verification-policy/prioritized
items.text:
Order the verification queue by application relevance and by how close the sender claims to be; drop the oldest entry when the queue overflows.

version 0.1.0; tiers medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source horizon_m m 300.0 [1.0, 10000.0] todo-calibrate: distance beyond which proximity adds no priority (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • priority: priority = round(1000 * relevance) + round(1000 * max(0, 1 - d/horizon)), where d is the distance from the node's believed position to the claimed one

Assumptions.

  • Distance is computed from the claimed position, because that is all a receiver has before verification — which means an attacker can raise its own priority by claiming to be close, and that is a real property of the policy rather than a modelling error.

Sources.

  • todo-calibrate: (prioritized policy: 'priority by relevance score and distance; oldest-drop when the queue exceeds queue_depth')

items.title: verification-policy/verify-all
items.text:
Verify every received SPDU in arrival order; drop on queue overflow. Nothing unverified reaches an application.

version 0.1.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Assumptions.

  • An overflowing queue refuses the newcomer rather than shedding the oldest, so the messages that survive are the ones that arrived while there was room.

Sources.

  • standard: IEEE 1609.2-2022 clause 5.2: the default receiver behaviour, against which the two relaxations below are measured

items.title: vru/pedestrian/social-force
items.text:
Pedestrians by the Helbing and Molnár force model: a relaxation towards the desired direction, an elliptical pairwise repulsion that looks one step ahead, a border repulsion from the kerbs of the walkable lane, and vehicles as borders with the SUMO crossing-gap threshold. Pedestrians walk the world's sidewalk and crossing lanes.

version 1.0.0; tiers medium; hosting in-process; draws random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source desired_speed m/s {"mean": 1.34, "std": 0.26} paper: Helbing & Molnár 1995, citing Henderson 1971/1974 max_speed_factor 1 1.3 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 tau s 0.5 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 V0 m²/s² 2.1 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 sigma m 0.3 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 U0 m²/s² 10.0 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 R m 0.2 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 step_width s 2.0 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 field_of_view deg 200.0 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 behind_weight 1 0.5 paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 jmCrossingGap m 10.0 code: SUMO jmCrossingGap default 10 m [, §B13] elliptical - true paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244 jaywalk_probability 1 0.0 code: a switch, off by default: no calibrated rate of crossing against the signal is cited, so none is assumed max_wait_s s 120.0 code: an engineering bound, two 60 s cycles, so a pedestrian at a crosswalk that never shows walk does not wait forever; not a behavioural value kerb_margin m 0.3 code: where a waiting pedestrian stands, back from the end of the pavement lane interaction_radius m 10.0 code: an engineering bound: with σ = 0.3 m the repulsion beyond a few metres is numerically zero speed_law - helbing1995 paper: Knoblauch, Pietrucha & Nitzburg, Field studies of pedestrian walking speed and start-up time, TRR 1538 (1996): means 4.95 / 4.11 ft/s, 15th percentiles 4.09 / 3.19 ft/s for pedestrians under 65 / 65 and over; σ derived assuming normality older_share 1 0.15 code: a choice near New York City's share of residents 65 and over (about one in six); no age count of Midtown's sidewalks was read red_crossing_share 1 0.0 paper: calibrated against Basch, Ethan, Zybert & Basch, Pedestrian behavior at five dangerous and busy Manhattan intersections, J. Community Health 40:789 (2015): of 21,760 pedestrians, about 2,319 crossings (10.6 %) began on don't-walk startup_median_s s 0.0 code: a choice below the HCM's 3.2 s pedestrian platoon start-up time; Knoblauch et al. 1996 measured start-up time but their values could not be read gap_margin_s s 2.0 standard: HCM pedestrian critical headway t_c = L/S_p + t_s (two-way stop-controlled pedestrian mode); t_s, the start-up and end clearance time, is to be measured locally and is not re-verified here crowd_slowing - false paper: Weidmann 1993, Transporttechnik der Fussgänger (ETH IVT Schriftenreihe 90): v = v0·(1 − exp(−1.913·(1/ρ − 1/5.4))) (secondary: the parameters as the pedestrian-flow literature quotes them); local density over a 5 m circle clipped to the walkway, a choice group_shares 1 [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0] paper: Moussaïd, Perozo, Garnier, Helbing & Theraulaz, The walking behaviour of pedestrian social groups and its impact on crowd dynamics, PLoS ONE 5:e10047 (2010): more than half of pedestrians walk in groups on a workday; the per-size split is a choice matching that share midblock - {"corridor_width_m": 1.0, "diagonal_max_deg": 35.0, "driver_yield_probability... code: crate::vru::midblock: the rate, the stopped-traffic factor and the driver yield probability are choices; the gap rule is the HCM critical headway, lane by lane fluctuation m/s² 0.0 todo-calibrate: Helbing & Molnár write "+ fluctuations" and records no magnitude (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • acceleration: dv/dt = (v0·e − v)/τ + Σ f_αβ + Σ f_αB + fluctuations
  • pedestrian repulsion: f_αβ = −∇_r V(b), V(b) = V0·exp(−b/σ), b = ½√((|r| + |r − y|)² − |y|²), y = v_β·Δt·e_β the closed-form gradient ∇_r b = ((|r| + |r−y|)/(4b))·(r̂ + (r−y)ˆ) is the standard reduction and is transcribed, not quoted: records the parameter table and the model's form, not this expression. elliptical = false falls back to the isotropic b = |r|.
  • border repulsion: f_αB = (U0/R)·exp(−d/R) away from the border
  • field of view: w = 1 if e·f ≥ |f|·cos(φ), else c 2φ = 200°, c = 0.5

Assumptions.

  • Pedestrians walk sidewalk and crossing lanes of the world; the lane's own width gives the two borders.
  • The lateral offset is clamped to the walkable half-width at the end of every step. The border potential is soft, so a finite step could otherwise cross a kerb; the clamp makes "pedestrians stay on walkable lanes" an invariant rather than a tendency.
  • A pedestrian about to step onto a crossing waits at the kerb unless its pedestrian signal shows walk (or it has none) and no vehicle is on the crosswalk or too close to yield (UVC §11-502(b), §11-203; the kinematic test of vru::crosswalk). One already on a crossing walks on. The wait is a desired speed that falls to zero over the last 2 m, and the kerb is a hard stop.
  • Crossing against the signal: the legacy switch jaywalk_probability (off by default) draws once per pedestrian per crosswalk; the observed behaviour instead makes red_crossing_share of pedestrians violators, who start on flashing or steady don't-walk only into a gap the HCM critical headway t_c = L/S_p + t_s accepts (L the crosswalk, S_p their own speed). Either still requires no vehicle hazard.
  • Mid-block crossing (crate::vru::midblock): a constant hazard per metre of eligible sidewalk walked, raised beside stopped traffic; straight or diagonal; the pedestrian waits at the kerb for a lane-by-lane (rolling) gap and walks a straight path to the far sidewalk, off every lane.
  • Groups (observed behaviour): a group shares one walk, starts side by side, walks at its slowest member's pace and takes its leader's compliance; a follower crosses mid-block where its leader does.
  • Every pedestrian reads the start-of-step positions of the others and of the vehicles, so the update is the same Jacobi update the vehicles use.

Limitations.

  • No jam state (§2.5 ignores it). A group is held together only by its shared walk and pace, not by an attraction term.
  • A pedestrian crossing mid-block walks a straight line at its desired speed and does not stop or run in the carriageway; the vehicles stop for it.
  • The attraction term of the 1995 model (shop windows, companions) is not implemented: it is optional in the paper and has no cited parameters.

Ignores.

  • Group behaviour, jam states and SUMO's stripe discretisation (medium relative to high).

Sources.

  • paper: Helbing & Molnár, "Social force model for pedestrian dynamics", Phys. Rev. E 51, 4282 (1995); arXiv:cond-mat/9805244

items.title: world/source/opendrive
items.text:
Reads an ASAM OpenDRIVE file by converting it with netconvert --opendrive-files and importing the result, with the converter's own log copied into the provenance.

version 1.0.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source pedestrian_layer - true code: : SUMO net.xml is the interchange format, and the table of what a SUMO import preserves and loses roads_licence - UNSTATED code: : "the format has no separate license". The network's data licence depends on where it came from, so the importer claims none unless the caller states one. default_lane_width_m m 3.2 todo-calibrate: sumo-net default_lane_width_m (calibration pending) default_speed_mps m/s 13.89 todo-calibrate: sumo-net default_speed_mps (calibration pending) signal_head_height_m m 5.0 todo-calibrate: sumo-net signal_head_height_m (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • request bit order: bit(s, link) = s[len(s) − 1 − link] SUMO writes a <request>'s response and foes strings with the highest link index first, so link 0 is the last character. Reading them left to right imports a junction's right of way exactly backwards.
  • internal chain: one connector lane per movement: the via lane's shape, concatenated with every internal lane the chain continues through
  • junction area: convex hull of the file's own shape, the junction's position and every lane end that meets it

Assumptions.

  • A net.xml's coordinates are Cartesian metres in the network's own frame, so the importer translates and never projects.
  • Lane index 0 is the rightmost in the direction of travel, which is SUMO's own convention and this project's (vwp-v1 §4.3).
  • A banned turn is the absence of a <connection>: netconvert has already applied every turn restriction by the time it writes the network.
  • A <request>'s response names the links this one gives way to, and every response is also a foe. A response without a foe is reported.
  • allow beats disallow when a lane states both, and a lane that states neither admits every class, which is SUMO's own default.
  • SUMO is installed: the conversion is netconvert's, not this crate's, and the world is only as good as that converter.

Limitations.

  • Buildings, land use and material classes are not in the format, so a SUMO world has none; the propagation environment class is the caller's default for the whole world rather than defaulted from lane density, which §1.1 records as TODO: calibrate.
  • An internal junction — the waiting position inside a large intersection — has no equivalent in this model, so a movement's chain of internal lanes is concatenated into one connector and the count is reported. A vehicle therefore cannot wait inside the junction.
  • A <tlLogic> that controls links at several junctions becomes one plan per junction with the same cycle and phases. The programme's identity is lost, so a coordinated corridor's junctions are no longer visibly one controller.
  • A per-connection class restriction cannot be expressed: a Connection carries no class mask, so the movement stays permitted unless it admits no class at all, and the loss is counted.
  • Geometry is not cut at a requested boundary — elements are kept or dropped whole — so a bounded import's extent can exceed the request by one edge.
  • <location projParameter> is not evaluated, so the metre frame stays in SUMO's projection while the geodetic anchor comes from origBoundary. The disagreement between that projection and this crate's local tangent plane is UNVERIFIED.
  • A walking area is an area in SUMO and a polyline here, so its geometry is the area's outline traversed as a path.
  • Everything netconvert itself drops is dropped here, including the pedestrian network where OpenDRIVE does not carry it as lanes and a signal's timing where the file only references it. Its log is the record of what was lost.
  • The intermediate network is written to a file named for the input's SHA-256 and deleted afterwards unless the caller keeps it, so the import is reproducible but not hermetic.

Ignores.

  • <roundabout edges>: only its nodes are read, to set the junction control.
  • Lane acceleration, changeLeft, changeRight, endOffset, customShape and the <neigh> element.
  • Actuated, delay-based and NEMA traffic-light programmes are carried into World::signal_programmes with their phases' minDur/maxDur (and NEMA's name, vehext, yellow, red) and <param> A delay-based programme runs as actuated (delay-based-as-actuated`), and SUMO's induction-loop detectors are not imported: the engine's own detectors call the phases.

Sources.

  • code: SUMO Road Networks documentation: the elements <edge>, <lane>, <junction>, <connection>, <tlLogic>, <request>
  • code: : SUMO net.xml is the interchange format, and the table of what a SUMO import preserves and loses
  • code: netconvert import formats: plain XML, OSM, VISUM, Vissim, OpenDRIVE, MATSim, SUMO, Shapefile, RoboCup, DlrNavteq/GDF

The thresholds are read off the Phase 1 Manhattan extract, where they have nothing near them: of 4 373 parts, every one that has a parent is 0.934 or more covered by it and the runner-up is 0.32 or less, and of the nine parts that more than one outline claims the covering fraction is either 1.0000 to four decimals or 0.9553 or less. The tie-breaks are each forced by a real case: the United Nations Secretariat inside the United Nations Headquarters campus for nesting, Rose Hill against the 156 m² building beside it for subdivision building_parts_as_max_height - outline height = max(own height, tallest building:part folded into it) code: OSM Simple 3D Buildings says a building:part subdivides its outline, so the structure's top is its tallest part's top. Collapsing the parts to that one number is this importer's simplification: Building has no sub-volume field and the vwp-v1 building record has no min_height column, so a stepped tower is one prism and the setback above a podium is filled in metres_per_level m 3.0 todo-calibrate: world/source/osm metres_per_level (calibration pending) default_height_m m 10.0 todo-calibrate: world/source/osm default_height_m (calibration pending) highway_class_defaults - SUMO osmNetconvert.typ.xml todo-calibrate: world/source/osm highway_class_defaults (calibration pending) bbox_clip_margin_m m 50.0 todo-calibrate: world/source/osm bbox_clip_margin_m (calibration pending) roof_spire_fraction - 0.5 todo-calibrate: world/source/osm roof_spire_fraction (calibration pending) crossing_width_m m 4.0 todo-calibrate: world/source/osm crossing_width_m (calibration pending) signal_head_height_m m 5.0 todo-calibrate: world/source/osm signal_head_height_m (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • lane offset: d_k = -(W/2 - (k + 0.5) w) from the way centreline, positive to the left of travel, W the carriageway width and k the lane index from the right
  • junction trim: each approach is cut back by r_j = clamp(max incident W/2 (+ 4.2 m stop-line setback at 3+ arms), 1 m, 25 m); then each edge end is pulled back by up to 7 m until every turn has R tan(theta/2) of tangent, R = 6.4 m (AASHTO P)
  • connector: the corner of the two tangent lines rounded into the largest circular arc between the lane ends (AASHTO simple curve), sampled every 6 deg; parallel offset lanes take a reverse curve; motor lane vertices rounded the same way up to R = 50 m
  • amber: per phase group, y = t + v / (2a + 2 G g) with t = 1 s, a = 3 m/s^2, G the approach grade, clamped to [3, 6] s (ITE 2020; MUTCD 2009 4D.26)
  • all-red: per phase group, r = (W + L) / v with W the connector length, L = 6.1 m, at most 6 s (ITE 2020; MUTCD 2009 4D.26)
  • building height: height tag; else building:levels x metres_per_level; else default_height_m; then, where roof:height > roof_spire_fraction x height, cut back to height - roof:height
  • lane width: mean of width:lanes; else width / total lanes; else the lane_width_m option; else the class default

Assumptions.

  • Right-hand traffic: lane 0 is the rightmost in the direction of travel, and a left turn is the movement that crosses opposing traffic.
  • A way's centreline is the centre of its carriageway, so lanes are laid out symmetrically about it.
  • A node shared by two or more ways of the same family is a junction; every other node is shape.
  • Signal plans are invented: the source carries presence only. Every plan is two-phase, pre-timed, uncoordinated (offset 0) and permissive for turns that cross opposing traffic.
  • The ground is flat at z = 0. layer, bridge and tunnel are read and keep two ways from being merged, but do not separate geometry vertically: ways on different levels connect only where they share a node, which they do not.

Limitations.

  • Dual carriageways are imported as two one-way streets, because the sausage-link merge is not implemented; a divided boulevard therefore has two centrelines and a median that is not modelled.
  • A class default speed is jurisdictional, so there is NO default preset: an import is refused until the scenario names one. sumo-german is SUMO's free-flow design speeds and keeps a netconvert comparison reproducible, and is not an urban legal limit; urban-us-nyc is the NYC statutory default. The report and the provenance name the preset, count the lanes that took a default, and warn when those defaults sit far above the limits the source itself states.
  • building:part geometry is not kept, only its HEIGHT. A part inside a building=* outline is folded into the outline so that one structure is one obstacle, and the outline's height becomes the taller of its own and the tallest part inside it (HeightSource::FromParts). The per-part volume is dropped, because the world model has no field for a sub-volume and the vwp-v1 building record has no min_height column to carry one: a stepped tower is therefore ONE prism as tall as its tallest part, so an obstacle model sees the setback above a podium filled in and over-estimates mass at high altitude. A part with no outline over it is kept as a building and counted.
  • A polygon the tags place below ground, or that is a station or public-transport area with no building tag, is not imported at all — not as a zero-height obstacle and not as land use.
  • A driving lane shorter than min_useful_lane_m is kept and counted rather than merged into its neighbour: merging changes the topology a turn restriction and a conflict matrix were built against, and dropping it disconnects whatever is on the other side.
  • A movement whose two lane ends are within a millimetre has no connector lane and therefore no conflict-matrix row, because the matrix is indexed by connector. It is still subject to turn restrictions, and it is counted as zero-length-connector.
  • Footways parallel to a road are imported where they are mapped, and are not snapped to the road; a city that maps sidewalks both ways will have both.
  • Dog-leg junctions are imported as two junctions a few metres apart.
  • A via-way turn restriction is counted and not applied: it spans more than one junction and has no single movement to ban.
  • Two opposing left turns are recorded as conflicting with no precedence, because neither the turn ranking nor priority-to-the-right settles them.

Ignores.

  • Terrain: no DEM is read, and every z is 0.
  • Traffic signal timing, phase counts and coordination, which the source does not carry.
  • Bus lanes, parking lanes, turn pockets and lane widths per lane: every lane of a way gets the same width and access.
  • Public transport routes, barriers, kerbs and traffic calming.

Sources.

  • code: osm2streets README (lane inference and the simplification list),
  • code: SUMO netconvert option defaults (--junctions.join 10 m, --tls.guess-signals 25 m, --tls.cycle.time 90 s, --tls.green.time 31 s, --tls.allred.time 0 s, --tls.yellow.min-decel 3 m/s^2), and §2.3
  • dataset: OSM Simple 3D Buildings (height, building:levels, min_height, building:min_level),
  • standard: FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2008 Ch. 5 (amber 3-6 s, all-red guidance),
  • standard: AASHTO Green Book (9-12 ft lanes; 12 ft on freeways and major arterials) and NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (10-11 ft urban street lanes)
  • standard: New York City citywide 25 mph default speed limit (NYC Local Law 139 of 2014, under NY Vehicle & Traffic Law §1643) and the NY State statutory maximum of 55 mph (NY VTL §1180(b))
  • code: SUMO default vType passenger length 5.0 m: a lane shorter than one vehicle cannot hold one, which is the threshold short-driving-lane is counted against

items.title: world/source/procedural-grid
items.text:
A rectangular lattice of two-way streets with signalised or priority junctions, generated deterministically from its parameters: the reference world for tests, calibration runs and the TR 36.885 urban grid scenario.

version 1.0.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source cols - 6 code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy rows - 6 code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy block_x_m m 120.0 code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy block_y_m m 120.0 code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy lanes_per_direction - 1 code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy lane_width_m m 3.5 code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy sidewalk_m m 0.0 standard: 3GPP TR 36.885 Table A.1.2-1, preset tr36885-urban signalised - false code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy crossings - false code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy block_buildings - false code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy rsu_at_junctions - false code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy speed_limit_mps m/s 13.89 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid speed_limit_mps (calibration pending) cycle_s s 60.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid cycle_s (calibration pending) amber_s s 3.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid amber_s (calibration pending) ew_green_share - 0.5 standard: Webster (1958), Road Research Technical Paper 39, and HCM 6th ed. ch. 19: effective green is split in proportion to the critical flow ratios; equal demand on both streets gives 0.5. The accepted range 0.1-0.9 leaves each street at least 5.4 s of green at the 60 s default cycle signal_head_height_m m 5.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid signal_head_height_m (calibration pending) crossing_width_m m 4.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid crossing_width_m (calibration pending) building_height_m m 20.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid building_height_m (calibration pending) rsu_antenna_height_m m 6.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid rsu_antenna_height_m (calibration pending) corner_radius_m m 0.0 standard: AASHTO Green Book 2018 Ch. 9: passenger-car edge radius for a 90° urban turn, 15 ft (4.5 m) — secondary; 0 in the presets, which reproduce reference layouts pedestrian_lanes - true standard: MUTCD 2009 §4E.06 (walk ≥ 7 s, clearance at 3.5 ft/s, ≥ 3 s buffer) for the pedestrian intervals; §3B.18 crosswalk placement at the corner. The walk network itself is the generator's geometry, not a sourced value bicycles_on_roads - false standard: UVC §11-1202: a person riding a bicycle upon a roadway has the rights and duties of a driver; off in the presets, which reproduce motor-only reference layouts rsu_antenna_gain_dbi dBi 5.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-grid rsu_antenna_gain_dbi (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • lane offset: d_k = (n − 0.5 − k) · w, to the right of travel
  • turn geometry: B(t) = (1−t)² P₀ + 2(1−t)t C + t² P₁, C at the intersection of the two tangent lines, sampled at 7 points
  • junction position: (x_i, y_j) = (half + i · block_x, half + j · block_y), half = n · w

Assumptions.

  • Right-hand traffic: lane 0 is the rightmost in the direction of travel, an east-bound lane lies south of its street's centreline.
  • Every street is two-way with the same number of lanes each way, every junction is a right-angled crossroads, and the ground is flat at z = 0.
  • Turning movements are right from the rightmost lane, straight from every lane, left from the leftmost. No U-turns are generated.
  • Signalisation, when on, is a two-phase fixed-time plan with permissive left turns and no coordination between junctions (offset 0 everywhere).
  • A procedural world has no real location: its origin is (0, 0) and its projection is nominal.

Limitations.

  • A perfect lattice is not a city: no dead ends, no one-way streets, no varying block sizes, no dual carriageways, no gradient. Use world/source/osm for a real network.
  • Two opposing left turns are marked as conflicting with no precedence, because neither the turn ranking nor priority-to-the-right settles them.
  • Buildings, when generated, are one box per block at a single invented height, which is a propagation obstacle of the right shape and the wrong size.

Ignores.

  • Sidewalks are a setback for the buildings, not lanes: no pedestrian network is generated.
  • Terrain: the generator produces no DEM, and every z is 0.

Sources.

  • code: legacy engine run.py L412-424, preset legacy
  • standard: 3GPP TR 36.885 Table A.1.2-1, preset tr36885-urban

items.title: world/source/procedural-radial
items.text:
The classic radial city: spokes from a central plaza crossed by concentric ring roads, generated deterministically from its parameters.

version 1.0.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source arms - 6 code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m rings - 6 code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m ring_spacing_m m 120.0 code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m lanes_per_direction - 1 code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m lane_width_m m 3.5 code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m dropout - 0.0 code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m signalised - false code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m netgenerate_spider.arms - 8 code: legacy/reference/sumo/mapgen.py L234-241: netgenerate --spider --spider.arm-number --spider.circle-number --spider.space-radius 100 --no-turnarounds --default.lanenumber 2, keys such as spider_8a4c netgenerate_spider.ring_spacing_m m 100.0 code: legacy/reference/sumo/mapgen.py L234-241: netgenerate --spider --spider.arm-number --spider.circle-number --spider.space-radius 100 --no-turnarounds --default.lanenumber 2, keys such as spider_8a4c speed_limit_mps m/s 13.89 todo-calibrate: procedural-radial speed_limit_mps (calibration pending) cycle_s s 60.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-radial cycle_s (calibration pending) amber_s s 3.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-radial amber_s (calibration pending) signal_head_height_m m 5.0 todo-calibrate: procedural-radial signal_head_height_m (calibration pending) junction_radius_factor - 1.5 todo-calibrate: procedural-radial junction_radius_factor (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • ring node position: (x, y) = (span + r·s·cos(2πa/arms), span + r·s·sin(2πa/arms)), span = rings·s
  • ring chord length: L = 2·r·s·sin(π/arms) — the polygon side, not the arc
  • dropout selection: ring edge i is removed when floor((i+1)·dropout) > floor(i·dropout)

Assumptions.

  • Right-hand traffic: lane 0 is the rightmost in the direction of travel.
  • Every street is two-way with the same number of lanes each way, and the ground is flat at z = 0.
  • Ring roads are chords through the ring nodes, so ring r is a regular arms-gon rather than a circle.
  • Turning movements are right from the kerb lane, straight on from every lane, left from the median lane; no turnarounds are generated, which is netgenerate's --no-turnarounds.
  • The dropout selection is deterministic decimation. The legacy engine drew the removed edges at random; this generator does not, so that a radial world needs no seed and is a pure function of its parameters.

Limitations.

  • The centre is a single junction with arms approaches. At eight arms and two lanes each way its connectors are geometrically crowded: a real radial city has a roundabout or a plaza there, and this generator has neither.
  • A chord ring with few arms is visibly a polygon, and its junction angles are the polygon's, not a circle's.
  • No buildings, no crossings, no sidewalks and no RSU sites: the grid generator offers those, this one does not.

Ignores.

  • Terrain: every z is 0 until a DEM is attached (see crate::dem).

Sources.

  • code: legacy engine roads.py L683-702 spider_graph(arms, rings, block), with arms/rings/block from grid_w/grid_h/grid_block_m
  • code: legacy/reference/sumo/mapgen.py L234-241: netgenerate --spider --spider.arm-number --spider.circle-number --spider.space-radius 100 --no-turnarounds --default.lanenumber 2, keys such as spider_8a4c

items.title: world/source/procedural-random
items.text:
An irregular road network grown from one junction by random attachment: oblique approaches, three-arm junctions, cul-de-sacs and uneven blocks, reproducible from its seed.

Equations.

  • candidate position: p = p_base + d·(cos θ, sin θ), θ ~ U[0, 2π), d ~ U[min_distance, max_distance]
  • loop closing: a candidate within min_distance of an existing junction becomes an edge to the nearest such junction instead of a new one
  • angle rule: |normalise(θ_new − θ_existing)| >= min_angle at both ends

Assumptions.

  • Right-hand traffic: lane 0 is the rightmost in the direction of travel.
  • Every street is two-way with the same number of lanes each way, straight between its two junctions, and the ground is flat at z = 0.
  • A junction is wherever two streets meet; the growth never creates a crossing without a junction, because a crossing candidate is rejected outright.
  • Turning movements are right from the kerb lane, straight on from every lane, left from the median lane; no turnarounds are generated, which is netgenerate's --no-turnarounds.

Limitations.

  • This is netgenerate --rand's idea, not its algorithm: SUMO's own growth rule, its option defaults and therefore its networks are not reproduced, and a world from this generator is not comparable with one from netgenerate.
  • The growth is unbounded unless max_radius_m is set, so the extent of a 150-iteration network is a draw rather than a parameter.
  • Loop closing is the only source of cycles, so a low min_distance_m gives a network that is nearly a tree and routes badly. The connectivity is reported, not controlled.
  • No buildings, no crossings, no sidewalks and no RSU sites.

Ignores.

  • Terrain: every z is 0 until a DEM is attached (see crate::dem).

Sources.

  • code: legacy/reference/sumo/mapgen.py L242-249: netgenerate --rand --rand.iterations N --rand.min-distance 80 --rand.max-distance 250 --no-turnarounds --default.lanenumber 2, keys such as rand_150

items.title: world/source/sumo-net
items.text:
Reads a SUMO net.xml into the same lane-level world the OSM importer produces: edges, lanes, junctions, connections, internal connectors, right-of-way matrices, traffic-light programmes and crossings, with a counted anomaly wherever the two formats disagree.

version 1.0.0; tiers abstract, medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source pedestrian_layer - true code: : SUMO net.xml is the interchange format, and the table of what a SUMO import preserves and loses roads_licence - UNSTATED code: : "the format has no separate license". The network's data licence depends on where it came from, so the importer claims none unless the caller states one. default_lane_width_m m 3.2 todo-calibrate: sumo-net default_lane_width_m (calibration pending) default_speed_mps m/s 13.89 todo-calibrate: sumo-net default_speed_mps (calibration pending) signal_head_height_m m 5.0 todo-calibrate: sumo-net signal_head_height_m (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • request bit order: bit(s, link) = s[len(s) − 1 − link] SUMO writes a <request>'s response and foes strings with the highest link index first, so link 0 is the last character. Reading them left to right imports a junction's right of way exactly backwards.
  • internal chain: one connector lane per movement: the via lane's shape, concatenated with every internal lane the chain continues through
  • junction area: convex hull of the file's own shape, the junction's position and every lane end that meets it

Assumptions.

  • A net.xml's coordinates are Cartesian metres in the network's own frame, so the importer translates and never projects.
  • Lane index 0 is the rightmost in the direction of travel, which is SUMO's own convention and this project's (vwp-v1 §4.3).
  • A banned turn is the absence of a <connection>: netconvert has already applied every turn restriction by the time it writes the network.
  • A <request>'s response names the links this one gives way to, and every response is also a foe. A response without a foe is reported.
  • allow beats disallow when a lane states both, and a lane that states neither admits every class, which is SUMO's own default.

Limitations.

  • Buildings, land use and material classes are not in the format, so a SUMO world has none; the propagation environment class is the caller's default for the whole world rather than defaulted from lane density, which §1.1 records as TODO: calibrate.
  • An internal junction — the waiting position inside a large intersection — has no equivalent in this model, so a movement's chain of internal lanes is concatenated into one connector and the count is reported. A vehicle therefore cannot wait inside the junction.
  • A <tlLogic> that controls links at several junctions becomes one plan per junction with the same cycle and phases. The programme's identity is lost, so a coordinated corridor's junctions are no longer visibly one controller.
  • A per-connection class restriction cannot be expressed: a Connection carries no class mask, so the movement stays permitted unless it admits no class at all, and the loss is counted.
  • Geometry is not cut at a requested boundary — elements are kept or dropped whole — so a bounded import's extent can exceed the request by one edge.
  • <location projParameter> is not evaluated, so the metre frame stays in SUMO's projection while the geodetic anchor comes from origBoundary. The disagreement between that projection and this crate's local tangent plane is UNVERIFIED.
  • A walking area is an area in SUMO and a polyline here, so its geometry is the area's outline traversed as a path.

Ignores.

  • <roundabout edges>: only its nodes are read, to set the junction control.
  • Lane acceleration, changeLeft, changeRight, endOffset, customShape and the <neigh> element.
  • Actuated, delay-based and NEMA traffic-light programmes are carried into World::signal_programmes with their phases' minDur/maxDur (and NEMA's name, vehext, yellow, red) and <param> A delay-based programme runs as actuated (delay-based-as-actuated`), and SUMO's induction-loop detectors are not imported: the engine's own detectors call the phases.

Sources.

  • code: SUMO Road Networks documentation: the elements <edge>, <lane>, <junction>, <connection>, <tlLogic>, <request>
  • code: : SUMO net.xml is the interchange format, and the table of what a SUMO import preserves and loses

items.title: world/terrain/copernicus-glo-30
items.text:
Reads a raster digital elevation model and resamples it bilinearly onto the world's own metre grid, so that the world's ground height comes from measured terrain instead of the z = 0 plane.

version 1.0.0; tiers medium, high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source cell_m m 30.0 code: (both DEMs are 30 m posts, so 30 m is the resolution the data carries) interpolation - bilinear code: ("resampled onto the world grid with bilinear interpolation") margin_m m 30.0 todo-calibrate: world/terrain/copernicus-glo-30 margin_m (calibration pending) void_search_cells - 8 todo-calibrate: world/terrain/copernicus-glo-30 void_search_cells (calibration pending) void_default_m m 0.0 todo-calibrate: world/terrain/copernicus-glo-30 void_default_m (calibration pending) min_plausible_elevation_m m -500.0 todo-calibrate: world/terrain/copernicus-glo-30 min_plausible_elevation_m (calibration pending) max_plausible_elevation_m m 9000.0 todo-calibrate: world/terrain/copernicus-glo-30 max_plausible_elevation_m (calibration pending)

Equations.

  • bilinear resampling: h(x, y) = Σ_k h_k · w_k over the four surrounding source samples, w = (1−tx)(1−ty), tx(1−ty), (1−tx)ty, tx·ty
  • void repair: h = Σ_present h_k·w_k / Σ_present w_k, falling back to the nearest non-void sample within void_search_cells
  • srtm tile georeferencing: sample (ix, iy) at (lon0 + ix/(n−1), lat0 + iy/(n−1)) degrees, (lat0, lon0) from the file name, n from the byte count

Assumptions.

  • The raster holds Copernicus COP-DEM-GLO-30 exported as an ASCII grid.
  • Heights are metres above the DEM's own datum, and that datum is taken to be the world's z = 0. Neither DEM's geoid is converted to an ellipsoidal height, and the offset between them (tens of metres in places) is not modelled.
  • A void is missing data, not sea level: it is interpolated or filled from a neighbour, never read as 0 m, unless the search finds nothing at all.

Limitations.

  • The GeoTIFF and DT2 distributions are not parsed; a GeoTIFF DEM must be converted to an ASCII grid first (gdal_translate -of AAIGrid).
  • The vertical datum is not converted, so an absolute height is only as good as the source's datum matching the world's.
  • A geodetic raster is sampled through the world's local tangent plane, so the resampling error grows with distance from the world origin exactly as the projection's does.

Ignores.

  • Slope-aware or bicubic resampling: specifies bilinear and the grid records that it was used.
  • Buildings and vegetation: both DEMs are surface-ish models whose treatment of canopy and roofs is not separated here.

Sources.

  • dataset: Copernicus DEM COP-DEM-GLO-30-F. Free of charge with reproduction, distribution, adaptation and modification rights, worldwide and unlimited in time. Resampling is a modification, so the attribution recorded is the modified-data wording: produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved. A redistributor must also add: The organisations in charge of the Copernicus programme by law or by delegation do not incur any liability for any use of the Copernicus WorldDEM-30. WorldDEM-10 is excluded. The distribution is a GeoTIFF this crate does not parse; the supported path is an ASCII-grid export.

items.title: world/terrain/los-profile
items.text:
The terrain elevation profile along a link, and the knife edges it puts in the way: the world-side query that the P.526 terrain diffraction model consumes.

version 1.0.0; tiers high; hosting in-process; draws no random numbers.

Parameter Unit Default Range Source sample_spacing_m m 30.0 dataset: SRTMGL1 (1 arc-second) and Copernicus COP-DEM-GLO-30 post spacing. Sampling at the source's own post spacing is the only interval that neither invents detail nor discards it. max_samples - 1024 todo-calibrate: los-profile max_samples (calibration pending) obstruction_threshold_m m 0.0 code: local-maximum test of the profile, as ITU-R P.526-14 Eq. 26/31/33 requires it min_profile_samples - 3 code: local-maximum test of the profile, as ITU-R P.526-14 Eq. 26/31/33 requires it

Equations.

  • line height: line(f) = a_z + (b_z − a_z)·f, f = s/total in the horizontal plane
  • clearance: h(s) = ground(s) − line(s); h > 0 obstructs
  • knife edge: an interior sample i with h_i > threshold, h_i > h_{i−1} and h_i >= h_{i+1}, contributing (d1, d2, h) = (s_i, total − s_i, h_i) These are the arguments of ν = h·sqrt(2(d1 + d2)/(λ·d1·d2)); the square root and J(ν) belong to the propagation model.

Assumptions.

  • The line between the two antennas is straight: no atmospheric refraction and no earth curvature. Over the 1 km at which a 5.9 GHz V2X link is already below sensitivity, the earth's bulge is about 2 cm, which is under the height quantum.
  • The ground between two samples is the linear interpolation the terrain grid gives, so a feature narrower than the sampling interval is invisible — as it is in the source data, whose posts are the same width apart.
  • Endpoint z values are absolute world heights, antenna height included. It is the caller's job to add the antenna height to the ground, which is what Site::antenna_position does.

Limitations.

  • Buildings, vehicles and foliage are not in the profile: the other obstacle models own those, and adding them here would double-count them.
  • The obstructed length is a trapezoidal estimate at the profile's resolution, not an exact intersection of the line with the surface.

Ignores.

  • Diffraction itself: this query returns geometry, and obstacle/terrain/knife-edge-p526 turns it into decibels.

Sources.

  • dataset: SRTMGL1 (1 arc-second) and Copernicus COP-DEM-GLO-30 post spacing. Sampling at the source's own post spacing is the only interval that neither invents detail nor discards it.

items.title: net
items.text:
Group: Network. The network layer between the application and the radio.

28 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see how to read these tables. Paths use [] for a list element and * for a map key.

Status Meaning wired partial

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description net.layer string wsmp wsmp, gn-btp advanced wired Which network layer: wsmp or gn-btp. net.channel_access string continuous, alternating advanced wired IEEE 1609.4 channel access on wsmp: continuous (one channel all the time, the deployed SAE J2945/1 profile; the default) or alternating (50 ms on the control channel, 50 ms on a service channel, a 4 ms guard at each switch: a safety message waits for the next control-channel interval). net.access_categories string single, etsi-profiles advanced wired Which EDCA queue each message waits in: single (every frame on AC_VO, the deployed SAE J2945/1 profile; the default) or etsi-profiles (the ETSI DCC profiles of TS 102 724: hazard DENMs on AC_VO, CAMs on AC_BE, forwarded GeoNetworking copies and everything else on AC_BK, so a busy channel serves warnings first). net.dcc_cbr string local, global advanced wired Which channel busy ratio the congestion control acts on (gn-btp only): local (the station's own measurement; the default) or global (the highest of its own, its neighbours' and their neighbours', carried in every GeoNetworking single-hop header, ETSI TS 102 636-4-2), so a station also backs off for congestion it cannot hear itself.

items.title: geonet
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description net.geonet.forwarding string on-air, overlay advanced wired How forwarded copies travel: on-air (each forward is a real frame that queues in the forwarder's MAC, contends, collides, counts in the channel busy ratio and passes the DCC gate; the default) or overlay (a protocol-only run over a disk of range_m at the hazard's instant, with no MAC: optimistic, but instant to compute). net.geonet.area_forwarding string cbf, simple advanced wired How a warning spreads inside its area: cbf (contention-based: the farthest receiver rebroadcasts first, the rest stand down) or simple (every receiver rebroadcasts once). net.geonet.non_area_forwarding string greedy, cbf advanced wired How a packet travels towards an area it is not yet in: greedy (to the neighbour nearest the area) or cbf. net.geonet.cbf_variant string etsi, dpd, gpc advanced wired What a contending vehicle does on hearing a copy: etsi (stand down, and take a later copy as new: many transmissions), dpd (stand down, never forward twice) or gpc (stand down only if the copy came from farther along). net.geonet.hop_limit integer [1, 255] advanced wired The most hops a warning may take; 10 by default (itsGnDefaultHopLimit). net.geonet.area_radius_m number m (0, 1784] advanced wired The warning area's radius around the hazard, metres; 1 000 m by default. net.geonet.range_m number m (0, 3000] advanced wired The single-hop range of the overlay forwarding, metres; 500 m by default. On the air the run's own link budget decides who hears a copy. net.geonet.repetition_interval_ms integer ms [0, 60000] advanced wired How often the originator repeats the warning, ms; 0 sends it once. net.geonet.repetition_duration_ms integer ms [0, 600000] advanced wired How long it keeps repeating, ms. Unset, the overlay repeats for 5 000 ms and the on-air DEN service for 15 000 ms (the C2C-CC stationary-vehicle profile); any value given, 5 000 included, is used as given. net.geonet.keep_alive_forwarding boolean advanced wired Keep-alive forwarding: vehicles in the area re-send a warning they stop hearing, so it reaches vehicles that arrive later. net.geonet.window_s number s (0, 600] advanced wired How long each warning is followed, seconds. net.geonet.cbf_min_time_ms integer ms [0, 1000]recommended 1 ms (EN 302 636-4-1 Annex H). advanced wired itsGnGeoBroadcastCbfMinTime, ms: the CBF timer of the farthest contender (EN 302 636-4-1 Annex H, 1 ms unless set). How long the farthest receiver waits before re-broadcasting a geo-broadcast warning. net.geonet.cbf_max_time_ms integer ms (0, 1000]recommended 100 ms (Annex H); 20 to 100 ms in studies. advanced wired itsGnGeoBroadcastCbfMaxTime, ms: the CBF timer of the nearest contender (Annex H, 100 ms unless set). How long the nearest receiver waits before re-broadcasting; the gap between the two timers decides how cleanly the farthest vehicle wins. net.geonet.max_comm_range_m number m (0, 5000]recommended 1,000 m (Annex H); about the real radio range in dense traffic, 300 to 500 m. advanced wired itsGnDefaultMaxCommunicationRange (DIST_MAX), m: the progress at which the CBF timer reaches its minimum (Annex H, 1 000 m unless set). The progress at which the contention timer reaches its minimum: the forwarding range the protocol assumes.

items.title: rsu_ip
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description net.rsu_ip.air string constant, schrecommended constant (default) until the service-channel path is built; sch to study WSA-gated access. advanced partial sch (IEEE 1609.3, the default: each relaying unit sends a signed WSA advertising the SCMS service with a WAVE Routing Advertisement, and a vehicle uses a unit only after it has verified that unit's WSA) or constant (the air hop is a fixed latency and rate, and a vehicle uses any relaying unit within range). How a vehicle without a modem reaches the SCMS through a roadside unit: a fixed link, or only after hearing the unit's signed service advertisement (WSA). Air 'constant' (default): a vehicle with no modem uses any relaying unit within 300 m and the hop is a fixed latency and rate. air 'sch' (P19.2): each unit with the provisioning-proxy or report-forward role signs and sends an IEEE 1609.3 WSA every wsa_interval_ms (PSID 0x23, IPv6 Routing, the WAVE Routing Advertisement; v2xw_msg::wsa), and a vehicle binds to a unit only while it holds a verified WSA from it no older than 1 s. A relayed misbehaviour report goes on the radio.channels service channel when the run has one (rule gap M11; a one-radio unit then needs alternating access). Downloads (top-up, re-enrolment, trust fetch) ride TCP/TLS on a service-channel session (transport/80211p-sch: the vehicle's contact window, EDCA AC_BE on the unit's measured CBR, 1609.4 intervals, link-budget loss) and the unit's line; a transfer that fails cuts its flow off, and the vehicle starts it again while a verified unit is in range (relayed_flows_cut_off). Under constant the air hop is the fixed link: the service-channel path (contact window, PER, SCH load) is P19.3-P19.4.* net.rsu_ip.wsa_interval_ms integer ms [20, 5000]recommended 100 ms (USDOT RSU Specification v4.1). advanced partial The WSA period under sch, ms: 100 (USDOT RSU Specification v4.1 App. D, RepeatRate 50 per 5 s). How often a relaying roadside unit sends its WSA under 'sch'. Applies when net.rsu_ip.air is sch. Air 'constant' (default): a vehicle with no modem uses any relaying unit within 300 m and the hop is a fixed latency and rate. air 'sch' (P19.2): each unit with the provisioning-proxy or report-forward role signs and sends an IEEE 1609.3 WSA every wsa_interval_ms (PSID 0x23, IPv6 Routing, the WAVE Routing Advertisement; v2xw_msg::wsa), and a vehicle binds to a unit only while it holds a verified WSA from it no older than 1 s. A relayed misbehaviour report goes on the radio.channels service channel when the run has one (rule gap M11; a one-radio unit then needs alternating access). Downloads (top-up, re-enrolment, trust fetch) ride TCP/TLS on a service-channel session (transport/80211p-sch: the vehicle's contact window, EDCA AC_BE on the unit's measured CBR, 1609.4 intervals, link-budget loss) and the unit's line; a transfer that fails cuts its flow off, and the vehicle starts it again while a verified unit is in range (relayed_flows_cut_off). Under constant the air hop is the fixed link: the service-channel path (contact window, PER, SCH load) is P19.3-P19.4.*

items.title: Choices
items.text:
The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

net.layer Value Label Meaning wsmp WSMP (IEEE 1609.3, US) The US short message protocol: a 5-octet header on a BSM. gn-btp GeoNetworking + BTP (ETSI, Europe) The European network and transport layers: 44 octets of headers on a CAM. net.channel_access Value Label Meaning continuous Continuous (one channel) The deployed US profile: safety messages go out on one channel as soon as they are made. alternating Alternating (IEEE 1609.4) One radio switches channel every 50 ms; a message made on the wrong half waits up to 54 ms, and one that would run into the 4 ms switch guard waits too. net.access_categories Value Label Meaning single One queue (AC_VO) Every message waits in the same top-priority queue, as deployed US radios do. etsi-profiles ETSI DCC profiles Hazard warnings jump the queue; CAMs and forwarded copies wait longer when the channel is busy. net.dcc_cbr Value Label Meaning local Own measurement Each radio throttles for the channel load it hears itself. global Two-hop maximum (ETSI GeoNetworking) Radios share their load in every header and throttle for congestion up to two hops away. net.fragmenter.id Value Label Meaning fragmenter/cert-cycle-partial-hybrid Post-quantum certificate spread over a cycle The hybrid certificate rides in the first messages of each five-message cycle. fragmenter/facilities-segmentation Independent segments (ETSI) Each segment is a message of its own (GeoNetworking only). fragmenter/generic-sdu Split into pieces A large message is sent in pieces and reassembled; it arrives only if every piece does. fragmenter/none No fragmentation A signed message larger than the network's limit is refused. net.backhaul.id Value Label Meaning backhaul/fixed Fixed line A wired link with a set latency and capacity. backhaul/fibre Fibre Metro fibre to the backend: 1 Gbit/s and well under a millisecond. backhaul/dsl DSL (copper) A VDSL2 phone line: 20 Mbit/s up, 80 down, about 9 ms each way. backhaul/microwave Microwave A point-to-point radio hop: 400 Mbit/s, about 0.2 ms, rare outages. backhaul/cellular Cellular The unit reaches the backend over the mobile network. backhaul/none None (offline) The unit has no backend link. net.uu.id Value Label Meaning cellular/uu/cell-capacity-mm1 Cellular with cell capacity Each cell's capacity shared by its users (an M/M/1 queue per device). cellular/uu/fixed-latency Cellular, measured latency A fixed one-way latency measured on a real network. cellular/uu/handover-outage Cellular with handovers Adds the interruption and loss of handovers between cells. cellular/uu/packet-pf Cellular, packet level Real base stations, a shared scheduler, retransmissions and TCP/TLS for backend traffic; slower to run. net.backend_net.id Value Label Meaning backend-net/fixed Fixed links Links between backend authorities with a set latency and capacity. net.geonet.forwarding Value Label Meaning on-air On the air (recommended) Each forwarded copy is a real frame: it queues, contends, can collide and loads the channel. overlay Protocol only (no MAC) Forwarding runs over a fixed radio range with no contention or collisions: optimistic reach. net.geonet.area_forwarding Value Label Meaning cbf Contention-based (CBF) The farthest receiver rebroadcasts first and the nearer ones stand down: few transmissions, the standard's choice. simple Flooding (simple) Every vehicle rebroadcasts the warning once: fast and robust, many transmissions. net.geonet.non_area_forwarding Value Label Meaning greedy Greedy Hand the warning to the neighbour nearest the area (the standard's default). cbf Contention-based Broadcast towards the area; the receiver that gets closest rebroadcasts first. net.geonet.cbf_variant Value Label Meaning etsi As evaluated in Artery (no duplicate check) A copy heard after forwarding is taken as new: very many transmissions (Amador et al. 2022). dpd With duplicate detection Each vehicle forwards a warning at most once; any copy makes a contender stand down, which can stall the spread. gpc Geographic cancellation (recommended) Stand down only when the copy came from farther along: near-full reach at low overhead (Amador et al. 2022). net.rsu_ip.air Value Label Meaning constant Constant air link The hop to a relaying roadside unit is a fixed delay and rate, and any unit in range serves. sch Advertised service (IEEE 1609.3) Each relaying unit sends a signed WSA for the SCMS service; a vehicle uses a unit only after it verified that unit's WSA.

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description nodes.default_obu string obu/unex-obu-301-craton2 obu/cohda-mk5, obu/cohda-mk6c-qualcomm-9150, obu/generic-automotive-soc-no-hsm, obu/pq-capable-hypothetical, obu/unex-obu-301-craton2, obu/unex-obu-301-craton2-softwarerecommended A shipped automotive profile; a post-quantum signature needs one with figures for it. basic wired The profile every equipped vehicle uses unless its class overrides it. The on-board unit hardware vehicles carry. It decides how long signing and verifying a message take. Model slot: family hardware-profile, see model parameters. nodes.compute_tier string medium abstract, medium, high advanced partial The compute tier. Status: abstract: signing and verification cost a microsecond and no node is ever compute-bound. medium: every operation costs the hardware profile's service time and queues FIFO behind one CPU server and the profile's HSM. high: the CPU runs as the profile's cores, so software cryptography and application tasks are served in parallel; it changes nothing for a profile whose cryptography runs on its HSM. Processor sharing, priority classes and HSM latency distributions are not built. nodes.backend_tier string medium abstract, medium, high advanced partial The backend tier. Status: abstract: backend entities never queue (64 servers, no fixed overhead). medium and high: each entity is an M/M/c with the deployment's servers and overhead, and the RA shuffles; high adds nothing over medium yet. nodes.verify_queue_depth integer messages [1, 4096]recommended 16 to 256; 64 is one second of 6 neighbours at 10 Hz. advanced wired How many received messages wait for signature verification before new ones are dropped, per node. 64 unless set (no profile publishes a depth). How many received messages can wait for signature verification; when the processor falls behind, messages beyond it are dropped. nodes.peer_cert_cache integer certificates [1, 65536]recommended 128 (engine default; no device publishes one); 16 to 1024. advanced wired How many peer certificates each vehicle or roadside unit holds before it forgets the least recently used one. 128 unless set (no profile publishes one). How many other stations' certificates each vehicle or roadside radio unit remembers; when it forgets one, that vehicle's next short-form message cannot be checked until its certificate is requested again. nodes.validated_cert_cache integer certificates 4096 [1, 1048576]recommended 4,096 (engine default; no device publishes one); 16 to 65,536. The peer certificate cache (128) usually forgets first. advanced wired How many validated end-entity certificates each device remembers, so a repeat signer costs only its signature check (least recently used evicted first). 4,096 unless set (v2xw_node::rxval::EE_CACHE; no device publishes one). The peer certificate cache usually bounds it first. How many already-checked certificates of other vehicles each device remembers, so a known sender costs only its signature check; a forgotten one is checked from scratch the next time it is heard. A small cache is what a certificate-flooding attack exhausts. nodes.hsm_sign_lower_us number us (0, 1000000]recommended Unset (every signature at the CRATON2's published <9 ms bound; no typical value is published); 613 us (software ECDSA P-256 on a Cortex-A53) to 9,000 us. advanced wired The lower edge of the HSM signing time, microseconds, for a profile that publishes only an upper bound (the CRATON2's "<9 ms"). Set, each signature takes a time drawn uniformly between this edge and the bound from the node's own random stream; unset, every signature takes the bound itself (the worst case). No typical value is published for the CRATON2/SECTON eHSM (searched 2026-10-13: Unex sheets, Autotalks pages, CMVP #3556/#4395 policies), so the default stays the bound. The fastest a hardware security module signs a message, when its maker only publishes a worst case; each signature then takes a random time between this and the worst case instead of always the worst case.

Which V2X radio vehicles use: DSRC (IEEE 802.11p, the original Wi-Fi-based standard), LTE-V2X (4G sidelink, 3GPP Release 14) or NR-V2X (5G sidelink, Release 16). radio.region string us, us-2016, eu advanced wired The regulatory region: its band plan, the channel each technology deploys on and the EIRP limits (v2xw_radio::regulation). Unset, the region's deployment channel for the technology. radio.channel_leakage boolean advanced wired Whether the run's own channels leak into each other through the transmitter mask and the receiver's selectivity (the ACIR of v2xw_radio::regulation). Unset is on; false is ideal channel filters. Only acts with radio.channels.

items.title: devices
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.devices.obu.tx_power_dbm number dBm 23.0 [-20, 33]recommended 20 dBm (SAE J2945/1) to 23 dBm (3GPP TR 36.885). basic wired Conducted transmit power at the antenna port, dBm; congestion control may lower it. How loudly each vehicle transmits. Louder reaches farther but interferes with more neighbours. radio.devices.obu.antenna_gain_dbi number dBi 3.0 [-10, 20] advanced wired Antenna gain, dBi, transmitting and receiving. radio.devices.obu.cable_loss_db number dB 0.0 [0, 20] advanced wired Loss of the cable between radio and antenna, dB, transmitting and receiving. radio.devices.obu.antenna_height_m number m [0.1, 15] advanced wired Antenna height above the road, metres; unset, 1.5 m on a car and 3 m on a truck or bus. radio.devices.obu.antenna_pattern string tr37885, rooftop, isotropic advanced wired The antenna's radiation pattern (v2xw_radio::antenna): TR 37.885's per vehicle type by default — a rooftop antenna on a car or van, front and rear panels on a truck or bus — every vehicle's on the roof, or none. radio.devices.obu.sampled_pattern.csv string advanced wired The table, as CSV text (a YAML block scalar): a header naming gain_db (dB relative to antenna_gain_dbi), azimuth_deg (counter-clockwise from the heading) or azimuth_cw_deg (clockwise), and optionally elevation_deg; then one sample a line. Interpolated linearly in dB. No default: the measurement is the scenario's. radio.devices.obu.sampled_pattern.rotation_deg number ° [-360, 360] advanced wired The mount's rotation from the heading, degrees counter-clockwise; default 0 (Veins SampledAntenna1D rotation, behaviour only). radio.devices.obu.sampled_pattern.rotation_jitter string none, uniform, normal advanced wired A per-vehicle random mount rotation on top: none (default), uniform in ±rotation_jitter_deg, or normal with σ = rotation_jitter_deg (Veins SampledAntenna1D random rotation, behaviour only). Keyed by seed and node. radio.devices.obu.sampled_pattern.rotation_jitter_deg number ° [0, 180] advanced wired The width of that rotation, degrees; default 0. radio.devices.obu.radios integer radios advanced wired How many 802.11p radios the unit carries: 1, the default (SAE J2945/1's on-board unit, continuously on the safety channel), or 2, which adds one on the service channel of radio.channels. Acts only with radio.channels. radio.devices.rsu.tx_power_dbm number dBm 23.0 [-20, 33] advanced wired Conducted transmit power at the antenna port, dBm. radio.devices.rsu.antenna_gain_dbi number dBi 3.0 [-10, 20] advanced wired Antenna gain, dBi, transmitting and receiving. radio.devices.rsu.cable_loss_db number dB 0.0 [0, 20] advanced wired Loss of the cable between radio and antenna, dB, transmitting and receiving. radio.devices.rsu.antenna_height_m number m [0.1, 15] advanced wired Antenna height above the ground, metres; unset, the site's own mast height. radio.devices.rsu.radios integer radios advanced wired How many 802.11p radios the unit carries: 2, the default, one on the safety channel and one on the service channel of radio.channels (the USDOT DSRC Roadside Unit Specification v4.1 calls for two radios), or 1. Acts only with radio.channels. radio.devices.rsu.off_channel.probability number [0, 1] advanced wired The share of sync intervals the unit leaves in, 0 to 1. radio.devices.rsu.off_channel.from_ms number ms [0, 100] advanced wired When it leaves, after the start of the UTC 100 ms sync interval, ms. radio.devices.rsu.off_channel.min_duration_ms number ms [0, 100] advanced wired The shortest time away, ms. radio.devices.rsu.off_channel.max_duration_ms number ms [0, 100] advanced wired The longest time away, ms. radio.devices.vru.tx_power_dbm number dBm 23.0 [-20, 33] advanced wired Conducted transmit power at the antenna port, dBm. radio.devices.vru.antenna_gain_dbi number dBi 0.0 [-10, 20] advanced wired Antenna gain, dBi, transmitting and receiving. radio.devices.vru.cable_loss_db number dB 0.0 [0, 20] advanced wired Loss of the cable between radio and antenna, dB, transmitting and receiving. radio.devices.vru.antenna_height_m number m 1.5 [0.1, 15] advanced wired Antenna height above the ground, metres. radio.devices.vru.radios integer radios advanced wired How many 802.11p radios the device carries: 1, the default (SAE J2945/9's personal device on the safety channel), or 2. Acts only with radio.channels.
