items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.range.margin_db number dB 10.0 [0, 40] advanced wired How far below the receiver's noise floor a line-of-sight arrival may fall before the transmission is no longer followed there, dB. radio.range.max_m number m [50, 100000] advanced wired A cap on the fully evaluated range, metres; beyond it only line-of-sight interference is counted. Unset, the link budget alone decides.

items.title: adjacent_channel[]
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.adjacent_channel[].rat string dsrc-80211p, lte-v2x-pc5, nr-v2x-pc5, hybrid advanced wired Its technology. radio.adjacent_channel[].channel integer channel number 172, 174, 176, 178, 180, 181, 182, 183, 184 advanced wired Its channel number; unset, the region's deployment channel for its technology. radio.adjacent_channel[].acir_db number dB advanced wired The adjacent-channel interference ratio, dB; unset, the region's mask for the emitter's technology combined with the minimum selectivity of this run's receivers (v2xw_radio::regulation::adjacent_acir_db). radio.adjacent_channel[].params json (serde_json::Value) advanced wired Where it is and when it transmits, as a jammer's: position_m, follow_node or path_m (with speed_mps, loop_path); power_dbm (23 by default), from_s, to_s, and period_ms with duty for an emitter that is not on all the time.

items.title: channels[]
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.channels[].channel integer channel number 172, 174, 176, 178, 180, 181, 182, 183, 184 advanced wired The IEEE channel number in the region's band plan (US 2016: 172-184; EU 172-184). radio.channels[].messages[] string advanced wired Messages[]

items.title: phy
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.phy.data_rate_mbps number Mbit/s [3, 27]recommended 6 Mbit/s (the US default); 3 for range, 12 to 18 for crowded channels. basic wired The data rate every safety frame is sent at, Mbit/s: one of 3, 4.5, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 or 27 (the eight 10 MHz OFDM rates of IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 17-4). A higher rate takes less air time per frame but needs a stronger signal, so it trades range for channel capacity. Unset is 6 Mbit/s, the SAE J2945/1 default. The 802.11p data rate (modulation and coding). Faster rates finish each frame sooner, so more radios fit on the channel, but they need a stronger signal, so range shrinks. radio.phy.noise_figure_db number dB [0, 15]recommended 6 dB (automotive module) to 9 dB (3GPP UE). advanced wired The receiver noise figure, dB: how much noise the receiver's own electronics add on top of the thermal floor of −104 dBm in 10 MHz. Unset is the hardware figure the PHY card cites (6 dB). How much noise the receiver's own electronics add; every extra dB costs about 10 % of range in free space. radio.phy.sensitivity_dbm number dBm [-105, -60]recommended -92 dBm (fielded units) to -85 dBm (ETSI minimum). advanced wired One receiver sensitivity at every data rate, dBm: a frame weaker than this is not decoded (Veins' minPowerLevel). Unset uses the per-rate table that radio.models.phy selects (fielded units, −92 dBm at 6 Mbit/s). The weakest frame the receiver decodes, at every data rate (Veins' minPowerLevel). radio.phy.cca_threshold_dbm number dBm [-100, -50]recommended -85 dBm (ETSI); -82 (ns-3); -65 (Veins). advanced wired The carrier-sense (CCA) threshold, dBm: energy above it makes a radio treat the channel as busy, defer its transmission and count the time in the channel busy ratio. Unset is −85 dBm (ETSI EN 302 571 §4.2.10.1). The signal level at which a radio hears the channel as busy and holds back; it also sets what the channel busy ratio counts. radio.phy.energy_detect_dbm number dBm [-100, -50]recommended -65 dBm (IEEE 802.11-2020 §17.3.10.6, 10 MHz); -62 (ns-3); -85 reproduces the older single-threshold carrier sense. advanced wired The energy-detect level, dBm: another channel's frame leaking through the channel filter holds carrier sense busy only above it (and, under SAE J2945/1, counts in the CBP only above it). Unset is −65 dBm, 20 dB above the 10 MHz minimum sensitivity (IEEE 802.11-2020 §17.3.10.6); never below cca_threshold_dbm. −85 dBm is the carrier sense before radio-fix4, which held a leak to the preamble level. The level at which another channel's frame, leaking through the filter, makes the radio hear its own channel as busy. radio.phy.capture_threshold_db number dB [0, 30]recommended Unset (error model); 4 to 10 dB to compare with threshold-based simulators. advanced wired A hard capture threshold, dB: a frame is decoded only while it stays this far above the interference plus noise (Torrent-Moreno 2009, Eq. 1). Unset uses the SINR trace against the error model, as Veins does. Replaces the error model with a hard rule: a frame survives only if it stays this many dB above interference plus noise.

items.title: mac
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.mac.edca_profile string by-region by-region, sae-j2945-1, en-302-663recommended By region (the default); SAE J2945/1 or EN 302 663 to compare the two on one map. advanced wired Which EDCA table the MAC contends with, and so where a BSM waits (EdcaProfileSpec). Unset is by-region: SAE J2945/1 Table 18 for 802.11p under a US region, ETSI EN 302 663 elsewhere (wiring::edca_profile). An explicit cw_min_* or aifsn_* below still wins over the table's own value. Which table of waiting times the radio uses before it sends: the US safety-message standard's, where a routine safety message waits a little longer than an emergency one, or the European default. radio.mac.periodic_access_category string vo, vi, be, bkrecommended Video for a US BSM (SAE J2945/1 user priority 5) or a European CAM; voice is a critical BSM's. advanced wired The access category periodic awareness messages (BSM, CAM, PSM, VAM, CPM, SPaT, MAP) are queued in: vo, vi, be or bk. Unset is vo, the highest, except for a BSM under SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (below). SAE J2945/1 §6.3.4 puts a BSM without a critical event flag at user priority 5, which is AC_VI (UPEDCA-001), and one with a flag at user priority 7, AC_VO (UPEDCA-002); EN 302 663 Annex C puts the CAM at vi. Unset under SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (MacSettings::edca_profile), a BSM is queued by its flags in exactly that way (wiring::bsm_queue_by_flags); set, it names the queue of every periodic message, the BSM included. The priority queue awareness messages wait in; higher priorities wait less before sending. radio.mac.event_access_category string vo, vi, be, bkrecommended Voice. advanced wired The access category event messages (DENM, forwarded hazard warnings) are queued in. Unset is vo (EN 302 663 Annex C). The priority queue hazard warnings (DENM) wait in. radio.mac.cw_min_vo integer slots [1, 1023]recommended 3 (standard) to 15 in dense traffic. advanced wired CWmin of the voice category, slots: a frame waits a random 0 to CWmin idle slots before it may start. A larger window means fewer collisions and more delay. Unset is 3 (EN 302 663 Table C.4). Broadcast never doubles it, so there is no CWmax to set. The random back-off window of the voice queue: a wider window spreads transmissions out, which means fewer collisions and more delay. radio.mac.aifsn_vo integer slots [2, 15]recommended 2 (standard). advanced wired AIFSN of the voice category, slots: the fixed idle wait before the countdown. Unset is 2. The fixed idle wait of the voice queue before its back-off countdown. radio.mac.cw_min_vi integer slots [1, 1023]recommended 15 under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18), 7 elsewhere (EN 302 663). advanced wired CWmin of the video category, slots. Unset is 15 for 802.11p under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18) and 7 elsewhere (EN 302 663). The random back-off window of the video queue. radio.mac.aifsn_vi integer slots [2, 15]recommended 4 under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18), 3 elsewhere (EN 302 663). advanced wired AIFSN of the video category, slots. Unset is 4 for 802.11p under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18) and 3 elsewhere (EN 302 663). The fixed idle wait of the video queue. radio.mac.queue_length integer frames [1, 1024]recommended 16 to 64. advanced wired How many frames each access category queues before it drops the next. Unset is 64. How many frames wait in each priority queue before new ones are dropped.

items.title: channel_model
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.channel_model.path_loss_exponent number [1.5, 6]recommended 1.8 (highway) to 3.5 (dense city). advanced wired A single-slope path-loss exponent: 2 is free space, about 2.7 to 3.5 a city street. Setting it, or the shadowing spread, runs the log-distance law (propagation/log-distance-shadowing) with these numbers over a free-space anchor at 10 m. Unset keeps the measured dual-slope fits. How fast the signal weakens with distance: 2 in free space, near 3 in a built-up street. Setting it runs the log-distance law. radio.channel_model.shadowing_sigma_db number dB [0, 15]recommended 3 to 4 dB in line of sight, 6 to 7 dB obstructed. advanced wired The log-normal shadowing standard deviation, dB: how much the received power wanders around the path-loss mean as buildings and trucks come and go. Unset keeps the fit's own (about 4 dB in line of sight, 6 to 7 dB obstructed, Abbas 2015). How much the signal wanders around its average as buildings and trucks block it. radio.channel_model.shadowing_decorrelation_m number m (0, 500]recommended 10 m (city) to 50 m (highway). advanced wired How far a vehicle moves before its shadowing is uncorrelated with what it was, metres (Gudmundson 1991). Unset is the environment's (about 10 m in a city). How far a vehicle travels before its shadowing changes completely. radio.channel_model.fading string none, rayleigh, rice, nakagamirecommended Leave unset (Nakagami m = 3); Rayleigh for a worst case. basic wired The small-scale fading law: none, rayleigh (no direct path), rice (a direct path rice_k_db stronger than the scatter) or nakagami (shape nakagami_shape). Unset keeps the tier's choice (Nakagami m = 3 for 802.11p). The fast signal fluctuation as vehicles move a few centimetres: Rayleigh has no direct path, Rice and Nakagami have one. It is the main cause of losses well inside range. radio.channel_model.fading_coherence string independent, dopplerrecommended independent (today's behaviour); doppler for burst-loss studies (Akki & Haber 1986; Rappaport 2002 Eq. 5.40c). advanced wired How the fade of one link changes from frame to frame: independent (each frame draws its own, the default) or doppler (one fade per coherence time, 0.423 / f_D with f_D from both ends' speeds and the carrier, so slow links fade in bursts and fast links decorrelate; Akki & Haber 1986, Rappaport 2002 Eq. 5.40c). Whether a link's fade carries over from one message to the next: with doppler, vehicles standing still (a queue at a red light) keep a bad fade for many messages in a row, while fast vehicles get a fresh fade with every message. radio.channel_model.nakagami_shape number [0.5, 20]recommended 1 to 5. advanced wired The Nakagami shape m when fading is nakagami (written m in the literature): 1 is Rayleigh, larger is milder. Unset is 3. The Nakagami shape m: 1 is Rayleigh, larger values are milder fading. radio.channel_model.rice_k_db number dB [-10, 30]recommended 3 to 10 dB. advanced wired The Rice factor K when fading is rice, dB: the direct path's power over the scattered power's. Unset is 6 dB. The strength of the direct path over the scattered ones in a Rice channel. radio.channel_model.nakagami_shape_far number [0.5, 20]recommended 0.75 to 1 beyond about 80-100 m. advanced wired The Nakagami m beyond nakagami_breakpoint_m, when fading is nakagami, for a channel that gets harsher with range (Veins-style: about 1.5 near, 0.75 far). Needs the breakpoint. Unset keeps nakagami_shape at every distance. The fading severity beyond the breakpoint distance, for a channel that gets harsher with range. radio.channel_model.nakagami_breakpoint_m number m (0, 5000]recommended 80 to 100 m. advanced wired The distance at which the Nakagami m switches to nakagami_shape_far, metres. The distance at which the fading switches to its far-away severity. radio.channel_model.building_wall_loss_db number dB [0, 40]recommended 9 dB (Sommer 2011 default); 2.4 dB for light construction. advanced wired How much each building wall the signal passes through costs (Sommer 2011 β), dB: 9 dB for the fitted default, about 2.4 dB for light construction. How much each building wall between two cars costs the signal (Sommer 2011's β, as Veins models it). radio.channel_model.building_loss_db_per_m number dB/m [0, 10]recommended 0.4 dB/m (Sommer 2011 default); 0.1-0.63 dB/m across the fitted rows. advanced wired How much each metre of path inside a building costs (Sommer 2011 γ), dB per metre: 0.4 for the fitted default. How much each metre of the path inside a building costs (Sommer 2011's γ). radio.channel_model.vehicle_blockage boolean recommended On for realism; off to measure what blockage costs. advanced wired Whether other vehicles between two antennas attenuate the signal (3GPP TR 37.885 NLOSv blockage). On by default with the city-street law; off makes vehicles radio-transparent, on charges them under every law. Whether trucks and cars between two antennas weaken the signal (3GPP TR 37.885 NLOSv). radio.channel_model.foliage boolean recommended Off (today); on with world.vegetation for suburban and rural maps with woods and tree-lined streets. advanced wired Whether a path through trees loses the foliage excess (ITU-R P.833 §3.1 with GEMV²'s 2.3 dB/m at 5.9 GHz, capped at the diffraction over the canopy: obstacle/foliage/p833). Needs world.vegetation. Unset is off. Whether trees between two antennas weaken the signal: about 2.3 dB per metre of trees at 5.9 GHz, up to what bending over the treetops would cost. Needs world.vegetation. radio.channel_model.density_sigma boolean recommended Off (today, a fixed spread); on for the measured dependence on surroundings. advanced wired Whether the log-distance law's shadowing σ grows with the vehicles and buildings around the link (GEMV², Boban et al. 2014 eq. 10: 3.3 dB on an empty road to 5.2 dB downtown for line of sight). Unset keeps the preset's fixed σ. Whether the signal's random variation grows with the traffic and buildings around each link, as measured in Porto (GEMV2): calmer on an empty road, rougher downtown. radio.channel_model.reflection boolean recommended Off (today); on for downtown maps, where reflections carry links round corners. advanced wired Whether a building-blocked link also receives the strongest single specular reflection off a building wall, power-summed with the shadowed path (GEMV², Boban et al. 2014 §IV-B.3, eqs. 6-8; ITU-R P.2040-3 Table 3 for the walls: obstacle/reflection/gemv2-single-bounce). Needs buildings. Unset is off. Whether a signal blocked by a building can still arrive by bouncing once off another building's wall, as it does down a street canyon: the bounce costs its longer path and the wall's reflection loss.

items.title: dcc
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.dcc.enabled boolean recommended On, except as the baseline of a congestion study. basic wired Whether 802.11p congestion control runs at all. false lets every radio send at its full rate and power however busy the channel is: the baseline a DCC study compares against. Unset is on (EN 302 571 requires it in Europe). Congestion control: radios slow down or turn their power down when the channel is busy, so the channel stays usable. Turn it off to measure what it buys. radio.dcc.cbr_target number [0.1, 0.95]recommended 0.6 to 0.7 (standard 0.68). advanced wired The channel load the ETSI adaptive algorithm steers towards, as a fraction of time busy. Unset is 0.68 (TS 102 687 V1.2.1 Table 3). The share of time busy the ETSI adaptive algorithm aims the channel at. radio.dcc.adaptive_alpha number [0.001, 0.5]recommended 0.016 (standard). advanced wired The ETSI adaptive smoothing factor α: how much of each new load measurement enters the running average. Unset is 0.016 (ibid.). How quickly the ETSI adaptive algorithm's load average follows new measurements. radio.dcc.adaptive_beta number [0.0001, 0.05]recommended 0.0012 (standard). advanced wired The ETSI adaptive gain β: how hard the allowed duty cycle reacts to the gap from the target. Unset is 0.0012 (ibid.). How strongly the ETSI adaptive algorithm changes the allowed airtime when the load is off target. radio.dcc.max_itt_ms number ms [100, 2000]recommended 600 ms (standard). advanced wired The longest interval SAE J2945/1 may stretch a BSM's spacing to under congestion, ms (vMax_ITT). Unset is 600 ms. The longest gap J2945/1 allows between one vehicle's BSMs under congestion. radio.dcc.density_coefficient number vehicles [1, 200]recommended 25 (standard). advanced wired The vehicle density at which SAE J2945/1 starts to stretch the interval (B, vehicles within 100 m). Unset is 25. How many neighbours within 100 m J2945/1 tolerates before it stretches the BSM interval. radio.dcc.power_control boolean recommended On (J2945/1); off for rate-only control. advanced wired Whether SAE J2945/1 also lowers the radiated power as the channel fills. Unset is on (J2945/1 §6.3.8); J3161/1 for LTE-V2X has none. Whether J2945/1 also turns the radiated power down as the channel fills. radio.dcc.min_power_dbm number dBm [-10, 20]recommended 10 dBm (standard). advanced wired The lowest power J2945/1's power control may go to, dBm (vRP_Min). Unset is 10. The lowest power J2945/1's power control may reach. radio.dcc.reactive_table string a1, a2recommended A.1 for secured CAMs at 6 Mbit/s; A.2 only for short frames. advanced wired ETSI reactive DCC's table (TS 102 687 V1.2.1 Annex A): a1 (frames up to 1 ms on air, Table A.1, the default) or a2 (up to 500 µs, Table A.2, twice the rates). Which ETSI reactive table sets the message rate in each congestion state: A.1 for frames up to 1 ms on air, A.2 (twice the rates) for frames up to 500 µs. radio.dcc.reactive_hold_ms number ms [0, 5000]recommended 0 (the tables give none) to 1,000 ms. advanced wired ETSI reactive DCC's state-hold time, ms: how long a state is held before the next step. 0 unless set (the tables specify no hysteresis). How long reactive congestion control stays in a state before it may step again; longer holds damp oscillation. radio.dcc.channel_quality string sae-j2945-1, fmvss150-nprmrecommended SAE J2945/1 Eq. 4 (the default); the FMVSS 150 NPRM smoothing only to reproduce older results. advanced wired SAE J2945/1's channel-quality indicator Π: sae-j2945-1 (unset) is 6.3.8.1 Eq. 4, the mean PER of the neighbours within 100 m capped at 0.3; fmvss150-nprm smooths it with weight 0.9 on the previous value, as the withdrawn FMVSS 150 NPRM transcribed it (11-j2945-1-conformance.md J3a). How SAE J2945/1 judges the channel from its neighbours' lost messages, which decides how often it assumes they missed its last BSM and sends an extra one.

items.title: sidelink
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description radio.sidelink.reservation_interval_ms integer ms [1, 1000]recommended 100 ms for 10 Hz BSMs; 20 or 50 ms for faster traffic. advanced wired How often a radio's reserved resource repeats, ms (the resource reservation interval, RRI). LTE allows 20, 50, 100 or a multiple of 100 up to 1,000 (TS 36.331 sl-ResourceReservationPeriod); NR also 1 to 99. Unset is 100 ms, one BSM period. How often a C-V2X radio's booked slot repeats; it should match how often the radio has a message to send. radio.sidelink.resource_keep_probability number [0, 0.8]recommended 0.8 (J3161/1); 0 to study fast reselection. advanced wired The probability a radio keeps its resource when the reselection counter runs out (probResourceKeep): 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 or 0.8 (TS 36.331). Higher keeps reservations stable for others to sense, but makes two radios that collide keep colliding. Unset is the profile's (0.8 under SAE J3161/1). The chance a radio keeps its booked slot when its counter runs out, rather than picking a new one. radio.sidelink.rsrp_threshold_dbm number dBm [-128, -60]recommended -128 dBm (NR studies) to -110 dBm (LTE studies). advanced wired The RSRP above which a resource another radio reserved is excluded from selection, dBm; it is raised 3 dB at a time until enough candidates remain (TS 36.213 §14.1.1.6). Unset is the profile's (−128 dBm NR, −110 dBm LTE studies). How strong another radio's booking must be for a radio to avoid that slot. radio.sidelink.sensing boolean recommended On; off only as a baseline. advanced wired Whether radios sense the channel before choosing a resource. false is the random selection baseline (Ali et al. 2021 §II.1). Unset is on. Whether radios listen before booking a slot. Off is the random-selection baseline. radio.sidelink.candidate_percent integer % [20, 50]recommended 20 % (LTE's fixed value); 35 or 50 % on NR. advanced wired The share of the selection window that must survive exclusion before a radio picks: 20 % (LTE's fixed value), 35 % or 50 % (NR only). Unset is 20 %. The share of resources that must remain after exclusion before a radio picks one. radio.sidelink.selection_window_ms integer ms [1, 100]recommended 100 ms at 10 Hz; at most the message interval. advanced wired How late after a message is ready its new resource may be (the selection window's end T2), ms. Shorter cuts latency but leaves fewer resources to pick from; at most the message interval. Unset is the profile's (100 ms at 10 Hz). How late after a message is ready its new resource may be. Shorter cuts latency but leaves fewer resources to pick from. radio.sidelink.noise_figure_db number dB [0, 15]recommended 9 dB (3GPP TR 36.885 UE); 6 dB for a good automotive module. advanced wired The UE receiver noise figure, dB: TR 36.885 Annex A.1.1's 9 dB unless set. It moves every sidelink noise floor (and the candidate range measured against it). How much noise a C-V2X receiver's own electronics add; every extra dB shortens the range at which a transport block still decodes. radio.sidelink.cbr_threshold_dbm number dBm [-112, -8]recommended -94 dBm (this build's default); -112 to -80 dBm in 2 dB steps (TS 36.331). advanced wired sl-ThresS-RSSI-CBR, dBm: the S-RSSI above which a sub-channel counts as busy in the channel busy ratio (TS 36.214 §5.1.30, TS 36.331 range -112 to -8 dBm in 2 dB steps). -94 dBm unless set; the CR limits and every CBR metric read it. The signal level above which a C-V2X sub-channel counts as busy in the channel busy ratio, which drives congestion control. radio.sidelink.align_generation boolean recommended Off (today's default, every LTE-V2X run unchanged); on for a deployment-faithful LTE-V2X latency. advanced wired Whether each radio generates its periodic BSM just before its reserved resource, as SAE J3161/1 has the application do, instead of on its own 100 ms clock: the BSM then waits a margin for its resource rather than up to a whole period. The phase follows every reselection; an interval it changes stays inside J2945/1's bounds. Unset is off. Whether each C-V2X radio builds its safety message just before its reserved slot, as SAE J3161/1 has deployed radios do, so the message waits a millisecond or two for the air instead of up to a tenth of a second. radio.sidelink.align_margin_ms number ms [0, 50]recommended 1 ms (the radio's processing time T1); an assumption until J3161/1's own figure is read. advanced wired How long before its reserved resource an aligned BSM reaches the radio, ms, on top of the device's longest signing time. Unset is the pool's processing time T1 (1 ms on LTE-V2X): an ASSUMPTION until J3161/1's figure is read. With aligned generation, how long before its reserved slot the signed message reaches the radio, on top of the longest time the device takes to sign it.

items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description scale.traffic.model string mobility/tiered/meso-micro, mobility/meso/queuerecommended mobility/tiered/meso-micro with a box around the area you study; leave the section out for a single microscopic map. advanced wired mobility/tiered/meso-micro — microscopic inside region, a queue network outside — or mobility/meso/queue, the whole world as queues. City scale: drive a map box vehicle by vehicle and everything outside it as queues (tiered), or the whole map as queues; the queues carry a whole city's traffic at a fraction of the cost. scale.traffic.region.min_lat_deg number ° advanced wired South edge, degrees north. scale.traffic.region.min_lon_deg number ° advanced wired West edge, degrees east. scale.traffic.region.max_lat_deg number ° advanced wired North edge, degrees north. scale.traffic.region.max_lon_deg number ° advanced wired East edge, degrees east. scale.traffic.meso.segment_length_m number m [1, 10000]recommended 98 m (SUMO MESO --meso-edgelength default); 50 to 200 m. advanced wired The longest a queue segment may be, metres (--meso-edgelength, 98). The longest stretch of road one queue covers; shorter segments place vehicles more precisely and cost more. scale.traffic.meso.tau_ff_s number s (0, 60]recommended 1.13 s (SUMO MESO --meso-tauff, Eissfeldt 2003); 0.9 to 1.5 s. advanced wired Headway from a free segment into a free one, seconds (--meso-tauff, 1.13). Time between vehicles leaving a jammed queue into a free-flowing one: the start-up loss of a jam. scale.traffic.meso.tau_jj_s number s (0, 60]recommended 1.4 s (SUMO MESO --meso-taujj); 1.1 to 1.8 s. advanced wired Headway from a jammed segment into a jammed one, seconds (--meso-taujj, 1.4). Time between vehicles leaving a jammed queue into another jammed one. scale.traffic.meso.jam_threshold number [0, 1]recommended Leave unset (SUMO's default); 0.2 to 0.8 when set. advanced wired The occupancy share above which a segment is jammed; absent, SUMO's speed rule. How full a queue must be before it counts as jammed; left out, SUMO's speed rule decides. scale.traffic.meso.junction_control boolean recommended On (SUMO MESO --meso-junction-control); off only to compare with an unsignalled queue network. advanced wired Whether a signal holds the head of a queue while its movement is not green. items.title: Cryptography
items.text:
The signature and encryption schemes, and whether the mathematics is done (real) or only charged for (modelled). Committees, where t-of-n servers share one authority's key, are a research option and not the US system.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description security.envelope string ieee1609.2 ieee1609.2, etsi103097recommended ieee1609.2 (US). advanced wired The envelope profile: ieee1609.2 or etsi103097. The secured-message format: IEEE 1609.2 (the US) or ETSI TS 103 097 (Europe). security.signature string ecdsa-p256 ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1, ecdsa-p384, hybrid-falcon512-ecdsa-p256, hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256, hybrid-mldsa65-ecdsa-p256, ml-dsa-44, ml-dsa-65, ml-dsa-87, falcon-512, falcon-1024, slh-dsa-sha2-128s, slh-dsa-sha2-128fnarrowed by security.crypto_mode when realrecommended ECDSA P-256, or a hybrid to study the cost of post-quantum security. basic partial The signature scheme, e.g. ecdsa-p256, hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256, ml-dsa-65 — any id in v2xw_sec::scheme::SIGNATURE_IDS. The digital signature on every message. ECDSA is what is deployed today; post-quantum signatures resist a quantum computer but are many times larger. Status: Any scheme in the registry (v2xw_sec::scheme::SIGNATURE_IDS; adding one is one module): classical ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1, ecdsa-p384; hybrids (ECDSA P-256 with Falcon-512, ML-DSA-44 or ML-DSA-65 concatenated); pure ML-DSA-44/65/87, Falcon-512/1024 and SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s/128f. Each changes the octets of every signed message and attached certificate on the air by its parts' published sizes (FIPS 204, FIPS 205, Falcon, SEC 1; a pure scheme replaces the ECDSA fields); an SPDU above the network MTU is refused and counted unless a fragmenter is selected. Each is charged its time: every signature and verification costs the sum of its parts on the hardware profile, a profile with no figure for a part falls back to the catalogue anchor it names (crypto_anchors; derived by cycle ratio where nothing is published, and flagged), and a profile that prices none is refused by name (the reference OBU publishes no post-quantum figure). brainpool and P-384 are charged the P-256 time. Only ecdsa-p256 runs in real crypto mode. A post-quantum scheme is the credential system's too (SCMS and CCMS): every certificate carries the post-quantum key and issuer signature, every signed backend message the post-quantum signature, authorities pay at the Raspberry Pi 5 liboqs figure (an upper bound for a server) and devices at the Cohda MK6's; there is no post-quantum butterfly, so a device generates one post-quantum key per pseudonym certificate or ticket and uploads each encrypted to the PCA or AA (v2xw_proto::hybrid). security.kem string ecies-p256 ecies-p256, ml-kem-512, ml-kem-768, ml-kem-1024, hybrid-ecies-p256-ml-kem-768recommended ecies-p256 (US). advanced wired The key-encapsulation scheme for encryption to the PCA and to devices, e.g. ecies-p256 or ml-kem-768 — any id in v2xw_sec::scheme::KEM_IDS. How a certificate response is encrypted to its device: ECIES on P-256 (IEEE 1609.2), or a post-quantum or hybrid scheme for study. security.threshold.protocol string frost-p256, cggmp21-ecdsa, umbrella, shamir-feldmanrecommended frost-p256. advanced wired The signing protocol for the PCA and the CRL Generator: an id in v2xw_proto::threshold::THRESHOLD_IDS (frost-p256, cggmp21-ecdsa, umbrella). The protocol a committee of servers uses to hold one authority's key together (not the US system). security.threshold.members integer servers [1, 64]recommended 5. advanced wired Committee size. How many servers form a committee. security.threshold.quorum integer servers [1, 64]recommended 3 of 5. advanced wired How many members must act: a quorum-of-members committee. How many committee members must take part to sign. security.threshold.roles[] string pca, crl, linkagerecommended All three for a committee study. advanced wired Which authorities run as committees: the pseudonym CA, the CRL Generator, the linkage authorities. security.threshold.linkage_members integer servers [1, 64]recommended Unset (the same as members). advanced wired The linkage committee's size and quorum, when linkage is a role (defaults to members and quorum). The linkage committee's size, when it differs from the others. security.threshold.linkage_quorum integer servers [1, 64]recommended Unset (the same as quorum). advanced wired See ThresholdSpec::linkage_members. The linkage committee's quorum, when it differs from the others. security.threshold.umbrella_leaves integer pseudonyms [1, 1000]recommended 20 (one US week's certificates). advanced wired For umbrella: leaf pseudonyms per umbrella credential. Under the umbrella protocol, how many pseudonyms one umbrella certificate covers. Applies when security.threshold.protocol is umbrella. security.threshold.umbrella_inner string frost-p256, cggmp21-ecdsa, umbrella, shamir-feldmanrecommended frost-p256. advanced wired For umbrella: the protocol the committee signs umbrellas with. Under the umbrella protocol, the signing protocol that signs the umbrella certificates. Applies when security.threshold.protocol is umbrella. security.threshold.preprocessed boolean recommended Off. advanced wired Whether the offline phase (FROST commitments, CGGMP21 presignatures) is done ahead of time, leaving the online round alone. Do the committee's offline round ahead of time, so a signing needs one online round. security.threshold.round_timeout_ms number ms (0, 60000]recommended 500 ms. advanced wired How long a coordinator waits for a round before excluding the silent, ms. How long the coordinator waits for a member in each round before giving up on it. security.threshold.retry_after_s number s (0, 3600]recommended 30 s. advanced wired How long it waits before retrying a session that ran out of members, s. How long a failed committee signing waits before it is retried. security.threshold.ask_all boolean recommended On. advanced wired Ask every live member and keep the first quorum (true), or exactly a quorum. Ask every live member and keep the first quorum to answer, rather than asking exactly a quorum. security.threshold.member_latency_ms number ms [0, 1000]recommended 20 ms (ASSUMPTION: a WAN between organisations). advanced wired One-way latency between a coordinator and a member, ms: separate organisations over a WAN. The one-way latency between committee members. security.crypto_mode string modeled modeled, realrecommended modeled for speed; real to check a result. advanced wired modeled costs the operations without doing the mathematics; real does the mathematics. Both are recorded in the manifest. Whether signing and verification are charged their measured time with the outcome modelled, or the mathematics is done on real bytes (P-256 only).

Which credential system issues the certificates vehicles sign with: the US Security Credential Management System (SCMS) or the European C-ITS trust model (ETSI TS 102 941). Every default's source: docs/reference/scms-constants.md. Vehicles top up over their backend link when the pool runs low and cannot sign once it is empty. 'protocol/etsi/ts102941' runs the ETSI ITS PKI: authorization tickets (certs_per_period a period, no linkage), TS 103 759 reports straight to the MA, and passive revocation only — the authority's decision blocklists the enrolment credential at the EA, the vehicle keeps its tickets until they expire and no reception is refused (TS 102 941 §6.1.4 NOTE 4). items.title: Receiver checks
items.text:
What a receiving vehicle accepts: how old or how far in the future a message may be, and which messages it verifies when it cannot verify all of them.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description security.verification_policy string verify-all verify-all, on-demand, prioritizedrecommended Verify every message, unless you study verification load. With detection on, expect a warning for any other choice. basic wired verify-all, on-demand or prioritized. Which received messages a vehicle checks the signature of. Checking everything is safest but can overload the security chip in dense traffic. Misbehaviour detection only judges messages whose signature was checked (a report's evidence is the accused's signed messages, SCMS Manager SM-MBR v1.0 §2.3.1.2.1), so verifying on demand or nearest first also blinds detection: in testing, on-demand cut reports from 897 to 79 and no attacker was revoked. security.on_demand_threshold number score (0, 1]recommended 0.5 (a time to collision of 1 s); 0.05 to 0.9. No published operating point (Krishnan & Weimerskirch 2011); sweep it. advanced wired The relevance score at or above which an on-demand node verifies a message from a signer it already knows. 0.5 unless set; refused under any other policy. Under on-demand verification, how threatening a known vehicle's message must look (from its time to collision, 0 to 1) before it is checked; lower checks more messages and costs more processor time. Applies when security.verification_policy is on-demand. security.prioritized_horizon_m number m [10, 2000]recommended 300 m (the DSRC/C-V2X awareness range); 100 to 1000 m. advanced wired The distance beyond which proximity adds nothing to a prioritized node's service priority, metres. 300 unless set; refused under any other policy. Under prioritized verification, how far away a sender can be and still be checked ahead of farther ones; senders beyond it get no head start for being near. Applies when security.verification_policy is prioritized. security.scms.rx_beacon_max_age_s number s 30.0 [0, 31536000]recommended By profile: 30 s in the US (SAE J2945/1 Table 11, the BSM validity period), 2 s in Europe (CAR 2 CAR Communication Consortium Basic System Profile RS_BSP_168); a year turns the check off for a study. advanced wired The receiver's generationTime relevance window (IEEE 1609.2 §5.2, v2xw_node::rxval::GenerationTimeWindow): the oldest a received BSM, CAM, PSM or VAM may be on the receiver's own clock, seconds. Unset, by profile (crate::credentials::generation_window): 30 under the US IEEE 1609.2 envelope (SAE J2945/1 Table 11), 2 under ETSI (C2C-CC BSP RS_BSP_168). Older ones are discarded unverified and never reach a detector. How old a received safety beacon (BSM, CAM, PSM, VAM) may be, by the receiver's own clock, before it is thrown away unchecked (IEEE 1609.2 relevance check). It makes an old replay harmless, and it is why a vehicle whose clock is badly wrong is ignored rather than reported for misbehaviour. Left unset it follows the profile: 30 s in the US, 2 s in Europe. Under the US window a replay a few seconds old is verified and must be caught by misbehaviour detection. security.scms.rx_max_age_s number s 600.0 [0, 31536000]recommended 600 s (RS_BSP_168). advanced wired The same for every other application message (SPaT, MAP, DENM, CPM, SRM, SSM), seconds (600 unless set, RS_BSP_168, under either profile). The same age limit for every other application message: signal phase, intersection maps, hazard warnings, collective perception. security.scms.rx_max_future_s number s 30.0 [0, 31536000]recommended By profile: 30 s in the US (SAE J2945/1 Table 11, the acceptable future data period), 0.04 s in Europe (RS_BSP_168); a year turns the check off for a study. advanced wired How far ahead of the receiver's own clock a generationTime may be, seconds. Unset, by profile: 30 under the US envelope (J2945/1 Table 11), 0.04 under ETSI (RS_BSP_168). How far ahead of the receiver's own clock a message's time stamp may be. A sender whose clock runs ahead is ignored past it. Left unset it follows the profile: 30 s in the US, 40 ms in Europe. The misbehaviour authority still sets aside report evidence stamped more than 40 ms after its report, whatever this says.

items.title: Certificate lifecycle
items.text:
How a vehicle gets and uses its certificates. It enrols once, receives 20 pseudonym certificates per week in batches from the RA, tops up before it runs out, and changes pseudonym while driving so it cannot be followed. Defaults are the US deployment's, with the source on each field.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description security.signer_id_policy.full_cert_every_ms integer ms [0, 3600000]recommended Unset (BSM 450 ms, SAE J2945/1 6.5.2 vMaxCertDigestInterval; CAM 1 s, ETSI TS 103 097). A value overrides both. advanced wired The cadence, milliseconds, for every message type. Unset, each message type takes its own standard's: a BSM attaches its certificate when 450 ms have passed since the last one that did (SAE J2945/1 §6.5.2 BSMSIGN-003, Table 21 vMaxCertDigestInterval), a CAM and every other message once a second (ETSI TS 103 097 §7.1.1). A value overrides both; 0 attaches it to every message. How often a message carries the full certificate rather than an 8-byte digest; receivers need the certificate once to verify the digests. Unset, each message type takes its standard's: a BSM every 450 ms, a CAM once a second. security.signer_id_policy.digest_otherwise boolean true recommended On. advanced wired Attach a digest the rest of the time. Send an 8-byte certificate digest between full certificates, which saves about 140 bytes a message. security.signer_id_policy.on_new_neighbour boolean recommended Off (the US cadence alone); on for the ETSI rule (TS 103 097 §7.1.1). advanced wired Also attach the certificate to the next BSM or CAM after a station this node has not heard before appears (the ETSI CAM rule, TS 103 097 V1.3.1 §7.1.1). Off by default, and left out of a scenario that does not set it. Send the full certificate in the next safety message whenever a vehicle it has not heard before comes into range, so the newcomer can check its signatures at once. security.pseudonym_change.strategy string by-region by-region, time, distance, j2945-1, nyc-pilot, c2c-cc, mix-zone, silentrecommended By region (US: SAE J2945/1). Time-based only to study the change rate itself. basic wired by-region (the default), time, distance, j2945-1, nyc-pilot, c2c-cc, mix-zone or silent (crate::pseudonym_policy). by-region is the rule of the envelope's region (PseudonymChangeSpec::effective_strategy). When a vehicle switches to a new anonymous certificate, so an eavesdropper cannot follow it across the city. The default follows the region: SAE J2945/1 in the US (every 5 minutes, but not within 2,100 m of the last change or during hard braking or an ABS event), every 5 minutes in Europe. security.pseudonym_change.period_s number s [1, 86400]recommended 60 to 300 s; 300 s is SAE J2945/1's interval. basic wired The period, seconds, when the strategy is time-based. How often a vehicle changes pseudonym under the time-based strategy. Applies when security.pseudonym_change.strategy is time. security.pseudonym_change.distance_m number m [1, 100000]recommended 2,000 m (the NYC pilot); 2,100 m is SAE J2945/1's vCertChangeDistance, which the j2945-1 strategy applies on its own. advanced wired The distance, metres, when the strategy is distance-based. Under the distance strategy, how far in a straight line from the last change point a vehicle must be before it changes pseudonym. Applies when security.pseudonym_change.strategy is distance. security.pseudonym_change.silent_period_s[] number s [0, 60]recommended None; 3 to 13 s (PRESERVE) for a privacy study. advanced wired A random silence after each pseudonym change, between from and to seconds, so a listener loses the vehicle; its safety messages stop too. security.pseudonym_change.mix_zone_radius_m number m [5, 500]recommended 30 m (one junction, Freudiger et al. 2007). advanced wired The mix zone's radius around a signalised intersection, metres (mix-zone). Under the mix-zone strategy, the radius of the zone at a signalised junction where vehicles change pseudonym together. Applies when security.pseudonym_change.strategy is mix-zone. security.pseudonym_change.mix_zone_min_age_s number s [0, 3600]recommended 60 s. advanced wired The age a pseudonym must reach before a mix zone changes it, seconds (mix-zone). The youngest pseudonym a mix zone changes, so a vehicle does not burn certificates at every junction. Applies when security.pseudonym_change.strategy is mix-zone. security.scms.lifecycle.i_period_s number s 604800.0 [1, 31536000]recommended 604,800 s (one week, CAMP-EE) on the real calendar; 60 to 3,600 s only with time.calendar compressed. advanced wired The i-period, s: how long one set of pseudonym certificates is current (one week, 604,800 s, CAMP-EE §2.1.5.3.2). Anything shorter needs time.calendar: compressed. How long one set of pseudonym certificates is current. The US system uses one week from its 2015-01-06 epoch; a shorter period compresses the calendar so a short run sees weekly events, and the run is then labelled compressed. security.scms.lifecycle.cert_lifetime_s number s 608400.0 [1, 31536000]recommended 608,400 s (the week plus one hour, CAMP-EE); at least the i-period. advanced wired A pseudonym certificate's lifetime, s: the i-period plus the overlap (10,140 min, one hour longer than the week, CAMP-EE §2.1.5.3.2). How long each pseudonym certificate is valid: the period plus an overlap, so a vehicle always holds a valid one across the change of week. security.scms.lifecycle.certs_per_period integer certificates 20 [1, 60]recommended 20 (the US profile); 5 to 60 (60 for vehicles that change often, such as taxis). basic wired Pseudonym certificates per i-period, all valid at once (20, CAMP-EE Table 2.1.2.6.2; at most 60). How many pseudonym certificates a vehicle may use in one week, all valid at once. More lets it change identity more often without reusing one, at the cost of bigger downloads, and one revocation then covers more certificates. The US profile issues 20 a week (CAMP-EE Table 2.1.2.6.2). security.scms.lifecycle.pool_periods integer i-periods 2 [1, 64]recommended 2 (engine default); 1 to 8 (a THEA device is pre-loaded with three years, more than any run uses). advanced wired i-periods a vehicle holds when the run starts (2). How many weeks of certificates a vehicle holds when the run starts. security.scms.lifecycle.topup_below_periods integer i-periods 1 [0, 64]recommended 1 (engine default); 0 to 4. advanced wired A vehicle asks for its next period when fewer than this many periods, the current one counted, remain (1; 0 turns top-ups off). A vehicle asks for its next week of certificates when fewer than this many weeks, the current one counted, remain; 0 turns top-ups off, so the pool only drains. security.scms.lifecycle.max_periods_ahead integer i-periods 156 [1, 520]recommended 156 weeks (three years, CAMP Primer); 1 to 156. advanced wired The most i-periods ahead the RA provisions a device (156, three years, CAMP Primer p.7: 3,120 = 156 × 20). The most weeks ahead the Registration Authority provisions a device; a request for more is cut to this. security.scms.lifecycle.cert_shuffle_threshold integer requests 1000 [1, 1000000]recommended 1,000 (CAMP's production value); 10 to 10,000 (Brecht et al. 2018 used 10,000). It acts on a device's first request only: every vehicle in a run is provisioned before it joins, and its weekly top-ups are the RA's pre-generation, which does not wait in this mix, so a run's results do not change. advanced partial Certificate requests that release the RA's shuffle before its window closes (1,000, CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67 shuffle_threshold). How many certificate requests the Registration Authority collects and mixes before passing them on, so the authority that signs the certificates cannot tell which vehicle asked when; a batch also leaves when its oldest request reaches the shuffle window. CAMP SCMS release 1.2.2, Table 67. Status: The RA's request shuffle acts on a device's first certificate request (CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67). Every vehicle in a run is provisioned before it joins (Phase2::provision, ScmsRun::preload), and its weekly top-ups are the RA's pre-generation, which goes to the ACA at the period boundary without waiting in this shuffle (CAMP Primer p.6), so a same-seed run is identical. Kept as the RA's policy. security.scms.lifecycle.cert_shuffle_window_s number s 172800.0 [0, 604800]recommended 172,800 s (two days, CAMP release 1.2.2); 3,600 to 172,800 s. Like the batch size, it acts on a device's first request, which a run makes before the vehicle joins. advanced partial The longest a certificate request waits in the RA's shuffle, s (2 days, CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67 max_cert_request_age). The longest a certificate request may wait in the Registration Authority's mix before it is passed on, full batch or not. A longer wait hides each request among more others and delays a vehicle's certificates. Status: As cert_shuffle_threshold: the request shuffle's longest wait, on a device's first certificate request, which a run makes before the vehicle joins (the pre-run provisioning collapses the window); in-run top-ups do not wait in it. security.scms.lifecycle.first_batch_delay_s number s 60.0 [0, 86400]recommended 60 s (engine default); 1 to 3,600 s. advanced wired How long after the RA's acknowledgement a device first polls for its batch, s (60). How long after the Registration Authority acknowledges a request the vehicle first asks for its batch. security.scms.lifecycle.download_poll_interval_s number s 300.0 [0.1, 86400]recommended 300 s (the US profile); 1 to 3,600 s. basic wired download-minWait, s: the wait between polls of a batch that is not ready (300, SCMS Manager EE profile Table 3). download-minWait: how long a vehicle waits before asking again for a certificate batch that is not ready yet. Shorter gets certificates sooner once the mix releases them, for more requests to the Registration Authority (SCMS Manager EE profile, Table 3). security.scms.lifecycle.max_download_polls integer polls 100 [1, 10000]recommended 100 (the US profile); 1 to 1,000. advanced wired download-maxReqs: how many polls a device makes before it gives up on a batch (100, SCMS Manager EE profile Table 3). download-maxReqs: how many times a vehicle asks for a batch that is not ready before it gives up on it (SCMS Manager EE profile, Table 3). security.scms.lifecycle.download_request_tolerance_s number s 5.0 [0, 3600]recommended 5 s (CAMP); 1 to 60 s. advanced wired How far a download request's generation time may be from the RA's clock, s (5, CAMP 1.2.2 SCMS-1203 ra.client-signature-ttl-sec). How far a download request's time stamp may be from the Registration Authority's clock before the request is refused as stale or replayed (CAMP release 1.2.2, SCMS-1203). security.scms.lifecycle.enrolment_lifetime_s number s 189216000.0 [1, 315360000]recommended 189,216,000 s (six years, CAMP release 1.2.2); 600 s to 220,752,000 s (seven years, CAMP release 1.1). advanced wired The enrolment certificate's lifetime, s (six years, CAMP 1.2.2 Table 3). How long a vehicle's enrolment certificate, its long-term identity with the system, stays valid. It must be renewed before it ends or the vehicle can get no more pseudonyms. security.scms.lifecycle.reenrol_lead_s number s 47347200.0 [0, 315360000]recommended 47,347,200 s (548 days, SCMS Manager's 12 to 24 months); 60 s to 63,072,000 s. advanced wired How long before the enrolment certificate expires the device re-enrols, s (548 days, SCMS Manager re-enrolment standard: 12 to 24 months). How long before the enrolment certificate expires the vehicle asks for its successor; the successor starts when the current one ends, so an early request costs no validity. security.scms.lifecycle.reenrol_download_delay_s number s 300.0 [0, 86400]recommended 300 s (the profile's download-minWait); 1 to 3,600 s. advanced wired The wait between a re-enrolment request and its download, s (300, the profile's download-minWait). How long after a re-enrolment request the vehicle downloads its new enrolment certificate. security.scms.lifecycle.ee_retry_timeout_s number s 10.0 [0, 3600]recommended 10 s (CAMP SCMS-522); 0 turns the retry off. advanced wired How long a device waits for the RA's answer before it retries the request, s (10, CAMP SCMS-522); 0 turns the retry off. How long a device waits for the Registration Authority's answer before it sends the request again. CAMP SCMS-522. security.scms.lifecycle.ee_retry_max_per_hour integer retries per hour 10 [0, 1000]recommended 10 (CAMP SCMS-523); 0 turns the retry off. advanced wired The most retries of an unanswered RA request a device makes per hour (10, CAMP SCMS-523); 0 turns the retry off. The most times a device retries an unanswered request in one hour. CAMP SCMS-523. security.scms.lifecycle.clock_skew_s number s 0.0 [0, 3600]recommended 0 (GNSS-disciplined clocks); 0.04 to 2 s brackets the receivers' freshness checks. advanced wired How far ahead the skewed devices' clocks run, s (0). How far ahead the clocks of the skewed devices run. A receiver judges a message's age by its own clock, so a skewed device's messages look old or from the future. security.scms.lifecycle.clock_skew_share number fraction 1.0 [0, 1]recommended 1 (every device) when a skew is set; 0.01 to 0.1 for a few faulty units. advanced wired The share of devices whose clock is skewed by clock_skew_s (1: every device). The share of devices whose clock carries the skew, chosen by a fixed hash of each device. security.scms.lifecycle.root_rollover_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset (no rollover); inside the run to study a rollover. advanced wired When the home provider's root rolls over, s into the run (absent: never). When, in seconds into the run, the home provider's root CA rolls over to a new key and devices receive the new trust list. security.scms.lifecycle.root_removal_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset; after root_rollover_at_s. advanced wired When the old home root leaves the trust list, s into the run (absent: never). When the old home root leaves the trust list; certificates under it stop verifying. security.scms.lifecycle.peer_root_removal_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset; inside the run to study a provider's removal. advanced wired When the peer provider's root leaves the trust list, s into the run (absent: never). When the other provider's root leaves the trust list; devices that install the new list refuse everything that provider certified. security.scms.lifecycle.ctl_genesis_sequence string auto auto, 0, 1recommended By date (auto), as the production series stands. advanced wired The sequence number of the run's first trust list: auto (absent: by the run's date, as the production series: 1 from 2025-07-16, 0 before), 0 or 1. A bare number is read as its word. The sequence number of the run's first trust list. By date, it follows the production series: 1 when the run starts on or after 2025-07-16, 0 before. security.scms.lifecycle.eac_review string none none, elector-policyrecommended None (the times are the votes); Elector Policy to study the real review delay. advanced wired Whether the SCMS Manager Board's review comes before an EAC vote: none (absent: the *_at_s times are the votes) or elector-policy (they are requests; the vote follows 10 business days after an addition, 24 h after a removal, Elector Policy v1.0 §2.4.2, §2.4.4-2.4.5). Whether the board's review delay comes before an EAC vote. Under Elector Policy the rollover and removal times are requests: an addition is voted 10 business days later (weekends and federal holidays skipped), a removal 24 hours later. security.scms.lifecycle.elector_replacement_pq string off off, dualrecommended Classical keys; Dual to study a post-quantum elector migration. advanced wired How an elector replacement signs its transition CTL: off (absent: classical keys) or dual (the outgoing P-384 elector and the incoming ML-DSA-65 key both sign; Elector Technical Specification v1.1 §2.5). How a replaced elector's transition trust list is signed. Dual adds the outgoing elector's classical signature and the incoming elector's ML-DSA-65 signature, so a device that knows either key accepts it. The ML-DSA-65 half is modelled (its size and cost), not real. security.scms.lifecycle.elector_replacement_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset; inside the run to study a change of elector. advanced wired When the EAC replaces an elector, s into the run (gov G-11, Governance:: replace_elector; absent: never). The first approved elector leaves, a new one joins and a transition CTL is decided, signed as elector_replacement_pq says. When the Electors' Advisory Committee replaces an elector: the first approved elector leaves, a new one joins, and a transition trust list is decided and published to every device. security.scms.lifecycle.root_addition_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset; inside the run to study a provider joining. advanced wired When the EAC adds a new root to the trust list, s into the run (Governance:: add_root; absent: never): a new provider's root, which issues nothing in this run. When the Electors' Advisory Committee adds a new provider's root to the trust list. The new root issues nothing in this run; devices install the new trust list. security.scms.lifecycle.root_termination_notice_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Unset; inside the run, with a fast-forward to reach a year, to study a provider leaving. advanced wired When the peer provider gives notice of its termination, s into the run (gov L-8; absent: never): its root may not leave the trust list before 365 days have run ([SM-PROV] §3.5.6). Starts the 365-day notice before the provider's root may leave the trust list (SCMS Manager Provider Requirements §3.5.6): a removal of the peer provider's root voted before the notice has run is refused. security.scms.lifecycle.test_ballot_interval_days integer days 0 [0, 730]recommended Off for runs under a year; 365 (yearly, per Elector Policy) for longer runs. advanced wired How long an elector may go without signing before the Board holds a Test Ballot, days (gov G-10; absent or 0: no ballot is scheduled; 365 is Elector Policy v1.0 §1.1's "at least yearly"). How long electors may go without signing before a test ballot, in days: once one has, every elector signs the current trust list's contents to show its key still works. security.scms.tls string 1.3 1.3, 1.2recommended 1.3 (default); 1.2 to compare with older devices. advanced wired The TLS version of every device-to-RA session (session-scmsAuth, SCMS Manager EE profile §2.1.18: TLS 1.2 or 1.3): 1.3 (default) or 1.2, whose handshake costs one more round trip before the first request. The TLS version a vehicle uses for its secure session with the Registration Authority over a cellular link. TLS 1.2 needs one more round trip to set up each session than TLS 1.3, so certificate requests and downloads start later. The US profile admits both (SCMS Manager EE profile 2.1.18).

items.title: Providers
items.text:
The companies that run an SCMS. Each runs its own root, intermediate CA, RA, pseudonym CA, linkage authorities and MA. Names are neutral labels. Where each one's servers sit, and its share of vehicles, are assumptions, because no provider publishes them.

Which provider this row changes: one the preset names, or any name under Custom providers. items.title: Misbehaviour authority
items.text:
How reports of bad messages reach the MA and how the MA decides. Covers what a vehicle stores and uploads, how the RA shuffles reports, the MA's decision rule, and whether a person reviews each case. The US pilots used manual review.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description security.scms.deployment.providers[].ma_mode string manual-review, automaticrecommended manual-review (the CV pilots). advanced partial Its MA's decision mode: manual-review (the CV-pilot operator review, the default) or automatic. items.title: Revocation
items.text:
What happens after a device is judged misbehaving: how fast its provider publishes the revocation list (CRL), how often vehicles fetch it, and how a receiver treats a list that is overdue.

Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description security.scms.deployment.providers[].crl_publication string sla-1-business-day, cadence, on-decisionrecommended sla-1-business-day (US). advanced partial When its CRL Generator publishes after a decision: sla-1-business-day (the SCMS Manager SLA, the US default), cadence (the run's crl_cadence_s) or on-decision. When the provider publishes a revocation: within one business day (the SCMS Manager SLA), on a fixed cadence, or at once. Status: The SCMS deployment (protocol/scms/camp only; refused otherwise). deployment.preset: us-production-2025 (default: two providers with neutral labels on one CTL signed by the five shared electors, quorum 3; each with its own offline root and ICA and its own ECA, RA, ACA (provider-b two), LA1, LA2, MA, CRL Generator and PG; no LOP, no CRL broadcast), us-test-ctl-2025 (the 2025-07-17 test CTL: six roots, five approved), camp-reference (the single SCMS with LOP and a central MA) or custom. providers[]: components, region (an ASSUMPTION; no provider publishes one), fleet_share (roadside units are split by it), on_ctl (off: a provider nobody trusts), ma_mode (manual-review with ma_review_s, or automatic) and crl_publication (sla-1-business-day, cadence, on-decision) for that provider's run only. latency region (great-circle distance at fibre_fraction of c plus per_link_ms, ASSUMPTION) or flat; options.lop (off: the proxy hop is transparent), options.butterfly (original only) and options.identification_certs (on: emergency vehicles sign SRMs under OBU identification certificates and pseudonyms permit no SRM; SC-P9.3). Every node trusts every root on the CTL and holds every such provider's chain. Each provider runs its own backend: vehicles and roadside units are split by fleet_share, every RA serves every provider's signed CRL, MAs share reports, the Backend view shows each provider's entities as <provider>/<role>, and a home root rollover re-certifies every peer's copy of the home hierarchy. Partial: extra ACA instances take no load. security.scms.lifecycle.crl_cadence_s number s [0, 2592000]recommended Unset (the business-day rule); 0 to 86,400 s (a daily list, the USDOT 2013 working assumption). basic wired A fixed CRL publication cadence, s. Absent: each provider's own rule (the US presets publish within one business day of a decision, SCMS Manager Provider Requirements §3.4.9). 0 publishes on decision. A fixed schedule for publishing the revocation list. Left unset, each provider follows its own rule: the US providers publish within one business day of a revocation decision (SCMS Manager Provider Requirements 3.4.9). 0 publishes the moment a decision is made. security.scms.lifecycle.crl_fetch_interval_s number s 3600.0 [0.1, 1209600]recommended 3,600 s (one hour, an engine assumption inside CAMP's weekly bound); 60 to 86,400 s. basic wired How often a cellular vehicle polls for a new CRL, s (3,600). How often a vehicle with a cellular link asks for a newer revocation list. Shorter means revoked senders are refused sooner, for more cellular traffic; CAMP requires at least one fetch a week. security.scms.lifecycle.crl_broadcast_interval_s number s 5.0 [0.1, 3600]recommended 5 s (the longest USDOT RSU v4.1 store-and-repeat interval); 1 to 60 s. advanced wired How often a roadside unit with the crl role repeats the CRL over the air, s (5). How often a roadside unit carrying the revocation list repeats it over the air to vehicles in range; only roadside units with the crl role do this, and the US deployment does not use it. security.scms.lifecycle.crl_background_entries integer revocations 0 [0, 1000000]recommended 0 (only this run's revocations); 10,000 for a list a few years old. advanced wired Earlier revocations already on the home provider's CRL when the run starts (0): a standing list makes every CRL download and lookup that much larger. Revocations already on the home provider's revocation list when the run starts, so every CRL download and lookup carries a list of realistic length. security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked string none none, ica, pca, ra, eca, la1, la2, ma, crlgrecommended None; the pseudonym CA to study a compromised CA (every pseudonym it issued is refused once the list arrives). advanced wired The SCMS component whose certificate a provider revokes during the run: none (absent), ica, pca, ra, eca, la1, la2, ma or crlg. The certificate goes on the hash CRL of the (cracaId, crlSeries) it names (series 2 or 256, [SMP] Table 1), and receivers that install that list refuse what it signed. An SCMS component (a CA, the RA, a linkage authority, the MA or the CRL signer) whose certificate its provider revokes during the run. The certificate goes on the provider's component revocation list (series 2, or the root-signed series 256), and every device that installs that list refuses what the component signed. security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked_provider string provider-a, provider-b, provider-c, provider-d, provider-e, provider-f (or another value)recommended Unset (the home provider, the first of the deployment). advanced wired Whose component component_revoked revokes: a provider of the deployment by name (absent: the home provider, the first). Which provider revokes its component, by name. Applies when security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked is ica, pca, ra, eca, la1, la2, ma, crlg. security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked_at_s number s [0, ∞)recommended Inside the run, early enough for the next publication and download (one business day under the US rule). advanced wired When the component revocation is decided, s into the run (needed with component_revoked). When, in seconds into the run, the provider decides the component revocation; it is published by the provider's revocation-list rule and reaches devices with their next list download. Applies when security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked is ica, pca, ra, eca, la1, la2, ma, crlg. security.scms.crl_overdue_tolerance_s integer s 1209600 [0, 31536000]recommended 1,209,600 s (two weeks, CAMP's value); 0 to 2,419,200 s to study a delayed or blocked revocation list. The next list is due a week after each one (nextCrl), so the rule acts only in runs that span weeks of calendar time. advanced wired overdue_CRL_tolerance (CAMP SCMS 1.2.2 Table 67), seconds: how long past a CRL's nextCrl a device keeps trusting the certificates that CRL governs before it refuses every message they sign. Two weeks (1,209,600 s) unless set. How long after a revocation list said the next one would be out a vehicle keeps trusting the certificates that list covers. Past it, the vehicle refuses every message those certificates sign, so a vehicle cut off from new lists (by an attacker or a dead link) stops trusting its neighbours. CAMP SCMS release 1.2.2, Table 67, overdue_CRL_tolerance. security.scms.crl_overdue_scope string craca craca, allrecommended craca (default); all to study the strict reading. advanced wired Which messages an overdue pseudonym CRL makes a device refuse (v2xw_node::rxval::CrlOverdueScope): craca (default), the signers whose CRACA is the overdue list's; all, every message while any held series-1 list is past nextCrl + the tolerance. CAMP SCMS 1.2.2 Table 67 has the device "rejecting all of them", which the sources leave to either reading. What a vehicle refuses once a revocation list it holds is overdue past the tolerance. craca: only messages from certificates that list covers (the same certificate authority); all: every message, as CAMP SCMS release 1.2.2 Table 67 has the device "rejecting all of them" and warning the driver. The sources leave both readings open; they differ only after a root or CRACA changeover, when a vehicle holds an old authority's list that is no longer renewed.

items.text:
The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

security.envelope Value Label Meaning ieee1609.2 IEEE 1609.2 (US) The secured-message format of the US SCMS. etsi103097 ETSI TS 103 097 (Europe) The European profile of the same structure; required by the ETSI credential system. security.signature Value Label Meaning ecdsa-p256 ECDSA P-256 The signature every deployed V2X system uses today: 64-octet signatures. ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1 ECDSA brainpool P-256r1 The European alternative curve; same size, charged the P-256 time. ecdsa-p384 ECDSA P-384 A longer curve: 32 more octets per signature; costs the device's P-384 figure, or its P-256 one times the published P-384 / P-256 ratio. hybrid-falcon512-ecdsa-p256 Post-quantum hybrid: Falcon-512 + P-256 Adds 666 octets per signature and 1,563 per certificate; needs a fragmenter and a profile with a Falcon figure. hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256 Post-quantum hybrid: ML-DSA-44 + P-256 FIPS 204 Dilithium beside P-256: the largest messages; needs a fragmenter and a profile with an ML-DSA figure. hybrid-mldsa65-ecdsa-p256 Hybrid: ECDSA P-256 + ML-DSA-65 Raw concatenation. The ML-DSA-65 time on Cortex-A and Cohda profiles is derived from ML-DSA-44 by the pqm4 cycle ratio. ml-dsa-44 Post-quantum: ML-DSA-44 pk 1,312 B, sig 2,420 B [FIPS 204 Table 2]. ml-dsa-65 Post-quantum: ML-DSA-65 pk 1,952 B, sig 3,309 B [FIPS 204 Table 2]. Cortex-A and Cohda times are derived from ML-DSA-44 by the pqm4 cycle ratio. ml-dsa-87 Post-quantum: ML-DSA-87 pk 2,592 B, sig 4,627 B [FIPS 204 Table 2]. Times derived as for ML-DSA-65. falcon-512 Post-quantum: Falcon-512 (FN-DSA) pk 897 B, padded sig 666 B [PQClean falcon-padded-512]. Key generation is slow (tens of ms on a Cortex-A72), which matters with no butterfly. falcon-1024 Post-quantum: Falcon-1024 (FN-DSA) pk 1,793 B, padded sig 1,280 B [PQClean falcon-padded-1024]. Cortex-A and Cohda times derived from Falcon-512 by the Cortex-M7 cycle ratio. slh-dsa-sha2-128s Post-quantum: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s pk 32 B, sig 7,856 B [FIPS 205 Table 2]; hash-based, so its security rests on SHA-2 alone. Signing takes about a second on a vehicle-class core: an authority scheme, not a V2V one. slh-dsa-sha2-128f Post-quantum: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128f pk 32 B, sig 17,088 B [FIPS 205 Table 2]: eight frames' worth of signature. security.kem Value Label Meaning ecies-p256 ECIES P-256 (deployed today) 33 B ephemeral point + 16 B wrapped AES-128 key + 16 B tag. ml-kem-512 Post-quantum: ML-KEM-512 ciphertext 768 B, encapsulation key 800 B [FIPS 203 Table 3]. ml-kem-768 Post-quantum: ML-KEM-768 ciphertext 1,088 B, encapsulation key 1,184 B [FIPS 203 Table 3]. ml-kem-1024 Post-quantum: ML-KEM-1024 ciphertext 1,568 B [FIPS 203 Table 3]; times derived from ML-KEM-768 by the pqm4 cycle ratio. hybrid-ecies-p256-ml-kem-768 Hybrid: ECIES P-256 + ML-KEM-768 Both encapsulations travel; no 1609.2 structure for it exists yet (derived). security.threshold.protocol Value Label Meaning frost-p256 FROST threshold Schnorr (RFC 9591, P-256) RFC 9591 §5, §6.4 (FROST(P-256, SHA-256): Ne = 33, Ns = 32) cggmp21-ecdsa Threshold ECDSA (CGGMP21) — 1609.2-compatible output CGGMP21, ePrint 2021/060 (non-interactive variant: 3 presign rounds + 1 online) umbrella Umbrella authority: t-of-n umbrella credentials over k derived leaves placeholder binding (owner's specification pending, brief §8.3) shamir-feldman t-of-n secret release (Shamir + Feldman), for linkage seeds Shamir 1979 secret sharing with Feldman 1987 verifiable shares (dealer model) security.threshold.roles[] Value Label Meaning pca Pseudonym CA A committee of servers signs pseudonym certificates; no single server holds the key. crl CRL Generator A committee signs the revocation list. linkage Linkage authorities A t-of-n committee releases linkage seeds, so revoking a vehicle needs a quorum. security.threshold.umbrella_inner Value Label Meaning frost-p256 FROST threshold Schnorr (RFC 9591, P-256) RFC 9591 §5, §6.4 (FROST(P-256, SHA-256): Ne = 33, Ns = 32) cggmp21-ecdsa Threshold ECDSA (CGGMP21) — 1609.2-compatible output CGGMP21, ePrint 2021/060 (non-interactive variant: 3 presign rounds + 1 online) umbrella Umbrella authority: t-of-n umbrella credentials over k derived leaves Cannot sign its own umbrellas: choose a signing protocol for the umbrella certificates. shamir-feldman t-of-n secret release (Shamir + Feldman), for linkage seeds Shamir 1979 secret sharing with Feldman 1987 verifiable shares (dealer model) security.crypto_mode Value Label Meaning modeled Costed (fast) Signing and verification take the hardware's measured time; the outcome is modelled. real Computed (exact, slow) Real ECDSA over real bytes. Only P-256 is available in this mode. security.protocol.id Value Label Meaning protocol/etsi/ts102941 European CCMS (ETSI TS 102 941) Authorization tickets, an enrolment authority and passive revocation. protocol/scms/camp US SCMS (CAMP) The US credential system: butterfly keys, two linkage authorities, linkage-value CRL. security.scms.deployment.preset Value Label Meaning us-production-2025 US system (2025) Two providers on one trust list, neutral labels a and b: the deployed US SCMS. us-test-ctl-2025 US test trust list (17 Jul 2025) Six roots, five approved; provider-f's root ships but is not trusted. camp-reference CAMP reference design One SCMS with LOP, CRL Store, RSU broadcast and a central MA at flat latency: the pre-2025 topology, not the US system. custom Custom providers You list the providers below; each starts as a copy of a US provider. security.scms.deployment.options.butterfly Value Label Meaning original Original butterfly key expansion The device sends signing and encryption caterpillar keys, the RA expands them into cocoon keys and the ACA encrypts each certificate to the device: the US profile. unified Unified butterfly Not deployed in the US: the US profile uses the original expansion only and the unified response key is unconfirmed, so this build refuses it. cubk Compact unified butterfly Not deployed in the US: the US profile uses the original expansion only and the compact unified response key is unconfirmed, so this build refuses it. security.scms.deployment.latency Value Label Meaning region Distance-based Great-circle distance between server sites at fibre speed, plus a fixed overhead per link (an assumption). flat Fixed latency Every backend link takes the backend network's fixed latency, wherever the servers are. security.scms.chain_file Value Label Meaning all-providers Every provider's CA certificates Each device holds the global chain file with every trusted provider's CAs, so it verifies any provider's vehicles at once. home-provider Only my provider's A device learns other providers' ICA and ACA over the air by P2PCD before it can verify their vehicles (an assumption). security.scms.crl_poll Value Label Meaning conditional Revocation list, if changed (one exchange) The vehicle asks the RA for its composite revocation list with If-Modified-Since: the list when it changed, a short 412 when not. info-status Status file first, then what changed The vehicle first fetches the RA's signed status of its lists (IEEE 1609.2.1 6.3.5.14), then downloads the revocation list only if it holds an older one. security.verification_policy Value Label Meaning verify-all Verify every message Every received message is verified, whatever it costs the security module. on-demand Verify on demand Only messages an application is about to act on are verified. Misbehaviour detection runs only on verified messages, so detection goes nearly blind (897 reports fell to 79 in testing). prioritized Verify nearest first When the module cannot keep up, the closest and most relevant senders are verified first. security.pseudonym_change.strategy Value Label Meaning by-region By region (US: SAE J2945/1) The region's own rule: SAE J2945/1 CERTCHG under the US IEEE 1609.2 envelope, every 5 minutes under ETSI. A scenario that sets period_s gets the time rule. time Every few minutes (time only) Change certificate after period_s of use (300 s unless set), however close the vehicle is to the last change point. distance Every few kilometres (NYC pilot) Change once the vehicle is distance_m in a straight line from the last change point; the NYC Connected Vehicle Pilot used 2 km. j2945-1 SAE J2945/1 (5 min unless within 2,100 m of the last change; not during a critical event) Change once 5 minutes have passed and the vehicle is at least 2,100 m in a straight line from the last change point (vCertChangeDistance), and never while its BSM carries a critical event flag (CERTCHG-001, -002); an expiring certificate still changes. nyc-pilot NYC CV pilot (2 km or 5 min) Change at 2 km in a straight line from the last change point or after 5 minutes, whichever comes first. c2c-cc European car makers' rule (C2C-CC) After 0.8-1.5 km, then 0.8 km plus 2-6 minutes, then every 10-35 km. mix-zone In mix zones at junctions Change inside a zone around each signalised junction, where many vehicles mingle. silent Never (keep one identity) No change: the baseline a tracker finds easiest. security.scms.lifecycle.ctl_genesis_sequence Value Label Meaning auto By date, as the production series Sequence 1 when the run starts on or after 2025-07-16 (the live production trust list), 0 before. 0 0 The first production trust list's number (2019-12-12), whatever the run's date. 1 1 The live production trust list's number (effective 2025-07-16), whatever the run's date. security.scms.lifecycle.eac_review Value Label Meaning none The times given are the votes The rollover and removal times are when the electors vote. elector-policy The times given are requests; the board reviews per Elector Policy Each time is a request; the vote follows 10 business days later for an addition and 24 hours later for a removal. security.scms.lifecycle.elector_replacement_pq Value Label Meaning off Classical keys A replaced elector's transition trust list is signed by the remaining P-384 electors only. dual Dual signatures (classical + ML-DSA-65) The outgoing elector's P-384 key and the incoming elector's ML-DSA-65 key both sign the transition trust list. security.scms.tls Value Label Meaning 1.3 TLS 1.3 One round trip to set up the session before the first request (the default; items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description seed string or integer 0x0000000000005eed recommended Any number. Keep it fixed while you compare settings. basic wired The master seed. Every sub-stream is derived from it (ADR 0004 §3); a scenario never sets a sub-stream seed, which is why there is no field for one. The random seed: the same settings and seed always give exactly the same run; change it to see another, equally likely, day.
