items.text:
The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

threats.attackers[].id Value Label Meaning threat/attacker/legacy/ConstPos Fake position: frozen Keeps claiming the first position it sent while it drives on. threat/attacker/legacy/ConstPosOffset Fake position: shifted Claims a position a constant distance from where it is. threat/attacker/legacy/RandomPos Fake position: random Claims a random position near itself, redrawn every message. threat/attacker/legacy/Teleport Fake position: teleporting Jumps its claimed position every fourth second. threat/attacker/legacy/SineWavePos Fake position: weaving Swings its claimed position from side to side across its lane. threat/attacker/legacy/ConstSpeedOffset Fake speed: shifted Adds a constant offset to the speed it claims. threat/attacker/legacy/RandomSpeed Fake speed: random Claims a random speed. threat/attacker/legacy/StopAndGo Fake speed: stop-and-go Alternates its claimed speed between stopped and fast. threat/attacker/legacy/ReversedHeading Fake heading: reversed Claims to be driving the opposite way. threat/attacker/legacy/HeadingOffset Fake heading: shifted Adds a constant offset to the heading it claims. threat/attacker/legacy/DataReplay Replay attack Re-sends its own earlier messages with their old timestamps. threat/attacker/legacy/SlowDrift Fake position: slow drift A position error that grows slowly from nothing, hard to notice. threat/attacker/legacy/AlongRoadOffset Fake position: along the road Shifts its claimed position along the road, so it stays on the map. threat/attacker/legacy/Sybil Ghost vehicles (Sybil) Sends extra signed messages for ghost vehicles that do not exist, each under its own valid pseudonym. threat/attacker/legacy/DelayedMessages Delayed messages Stamps its messages with a stale generation time. threat/attacker/legacy/InvalidSignature Invalid signature Signs with a key that does not match its certificate. threat/attacker/legacy/ExpiredCert Expired certificate Presents a certificate past its validity. threat/attacker/legacy/NotYetValid Certificate not yet valid Presents a certificate whose validity has not begun. threat/attacker/legacy/OutOfOrder Out-of-order timestamps Stamps messages with times that go backwards. threat/attacker/legacy/Disruptive Everything inconsistent Falsifies position, speed and heading at once, inconsistently. threat/attacker/legacy/PosSpeedInconsistent Moving while claiming to stop Its position advances while it claims to be almost stopped. threat/attacker/legacy/PosHeadingInconsistent Sideways while claiming straight Its position swings sideways while it claims a straight heading. threat/attacker/legacy/EventualStop Fake stop Drives honestly, then freezes its claimed position while claiming to creep. threat/attacker/legacy/DoS Message flood (DoS) Not runnable yet: a flood needs extra transmissions per interval. threat/attacker/legacy/DoSRandom Random flood (DoS) Not runnable yet: a flood needs extra transmissions per interval. threat/attacker/legacy/VruImpersonation Posing as a pedestrian Not runnable yet: a BSM does not carry a station type. threat/attacker/legacy/VruPositionSpoof Fake pedestrian Not runnable yet: a BSM does not carry a station type. threat/attacker/legacy/FakeHazard Fake hazard warning Not runnable yet: the host does not send an attacker's event messages. threat/attacker/legacy/SelectiveDrop Drops relayed messages Not runnable yet: vehicles here relay nothing. threats.jammers[].id Value Label Meaning attacker/jammer/constant Constant A constant wideband jammer: continuous OFDM-like noise in the channel, entering every receiver's noise term for as long as it is on. attacker/jammer/pulsed Pulsed A duty-cycle jammer: wideband noise for a fraction of a fixed period, with a per-jammer phase drawn from the Attack stream. attacker/jammer/reactive Reactive A reactive jammer: wideband noise only while energy above a trigger threshold is sensed, which is the profile whose losses are uncorrelated with SINR dips. threats.compromised_rsu_attack.id Value Label Meaning threat/attacker/compromised-rsu Compromised roadside unit A trusted unit under an attacker's control poisons or drops what it relays. threats.eavesdropper.id Value Label Meaning threat/observer/passive-privacy Roadside eavesdropper Passive sniffers at a share of the signalised junctions try to link each car's pseudonyms.

items.title: time
items.text:
Group: Run. What this scenario is, who wrote it, and what it is based on.

11 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see how to read these tables. Paths use [] for a list element and * for a map key.

Status Meaning wired partial refused

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description time.t0 string 2027-03-04T07:00:00Z advanced wired The civil instant SimTime zero corresponds to, RFC 3339. It is what the 1609.2 generationTime is stamped from, and it is scenario data, not a wall-clock read. time.duration_s number s 60.0 (0, ∞)recommended 1 to 15 minutes to watch; 1 hour or more as a batch run. basic wired How long the run lasts, simulated seconds. How much simulated time the run covers. A vehicle changes its pseudonym about every 5 minutes (SAE J2945/1), so privacy and credential studies need longer runs than radio studies. time.mobility_step_ms integer ms 100 [10, 100] advanced wired The mobility period, milliseconds. ADR 0004 decision 2 allows 10–100. time.des_resolution string 1us 1ns, 1us, 1ms advanced refused The resolution models are promised, e.g. 1us. The kernel is always nanoseconds; this is the guarantee a model may rely on. Status: The resolution the run promises its models. The kernel keeps nanoseconds whatever this says; the loader refuses a resolution the run cannot keep — '1ms' with a PHY or MAC that times frames in microseconds, or a time-dilation window off the promised grid. time.metric_period_s number s [0.1, 3600] advanced wired How often every metric provider flushes a window into a metric.sample, simulated seconds; 1 s when left out. A run of days at a minute's period writes a sixtieth of the samples — the long-run option that keeps metrics.json and the page's series a usable size — and each sample then summarises a minute instead of a second. Left out of the serialised scenario when not set, so no existing scenario's hash moves. time.warmup_s number s [0, ∞)recommended 10 to 20 % of the run; 30 to 60 s on a city extract. basic wired The warm-up period, simulated seconds: how long the run fills with traffic before it is measured. No metric sample is recorded for a window that ends inside it, so the charts and the metric summaries describe the steady state rather than an empty map filling up (the transient-deletion practice of Law, Simulation Modeling and Analysis, 5th ed., §9.5.1). The run report's whole-run counters still include it. Unset is none. How long the run fills with traffic before it is measured: charts and metric summaries skip it, so an empty map filling up does not drag the averages down. time.calendar string real, compressed advanced wired Which calendar the credential system runs on. real, the default, is the deployment's: one-week i-periods counted from the US epoch, 2015-01-06 04:00 Eastern ([SMP] §2.1.17 Table 2), so a run starting 2026-10-16 provisions i = 614. compressed is the only way to state a shorter security.protocol.params.i_period_s: its i-period numbers, validity windows and every calendar-driven wait are not the deployment's, and the manifest and the run report say so. Left out of the serialised scenario when real, so no existing scenario's hash moves.

items.title: traffic
items.text:
Group: Traffic. What moves and what transmits: the fleet, its size, roadside units and the backend.

70 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see how to read these tables. Paths use [] for a list element and * for a map key.

Status Meaning wired partial

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description traffic.right_turn_on_red boolean recommended Leave empty to follow the city's rule. basic wired Whether a right turn may be made on a steady red after a full stop. Absent follows the jurisdiction's rule (New York City prohibits it unless signed; most of the US permits it). Whether drivers may turn right on a red light after stopping. Legal in most of the US, banned in New York City. traffic.dynamic_rerouting boolean advanced wired Whether drivers change route when the travel times they see change or a street closes. On by default. traffic.reroute_period_s number s [0, 3600]recommended 0 (off) for a baseline; 60 to 300 to model navigation-app drivers. basic wired Congestion-aware rerouting: every vehicle re-plans its route this often, seconds, on the speeds the lanes have shown over the last three minutes, as SUMO's rerouting device does. 0 (the default) routes on free-flow times and re-plans only for a closure. Needs dynamic_rerouting. How often drivers check for a faster way round the traffic, as a navigation app does. Off, every driver keeps the route it chose on free-flowing roads; on, jams push traffic onto parallel streets. traffic.lane_changes boolean advanced wired Whether drivers change lane to overtake or to reach the lane their next turn needs (MOBIL). On by default; off keeps every vehicle in the lane it started in. traffic.strategic_lane_choice boolean advanced wired Whether a driver picks the lane their route needs ahead of a turn and changes into it, rather than only routing from the lane they happen to be in. On by default; needs lane_changes. traffic.keep_junctions_clear boolean advanced wired Whether a driver keeps out of a junction until there is room beyond it and yields to vehicles already inside it ("don't block the box"). On by default. traffic.gridlock_timeout_s number s [0, 3600]recommended 300 (SUMO's default); 0 to see raw gridlock. basic wired Gridlock resolution: a vehicle that has stood still this long, seconds, is moved on along its route to the next lane with room and counted, as SUMO's time-to-teleport option does (default 300 s). 0 turns it off. When a vehicle has been stuck this long in a jam the network cannot clear, it is moved on along its route and counted, as SUMO does. A run that counts many has unrealistic demand or a network fault. traffic.critical_gap_factor number [0.5, 2]recommended 1 (the Highway Capacity Manual's gaps); 0.8 to 1.2. basic wired A multiplier on the critical gaps and follow-up times drivers accept at junctions without signals (HCM 6th ed. ch. 20 two-way-stop table: 4.1 s for a major-road left turn to 7.1-7.5 s for a minor-road left). Below 1 drivers take shorter gaps, above 1 they wait for longer ones. Unset is 1, the table. How big a gap in the main-road traffic drivers wait for before pulling out at a junction without lights, or turning right on red where that is allowed: below 1 they squeeze in, above 1 they wait longer. traffic.permitted_left_gap_s number s [2.5, 8]recommended 4.5 s (HCM); 4 to 5.5 s. advanced wired The critical headway a permitted left turn on a green accepts in the oncoming traffic, seconds. Unset is 4.5 s (HCM 6th ed. ch. 31). The gap in oncoming traffic a driver waits for before turning left across it on a green light. traffic.turn_lateral_accel_mps2 number m/s² [0, 10]recommended 5.5 m/s² (SUMO); 3 to 6 m/s². advanced wired The average sideways acceleration a turn through a junction is driven at, m/s²: a corner of radius R is taken at sqrt(a·R) at most. Unset is 5.5 m/s² (SUMO netconvert --junctions.limit-turn-speed). How fast drivers take corners through a junction: higher values let them turn faster. traffic.turn_curve_window_m number m [0, 30]recommended 0 m (SUMO, average); 6 m to slow for the apex. advanced wired The arc length, m, over which a junction connector's radius is judged for its turn speed. Unset (or 0) averages the radius over the whole connector, as SUMO netconvert does; a window (6 m suggested) takes the tightest arc of that length, so drivers slow for the apex of a corner, not only for its average. Whether drivers slow for the sharpest part of a corner (a few metres) or only for its average curve, which is what SUMO does. traffic.lc_strategic number [0, 10]recommended Unset (today's MOBIL); 1 (SUMO default); 0.5 to 4. advanced wired SUMO LC2013's eagerness for the lane changes a route needs: it scales how far ahead of the turn the change becomes due (10 s at the look-ahead speed, twice that to the left). Setting any lc_* field drives discretionary lane changes by LC2013's motivations instead of MOBIL; unset lc_* fields take SUMO's default 1. How early drivers move into the lane their next turn needs: higher values change lane further before the junction. traffic.lc_cooperative number [0, 1]recommended Unset (today's MOBIL); 1 (SUMO default); 0 to 1. advanced wired LC2013's willingness to change lane to let a neighbour that must merge in (0 never, 1 always unless it costs speed). See lc_strategic. How willing drivers are to move over to let in a car that must merge into their lane. traffic.lc_speed_gain number [0, 10]recommended Unset (today's MOBIL); 1 (SUMO default); 0.5 to 2. advanced wired LC2013's eagerness to change lane for speed: the speed-gain threshold is 0.2 / lc_speed_gain (0 turns speed-gain changes off). See lc_strategic. How readily drivers change lane to get past slower traffic; setting any of the lane-change eagerness settings switches to SUMO's LC2013 lane-changing. traffic.lc_keep_right number [0, 10]recommended Unset (today's MOBIL); 1 (SUMO default); 0 to 2. advanced wired LC2013's eagerness to move back right when the right lane is free (0 off). See lc_strategic. How readily drivers move back into the right lane when it is free, as the keep-right rule asks. traffic.heavy_vehicle_gap_terms boolean recommended Off (today); on for HCM heavy-vehicle gaps (+1 s, +2 s on wide roads). advanced wired Whether trucks, buses and coaches wait for longer gaps than cars when yielding: the HCM 6th ed. heavy-vehicle terms (Exhibit 20-11: +1.0 s critical gap on a major road of under four lanes, +2.0 s on four or more; +0.9 / 1.0 s follow-up), at unsignalised junctions and on a permitted left. Unset is off. Whether trucks and buses, which accelerate slowly, wait for longer gaps in traffic than cars before pulling out or turning left across it. traffic.critical_gap_cv number [0, 0.5]recommended 0 (today); 0.18 for realistic drivers (field spreads 0.15 to 0.2). advanced wired The spread of drivers' critical gaps: each driver's is lognormal around the HCM value with this coefficient of variation (0.15-0.2 in field studies, SUMO P1; 0.18 is the realistic preset), at unsignalised junctions, on a permitted left and on a right turn on red. Unset is 0: every driver the HCM value. How much drivers differ in the gap they wait for before pulling out or turning across traffic: 0 gives everyone the same gap. traffic.time_to_impatience_s number s [0, 3600]recommended 0 (off, today); 180 s (SUMO) for realistic waiting. advanced wired Seconds of standing after which a yielding driver's impatience is full and its critical gap has fallen to impatience_gap_floor of its own (SUMO --time-to-impatience, 180 s). Unset is 0: no impatience. How long a driver waiting to pull out or turn across traffic stands before they accept the shortest gap they ever will; the longer they wait, the smaller the gap they take. traffic.impatience_gap_floor number [0.3, 1]recommended 0.7; 0.5 to 0.9. advanced wired The critical gap at full impatience as a share of the driver's own. Unset is 0.7. How short a gap a driver who has waited a long time accepts, as a share of the gap they wanted at first. traffic.impatience_foe_braking boolean recommended Off; on for SUMO-like assertive drivers. advanced wired Whether an impatient driver judges an approaching foe as if it would brake at impatience times 4.5 m/s² (SUMO's blend toward the foe's braking arrival). Unset is off. Whether an impatient driver pulls out counting on oncoming cars to brake for them. traffic.permissive_sneakers integer vehicles per lane per cycle [0, 4]recommended 0 (today); 2 (HCM) for realistic left turns. advanced wired How many permitted left turners per lane may complete the turn in the amber that ends a permissive green, the HCM's "sneakers" (2 per cycle). Each must cross the stop line before the red. Unset is 0: none. How many drivers waiting to turn left on a green may finish the turn as the light turns yellow, when oncoming traffic stops; without them a left turn into steady oncoming traffic can wait for minutes. traffic.standing_leader_stop boolean recommended Off (today); on for smooth stops behind queues (the realistic benchmark sets it). advanced wired Whether a driver closing on a standing vehicle brakes at no less than the constant deceleration that stops it at its standstill gap, as at a stop line, instead of being stopped in one step when the car-following model's braking (which scales with its acceleration, low for vans and trucks) arrives too late. Unset is off. Whether drivers coming up behind a stopped car brake smoothly to stop at their usual gap, as they do at a stop line, rather than braking late and stopping abruptly (vans and trucks, whose following model brakes gently, were stopped in one step). traffic.depart_speed_max boolean recommended Off (today, SUMO's default); on for freeways and other roads entered at speed (SUMO departSpeed=max). advanced wired Whether a trip enters the road already moving, at the highest safe speed there (SUMO's departSpeed="max") instead of at rest (SUMO's default, departSpeed="0"): a freeway entry merges at speed. Unset is off. Whether cars enter the road already moving, at the fastest speed that is safe there, as traffic joining a freeway does, rather than appearing parked in the lane and pulling away from rest. traffic.lane_bend_speed boolean recommended Off (today); on with turn_curve_window_m 6 for kinked city streets (the realistic benchmark sets it). advanced wired Whether the bends of a through lane's polyline are driven no faster than the turn-speed rule allows (turn_lateral_accel_mps2 over the tightest turn_curve_window_m, 6 m when unset), as a junction connector is. Unset is off. Whether drivers slow for sharp bends in a street's mapped centreline as they do for corners at junctions; without it a car follows a kink in the map at full speed. traffic.depart_at_speed boolean recommended Off (today); on for realistic map edges (no false halts or stopped-vehicle warnings there). basic wired Whether a vehicle entering the map from outside it (its origin a lane no road of the map feeds, at the map's edge) is put on at the start of that lane at its desired speed, capped by the speed that is safe behind the vehicle ahead and that can still stop at the lane's end, as SUMO's departSpeed="desired" with departPos="base" does. Origins inside the network stay at rest. Unset is off. Whether cars entering the map from outside it are already moving, as real traffic crossing the map's edge is, instead of starting from rest at the edge; cars starting inside the map still start from rest. traffic.reroute_share number [0, 1]recommended 1 (every driver, today); about 0.3-0.6 for today's navigation-app use in a US city. basic wired The share of drivers who re-route on information, 0-1, drawn once per driver (SUMO device.rerouting.probability). The rest keep the route they chose and detour only round a closure they can see. Unset is 1: every driver. The share of drivers who change route on information (a navigation app or a received V2X warning); the rest keep the route they chose and only detour round a closure they can see. traffic.reroute_source json (v2xw_mobility::routing::dynamic::RerouteSource) recommended navigation (today); v2x to measure what V2X hazard warnings are worth to routing. basic wired Where those drivers learn that the road has changed: navigation (a navigation app: network-wide, on speeds smoothed over three minutes, and every closure) or v2x (only a DENM or TIM their own unit received and verified, placing a blocking event on their route: local and belief-only). Unset is navigation. Where re-routing drivers learn that the road has changed: a navigation app, which sees the whole network a few minutes late, or only the V2X hazard warnings their own car received, which are local and immediate.

items.title: signals
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description traffic.signals.control string fixed-time, actuated, nemarecommended fixed-time for a repeatable baseline; actuated to study signal timing or SPaT that changes; nema for US controller behaviour (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed.). basic wired Fixed-time, single-ring vehicle-actuated, or the NEMA dual ring. How the traffic lights decide when to change: on a fixed clock, or actuated by detectors in the road that hold a green while cars keep coming and end it early when the street goes quiet, as most US suburban and many city signals do. nema runs the US eight-phase dual-ring controller: both directions' throughs and lefts time side by side, with pedestrian push buttons, left-turn arrows, coordination and emergency-vehicle priority. traffic.signals.min_green_s number s [2, 60]recommended 7 s; 5 to 15 s (FHWA Signal Timing Manual). advanced wired The shortest an actuated green runs, seconds. Under actuated control, the shortest a green runs once it starts, even if no more cars arrive, so the queue stored at the stop line can start up and clear. traffic.signals.max_green_s number s [5, 180]recommended 45 s; 30 to 60 s (FHWA Signal Timing Manual). advanced wired The longest an actuated green runs while another approach waits, seconds. Under actuated control, the longest a green may be held by arriving cars while another approach waits. traffic.signals.passage_s number s [0.2, 10] advanced wired The gap between detections that ends an actuated green, seconds (the passage time or unit extension). traffic.signals.detector_m number m [1, 150]recommended 12.2 m (40 ft stop-line loop, FHWA); 6 to 30 m. advanced wired How far back from the stop line the detector sees, metres. Under actuated control, how far back from the stop line the detector loop reaches; cars inside it hold the green. traffic.signals.detector_placement string stop-line, sumorecommended stop-line (FHWA) for US practice; sumo to compare with a SUMO actuated run. advanced wired Where the extension detectors are: a stop-line presence loop (the default) or SUMO's upstream induction loop at 2 s of travel from the stop line. Under actuated control, where the vehicle detectors sit: a loop at the stop line, or SUMO's single loop per lane about two seconds of travel upstream, which ends the green sooner once a platoon has passed. traffic.signals.short_link_clearance_m number m [10, 200]recommended Off for the plans as imported; 30 to 90 m (4 to 12 queued cars at the HCM's 7.62 m each). advanced wired Short-link clearance: a driving lane shorter than this between two signalised junctions gets a downstream green that starts just before the upstream green that fills it (crate::actuated::clear_short_links), metres. Absent is off. Where two traffic lights are this close, the downstream light turns green for the short street between them just before the upstream one does, so cars are not held at a green light by a full block ahead (closely spaced signals, FHWA Signal Timing Manual ch. 6). traffic.signals.green_wave_speed_mps number m/s [1, 40] advanced wired A green wave: every signal's offset set so that a vehicle at this speed meets green after green travelling in green_wave_heading_deg. Absent keeps the plans' own offsets. traffic.signals.green_wave_heading_deg number ° [0, 360] advanced wired The direction the green wave runs, degrees clockwise from north (90 is eastbound). traffic.signals.nema.ring1[] integer NEMA phase advanced partial Ring1[] Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.ring2[] integer NEMA phase advanced partial Ring2[] Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.barrier_phases[] integer NEMA phase advanced partial Barrier phases[] Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.barrier2_phases[] integer NEMA phase advanced partial Barrier2 phases[] Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.lefts string lead-lead, lag-lag, lead-lagrecommended lead-lead, the most common US sequence (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed. §5.1.3.6). advanced partial Lead-lead, lag-lag or lead-lag lefts. Whether the left-turn arrows come before or after the opposing through traffic's green. Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.left_turn_mode string protected-permissive, protected, permissive advanced partial Protected-permissive, protected-only or permissive-only lefts. Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.permissive_display string fya, green-ball advanced wired The permissive left's face: flashing yellow arrow or circular green. traffic.signals.nema.left_min_green_s number s [2, 60]recommended 4 s; 2 to 5 s (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed., Exhibit 6-4). advanced partial A left-turn phase's minimum green, seconds (through phases use traffic.signals.min_green_s). Under the NEMA dual-ring controller, the shortest a protected left-turn arrow runs once it starts. Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.left_max_green_s number s [5, 180]recommended 25 s; 15 to 30 s (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed., Exhibit 6-9). advanced partial A left-turn phase's maximum green, seconds (through phases use traffic.signals.max_green_s). Under the NEMA dual-ring controller, the longest a protected left-turn arrow may be held by arriving cars while another phase waits. Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.left_passage_s number s [0.2, 10] advanced partial A left-turn phase's passage time, seconds (through phases use traffic.signals.passage_s). Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.yellow_s number s [3, 6] advanced partial Every phase's yellow change interval, seconds. Absent takes each plan's own amber. Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.red_clear_s number s [0, 6] advanced partial Every phase's red clearance, seconds. Absent takes each plan's own all-red. Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.walk_s number s [4, 30] advanced partial The pedestrian walk interval, seconds. Absent is world.signals.pedestrian_walk_s, else 7 s (MUTCD 2009 §4E.06 ¶11). A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.soft_recall[] integer NEMA phase advanced partial Soft recall[] Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.max_recall[] integer NEMA phase advanced partial Max recall[] Status: The NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller (control: nema): rings, barriers, lead/lag, the three left-turn modes and both permissive faces, left-turn timing, recalls, yellow, red, pedestrian calls, recall and timing, and coordination run. A NEMA junction does not serve priority requests yet. traffic.signals.nema.ped_recall[] integer NEMA phase advanced wired Ped recall[] traffic.signals.nema.coordinate_phases[] integer NEMA phase advanced wired Coordinate phases[] traffic.signals.nema.coordination boolean advanced wired Coordinated operation: a common cycle, an offset and force-offs [SUMO coordinate-mode, default false]. traffic.signals.nema.force_off string floating, fixed advanced wired Floating or fixed force-offs [SUMO fixForceOff. traffic.signals.nema.controller_type string ts2, type170 advanced wired TS 2 or Type 170: where the coordination offset is referenced [SUMO controllerType.

items.title: kerbside
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description traffic.kerbside.enabled boolean recommended On for city realism; off for a clean baseline. basic wired Whether vehicles stop at the kerb at all. Unset is on. Whether buses stop at stops, taxis pick up and delivery vans double-park, briefly blocking a lane as they do in a real city. traffic.kerbside.bus_stop_spacing_m number m [100, 2000]recommended 200 to 400 m for local buses. advanced wired The distance from one bus stop to the next along a bus's route, metres. Unset is 260 m. How far apart bus stops are along a bus route. traffic.kerbside.bus_dwell_mean_s number s [5, 300]recommended 15 to 60 s (TCQSM). advanced wired The mean time a bus stands at a stop, seconds. Unset is 60 s. How long a bus stands at each stop on average. traffic.kerbside.taxi_share number [0, 1]recommended 0 outside a downtown; 0.2 to 0.3 in Midtown Manhattan. advanced wired The share of passenger cars that are taxis or for-hire cars and stop at the kerb once on their trip. Unset is the jurisdiction's (0, or 0.3 in Midtown Manhattan). The share of cars that are taxis or ride-hail cars making one kerbside stop. traffic.kerbside.taxi_dwell_median_s number s [5, 600]recommended 20 to 60 s. advanced wired The median time a taxi stands at the kerb, seconds. Unset is 30 s. How long a taxi stands at the kerb for a pick-up or drop-off. traffic.kerbside.delivery_stop_share number [0, 1]recommended 0.3 to 0.6. advanced wired The share of delivery vans and trucks that make one delivery stop on their trip. Unset is 0.6. The share of vans and trucks that stop once on their trip to deliver. traffic.kerbside.delivery_dwell_median_s number s [30, 3600]recommended 5 to 15 minutes. advanced wired The median time a delivery stop lasts, seconds. Unset is 600 s. How long a delivery stop lasts.

items.title: vehicle_dynamics
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description traffic.vehicle_dynamics.grade boolean recommended Off (today); on for hilly maps (SUMO's KraussPS slope term). advanced wired The slope term: a vehicle's acceleration less g times the sine of the road's grade, as SUMO's KraussPS has it. Unset is off. Whether hills slow vehicles down: on a climb a driver gets less acceleration from the same pedal, and on a descent the car holds its speed. Needs a map with terrain heights; flat maps are unchanged. traffic.vehicle_dynamics.power_limit boolean recommended Off (today); on with grade for hilly maps and freight corridors. advanced wired The power term: no more acceleration than the engine's power gives after rolling and air resistance, for the classes with a sourced road-load row (passenger car, tractor-trailer, rigid truck, bus, coach and van). Unset is off. Whether an engine's power limits how fast a vehicle can speed up, so a loaded tractor-trailer crawls up a long climb at about 46 km/h on a 5% grade while a car keeps the limit. Applies to cars, tractor-trailers, rigid trucks, buses, coaches and vans, from cited figures (FTA bus tests, EPA road loads, NCHRP 505); motorcycles have none yet.

items.title: emergency_yield
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description traffic.emergency_yield.enabled boolean recommended Off (today); on for emergency-vehicle studies, where travel time through traffic is the point. advanced wired Whether drivers yield at all. Unset is off. Whether drivers get out of the way of an ambulance, fire engine or police car running its lights and siren: in the US they move to the right-hand lane and stop, clear of the junction, until it has passed (NY VTL 1144(a)). Off, an emergency vehicle has to queue like everyone else. traffic.emergency_yield.reaction_distance_m number m [1, 500]recommended 25 m (SUMO's bluelight default); more on a quiet street where a siren carries, less in heavy traffic. advanced wired How far behind a driver an emergency vehicle with its siren on is noticed, metres (gap from its front bumper to the driver's rear). Unset is 25 m, SUMO's bluelight device reactiondist default. How far behind a driver an emergency vehicle is when they notice it and start to pull over. traffic.emergency_yield.red_pass_speed_mps number m/s [0, 10]recommended 0 (a full stop, the fire-service rule); 2 to 4 m/s for services that let their drivers roll through slowly. advanced wired The speed an emergency vehicle slows to at a red before it passes on, once the junction is clear, m/s (UVC §11-106(b)2). Unset is 0: a full stop first, as fire-service practice has it. How slowly an ambulance or fire engine takes a red light it is allowed to pass: 0 means it stops first, then goes once the junction is clear.

items.title: Choices
items.text:
The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

traffic.signals.control Value Label Meaning fixed-time Fixed time Every signal runs its plan's clock: each phase lasts its stated time, whatever the traffic. actuated Actuated (single ring) Detectors hold a green while cars keep arriving and end it early when the approach goes quiet, one phase at a time. nema NEMA dual ring (eight phases) Two rings of four phases time concurrently and meet at barriers, as US controllers do (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed.), with protected, permissive or protected-then-permissive lefts. Junctions that do not map keep the single ring. traffic.signals.detector_placement Value Label Meaning stop-line Stop line A presence loop covering the last detector_m of every approach lane (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2e, ch. sumo Sumo SUMO's actuated default (MSActuatedTrafficLightLogic): one induction loop per approach lane, the lane's speed limit times detector-gap = 2 s upstream of the stop line (at least 1 m, at most the… traffic.signals.nema.lefts Value Label Meaning lead-lead Lead-lead Both left turns go before their opposing throughs: the most common US sequence (FHWA STM 2nd ed. §5.1.3.6). lag-lag Lag-lag Both left turns go after their opposing throughs. lead-lag Lead-lag One left leads and the opposing left lags, which suits a green wave in both directions. traffic.signals.nema.left_turn_mode Value Label Meaning protected-permissive Protected, then permissive A green arrow first, then lefts may turn through gaps in the oncoming traffic. protected Protected only Lefts turn only on their own green arrow (even from a lane shared with the through, which they then block). permissive Permissive only No left-turn phase: lefts turn through gaps in the oncoming traffic. traffic.signals.nema.permissive_display Value Label Meaning fya Flashing yellow arrow The permissive left shows a flashing yellow arrow (MUTCD 2009 §4D.20). green-ball Circular green The permissive left shows the circular green of the through (MUTCD 2009 §4D.18). traffic.signals.nema.force_off Value Label Meaning floating Floating force-offs Each side-street phase ends by its own split, so time it leaves goes to the coordinated main street. fixed Fixed force-offs Force-off points are fixed in the cycle, so a later phase may use time an earlier one left. traffic.signals.nema.controller_type Value Label Meaning ts2 NEMA TS 2 The coordination offset is measured to the start of the coordinated green. type170 Type 170 The coordination offset is measured to the start of the coordinated yellow.

4 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see how to read these tables. Paths use [] for a list element and * for a map key.

items.title: General
items.text: Setting Type Unit Default Range or choices Level Status Description weather.initial string clear clear, rain, snow, sleet, fog, windrecommended Clear, unless weather is what you study. basic wired The kind of weather the run starts in. The weather at the start of the run: rain and fog slow drivers down and weaken radio signals. weather.intensity number 0.0 [0, 1]recommended 0.3 (light) to 0.8 (heavy). basic wired How hard it is doing it, on [0, 1]. Absent means unrestricted. weather.surface string dry, wet, flooded, snow, ice advanced partial The road surface, which need not follow from the kind. Status: Caps braking at the surface's grip, mug (wet 0.5, snow 0.25, ice 0.1; secondary friction figures), which also shrinks the comfortable braking the car-following model plans with. A dry surface is not capped.*

Unset joins none. Imported worlds only. Two traffic lights this close together on an imported map run as one junction with one plan, so cars are never fed into the short gap between them faster than it empties.

items.title: V2X-SCMS-MBD dataset: release schema v1 (draft)
items.text: Status: draft for review, 2026-11-03. Nothing here is exported yet; §10 lists what the engine must gain first. Supersedes nothing: the legacy ma-dataset profile (08-measurement-and-data.md §6) stays for the internal tools.

items.title: 1. What the dataset is
items.text:
Every run is published as two observer views of the same traffic plus the answers:

View Who sees it One row is Closest existing dataset local each vehicle's OBU a message it received, a check that fired, a report it filed VeReMi, VeReMi Ext, NextGen global the Misbehavior Authority a report it decrypted, a decision, a CRL entry DARE (the only report-level set) truth nobody in the system who really sent what, which attack, what happened downstream VeReMi GroundTruth file

The same message can be followed from the air, to a neighbour's check, to the report, to the MA's decision, to the CRL, to the moment neighbours stop trusting the attacker. No existing dataset links those steps.

items.title: 2. Lessons from the existing datasets
items.text:
Dataset Format What we keep What we fix VeReMi 1.0 (2018) JSON per receiver (type 2 own GPS, type 3 received BSM) + GroundTruthJSONlog per-receiver layout; truth in a separate file joined by message id sender is the real module id inside a receiver file (a label leak) VeReMi Ext (2020) same, sliced, -A<code> file names, F2MD codes 0–19 the attack codebook, kept as a crosswalk column senderRealId; the attack code in the file name; random-message splits VeReMi NextGen (2026) JSON → Parquet; receiver and sender blocks inline; 50/10/40 split Parquet; a held-out area for testing; the receiver's own state on each row sender_id and attacker written inline next to the features; no security fields; no report or MA layer DARE (2020) one JSON report: Metadata, Messages (evidence), Checks (scores) report = metadata + evidence + check scores senderRealId/reportedRealId inside the report; invented format; no revocation, so no outcome SPADE (2026), CARLA-V2X-MBD (2026) CSV per record, perception features inline receiver-side context (RSSI, receiver pose) no PKI at all; perfect perception; labels inline

Three rules follow:

  1. No answer inside an observer file. Truth lives in truth/. A linter refuses the release if any local/ or global/ column is ground truth.
  2. Join keys are computed from the bytes. Any party holding a message can compute its digest, so the key reveals nothing a real observer could not learn (§5).
  3. Splits are by run, never by message. Random message splits put one car's neighbouring BSMs in train and test, which inflates VeReMi scores.

items.title: 3. File layout
items.text:
v2x-scms-mbd/
  README.md                         dataset card (Hugging Face YAML header + datasheet)
  croissant.json                    MLCommons Croissant metadata (with RAI fields)
  schema/<table>.json               columns, types, units, visibility, description
  runs.parquet                      one row per run (§4)
  local/{ego,rx,checks,reports,pki}/split=<s>/run=<id>/part-*.parquet
  global/{reports,decisions,crl}/split=<s>/run=<id>/part-*.parquet
  truth/{devices,pseudonyms,transmissions,receptions,reports,timeline,app_effects}/...
  ml/{local,global}/split=<s>/...   flat, labelled training tables (§8)
  compat/veremi/<run>.zip           VeReMi Ext JSON per receiver + ground truth
  compat/dare/<run>.zip             DARE-style report JSON + a separate id file
  wire/{rx,reports}/...             raw signed bytes (full tier only)
  scenarios/<run>.yaml              scenario + seed: regenerates the run exactly

Format. Apache Parquet, zstd, row groups around 128 MB, files at most 1 GB. Lists and structs are native Parquet types, never JSON strings, so the Hugging Face viewer can filter on them.

Conventions. - Times are int64 ns since run start (*_ns); runs.t0_utc anchors them. - On-wire clocks are kept raw: 1609.2 generation_time_us (TAI µs since 2004) and J2735 sec_mark_ms. - Positions come twice: lat_deg/lon_deg as broadcast, and x_m/y_m in local ENU metres from runs.origin_*. - Units are in the column name: _m, _mps, _mps2, _deg, _dbm, _bytes.

Tiers. - mini: a handful of runs, under 500 MB, for the viewer and a quick start. - standard: every run, without wire/ and true kinematics. - full: everything.

items.title: 4. runs.parquet
items.text:
One row per run. It is the only place experiment settings appear, so a model can't read them off the rows.

Column Example Notes run_id r0007 partition key everywhere split train train / validation / test, assigned per run heldout_attacks [FakeHazard] attacks absent from train, for zero-day tests city, world_source manhattan, osm t0_utc, duration_s, origin_lat_deg, origin_lon_deg vehicles, equipped_fraction, demand_veh_per_h rat, bsm_rate_hz dsrc-80211p, 10 scms_mode in-loop in-loop / abstracted / off, for paired comparisons calendar real or compressed with calendar_factors (shuffle window, CRL cadence) local_suite, ma_policy sm-mbr-us, device-k(k=3,w=3600s) attacker_fraction, attack_mix 0.10, [{id, fraction, from_s, to_s, params}] instrumented_receivers 25 §6.2 engine_version, git_sha, scenario_hash, seed regeneration

items.title: 5. Identifiers
items.text:
Key What it is Who can compute it Appears in spdu_digest first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the signed message (1609.2 SPDU) anyone holding the message local, global (evidence), truth cert_id the signing pseudonym certificate's HashedId8 (1609.2) anyone holding the message local, global, truth report_id first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the signed MBR reporter, MA local, global, truth la_link opaque token, equal for two certificates of one device the MA, only after asking the Linkage Authorities global (nullable), truth receiver_ref opaque id of the OBU that wrote a local row that OBU local, truth rx_id unique id of one reception row — local, truth tx_id, device_id the engine's transmission and device ids oracle only truth only

A verbatim replay has the same bytes, so it has the same spdu_digest as the original. That is real: the receiver also can't tell them apart from the bytes. Truth resolves it per reception (truth/receptions.rx_id → tx_id).

items.title: 6.1 Tables
items.text:
local/ego: the receiver's own state at 10 Hz (VeReMi type 2). run_id, receiver_ref, t_ns, x_m, y_m, lat_deg, lon_deg, speed_mps, heading_deg, accel_mps2, pos_accuracy_m, own_cert_id

local/rx: one row per message the receiver decoded (VeReMi type 3, extended).

Group Columns keys run_id, receiver_ref, rx_id, t_rx_ns, spdu_digest radio rssi_dbm, cbr (receiver's channel busy ratio), size_bytes security psid, cert_id, signer_kind (digest or certificate), issuer_id, verify_result (ok, bad_signature, expired, not_yet_valid, on_crl, unknown_issuer, not_checked), verify_latency_us, generation_time_us BSM content msg_type, msg_cnt, temp_id, sec_mark_ms, lat_deg, lon_deg, x_m, y_m, elevation_m, pos_accuracy{semi_major_m, semi_minor_m, orientation_deg}, speed_mps, heading_deg, accel{long, lat, vert, yaw_rate}, brakes, transmission, length_m, width_m, event_flags receiver context ego_x_m, ego_y_m, ego_speed_mps, ego_heading_deg (copied from ego, as NextGen does), range_m (computed from the claimed position)

Other message types (SPaT, MAP, CPM, DENM-like hazard) use the same keys and security group. Their content goes in local/rx_<type> tables.

local/checks: one row per check result on a received message. run_id, receiver_ref, t_ns, rx_id, cert_id, suite, check, fired, score, excess - suite is one of: - sm-mbr-us: the deployed US CV-pilot checks: ConstantPosition, RandomPosition, MaxSpeed, MaxAcceleration, BrakeAcceleration, Distance; - research: the 17 legacy checks, such as positionSpeedInconsistency, headingInconsistency, staleOrReplay, sybilCoLocation, beaconFrequency, mapOffRoad and kalmanConsistency; - ts103759: the ETSI set, including the perception cross-check and CPM consistency. - The optional wide table local/check_scores holds one row per reception with one column per check. It is DARE's Checks block.

local/reports: every MBR this OBU created, and what became of it in its store. run_id, receiver_ref, report_id, t_created_ns, subject_cert_id, mbr_type, subtypes, evidence_spdu_digests[], size_bytes, fate (uploaded, evicted, expired, pending_at_end), t_uploaded_ns, path (cellular / rsu_relay), weight_at_upload

local/pki: the OBU's own credential life. run_id, receiver_ref, t_ns, event (enrolled, batch_downloaded, pseudonym_change, crl_downloaded, download_refused), cert_id, crl_series, crl_number, crl_entries, bytes, latency_ms

items.title: 6.2 Size control
items.text:
A sample 40-car, 70 s run produced 27,854 transmissions and 164,980 receptions: 58 MB as VeReMi JSON, about a tenth of that in Parquet.

At 200 cars, 10 Hz and around 30 neighbours, one hour is roughly 200 M reception rows. So local/rx and local/ego are written in full only for instrumented_receivers randomly chosen OBUs per run, listed in runs. checks, reports and pki are written for every OBU, because the MA side depends on all of them.

items.title: 7. Global view (what the MA knows)
items.text:
global/reports: one row per MBR the MA decrypted. The fields are the US CV-pilot report's (SM-MBR v1.0 and its ASN.1 v1.1: EeMaApplicationSpecificMisbehaviorReport, Psid20Mbr, SignedBsmsWithCertificate), decoded.

Group Columns keys run_id, ma_id, report_id, t_received_ns report header generation_time_us, generation_location{lat_deg, lon_deg, elevation_m}, psid (0x20), reporter_cert_id accusation subject_cert_id, subject_issuer, mbr_type (1VInconsistent, Implausible, ObsImplausible), subtypes[{code, name, params}], nonstandard_triggers[] (research-suite checks with no SM-MBR code, flagged) evidence evidence[{spdu_digest, generation_time_us, sec_mark_ms, msg_cnt, lat_deg, lon_deg, speed_mps, heading_deg, accel_long_mps2, brakes, pos_accuracy_m}], evidence_start_us, evidence_end_us MA processing set_aside (null, or unverifiable / time_implausible), la_link (null until the policy asks the LAs), la_link_t_ns

The MA never learns the reporter's enrolment identity. The RA authenticates the upload but can't read it. So no reporter device id appears here.

global/decisions: one row per MA decision. run_id, ma_id, t_ns, subject_kind (pseudonym / device), subject_cert_id, la_link, decision (revoke, dismiss, monitor), rule, report_ids[], n_reports, n_distinct_reporters

global/crl: what the MA caused to be published. run_id, t_issued_ns, crl_series, crl_number, entry_kind (linkage_seed / hash_id), la_link, i_period, t_effective_ns

items.title: 8. Truth (the answers)
items.text:
Table Key Content truth/devices device_id class (vehicle / RSU / VRU), provider, GNSS class, label (benign / faulty / malicious), attack_id, attack_params, attack_start_ns, attack_end_ns, joined/left times, la_link, receiver_ref if instrumented truth/pseudonyms cert_id device_id, validity window, first and last use truth/transmissions tx_id device_id, spdu_digest, label, attack_id, family, crosswalk codes (veremi_ext_code, veremi1_code, nextgen_name, dare_name), fields_falsified[], magnitude, true x_m, y_m, speed_mps, heading_deg, accel_mps2 at transmission, the sender's honest error (gnss_error_m, fix_to_stamp_ms) truth/receptions rx_id tx_id, sender device_id, label, true distance truth/reports report_id reporter and subject device_id, subject_label, verdict (true_accusation / false_accusation), store fate, arrival at MA truth/timeline device_id per misbehaving or falsely accused device: attack start, first falsified message, first local detection, first report created, uploaded, at MA, decision, CRL published, CRL at first / median / 95th-percentile neighbour, last malicious message accepted. That is the "how long a bad actor stays trusted" breakdown. truth/app_effects row warnings an application raised because of a falsified or faulty message (false FCW, EEBL, IMA, RLVW): app, receiver, tx_id, severity, driver_reaction truth/kinematics (device_id, t_ns) 10 Hz true state, full tier only

Labels exist at five levels: 1. message: label, attack_id; 2. pseudonym; 3. device; 4. report: true or false accusation; 5. outcome: correct revocation, wrongful revocation, or missed attacker. The outcome is derived from devices and global/decisions.

faulty is a first-class label: an honest device whose data is wrong beyond specification (GNSS error, timestamp lag). DARE's "malfunctions" are the precedent. It is the class Paper 1 measures.

ml/ tables are convenience copies for people who only want to train: - ml/local: local/rx joined with truth/receptions.label and attack_id; - ml/global: global/reports joined with truth/reports.verdict.

They are clearly named as joined, the same way NextGen ships its rows. The local and global folders stay clean.

items.title: 9. Attacks
items.text:
The engine's catalogue: 46 named, 43 runnable today (crates/v2xw-threat/src/catalog.rs). The VeReMi-Ext code is filled in only where the behaviour matches F2MD's (dataset/veremi.rs); anything else exports as 1024 (unnamed).

Family Attacks VeReMi-Ext / NextGen / DARE closest Where it shows Position ConstPos, ConstPosOffset, RandomPos, Teleport, SineWavePos, SlowDrift, AlongRoadOffset 1, 2, 4 / constantPositionOffset, randomPositionOffset / position malfunction local plausibility Speed ConstSpeedOffset, RandomSpeed, StopAndGo 6, 7 / constantSpeedOffset, randomSpeedOffset, suddenStop local plausibility Heading ReversedHeading, HeadingOffset – / reversedHeading local plausibility Inconsistent state PosSpeedInconsistent, PosHeadingInconsistent, EventualStop 9 / suddenStop / sudden stop local consistency Timing DelayedMessages, OutOfOrder, DataReplay 12 / timeDelayAttack, dataReplay / delayed, data replay local timing Identity Sybil, GhostVehicles 16 / trafficCongestionSybil / Sybil, traffic congestion local and MA (one la_link, many certificates) Credentials InvalidSignature, ExpiredCert, NotYetValid, WrongRegionCert – security layer (verify_result) Flooding DoS, DoSRandom, Disruptive, OversizedFlood 13 / dosAttack / DoS, disruptive radio and CBR, rate Application FakeHazard, VruImpersonation, VruPositionSpoof, FakeCpm – applications and perception cross-check Suppression and relay SelectiveDrop, RelayReplay – / dataReplay (partly) reception gaps, duplicate digests Jamming ConstantJamming, ReactiveJamming, RandomDutyJamming – radio only (no messages to label) Compromised RSU FalseCrl, SuppressForwardedReports, PoisonForwardedReports (FalseSpat, FalseMap and FalseCtl declared, not yet driven) SPADE's classes once SPaT is driven PKI, report path Against the MA ReportPoisoning, BenignClassMimic (evasion) – global only Privacy PrivacyObserver (passive tracker; labels tracking success, not messages) – truth only

Benign faults (label faulty): GNSS error classes, fix-to-stamp lag, smoothing artefacts. They are set per device class in the scenario.

To add for full coverage: - NextGen: feignedBraking, accelerationMultiplication, positionMirroring, zeroSpeedReport. - VeReMi Ext: uniform RandomPos (4), ConstSpeed (5), neighbour DataReplay (11), DoSDisruptive and the Sybil combinations (15, 17–19). - SPADE: wire FalseSpat and FalseMap. RLVW and GLOSA already consume signed SPaT and MAP (v2xw-node/src/apps.rs), so the validator note refusing them is stale.

Each is one model in the catalogue. Every run in the loop gets the full downstream chain for free.

items.title: 10. Quality gates (each must be shown able to fail)
items.text:
1. Leakage linter: no truth column in local/ or global/. It exists as dataset/leakage.rs; extend its key list to this schema.
  2. Shortcut audit: a classifier trained on metadata only (cert_id statistics, message rate, size, msg_cnt) must score near chance on attacks whose definition isn't rate or size. VeReMi's message-rate shortcut is the precedent (veremi-audit).
  3. Join completeness: every global/reports.evidence[].spdu_digest resolves in truth/transmissions, and every rx_id in truth/receptions.
  4. Grid scan: floats on their declared grid (dataset/grids.rs).
  5. Manifest: SHA-256 per file. Runs regenerate bit-for-bit from scenarios/ plus git_sha.

items.title: 11. Publication
items.text:
• Hugging Face is the primary host. Each table is a config, and each config's train / validation / test splits are data_files globs over the split= partitions. The viewer and SQL console work on every config except compat/ and wire/ (zips and binaries). Use load_dataset("<org>/v2x-scms-mbd", "global_reports").
  • Zenodo holds the frozen version: a DOI, the compat zips, the full tarballs. It mirrors the same tag.
  • Licences: CC-BY-4.0 for data, the same as VeReMi NextGen. The engine's licence for code.
  • The card follows Datasheets for Datasets. DATASHEET.md (dataset/datasheet.rs) supplies its sections. Croissant goes beside it.

items.title: 12. What the engine must gain first
items.text:
1. A dataset exporter on v2xw run. Today DatasetWriter is called only by tests. A run writes raw channel dumps that mix views; for example, ma_report carries the reporter's node id.
  2. local/rx with the security group. Join phy.rx, node.verify and node.tx content. The VeReMi exporter drops these fields.
  3. spdu_digest and report_id from the real bytes. Add truth/receptions.
  4. Instrumented-receiver sampling (§6.2).
  5. Native list and struct columns. subtypes and spans are JSON strings today.
  6. The DARE compat writer.
  7. Streaming export. A 40-car, 70 s run hit heavy.sh's 4.5 GB cap in the JSONL stage.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: How to set up, what a change must pass, and how to work on the documentation. Code rules are on Conventions; building and test layout on Building and testing.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
Need Version / source Rust pinned in rust-toolchain.toml (1.98.1, with rustfmt, clippy and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target); rustup installs it on first use just the task runner (just --list) Python and uv the python/ package (optional) Node and pnpm the Studio UI under ui/ (optional) SUMO optional: the high mobility tier and cross-validation (just sumo-install prints how) 
just setup          # cargo fetch; uv sync --project python; pnpm --dir ui install
just build          # cargo build --workspace
just check          # cargo check --workspace --all-targets

Tests that import the Manhattan extract need worlds/cache/manhattan.osm.xml (worlds/fetch.sh manhattan; git-ignored). On a machine with little memory, build the release binaries one job at a time (just build-cli, just build-server).

items.title: Making a change
items.text:
1. Branch from main; never commit to main directly.
  2. Keep the change to one concern. A new model, setting, detector or metric follows its recipe under Extending.
  3. Run the gates below locally, scoped to the crates you touched while iterating (cargo test -p <crate>, cargo test -p <crate> --test <file>); the full workspace suite is long.
  4. If the change moves a run's output on purpose, re-bless the golden digests and say so in the commit: V2XW_CONFORMANCE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p v2xw-conformance --test kit golden.
  5. If the change adds or edits a setting, run just docs-gen and commit the regenerated reference.

items.title: Commit messages
items.text: Subject <area>: <what changed> in plain descriptive language (v2xw-sec: ..., scenarios: ..., docs: ...), body explaining why where it is not obvious. No internal tracker ids or narrative.

items.title: The gates
items.text:
Gate Command Runs in CI formatting cargo fmt --all -- --check (just fmt-check) ci.yml job rust, on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows lints cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings (just lint) rust tests, including the conformance kit (tests/conformance is a workspace member) cargo test --workspace (just test) rust toolchain pin the installed rustc must equal rust-toolchain.toml rust cross-platform determinism each platform imports tests/fixtures/midtown-6block.osm.xml and prints the world and payload digests (just world-hash); all three must agree and no value may be off its grid determinism, determinism-compare UI pnpm --dir ui typecheck && pnpm --dir ui test (just ui-test) local only validation suites just validation-report [--quick], just cross-validate (needs SUMO) local only (tools)

just ci runs fmt-check, lint and test in one go.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
The site is built with Zensical from mkdocs.yml and docs/, and deployed to GitHub Pages by .github/workflows/docs.yml on every push to main that touches docs/, mkdocs.yml, crates/, tools/docs/ or the workflow.

pip install -r tools/docs/requirements.txt   # pins zensical
just docs-gen       # regenerate docs/configuration/reference/ from the engine
just docs-serve     # live-reload preview at http://localhost:8000
just docs-build     # build into site/ (zensical build --clean); warns on broken links
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --open        # the Rust API docs

The CI workflow does the same: generate the reference (dump_settings → tools/docs/gen_config_reference.py), zensical build --clean, then cargo doc --workspace --no-deps copied into site/api/.

Where What mkdocs.yml nav the site structure; a new page needs an entry, and the generator fails if a generated page is missing from it docs/configuration/reference/ generated; never edit by hand docs/README.md the map for readers browsing the repository; excluded from the site docs/reference/ curated tables, some embedded by the assistant docs/protocol/vwp-v1.md the normative wire specification

Rules for documentation:

  • The code is the truth. Every claim is checked against the code it describes; leave out what cannot be verified. Describe what is implemented, not what is planned, and say where a model is simplified.
  • Cite the standards and papers the code implements, with sections, as the code does (Standards and references). Do not quote licensed standard text (SAE J2735, IEEE 1609) at length; field names are fine.
  • Link instead of repeating. One page owns each topic.
  • Real commands only, and paths relative to the repository root.
  • Pages use admonitions for notes and warnings, tables for parameters, mermaid for data flow and $...$ / $$...$$ (MathJax) for equations.

items.title: Notes for coding agents
items.text:
AGENTS.md at the repository root is the entry point: the map of the workspace, the commands, and the invariants that must not break (determinism, the canonical digest, scenario hashes, belief versus ground truth, model cards, no invented defaults). Then:

  • read the crate's src/lib.rs module table before the module;
  • prefer cargo check -p <crate> --all-targets and scoped tests over workspace builds;
  • prove a new check can fail before trusting it (inject the fault, see it go red, restore; tools/mutate/mutate.py restores the file's mtime so cargo rebuilds);
  • never let a setting reach the Studio without a range or menu, units and a status (Extending: settings);
  • keep AGENTS.md's links consistent when moving a page.

items.title: Conventions
items.text: The rules below are enforced by code (a compiler attribute, a CI gate, a test) unless the row says otherwise. AGENTS.md states the same invariants for coding agents.

items.title: Workspace layout and layering
items.text:
The workspace (Cargo.toml, resolver 3, edition 2024) has every directory under crates/ and tests/conformance as members. examples/ is a separate cargo workspace that builds the way an external crate would. Crate roles and exact dependency edges are in Crates; the layer picture is in Architecture.

Rule Why v2xw-core depends on no other workspace crate it is the contract every model is written against each model crate owns one domain and does not reach into another's (mobility never touches radio or security; radio treats a frame as a length, MCS and access category) a model can be replaced without touching its neighbours metrics read recorded channels, never engine state a metric computed live and from a recording must agree v2xw-engine is the only place model crates are composed wiring is in one place (wiring.rs, driving.rs, phase2.rs) node, detector, attacker and MA code reads only what a fielded device could know (v2xw_core::nodeview, v2xw_threat::obs) belief and ground truth stay apart; see the firewall

Each crate's src/lib.rs opens with a module table naming where each concern lives.

items.title: Determinism
items.text:
Same scenario, seed, build and plug-in set give byte-identical outputs on every platform and thread count. The full contract is on Determinism and time; in code it means:

Do Never draw randomness from a keyed v2xw_core::rng::RngStream checked out through the model's context (ctx.rng(domain, entity)), keyed so the draw does not depend on event order rand::thread_rng, a shared generator, a private seed call transcendentals through v2xw_core::math (pure-Rust libm); sqrt is exempt because IEEE 754 makes it exact f64::sin, .exp(), .ln(), .powf(), .atan2(), .hypot() and the rest take time from the simulation clock (v2xw_core::SimTime); the manifest timestamp is an argument (Engine::build(scenario, build_utc)) SystemTime::now, Instant::now, UNIX_EPOCH below the transport use BTreeMap, BTreeSet, IndexMap or a sorted Vec std::collections::HashMap / HashSet anywhere engine-facing quantise floats to their declared grid before recording, exporting or digesting (v2xw_core::math::quantize_to; record constructors do it) write a raw f64 into a digest run parallel work as a pure map merged in id order let thread scheduling order reach a result

items.title: The determinism and truth firewall
items.text:
Text rules over the source tree, in tests/conformance/src/firewall.rs (driven by tests/kit/firewall_suite.rs) and in the node's own sentinel (crates/v2xw-node/src/firewall.rs, driven by crates/v2xw-node/tests/firewall_sentinel.rs):

Check Forbidden text Applies to Exempt ground-truth Kinematics, .world(), .actors(), ActorId; a gt_ field read outside telemetry; truth types bound on the security bridge v2xw-node the rule table itself wall-clock SystemTime::now, Instant::now, UNIX_EPOCH every crate crates/v2xw-cli/src/wall.rs, crates/v2xw-server/src/http.rs (the transport's liveness and seek budgets) hash-order HashMap, HashSet every crate v2xw-metrics/src/arrow_out.rs, v2xw-record/src/export/schema.rs (Arrow metadata, typed as a std map by the arrow crate) transcendental .sin(, .cos(, .tan(, .exp(, .exp2(, .ln(, .log10(, .log2(, .powf(, .atan2(, .asin(, .acos(, .atan(, .hypot(, .cbrt(, .sinh(, .cosh(, .tanh( every crate none

The scanner recurses into subdirectories, sorts its file list, skips comments and closes #[cfg(test)] blocks rather than latching them. Exemptions are data in the rule table, each with its reason. CI's determinism job also imports the committed fixture tests/fixtures/midtown-6block.osm.xml on Linux, macOS and Windows and fails unless all three print the same world and payload digests.

items.title: Golden digests
items.text:
tests/conformance/golden/*.json pin, per fixed scenario, the scenario hash, world hash, a digest over every record and per-channel counts. A change that moves them is an output change. Re-bless only when the change is intended:

V2XW_CONFORMANCE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p v2xw-conformance --test kit golden

A new optional scenario field must serialise as absent at its default (#[serde(skip_serializing_if = ...)]) so existing scenario hashes do not move.

items.title: Error handling
items.text: Rule Where library crates define typed errors with thiserror, marked #[non_exhaustive], with #[from] conversions up the stack (EngineError wraps ScenarioError, RegistryError, WorldError, MobError, CoreError, MetricError, RecordError) crates/v2xw-engine/src/error.rs and each crate's error module a scenario error names the dotted field and the conflict (ScenarioError::Conflict), never a line number and a serde message; only scenario::validate builds it crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/validate.rs the validator returns every error, not the first validate::validate(&Scenario) -> Vec<ScenarioError> where no cited value exists for a vendor- or jurisdiction-specific number, the code refuses rather than guesses hardware profiles, speed presets malformed recorded or wire input is an error in debug and release builds, not a panic crates/v2xw-record/tests/overflow.rs

items.title: Units in names
items.text: A scenario field's unit is part of its name (duration_s, mobility_step_ms, tx_power_dbm, rate_veh_per_h), so a value cannot be separated from its unit. The published surface reads the unit back off the suffix (UNIT_SUFFIXES in scenario/publish.rs: _s, _ms, _us, _ns, _m, _km, _mps, _mps2, _hz, _db, _dbm, _dbi, _deg, _kbps, _mbps, _veh_per_h). A numeric leaf whose name cannot carry its unit declares it in publish.rs, and the test every_number_publishes_a_unit fails the build otherwise. Use the same suffixes for struct fields and local variables in model code.

items.title: Model cards
items.text:
Registry::register refuses a model without a complete v2xw_core::card::ModelCard:

  • an id family/name, a version, a tier and a purpose;
  • the equations;
  • every parameter with a unit, a default, a range and a source, or todo-calibrate with a calibration plan;
  • assumptions, limitations, what it ignores, and how it was validated;
  • determinism: whether it draws random numbers and from which declared domains.

The step-by-step is in Extending: models.

items.title: Citing standards
items.text: A number or rule taken from a standard or paper is cited in the comment beside it, by document and section, as the code does throughout (IEEE 1609.2 §5.2, TS 102 687 §5.4, SAE J2945/1 §6.3). A hard-coded value with no source is either marked todo-calibrate on its card or refused. Licensed standard text (SAE J2735, IEEE) is never quoted at length; field names and short identifiers are fine. The bibliography of what the code cites is Standards and references.

items.title: Documentation in code
items.text:
• #![deny(missing_docs)] in every library crate except v2xw-demand, v2xw-interop and v2xw-netval.
  • #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in every library crate except v2xw-cli (deny), v2xw-demand and v2xw-interop.
  • A doc comment says what the item is, its unit, and its source. It does not narrate how the code came to be.

items.title: Formatting and lints
items.text:
Gate Command rustfmt cargo fmt --all -- --check clippy, warnings denied, all targets cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings tests cargo test --workspace

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs all three on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows. Warnings are denied on the clippy line rather than through RUSTFLAGS, so a warning in a dependency under a new compiler does not break the build. The toolchain is pinned in rust-toolchain.toml (channel 1.98.1, with rustfmt, clippy and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target), and CI asserts the installed compiler matches the pin.

items.title: Settings
items.text: A new scenario setting must reach the Studio as a menu with units, not a free text box: a range in validate::BOUNDS or a closed set in validate::CHOICES, a KEY_STATUS row, a label and description in scenario::options, and a level in scenario::guide. The publish tests fail otherwise. See Extending: settings.

items.title: Checks that can fail
items.text: A check is trusted only once it has been seen to fail. Validation suites run every check with an injected fault; for a new unit or integration test, inject the fault by hand or with tools/mutate/mutate.py and confirm it goes red (tools).

items.title: Commits
items.text: Short subject in the form <area>: <what changed> (docs: ..., scenarios: ..., v2xw-sec: ...), in neutral descriptive language, one logical change per commit. See Contributing.

items.title: Recording format
items.text: A run's outputs and their on-disk format, for someone writing a reader, an exporter or a tool over recordings. The user-level view (what each file is for, the channel list by visibility, the record levels) is in Metrics and outputs; the binary frame layouts are normative in VWP v1. Code: crates/v2xw-record (container, writer, reader, index, exporters), crates/v2xw-core/src/manifest.rs and crates/v2xw-engine/src/manifest.rs (manifest), crates/v2xw-cli/src/run.rs and checkpoint.rs (run directory, checkpoints).

items.title: The run directory
items.text:
v2xw run <scenario> --out <dir> writes:

File Content Reproducible recording.mcap the MCAP container: every record, the manifest as metadata, the resolved scenario as the attachment scenario.yaml (and the world payload as world.vwb with --attach-world) the data section is; the file's SHA-256 is not (digests) scenario.resolved.yaml the scenario after migration, base merge and defaults: what ran yes metrics.json every metric.sample record yes run-report.json event, frame and record counts per channel, and the recording's content_digest yes manifest.json the run manifest with the files above digested and data_digest finalised all but build_utc and the recording file's own digest progress.jsonl progress lines (--progress-every) no (wall-clock timings) checkpoint.json a resumable checkpoint (--checkpoint-every) see checkpoints

Exporters named in the scenario's exporters list add their own files beside these (Datasets and exports).

items.title: The MCAP container
items.text:
MCAP with zstd chunks, profile v2xw, readable by standard MCAP tools. Two topic namespaces with different encodings, never mixed on one topic (the writer refuses):

Namespace Topics Message encoding Schema Holds vwp/… vwp/hello, vwp/keyframe, vwp/delta, vwp/telemetry, vwp/metric, vwp/provenance, vwp/event/<channel> vwp1 vwp.v1.<Type>; the schema data is the layout table from the specification, so the file describes itself VWP binary frames stored verbatim (transport flag bits cleared) record/… record/<channel>, one per channel family json jsonschema: the channel, its visibility and the grid of every float serde v2xw_core::OwnedRecord rows, the input to the Parquet, Arrow IPC and JSONL exporters

Storing the snapshot frames as the bytes that went over the wire is what makes replay byte-identical to the live stream (VWP §7.2): RecordingWriter::write_frame stores them, Reader::replay hands them back, and nothing rebuilds a frame from decoded state. crates/v2xw-record/tests/byte_identity.rs checks it.

items.title: Channel metadata
items.text:
Every MCAP channel carries:

Key Value channel the record channel name (node.tx, ...) visibility gt, node, node-and-gt, public, derived, mixed or meta ground_truth true when any part of the record is ground truth, so a consumer can filter without the catalogue encoding_kind vwp1 or record vwp_channel_id, vwp_msg_type the numeric ids on vwp/… topics

File-level metadata v2xw.manifest holds the manifest JSON.

items.title: The channel catalogue
items.text:
v2xw_record::channels::CHANNELS is one table for the recorder (topic, schema, metadata), the NODE-only profile (which channels to strip) and the exporters (which tables to write). Each ChannelSpec has a name, a wire_id (its id in an Event frame, or None for a record-only channel), a visibility and, for Event payloads, a fixed payload_bytes. 49 channels; with a VWP Event wire id:

Wire id Channel Visibility Event payload (bytes) 1 gt.kinematics gt §3.6.11 2 gt.attack.action gt §3.6.12 3, 4 gt.spawn, gt.despawn gt 10 node.tx node §3.6.4 11 phy.rx node-and-gt §3.6.5 12 mac.cbr node §3.6.13 13 net.frag node §3.6.14 14 node.verify node §3.6.6 15 node.telemetry node 16 node.neighbor node §3.6.15 20 sec.cert node §3.6.7 21 proto.msg node §3.6.16 22 proto.revocation public §3.6.10 30 det.observation node §3.6.8 31, 32, 33 ma.report, ma.case, ma.decision node §3.6.17 40 app.warning node §3.6.9 50 metric.sample derived §3.7 60, 61 snapshot.keyframe, snapshot.delta mixed Keyframe / Delta frames (§3.3, §3.4) 70 manifest meta

The other channels are record-only: app.advice, app.outcome, backend.state, gt.device_exposure, gt.subject, ma.received, msg.latency, net.bytes, net.reassembly, node.credentials, node.drop, node.p2pcd, node.rx, node.security, phy.prr, pki.case, pki.flow, pki.knowledge, pki.report_fate, pki.state, privacy.link, privacy.track, scenario.event, sec.pseudonym, signal.priority, traffic.control.

items.title: Encoders and quantisation
items.text:
No float reaches a recorded, exported or digested artefact in raw form: one writer-side encoder quantises each value to its declared grid, and a scan fails the build if a value sits off it.

Quantity Wire Scale Reference keyframe x, y i32 millimetres the run's origin keyframe z i16 centimetres the run's origin delta x, y, z i16 millimetres the previously transmitted quantised value, so error does not accumulate heading u16 binary radians absolute speed i16 1/128 m/s absolute acceleration i16 1/64 m/s² absolute

(v2xw_record::quant; VWP §3.2.) The remaining floats (the Hello origin and bounding box, f32 node positions and class dimensions, ten Telemetry fields, MetricSample.value) have grids listed in v2xw_record::grid, which scan_frame enforces. Record channels quantise through v2xw_core::math::quantize_to in the record constructors; the exporters quantise each column to the grid its schema declares and write the grids beside the data as schema.json, which export::scan reads back.

The snapshot producer (v2xw_record::encoder::SnapshotEncoder) is a pure function of the snapshots it is fed. Its Cadence { keyframe_period, mobility_step } comes from the scenario (v2xw run --keyframe-ms, default 1000 ms, a whole number of mobility steps); Cadence::DEFAULT is 1 s keyframes and 100 ms steps. One delta per mobility step; only actors whose quantised pose, state, verified neighbours or lane changed appear in it.

items.title: Chunks, the index and seek
items.text:
• Chunk boundaries fall before a keyframe once the chunk reaches chunk_target_bytes; a GOP larger than the target is split between deltas. A chunk is therefore bounded by about twice the target plus one message, whatever the keyframe period. RecordingSummary::largest_chunk_bytes and largest_gop_bytes report what a run reached.
  • zstd runs single-threaded (compression_threads = 0): the multithreaded encoder is not byte-deterministic.
  • v2xw_record::index::SeekIndex reads the 20-byte footer, the summary section and each chunk's message index, then fetches only the chunks a seek needs. Every offset and length from the file is checked arithmetic, bounded by the buffer it describes and cross-checked against the chunk index; a chunk's CRC is verified before anything in it is parsed. Malformed input is a named RecordError, never a panic (tests/overflow.rs in debug and release, tests/fuzz_corrupt.rs).
  • Reader::seek(t) finds the keyframe at or before t and applies the deltas up to it (VWP §7.3); the budget is 100 ms (§7.4).

items.title: Visibility profiles
items.text: v2xw_record::profile implements the NODE-only profile (VWP §5): ground-truth channels are dropped whole; a mixed or node-and-gt record keeps its node-visible fields with the ground-truth ones blanked. An unequipped actor transmits nothing, so its slot is empty; an equipped actor keeps its pose. The live producer and the stripper share one blanking implementation, so a full recording replayed as node equals a live node run byte for byte. v2xw run --node-only records the profile; ExportProfile::NodeOnly exports it, and a NODE export and a ground-truth export never share a file.

items.title: The manifest
items.text:
v2xw_core::manifest::Manifest, written as manifest.json and as the v2xw.manifest metadata record:
