items.title: Digests
items.text: Digest Over Where Compare it? content_digest SHA-256 over every message's topic, log_time and bytes in stored order (Reader::content_digest) run-report.json yes: a run's identity; two runs of one scenario, seed and build must agree file SHA-256 of recording.mcap the bytes on disk manifest.json files no: the mcap writer emits summary records from a hash map, so the index order can vary data_digest SHA-256(for rel in sorted(paths): rel ‖ hex(sha256(file))), hex text of each file digest, no separator (Manifest::finalize) manifest.json yes, for the reproducible files stream_digest SHA-256 of every record as produced, nothing written (--no-recording --digest) CLI output for scaling runs at different thread counts golden records scenario hash, world hash, a digest over every record, per-channel counts tests/conformance/golden/*.json the conformance kit (Conventions) metric digest over the run summary's metrics; diagnostic metrics are kept apart and excluded v2xw_metrics::RunSummary::digest yes

items.title: Checkpoints
items.text:
v2xw run --checkpoint-every 1h writes checkpoint.json and closes recording segments at each checkpoint. It holds the inputs (resolved scenario, its hash, world hash, build timestamp), the instant t, the record digest at t with the record count, and how much of each output was complete at t (closed segments, metrics.json bytes and samples, progress.jsonl lines).

v2xw resume <checkpoint.json> rebuilds the engine, re-runs to t with outputs off, refuses to continue unless the record digest at t matches, truncates the outputs to what was complete at t, and carries on. The engine's memory is not serialised, so a resume costs the re-run to t. The finished outputs equal an uninterrupted run's (crates/v2xw-cli/tests/longrun.rs). v2xw-server --resume <checkpoint.json> serves such a run paused at its checkpoint.

items.title: Reading a recording
items.text:
RustPythonWebAssemblyCommand line 
use v2xw_record::reader::Reader;

let mut r = Reader::open("runs/x/recording.mcap")?;     // or open_paged / open_bytes
r.require_chunk_checksums(true);                        // refuse chunks without a CRC
let report = r.verify()?;                               // VerifyReport
assert!(report.integrity_verified());
let digest = r.content_digest()?;                       // [u8; 32]
let manifest = r.manifest_json();                       // Option<&str>
for ch in r.channels() { /* ChannelMeta { id, topic, message_encoding, schema_id, metadata } */ }
let rows = r.records(Some("node.tx"))?;                 // Vec<RecordedRecord>
let frames = r.replay()?;                               // Vec<RecordedFrame>, byte-identical
let at = r.seek(30_000_000_000)?;                       // SeekResult at t = 30 s
let scenario = r.attachment("scenario.yaml")?;          // the resolved scenario

Reader::open reads the file into memory; open_paged reads only the footer, summary and message indexes and fetches the chunks a seek needs. VerifyReport counts frames, records, keyframes, deltas, unknown message types (counted, not refused), provenance ids and references, the snapshot span and its largest gap, and chunks with and without a checksum. Tabular export: v2xw_record::export (Parquet, Arrow IPC, JSONL).

import v2xw

rec = v2xw.Recording.open("runs/x/recording.mcap")
rec.require_chunk_checksums(True)
report = rec.verify()                       # dict
digest = rec.content_digest()               # hex
rec.manifest, rec.channels, rec.ground_truth_channels
rows = rec.records("node.tx", limit=100)    # list of dicts
batch = rec.arrow("node.tx")                # pyarrow.RecordBatch; ground_truth=False drops GT columns
ipc = rec.table("node.tx")                  # Arrow IPC bytes; v2xw.read_ipc(ipc)
rec.table_schema("node.tx")

See Python API.

crates/v2xw-wasm compiles the same reader for wasm32-unknown-unknown and adds a range-fetched byte source (ranges), resolved pose columns at an instant (scene) and the seek loop the JavaScript class calls (session). The Studio replays recordings in the browser this way with no replay-specific code path. Building it needs a clang with the WebAssembly back end (the container's zstd is C); see crates/v2xw-wasm/README.md and scripts/build-wasm.sh.

v2xw info runs/x/recording.mcap      # manifest, channels, verification report

Any MCAP tool (the mcap CLI, Foxglove) lists topics and messages; vwp/… payloads decode with the layout tables in their channel schema or in VWP v1.

items.title: Engine server and RPC
items.text: crates/v2xw-server serves one run (live from the engine, or the synthetic fixture) to browsers, notebooks and scripts: the binary VWP stream over a WebSocket and a JSON-RPC 2.0 control surface over the same socket and over HTTP. The normative wire specification is VWP v1; this page is the developer's map of it, with every method of v2xw_server::rpc::METHODS.

items.title: Starting a server
items.text:
Command Serves v2xw-server --scenario <file> a live engine run of the scenario, with the agent's endpoints and watcher v2xw-server (no --scenario) the synthetic fixture: a deterministic procedural grid with --actors, --grid, --block, --duration, --seed; every number it reports is a fixture value v2xw serve --scenario <file> the same live run with the agent's endpoints, through the main CLI v2xw serve --attach <url> only the agent's endpoints, in front of an engine already running just serve <scenario> / just serve-fixture [ACTORS] the two above on port 8787 ./run-sim.sh [scenario] builds if needed and starts the engine with the agent on

v2xw-server options:

Option Default Meaning --scenario <p> none (fixture) scenario to run --record <p> none write the MCAP recording here --build-utc <t> now, read by the binary manifest timestamp (the engine reads no clock) --retain <n> / --retain-mb <n> 36000 steps / 1024 MB history kept for run.seek --lookahead <n> 64 steps the kernel may run ahead of the stream --resume <p> none open a v2xw run --checkpoint-every run at its checkpoint.json and serve it paused there --port <n> 8787 TCP port; 0 picks an ephemeral one --host <addr> 127.0.0.1 bind address; a non-loopback bind needs --token --token <t> none bearer token required on the upgrade and on every HTTP request --speed <x> 1 multiple of real time; 0 is unthrottled --paused off start paused at t = 0 --label <s> human label in Hello --no-agent off serve without the agent's endpoints and watcher --env-file <p> ./.env when present where the agent's model-provider keys are read from --quiet off no banner

From Rust: v2xw_server::serve_scenario(ServerOptions, path, LiveOptions), serve_stub(ServerOptions, StubOptions) and serve_replay(ServerOptions, recording, world, world_json) each return a running VwpServer. ServerOptions { bind, token, extension } takes an extra axum::Router merged on the same origin, which is how the agent's routes are added. No shipped binary serves a replay; the Studio replays recordings in the browser through v2xw-wasm (Recording format).

items.title: Transports
items.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Server["v2xw-server (one run)"]
        E["Engine trait<br/>LiveEngine / StubEngine / ReplayEngine"] --> R[Run]
        R --> WS["GET /vwp/v1<br/>WebSocket"]
        R --> RPC["POST /rpc"]
        R --> W["GET /world/{hash}.vwb|.json"]
        R --> S["GET /rpc/schema"]
        R --> H["GET /healthz"]
        A["/agent/* (v2xw serve, v2xw-server)"]
    end
    WS -- "binary: VWP frames" --> C[Studio / client]
    WS -- "text: JSON-RPC + notifications" --> C
    RPC --> N[CLI, notebook, CI]
Endpoint Purpose Spec GET /vwp/v1?run=&session=&resume=&profile=full\|node&compress=zstd\|none&v=1 WebSocket, subprotocol vwp.v1. Binary frames carry the stream; text frames carry JSON-RPC §1.1, §1.2 POST /rpc the same methods, one call per request; connection-scoped methods return -32009 §6.2 GET /rpc/schema the OpenRPC 1.3.2 document (rpc.discover's result) §6.3 GET /world/{hash}.vwb, .json the world geometry, vwp-world/1, content-addressed and immutable §4 GET /healthz liveness §1.1

Every response carries the cross-origin isolation headers (Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin). A missing or wrong bearer token is HTTP 401, never a WebSocket close.

Stream topic Spec handshake (Hello), reconnect and resume by session token and seq §1.3, §1.4 backpressure: bounded queues, drop policy, stream.drop §1.5 24-byte frame header, flags, message types, symbol table, compression §2 Hello, Keyframe, Delta, Telemetry, Event, MetricSample, Provenance, WorldChunk, Error, Bye §3 full and node visibility profiles §5 replay, byte identity, seek §7 versioning §8

Every frame the server sends is built by v2xw-record's encoder (v2xw_record::wire); only the connection-scoped Error and Bye frames are written in http.rs.

items.title: JSON-RPC conventions
items.text:
• JSON-RPC 2.0, single objects only (a batch array is refused with -32600); params by name. §6.1
  • Long operations return a Job ({job_id, state, progress, message, outputs}) and finish with job.progress / job.done notifications.
  • rpc.discover (or GET /rpc/schema) returns every method's params schema, result schema and error list; the shared schemas (SimTimeNs, RunId, NodeId, Sha256Hex, ValueRef, Provenance, ValidationError, WorldImportResult, Job) are in §6.5.
  • Times are integer nanoseconds since the scenario's time.t0.

items.title: Notifications
items.text:
Server to client, never requests (§6.14):

Notification When run.state the run's state changes stream.drop backpressure dropped frames for this connection job.progress, job.done a long operation progresses or ends view.changed the connection's view changed log a server log line validation validation results for a staged scenario experiment.progress an experiment's progress node.feed the followed node's messages and queues, while a view.follow {feed} stands

items.title: Agent endpoints
items.text:
Served on the same origin by v2xw-server and v2xw serve unless --no-agent is given (then only GET /agent/status answers, with available: false). The agent reaches the engine through the same JSON-RPC as any client, so it has a Studio user's authority. Model keys stay in the server process (read from the environment or --env-file) and are never returned. See Assistant.

Endpoint Does GET /agent/status whether a model is attached, which one, where its key comes from (named, never shown) POST /agent/ask {prompt} starts the agent on a prompt; follow-ups continue the conversation POST /agent/run {base} runs a shipped scenario and analyses it, no model needed POST /agent/analyse analyses the run on screen, no model needed GET /agent/events?job=&after= a job's events from after: plan, changes, progress, analysis, report POST /agent/stop stops the job at its next check, pausing a run it started POST /agent/reset forgets the conversation POST /agent/undo {setup} gives the settings window back what it held before that setup GET /agent/watch?after= the always-on watcher: what it noticed about the runs since after GET /agent/summary the last finished run's summary: verdict, layers, problems, overview, analysis POST /agent/compare-signatures {document?, scenario?, schemes?, duration_s?}, GET the same runs one scenario under several signature schemes on a thread; GET reports progress and the result

The watcher reads run.status once a second and the run's evidence every few seconds; it never pauses, steps or changes a run.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
# start a fixture server paused, then drive it over HTTP
v2xw-server --actors 50 --paused --no-agent &
curl -s localhost:8787/rpc -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"run.status"}'
curl -s localhost:8787/rpc -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"run.step","params":{"unit":"second","count":5}}'
curl -s localhost:8787/rpc -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"scenario.schema","params":{"sections":["groups","statuses"]}}'
curl -s localhost:8787/rpc/schema > openrpc.json

items.title: Tests
items.text: Test Holds crates/v2xw-server/tests/rpc.rs METHODS equals the OpenRPC method list and the client's VWP_METHODS, by name and order cargo test -p v2xw-conformance --test vwp the VWP v1 checklist (§10), one test per item crates/v2xw-record/tests/byte_identity.rs replayed frames equal live frames

items.title: Validation and conformance tools
items.text:
Two kinds of independent checking sit beside the engine's own tests (Building and testing):

  • Rust validation suites (crates/v2xw-netval, crates/v2xw-trafficval) that hold each model to a reference outside the crate that implements it, and prove each check can fail by running it again with a named fault injected.
  • Python tools under tools/ that check the engine's wire output with code that shares nothing with the Rust: their own ASN.1 compiler and codec, their own elliptic curve and certificate arithmetic, written from the standards.

The rule every tool keeps

A check is trusted only once it has been seen to fail. Each suite or tool below has a faulted mode (Mode::Faulted, --mutate, --inject, oracle.py mutate), or is driven by tools/mutate/mutate.py.

items.title: Python environment
items.text:
The tools run with python3 -I (isolated mode, so nothing in the working directory is imported). The ones that decode PDUs need the oracle's pinned packages:

python3 -m venv .venv-oracle
.venv-oracle/bin/pip install -r tools/oracle/requirements.txt   # asn1tools, cryptography, mcap, PyYAML

The tools that need no packages say "standard library" below.

items.title: v2xw-netval: the network stack
items.text:
Every layer of the network simulation against its reference: the physical layer against published equations, distributions and receiver tables; access against IEEE 802.11 / ETSI EN 302 663, ETSI TS 102 687, SAE J2945/1 and the 3GPP sidelink procedures; the network layer and messages against their header tables and an independent decoder; the security envelope against OpenSSL; whole runs against conservation, metamorphic and determinism properties and an independent reference implementation.

Layer (Layer) Modules Physical phy, linklevel Access access, sps, etsi Network net Security sec End to end e2e, differential

Each Check runs in Mode::Honest (must pass) and Mode::Faulted (a named, realistic fault such as a rounded constant, a misread table row or a backoff counter that restarts instead of freezing; must fail). The fault is injected at the boundary between model and check, so no rebuild per fault is needed. A check that passes with its fault in place is reported as unable to fail.

cargo run --release -p v2xw-netval --bin netval-report             # writes target/validation/network.md
cargo run --release -p v2xw-netval --bin netval-report -- --quick  # leaves out the checks that run the engine
cargo run --release -p v2xw-netval --bin netval-report -- --only <ID,...>   # prints, writes nothing

The exit status is non-zero when any check fails or cannot fail. A check that needs a missing external tool reports Skip with the reason.

items.title: v2xw-trafficval: traffic and mobility
items.text:
Group Module Holds model model IDM, MOBIL, gap acceptance and social force against their papers; the ring fundamental diagram; string stability; the Sugiyama ring calibration calib saturation flow, start-up lost time, speeds and accelerations, turning, critical gaps, pedestrians and motorcycles against published measurements safety safety time-to-collision and post-encroachment time, SSAM thresholds, conflicts per vehicle-kilometre invariants invariants, nema_safety the traffic auditor's classes at zero on every shipped scenario and at peak density; metamorphic properties; no conflicting greens and no red entry under the NEMA dual ring cities cities Manhattan, Portland and Berlin import and run with the auditor clean

Each check runs as shipped (its tested rows inside their bands) and with a fault injected (at least one row must leave its band). A row no fault turned red is reported as not proved. Wall-clock time goes to the terminal only, so two runs write the same report.

cargo run --release -p v2xw-trafficval --bin traffic_validation -- [--quick] [--only SUBSTR] \
    [--out target/validation/traffic.md] [--json FILE] [--list]
cargo run --release -p v2xw-trafficval --bin traffic_calibration -- [--quick] [--out FILE]

traffic_calibration writes target/validation/traffic-calibration.md: fundamental diagrams on a city ring and a freeway ring (Greenshields and triangular fits, capacity against HCM 6th ed. Exhibit 12-6), stop-and-go wave speed, headways, the human-driver population, the IDM rest gap and string stability against theory, the Sugiyama ring, and each figure beside SUMO's default driver (Krauss, σ = 0.5). It exits 1 when a held figure leaves its band.

just validation-report [--quick] runs both report binaries. The city checks need the city extracts (worlds/fetch.sh <id>).

items.title: The SCMS oracle (tools/oracle)
items.text:
An independent implementation of the IEEE 1609.2 / 1609.2.1 codec and cryptography, written from the standards without reading the Rust. Everything else in this page that decodes a PDU uses it.

Part Contents asn1/ the committed ASN.1 modules: ieee1609.2-2022, ieee1609.2.1-2022, ieee1609.3 scms_oracle/coer.py asn1tools COER over those modules scms_oracle/{ec,prims,ecqv,butterfly,linkage}.py ECDSA, ECQV as profiled by 1609.2, butterfly key expansion, linkage values scms_oracle/{certs,chain}.py certificate construction and the chain rules scms_oracle/{ctlfiles,real}.py the published SCMS Manager CTL and chain files scms_oracle/{faults,emit,corpus,records,time1609}.py named faults, vector emission, corpora, MCAP records, 1609.2 time transcribe/ run once by hand: transcribes the IEEE 1609.2a, CAMP, NIST CAVP and RFC 4231 vectors into crates/v2xw-sec/tests/vectors, each value with its citation and the source's sha256 (values only; the source texts are not redistributable) 
.venv-oracle/bin/python -I tools/oracle/oracle.py selftest        # reproduce every vector in crates/v2xw-sec/tests/vectors
.venv-oracle/bin/python -I tools/oracle/oracle.py mutate          # each named fault must turn its target checks red
.venv-oracle/bin/python -I tools/oracle/oracle.py emit [--out DIR]   # write oracle vectors for the Rust tests
.venv-oracle/bin/python -I tools/oracle/oracle.py verify-emitted  # recompute the emitted files byte for byte
.venv-oracle/bin/python -I tools/oracle/oracle.py coer TYPE HEX   # decode and re-encode one value (canonical check)

items.title: Codec and certificate cross-checks
items.text:
Tool Proves Run asn1-xcheck/xcheck.py the generated rasn bindings in v2xw-msg and an independent codec (asn1tools, its own parser and X.696 OER encoder) agree byte for byte in both directions on random values of every 1609.2 / 1609.2.1 type xcheck.py gen OUT [--n 200] [--seed N] writes TypeName HEX lines that crates/v2xw-msg/tests/scms_coer_xcheck.rs decodes and re-encodes; xcheck.py verify IN checks lines Rust wrote; xcheck.py diff-editions prints the code-level differences between the 2022 and 2025 module editions chain-xcheck/chain_xcheck.py the Rust chain validator (v2xw_sec::chain::validate) gives the oracle's verdict on random certificate chains, and re-issues byte-identical certificates chain_xcheck.py gen OUT [--n 500] [--seed N] writes crates/v2xw-sec/tests/vectors/xcheck/chains.json, read by crates/v2xw-sec/tests/chain_xcheck.rs; verify OUT regenerates and compares scms-artefacts/xcheck_crl.py the Rust-emitted CRL and CTL vectors (crates/v2xw-sec/tests/crl_ctl_vectors.rs) decode, verify and match under the oracle's own COER, hashing, ECDSA and linkage code xcheck_crl.py [DIR] pki_view/check_jer.py the PKI view's JER rendering of each SPDU layer (inspect.pdu) equals asn1tools' JER of an independent OER decode V2XW_PKI_OUT=<dir> cargo test -p v2xw-proto --test pki_view, then check_jer.py <dir>

Limits stated by the tools: asn1tools implements BASIC-OER, so canonical rules are checked by byte equality in both directions; open types are encoded per X.696 §30 by a patch in xcheck.py; WITH COMPONENTS and CONTAINING constraints are enforced by neither codec. chain_xcheck.py generates chains only where the oracle's rules are complete; the rest (chains longer than 8, bitmap SSPs, sub-region containment, certRequestPermissions, duplicate PSIDs) is covered by Rust negative tests.

items.title: PDU checkers
items.text:
Each Rust test writes a corpus when its environment variable is set; the Python driver decodes and verifies every PDU in it with the oracle and prints one verdict line.

Driver Corpus Checks pdu_check/check_pdus.py V2XW_PDU_OUT=<dir> cargo test -p v2xw-proto --test pdu_layer every 1609.2.1 SPDU of the provisioning flows: canonical COER of each layer, protocol and PDU versions, PSID 35 header, signer chains (explicit and ECQV-implicit) to the emitted PKI, signatures, ECIES and AES-CCM to the RA pdu_check/check_appcerts.py V2XW_APPCERT_OUT=<dir> cargo test -p v2xw-proto --test appcert the RSU application and OBU identification certificate exchange, including re-derived certificate keys pdu_check/check_mbr.py V2XW_PDU_OUT=<dir> cargo test -p v2xw-proto --test mbr corpus_for_the_oracle US misbehaviour reports: encrypted to the MA certificate, signed by the reporter's pseudonym certificate, PSID 0x26, payload decoded with pdu_check/asn1/CvpdMbdWire.asn pdu_check/check_run_crl.py V2XW_PDU_OUT=<dir> cargo test -p v2xw-proto --test crl_issuance a_revocation_publishes issued SecuredCrls: signer, CrlSsp, CRACA, series, and linkage-CRL matching revokes exactly the revoked certificates pdu_check/mutate_rules.py as check_pdus.py / check_appcerts.py fault injection for the rule checks those drivers added: each fault, applied after the signature checks, must turn the verdict red conformance/check_run.py V2XW_CONFORMANCE_OUT=<dir> cargo test -p v2xw-engine --test conformance every PDU of a whole engine run (the capture is the recording plus the recipients' private keys): canonical COER, signed and encrypted layers, chains to a CTL the tool verified itself, signer roles. --mutate runs its faults; --json OUT writes the findings pki_view/aca_blindness.py a run directory the RA strips the enrolment identity before the ACA (IEEE 1609.2.1 §4.1.3): no ACA-bound PDU contains an enrolment certificate or its HashedId8. --inject plants one and the leak count must rise

Independence

The primitives in every driver are the oracle's. check_run.py's rules were derived from the ASN.1 modules and the design specification only, without reading the Rust that builds the PDUs. The pdu_check/ drivers' rules were written alongside the Rust they test, so only their primitives are independent; their headers say so.

items.title: tools/mutate/mutate.py
items.text:
Injects one fault into a source file, runs a command, restores the file and sets its modification time to now, so the next cargo build recompiles the restored source (a restored copy with an old mtime would leave cargo linking the faulted build).

python3 -I tools/mutate/mutate.py <file> '<old>' '<new>' -- cargo test -p <crate> --test <t> <filter>

<old> must occur exactly once. It prints RED (the check failed, so it can fail), GREEN (the fault was not caught) or RESTORE FAILED, and exits 0 only for RED.

items.title: Extending: detectors
items.text:
A local misbehaviour detector runs on each receiver, judges every delivered message against what that receiver believes, and produces a verdict that the node turns into a misbehaviour report. This page walks through examples/detector-heading-rate, then shows where the engine's own suites are wired so a new suite can be added. Model background: Threats and misbehaviour detection. Card and registration rules: Extending: models.

flowchart LR
    RX["delivered message<br/>(verified by the node)"] --> OBS["ObservedMessage<br/>+ SelfBelief + LocalEnvironment"]
    OBS --> DET["Detector::on_message"]
    DET --> V["Verdict<br/>subject, fingerprint, fired"]
    DET --> R1["det.observation record"]
    V --> MBR["MisbehaviourReport::from_verdict"]
    MBR --> MA["Misbehaviour Authority<br/>(detection.ma)"]

items.title: The trait
items.text:
v2xw_threat::detect::Detector (re-exported as v2xw_threat::Detector):

pub trait Detector: Model {
    fn on_message(
        &mut self,
        ctx: &mut dyn ThreatCtx,
        me: &SelfBelief,
        m: &ObservedMessage,
        env: &dyn LocalEnvironment,
    ) -> Verdict;

    fn cost(&self) -> DetectorCost;     // DetectorCost { per_message_us }
}

There is no world, actor id or true position in the signature: a detector cannot ask for ground truth because the argument types carry none.

items.title: Inputs
items.text: Argument Type (v2xw_threat::obs, ctx) What it holds ctx ThreatCtx now() (simulated time, for record timestamps only), rng(domain, entity) (keyed stream), emit(record) me SelfBelief the receiver's own node id, believed_time (its own clock), believed position, radio range m ObservedMessage signer (the certificate HashedId8, the only identity a receiver has), kind, received_at, claimed_generation_time, claimed position, speed, heading and broadcast position confidence, repetitions in this interval, the certificate validity window, the declared station_type, BSM extras (secMark, accelSet.long), and verification (what the node concluded about the signature) env LocalEnvironment the node's own map store: distance_to_road_m(x, y). A node with no map passes NoMap, whose answer is that every point is on the road

items.title: The verdict
items.text:
Field Meaning subject the signer digest in hex (m.signer_hex()) fingerprint every check's score, indexed by DetectorId (the detnorm_* columns a fusion model reads) fired the checks that fired, as Observation { detector, score, subject, at }, highest score first; fired() and leading() read it

Scores are normalised so that 1 is the firing threshold in every check, which is what lets checks in metres, degrees and seconds be compared and fused.

items.title: Walkthrough: detector-heading-rate
items.text:
A vehicle cannot turn arbitrarily fast. The detector keeps the last heading each signer claimed and scores the change over the interval the two beacons claim to span:

\[ \text{score} = \frac{\lvert \angle(\psi_\text{now} - \psi_\text{before}) \rvert}{\Delta\psi_\text{max}} \] 
impl v2xw_threat::Detector for HeadingRate {
    fn on_message(&mut self, ctx: &mut dyn ThreatCtx, me: &SelfBelief,
                  m: &ObservedMessage, _env: &dyn LocalEnvironment) -> Verdict {
        let subject = m.signer_hex();
        let mut fingerprint = Fingerprint::default();
        let mut fired = Vec::new();

        // 1. gate: beacons only, attributable (valid signature), fast enough to have a heading
        if !(matches!(m.kind, ObservedKind::Beacon)
             && m.verification.is_valid()
             && m.claimed_speed_mps >= self.params.min_speed_mps) {
            return Verdict { subject, fingerprint, fired };
        }
        // 2. interval from the *claimed* generation times (the sender's own timeline)
        // 3. score, quantised onto its 1e-3 grid BEFORE the threshold comparison
        let score = self.score(last.heading_rad, m.claimed_heading_rad);
        fingerprint.set(DetectorId::HeadingInconsistency, score);
        if score >= 1.0 && streak >= self.params.min_consecutive {
            fired.push(Observation { detector: DetectorId::HeadingInconsistency, score,
                                     subject: subject.clone(), at: me.believed_time });
            let host_now = ctx.now();
            ctx.emit(v2xw_threat::DetObservation { t: host_now, node: me.node,
                detector: MODEL_ID.to_string(), subject: subject.clone(), score: Some(score) });
        }
        // 4. remember this beacon per signer (a BTreeMap, never a HashMap)
        Verdict { subject, fingerprint, fired }
    }
    fn cost(&self) -> DetectorCost { DetectorCost { per_message_us: 1.0 } }
}

Rules this example demonstrates:

Rule In the code belief, never truth the argument types; no world is reachable decisions on the node's clock thresholds compare me.believed_time and claimed times; ctx.now() only stamps the emitted record so channels share one timeline quantise before comparing math::quantize_to(change_deg / max_heading_change_deg, 1e-3), so a last-bit difference in a transcendental cannot flip a firing between platforms no content check on an unattributable message gate on m.verification.is_valid(); a bad signature is not the signer's claim abstain, don't score zero, when an input is missing a first beacon from a signer, or claims out of order, produce no score transcendentals through v2xw_core::math math::sin_cos, math::atan2 in angle_difference_rad declared cost cost() is charged against the node's CPU budget; the value is on the card with a calibration plan

Its card follows Extending: models, with Family::Detector and the id example/detector/heading-rate.

Check names are a closed set

Verdict names checks with DetectorId, a closed enumeration of the engine's own checks (PositionSpeedInconsistency, PositionJump, HeadingInconsistency, StaleOrReplay, ConstantPositionFrozen, ImplausibleAcceleration, SybilCoLocation, AcceptanceRangeThreshold, BeaconFrequency, SignatureVerification, CertValidity, MapOffRoad, VruImpersonation, DenmPlausibility, KalmanConsistency, ImplausibleSpeed, BrakeAcceleration). A new check must report under the nearest existing id (the example uses HeadingInconsistency) or add a variant. The det.observation record carries the detector name as a string, so it can name a new detector.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
Use v2xw_threat::CollectingCtx as the host: it owns an RngRegistry and keeps every emitted record, so a test asserts on the same numbers and records the engine would see. The example also exposes beacon(...) and belief(...) helpers to build inputs.

Then run the plug-in conformance suite (v2xw-conformance as a dev-dependency, path tests/conformance). The example's conformance module is the template:

impl PluginUnderTest for Subject {
    fn model(&self) -> &dyn Model { &self.model }
    fn entities(&self) -> Vec<EntityRef> {               // a detector acts for a node
        vec![EntityRef::Node(NodeId::new(1)), EntityRef::Node(NodeId::new(2))]
    }
    fn exercise(&self, ctx: &mut ProbeCtx, e: EntityRef) -> Vec<f64> {
        let mut detector = HeadingRate::with_defaults();  // fresh per call: exercise is &self
        /* script six beacons with ctx.set_now(t), return each fingerprint score */
    }
    fn sources(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> { vec![PathBuf::from(file!())] }
    fn quantum(&self) -> f64 { SCORE_QUANTUM }
    fn runs_as_node(&self) -> bool { true }   // emitted records must not carry ground truth
}

#[test]
fn the_conformance_suite_passes() {
    assert!(run_suite(&Subject::new(), 0x5EED).complete());
}

report.passed() tolerates a check the suite could not run; report.complete() requires every check to have run (it needs sources() and quantum()).

cd examples && cargo test -p v2xw-example-detector

items.title: From verdict to report
items.text: v2xw_threat::report::MisbehaviourReport::from_verdict(report_id, reporter, reporter_cert_digest, &verdict, &evidence) returns None when nothing fired; otherwise a report whose reason_codes and detector_outputs are the fired checks, whose subject is the signer digest, and whose floats are quantised at construction. Every identity in it is a pseudonym certificate digest. The engine batches reports per reporter at the report interval (REPORT_INTERVAL_S = 1 s by default, report_interval_s in the suite's params) and submits them through the credential protocol to the MA pipeline (detection.ma). Records: det.observation (per firing), the MA report records, and the MA's decisions (Metrics and outputs).

items.title: Adding a suite the engine runs
items.text:
detection.local[] accepts exactly the suites compiled into the engine, all in crates/v2xw-engine/src/phase2.rs:

Id Suite Notes detect/legacy-12 v2xw_threat::detect::Legacy12 the research suite detect/us-sm-mbr v2xw_threat::us_mbr::UsSmMbr the strict US misbehaviour profile; the default under the US SCMS deployment when detection.local is empty detect/ts103759 v2xw_threat::ts103759::Ts103759Suite the ETSI TS 103 759 observations; must be listed alone

Any other id is refused at load with an error naming detection.local[i]. To add one:

  1. Implement Detector in v2xw-threat (or a crate the engine depends on), with a card.
  2. In phase2.rs: add an id constant beside LEGACY_12; accept it and parse its params in detection_params (refuse unknown keys with an error naming detection.local[i].params.<key>); add a LocalSuite variant and build it in Phase2::local_suite; dispatch it in LocalSuite::on_message; and return its id from local_suite_id.
  3. Register its card in the engine's catalogue so the slot lists it with its parameters (scenario::publish's catalogue registers the TS 103 759 card this way).
  4. Add a same-seed engine test that selecting it changes the reports, and run just docs-gen.

Python detectors

A Python object can stand behind the Detector family through python/v2xw/plugins.py, called once per window with an Arrow record batch. See Plugins.

items.title: Extending: metrics
items.text:
A metric provider reads recorded channels and turns them into metric.sample values with units, sample counts and intervals. This page walks through examples/metric-detector-load, then covers registration, health direction and the invariant checks. What each shipped metric means: Metrics and outputs. Card rules: Extending: models.

flowchart LR
    REC["recorded records<br/>(OwnedRecord per channel)"] --> PS["ProviderSet<br/>dispatch by channel (BTreeMap)"]
    PS --> P["MetricProvider::on_event / on_decoded"]
    CLK["Observe event every<br/>time.metric_period_s"] --> F["MetricProvider::flush(at)"]
    P --> F
    F --> S["MetricSample<br/>quantised, with n and interval"]
    S --> SUM["RunSummary, metrics.json,<br/>metric digest"]

items.title: The trait
items.text:
v2xw_metrics::MetricProvider (in crates/v2xw-metrics/src/provider.rs):

pub trait MetricProvider: Model {
    fn defs(&self) -> Vec<MetricDef>;                 // the metrics it computes
    fn subscribe(&self) -> Vec<ChannelName>;          // the channels it reads
    fn on_event(&mut self, ev: &EventRecord);         // one record, in run order
    fn flush(&mut self, at: SimTime) -> Vec<MetricSample>; // close the window ending at `at`

    // defaulted
    fn on_decoded(&mut self, ev: &Decoded<'_>) { self.on_event(ev.record()) }
    fn on_pause(&mut self, from: SimTime, to: SimTime) {}   // a time.fast_forward window
    fn rejected(&self) -> u64 { 0 }                        // records it could not decode
    fn validate_defs(&self) -> Result<()>;                 // MetricDef::validate on each def
    fn def(&self, name: &str) -> Option<MetricDef>;
}
Rule Why read channels, never engine state a metric computed live and from a recording must agree; there is no world in the signature flush drains per-window accumulators flushing twice at one instant gives the samples once, then an empty or insufficient set. Whole-run accumulators (a revocation's stage times, a confusion matrix) are not drained; say which is which in the definition count what you cannot decode on_event returns (); increment a counter and return it from rejected(). ProviderSet::rejected_total puts the sum in the manifest integers for counts and bytes accumulate as u64; floats only in the final estimate

Windows close on the engine's Observe events, every time.metric_period_s (1 s when unset).

items.title: Declaring a metric: MetricDef
items.text:
MetricDef::new(REPEAT_SHARE, "ratio",
        Agg::ratio("observations about a (node, subject) pair already seen in this window",
                   "observations after the first sighting of each pair"),
        Visibility::Node, Quantum::RATIO,
        "Of the observations one detector produced in the window, the share that ...")
    .with_dims([Dim::T, Dim::Detector])
    .with_source(source)
    .with_min_samples(self.min_samples)
    .not_accounting_for("whether any subject was really misbehaving: that is ground truth ...")
    .not_accounting_for("repeats across windows ...")
Field Meaning name stable name (pdr, verify_rate, ...); what a scenario's metrics: list and every export use unit ratio, ms, B/s, 1/s, s, veh/h, count, ... dims the closed Dim set: T, node, vehicle class, distance bin, density bin, region, protocol, RAT, tier, run, and per-metric dimensions such as cause, channel, detector. A new Dim is a schema change agg Sum, Mean, Max, Count, Quantile, Ratio { numerator, denominator }, Rate, Distribution visibility v2xw_core::ctx::Visibility; a metric derived from a ground-truth channel is Gt, and the tag propagates into every export definition_md the definition and formula, in Markdown source the citation, where one exists quantum the grid the writer quantises every value onto (Quantum::RATIO, Quantum::COUNT, ...) min_samples below this many samples the value is reported insufficient, not as a point estimate not_accounted what the number excludes; must be non-empty min_value, max_value the physically possible range (zero for a latency, one for a proportion), checked by invariants::check_metric_ranges breakdown, breakdown_only one dimension a live view shows as its own series, with the values it will take health filled by MetricDef::new from health::band_for(name) diagnostic a machine-dependent runtime figure, excluded from every digest

MetricDef::validate refuses an empty name, unit or definition, an empty not_accounted, a quantile outside [0, 1], a ratio without numerator or denominator text, an empty range, a breakdown on an undeclared dimension, and a duplicated dimension.

items.title: Producing values: MetricSample and stats
items.text:
Build samples with MetricSample::new(&def, at, dims, value); it carries the definition's unit, quantum, visibility and aggregation. The value is a SampleValue:

Variant Build it with Use for Count { .. } SampleValue::count(n) an exact integer count; never quantised, never insufficient (zero events is a measurement) Ratio(RatioEstimate) stats::Proportion::estimate(min_trials, level) a proportion with its Wilson interval, or Insufficient below min_trials Ratio(RatioEstimate::RatioOfSums { .. }) stats::ratio_of_sums(num, den, n, min_n) a ratio of sums (bytes per message, ...), deliberately without an interval Distribution(DistributionSummary) stats::Distribution::observe(x), then .summary(min_samples) percentiles, extremes, mean, with the interpolation rule Scalar(Estimate) Distribution::mean, Distribution::sum a scalar with its sample count, or a refusal

Never compute an interval yourself: stats::wilson_interval is the one implementation. Three firings out of four is not 75 %.

items.title: Walkthrough: metric-detector-load
items.text:
Two metrics over det.observation, per detector:

Metric Shape Says example_det_firings count observations the detector produced in the window example_det_repeat_share proportion with Wilson interval share of those about a subject the same node had already flagged in this window 
impl MetricProvider for DetectorLoad {
    fn defs(&self) -> Vec<MetricDef> { vec![self.def(FIRINGS), self.def(REPEAT_SHARE)] }

    fn subscribe(&self) -> Vec<ChannelName> {
        vec![DetObservationView::channel_name()]   // from the record type: cannot be misspelled
    }

    fn on_event(&mut self, ev: &EventRecord) {
        if ev.channel != DetObservationView::CHANNEL { return; }
        match decode::<DetObservationView>(ev) {
            Ok(view) => self.observe(view.node, &view.detector, &view.subject),
            Err(_) => self.rejected += 1,           // counted, never swallowed
        }
    }

    fn flush(&mut self, at: SimTime) -> Vec<MetricSample> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (detector, window) in core::mem::take(&mut self.windows) {   // drain = windowed
            let mut dims = Dims::new();
            dims.insert(Dim::Detector, DimValue::label(detector));
            out.push(MetricSample::new(&self.def(FIRINGS), at, dims.clone(),
                                       SampleValue::count(window.firings)));
            out.push(MetricSample::new(&self.def(REPEAT_SHARE), at, dims,
                SampleValue::Ratio(window.repeats.estimate(self.min_samples, self.level))));
        }
        out
    }

    fn rejected(&self) -> u64 { self.rejected }
}

Both metrics are Visibility::Node because det.observation is node-visible. The accounting lives in a plain method (observe) so tests can feed typed values without building JSON records. Per-window state is in a BTreeMap.

det.observation is opt-in

The engine records det.observation only when the scenario's metrics: list names the detection-scores group or one of its metrics, so a provider over it sees records only in such runs.

items.title: Register it
items.text:
pub fn register(registry: &mut Registry, set: &mut ProviderSet)
    -> v2xw_metrics::Result<ModelRef> {
    set.register(registry, Box::new(DetectorLoad::new()))
}

ProviderSet::register validates the card and every MetricDef, registers the card in the Registry (a provider is mutated on every event, so the live object stays in the set and Registry::get_model answers None for it), and indexes the provider by channel.

In the engine, crates/v2xw-engine/src/wiring.rs builds a run's set in build_metrics_for:

Provider group Installed when v2xw_metrics::register_all: comms, latency, awareness, load, overhead, frag, security, detection, safety, runtime metrics: [all], or a named list containing one of the provider's metric names energy (v2xw_energy::EnergyProvider) the scenario has an energy: section, or names one of its metrics signing (v2xw_metrics::signing) metrics names signing or a sig_* metric traffic control (v2xw_metrics::traffic) the scenario has a traffic: section, or names the group or a metric detection scores metrics names detection-scores or one of its metrics

A named metrics: list selects by metric name: a provider is installed when it defines at least one metric the scenario asked for. A new built-in provider goes into register_all (part of all) or behind an opt-in group in build_metrics_for; an opt-in keeps the digests of existing all scenarios unchanged.

metrics: [all]                      # every provider in register_all
metrics: [pdr, cbr, e2e_latency]    # only the providers that define these
metrics: [all, signing]             # all plus an opt-in group

items.title: Health direction and bands
items.text:
Table File Read by HealthBand per metric name: which direction is better, the caution and unhealthy thresholds, three one-line notes, the source and its basis (standard, literature, engineering) crates/v2xw-metrics/src/health.rs, band_for MetricDef::health, the Studio's cards, the run summary, the assistant's analyst direction only, for metrics without a band: BANDED, HIGHER, NEUTRAL, and name hints (recall, delivery, ...) crates/v2xw-metrics/src/polarity.rs the server's run comparison, the Studio

A band's judged suffix says which series it applies to ("" the headline, .p99 a percentile, [100m] a breakdown value). A band is a judgement about the acceptable, not the possible range (that is min_value/max_value). For a headline metric, add a band with its source, or a direction in polarity.rs. The Studio reads ui/apps/studio/src/metrics/polarity.generated.json; regenerate it with:

V2XW_REGEN_POLARITY=1 cargo test -p v2xw-metrics polarity

The test studio_table_is_current fails when the file is stale.

items.title: Invariant checks
items.text:
v2xw_metrics::invariants holds runnable checks over an EventLedger built from the same records, each returning the subject and the numbers of every violation:

Check Holds check_i_r3 every lost frame has exactly one cause, every received frame none; busy time at least own airtime check_i_n1 every byte is attributed to exactly one bucket check_i_n2 a fragmenter's card documents its reassembly timeout and loss amplification check_i_m1 mobility output within a step is ordered by actor id check_i_p4 revocation stage timestamps are emitted in order check_i_t2 no record carries a visibility its channel may not carry; nothing ground-truth on a node channel check_i_t3 every attack action that changed bytes is on a ground-truth channel and matches a transmission check_i_s1 modelled and real crypto give identical outcomes and sizes check_i_c1 two runs emit byte-identical records check_d9_quantisation every sample value is finite and on its grid check_m_*, check_metric_ranges reception, delivery, latency, byte and share consistency; values inside min_value/max_value

check_all(&ledger, &samples) runs them; a check with no data reports skipped with the reason. A new metric gets check_metric_ranges for free from its declared range; a new accounting rule gets its own check here.

items.title: Test it
items.text:
#[test]
fn the_card_validates_and_so_does_every_definition() {
    card(v2xw_metrics::stats::DEFAULT_MIN_SAMPLES).validate().expect("the card must validate");
    DetectorLoad::new().validate_defs().expect("every definition must validate");
}

Then: feed records and assert on the flushed samples (one subject flagged repeatedly is all repeats; distinct subjects are none), flush twice and check the second is empty, feed a malformed record and check rejected(), and show each test fails when its rule is broken.

cd examples && cargo test -p v2xw-example-metric

items.title: Extending: models
items.text:
A model is an object that implements one family trait and carries a model card. This page walks through adding one, using the two worked examples in examples/: propagation-log-distance (a radio model that draws randomness) and carfollowing-constant-time-gap (a pure mobility model). The rules every extension keeps are on Conventions; the overview of every extension point is Extending.

flowchart LR
    A["1. implement the<br/>family trait + Model"] --> B["2. build the card"]
    B --> C["3. register<br/>Registry::register_model"]
    C --> D["4. test, incl. the<br/>plug-in conformance suite"]
    D --> E["5. make it selectable<br/>from a scenario slot"]

items.title: 1. Implement the family trait
items.text:
Every family trait extends v2xw_core::model::Model, whose one required method returns the card. A registered model therefore always has a card, and the card is reachable from the live object.

pub trait Model {
    fn card(&self) -> &ModelCard;            // required
    fn tiers(&self) -> &[Tier];              // from the card
    fn implements_tier(&self, tier: Tier) -> bool;
    fn id(&self) -> &str;
    fn version(&self) -> &str;
    fn family(&self) -> Family;
    fn id_at_version(&self) -> String;       // "id@version", how scenarios and manifests name it
}

Model is dyn-compatible; the registry stores a ModelHandle = Arc<dyn Model + Send + Sync>, so a model must be Send + Sync (no Rc, Cell or thread-local state).

Family (v2xw_core::card::Family) Trait propagation, fading, obstacle, phy, mac, dcc v2xw_radio::traits::{Propagation, Fading, ObstacleModel, Phy, Mac, Dcc} mobility, vru, gnss, clock v2xw_mobility::traits::{CarFollowing, LaneChange, IntersectionControl, Router, Demand, VruMobility, GnssModel, ClockModel} net, fragmenter v2xw_net::netlayer::NetLayer, v2xw_net::frag::Fragmenter codec v2xw_msg::codec::MessageCodec crypto-backend v2xw_sec::crypto::CryptoBackend verification-policy, service-model, safety-app v2xw_node::policy::VerificationPolicy, v2xw_node::server::ServiceModel, v2xw_node::safety::SafetyApp attacker, detector, ma-pipeline v2xw_threat::attack::Attacker, v2xw_threat::detect::Detector, v2xw_threat::ma::MaPipeline (detectors) metric v2xw_metrics::MetricProvider (metrics) emission, energy v2xw_energy::traits::{EmissionModel, EvEnergyModel} protocol (threshold) v2xw_proto::threshold::ThresholdProtocol (template: crates/v2xw-proto/src/threshold/template.rs)

Family is closed: a new family means a new trait, a new variant, a conformance suite and a Python base class.

items.title: The propagation example
items.text:
impl<C: Ctx + ?Sized> Propagation<C> for LogDistance {
    fn tier(&self) -> Tier { self.tier }

    fn loss_db(&mut self, ctx: &mut C, tx: &RadioEndpoint, rx: &RadioEndpoint,
               f_hz: f64, _los: &LosResult, _w: &WeatherState) -> LossBreakdown {
        let d = tx.pos.distance(rx.pos);
        let path = self.params.path_loss_db(d, f_hz);           // uses v2xw_core::math::log10
        let shadow = if self.params.shadowing_sigma_db > 0.0 {
            let link = LinkKey(tx.node, rx.node);                 // directed: (a,b) != (b,a)
            ctx.rng(RngDomain::Shadow, EntityRef::Link(link))
                .normal(0.0, self.params.shadowing_sigma_db)
        } else { 0.0 };
        LossBreakdown::new(path, shadow, 0.0, 0.0, tx.gain_dbi + rx.gain_dbi)
    }
}

It computes \(PL(d) = PL_0 + 10\,n\,\log_{10}(d/d_0) + X_\sigma\), \(X_\sigma \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)\), with \(PL_0\) the Friis loss at \(d_0 = 10\) m. Points to copy:

  • Randomness only from the context. ctx.rng(domain, entity) checks out a keyed stream; the key (Shadow, this directed link) makes the draw independent of event order, other links and thread count. Never own a generator.
  • Transcendentals through v2xw_core::math (math::log10, not f64::log10).
  • No per-call state unless keyed in a BTreeMap by entity; the model stays Sync.
  • The arithmetic is callable without an engine (LogDistanceParams::path_loss_db), so tests can assert on the equation directly.
  • Ignored inputs are named (_los, _w) and listed on the card's ignores.

items.title: The car-following example
items.text:
impl CarFollowing for ConstantTimeGap {
    fn accel(&self, ego: &VehicleView, leader: Option<&LeaderView>,
             lane: &LaneView, w: &WeatherState) -> f64 { /* ... */ }
}

\(e = g - (s_0 + T v)\); following: \(a = k_\text{position}\, e + k_\text{speed} (v_\text{lead} - v)\); free road: \(a = k_\text{free} (v_0 - v)\), clamped to the driver's comfortable limits. accel takes no context: a car-following model must be pure, and driver heterogeneity (T, s0, a_max, b) arrives per vehicle in a DriverProfile (CarFollowing::profile). A stop line, signal or junction arrives as a virtual leader. Optional hooks: begin_step(now, dt) for discrete-time models and cooperative() for models that read V2X.

items.title: 2. Build the card
items.text:
v2xw_core::card::ModelCard; read the example's card() function before the model.

Field Content id family/name, matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(/[a-z0-9-]+)*$; never changed once published. The examples use an example/ prefix family, version, api_version the Family; the model's semver (bump it when the numbers change); v2xw_core::card::API_VERSION (1.0.0) tier non-empty list of abstract, medium, high purpose one paragraph equations Equation { name, latex_or_text, notes } parameters Parameter { name, unit, default, range, source, calibration }: every number the model reads assumptions, limitations, ignores lists of sentences; what a reader of a result checks first sources Source { kind, ref, accessed, note }; kind is standard, paper, datasheet, dataset, code or todo-calibrate validation status (unvalidated, unit-tested, literature-checked, field-checked), references, test names determinism uses_rng and the rng_domains drawn from; the conformance suite checks the declaration against what the model drew cost optional per-call cost class

ModelCard::validate (run by every register* call) refuses:

Error (CardError) When InvalidId the id does not match the pattern EmptyField empty version, api_version, purpose, or no tier DuplicateParameter two parameters share a name DefaultOutOfRange a parameter's default lies outside its own range MissingCalibration a todo-calibrate source without a non-empty calibration plan ApiVersionMismatch api_version is not one this engine implements

A number nobody publishes is declared honestly. The car-following example's three gains are a manufacturer's calibration, so each is Source::todo_calibrate(...) with a calibration plan, and the card says unvalidated:

Parameter {
    calibration: Some(plan.to_string()),
    ..Parameter::new("k_position", "1/s^2", json!(params.k_position),
                     Source::todo_calibrate("proportional gain on the spacing error; ..."))
}

A scenario overrides a parameter by name in params. ParamSet::resolve(card, overrides) merges the overrides over the card's defaults and refuses an unknown name, a JSON type different from the default's, or a value outside the declared range.

items.title: 3. Register it
items.text:
pub fn register(registry: &mut Registry) -> Result<ModelRef, RegistryError> {
    let model: ModelHandle = Arc::new(LogDistance::medium());
    registry.register_model(model)
}
Call Use Registry::register(card) card only (catalogue entry, no live object) Registry::register_model(handle) the live model; the card is taken from it, so they cannot disagree register_with_licence, register_model_with_licence in process under a declared licence; refuses a copyleft or unknown licence (LicenceRequiresOutOfProcess) register_out_of_process, register_model_out_of_process a model that runs in its own process, any licence

Registration validates the card, checks the API version, refuses a duplicate id with a different card, hashes the card's canonical bytes (the content hash the run manifest pins) and stores it. Registry::get_model_by_id and resolve find it again.

items.title: 4. Test it
items.text:
Each example's tests are the template. At minimum:

  • card().validate() succeeds and register succeeds;
  • the equation: one assertion that distinguishes the model from its nearest neighbour (the propagation example pins the \(10n\) dB-per-decade slope, which fails at \(n = 2\));
  • a family property (propagation loss never decreases with distance);
  • determinism: two links draw different values, a reversed link is a different link, the same seed reproduces;
  • a test shown to fail: change the value the test is about and watch it go red (tools/mutate/mutate.py automates this).

A propagation model's tests need a Ctx; the example's TestCtx (an RngRegistry, a Scheduler, a ParamSet, a ProvenanceLog) is the smallest one and can be copied.

Then run the plug-in conformance suite from tests/conformance (crate v2xw-conformance):

use v2xw_conformance::plugin::{PluginUnderTest, ProbeCtx, run_suite};

struct Subject(LogDistance);
impl PluginUnderTest for Subject {
    fn model(&self) -> &dyn Model { &self.0 }
    fn entities(&self) -> Vec<EntityRef> { /* two or more */ }
    fn exercise(&self, ctx: &mut ProbeCtx, e: EntityRef) -> Vec<f64> { /* one unit of work */ }
    fn sources(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> { vec![/* your .rs files */] }   // empty = scans unchecked
    fn quantum(&self) -> f64 { 1e-3 }      // the grid every output must sit on
    fn runs_as_node(&self) -> bool { false } // true: no emitted record may carry ground truth
}

let report = run_suite(&Subject(LogDistance::medium()), 0x5EED);
assert!(report.passed(), "{report}");
Property How it is established owns no RNG source scan for rand::, thread_rng, generator types, a second RngRegistry reads no wall clock source scan for the firewall's wall-clock needles reaches no ground truth source scan for the ground-truth needles, plus the visibility of emitted records valid card, every default cited ModelCard::validate plus a source on every parameter deterministic under reordering the entities exercised forwards, backwards and on eight threads, compared value for value outputs quantised every returned value on quantum()

examples/detector-heading-rate wires the suite up in its conformance module.

cd examples && cargo test                       # all four examples
cd examples && cargo test -p v2xw-example-propagation

items.title: 5. Make it selectable
items.text:
Registering puts a model in the registry, the manifest and the published models list. A scenario can select it only where the engine builds that slot from an id, and each slot accepts a fixed set of ids. To add a built-in model to a slot, edit the engine:

Slot Where the id is turned into an object radio.models.<family> (propagation, fading, per, phy, obstacle, sidelink, dcc) crates/v2xw-engine/src/wiring.rs: add the id to RADIO_MODEL_FAMILIES, parse it and its params in radio_models (for propagation, a PropagationChoice variant), and build it in build_radio_at actors.vehicles.driving.car_following / .by_class.* crates/v2xw-mobility/src/carfollowing/library.rs: one CfFactory { id, short, cooperative, build, card } line in FACTORIES; crates/v2xw-engine/src/driving.rs builds what the scenario names detection.local[], threats.attackers[].id, detection.ma crates/v2xw-engine/src/phase2.rs (detectors) net.layer, net.fragmenter, messages.generator, ... the slot's builder in crates/v2xw-engine/src/; the card goes in wiring::register_all metrics v2xw_metrics::register_all (metrics)

The published settings surface reads each slot's selectable ids from the registry through scenario::options::slot_values, so once the card is registered (in wiring::register_all or, for catalogue-only cards, scenario::publish's catalogue) and the slot builds it, the Studio and the generated model reference list it with its parameters. Run just docs-gen to regenerate the reference.

Example scenario use once wired:

actors:
  vehicles:
    driving:
      car_following: { model: krauss }                 # short name or full id
      by_class:
        truck: { model: gipps }
        passenger: { model: cacc-ploeg, share: 0.4 }   # 40 % of cars
radio:
  models:
    propagation: { id: propagation/two-ray-interference, params: { epsilon_r: 1.02 } }

Out-of-tree models are not selectable from a scenario

The slots above accept the ids compiled into the engine. A model in your own crate (like the examples/ crates) registers, validates, hashes and passes the conformance suite, but a scenario cannot name it until the slot's builder in the engine learns its id. See Plugins for what is supported out of tree.

Finally, add a same-seed test that selecting the model changes the run, and a model page entry if it is a new law.

items.title: Extending: plugins
items.text: What can be written outside the engine's own crates, how it registers, and what a scenario can then do with it. The short answer: an out-of-tree Rust or Python model can be written, carded, registered, tested and conformance-checked against the engine's own traits; a scenario can select only the models compiled into the engine's slots, and a Python Misbehaviour Authority policy is the one plug-in that runs inside a full run.

items.title: What is supported
items.text: Extension Where it lives Registers Runs inside v2xw run / the Studio Selected by a model in any family (Rust, out of tree) your crate, depending on v2xw-core and one family crate Registry::register_model no, until a slot builder in the engine names its id (models) n/a a model added to an engine slot (Rust, in tree) a model crate plus the slot's builder in v2xw-engine wiring::register_all / the slot's catalogue yes its id in the slot a signature or KEM scheme crates/v2xw-sec/src/scheme/ (in tree) one line in SIGNATURE_SCHEMES / KEM_SCHEMES yes security.signature, security.kem a threshold protocol crates/v2xw-proto/src/threshold/ (in tree) one line in THRESHOLD_PROTOCOLS yes security.threshold.protocol a Python car-following model your module, subclassing v2xw.plugins.CarFollowing .attach() gives a CarFollowingModel handle no: callable directly and through the conformance kit n/a a Python detector v2xw.plugins.Detector .attach() gives a DetectorModel handle no: callable directly and through the conformance kit n/a a Python MA decision rule v2xw.plugins.MaPolicy passed to v2xw.run(scenario, ma_policy=obj) yes, in a run started from Python the ma_policy argument (a scenario file cannot name it)

items.title: Rust plug-ins: the examples/ workspace
items.text:
examples/ is a separate cargo workspace of four crates, each a real plug-in built the way an out-of-tree crate is: every dependency spelled out with a version (v2xw-core = { path = "../crates/v2xw-core", version = "0.1.0" }), nothing inherited from the root workspace, its own lock file and target directory. Building them never changes the engine's build.

Crate (package) Family Trait Walkthrough propagation-log-distance (v2xw-example-propagation) propagation v2xw_radio::traits::Propagation models carfollowing-constant-time-gap (v2xw-example-carfollowing) mobility v2xw_mobility::traits::CarFollowing models detector-heading-rate (v2xw-example-detector) detector v2xw_threat::Detector detectors metric-detector-load (v2xw-example-metric) metric v2xw_metrics::MetricProvider metrics 
cd examples
cargo test                               # all four
cargo test -p v2xw-example-detector      # one, including the conformance suite

To start your own, copy the closest example to a new crate, change MODEL_ID (keep an example/ or your own prefix so it cannot be mistaken for a shipped model), and keep the dependency table explicit. Add v2xw-conformance (path tests/conformance) as a dev-dependency to run the plug-in suite.

items.title: Registration and licences
items.text:
v2xw_core::registry::Registry validates the card, checks api_version against v2xw_core::card::API_VERSION (1.0.0), refuses a duplicate id with a different card, hashes the card into the manifest's content hash, and applies a licence gate:

Licence In process Apache2, Mit, Bsd, Mpl2, Unspecified allowed (register_model_with_licence) Gpl, Lgpl, Other(..) refused in process (LicenceRequiresOutOfProcess); register with register_out_of_process / register_model_out_of_process

The engine itself is Apache-2.0 and links only Apache-compatible code. Registering out of process records the card and the hosting; no out-of-process host for running such a model ships with the engine.

items.title: A signature or KEM scheme
items.text:
The scheme registry in crates/v2xw-sec/src/scheme/mod.rs is read by the scenario loader, the published schema, the node's signing cost, the over-the-air octets, the fragmenter, the credential system's sizes and charges, and the recorded run, so one entry is the whole change.

  1. Copy crates/v2xw-sec/src/scheme/template.rs (compiled, deliberately unregistered) to scheme/<your_scheme>.rs.

  2. Fill in the SignatureScheme:

    pub const MY_SCHEME: SignatureScheme = SignatureScheme {
    id: "my-scheme",                       // what security.signature names; stable, unique
    label: "My scheme",                    // what the settings window shows
    mode: SchemeMode::PostQuantum,         // Classical, Hybrid or PostQuantum; must match the parts
    parts: &[Part {                        // wire order; sizes and costs add
        primitive: PrimitiveId::ML_DSA_44,
        op_prefix: "ml-dsa-44",            // hardware-profile ops <prefix>-sign/-verify/-keygen
        post_quantum: true,
    }],
    standard: "FIPS 204 (2024)",           // the standard or draft, with clause
    real_crypto: false,                    // true only if crypto::Real executes every part
    defines: None,                         // Some(fn) when a part's primitive is new
    notes: "...",
};

  3. A primitive new to the catalogue gets a fn returning its PrimitiveDescriptor: sizes from the specification, one CostRow per published benchmark with its citation, or a cost_ratio to a sibling with a shared reference platform rather than an invented number. Set defines: Some(that_fn).

  4. In scheme/mod.rs: pub mod <your_scheme>; and one line in SIGNATURE_SCHEMES (or KEM_SCHEMES for a KEM).
  5. cargo test -p v2xw-sec scheme: the registry tests check the id is unique, the mode matches the parts, every part is in the catalogue and every post-quantum part is priced on the V2X hardware profiles.

hybrid_mldsa65.rs is a worked example. Under security.crypto_mode: real the loader accepts only schemes with real_crypto: true.

items.title: A threshold protocol
items.text: Copy crates/v2xw-proto/src/threshold/template.rs: define sign_rounds (one StarRound per online round, with request and response payload sizes, each cited, per-member and coordinator computation, and whether shares are verified), dkg_rounds and refresh_rounds, and the guarantees (identifiable_abort, verifies_as, knowledge). Add ENTRY to THRESHOLD_PROTOCOLS in threshold/mod.rs and run cargo test -p v2xw-proto threshold. security.threshold.protocol then accepts the id.

items.title: Python plug-ins
items.text: python/v2xw/plugins.py (Python half) and crates/v2xw-py/src/plugins.rs (Rust half) put a Python object behind an engine trait. The full API is on Python API.

items.title: The rules
items.text:
A plug-in is a function of its inputs; the engine's reproducibility depends on it:

  1. no randomness of its own (random, numpy.random, secrets, os.urandom): neither family is given a stream, and the card's determinism.uses_rng is always False;
  2. no wall clock (time.time, time.perf_counter, datetime.now); simulated time arrives as an argument;
  3. no platform libm (math.exp, ** on floats, numpy ufuncs): use v2xw.math, the engine's pure-Rust implementation;
  4. no iteration over a set, or a dict keyed by hashed values, where the order reaches a result;
  5. no hidden state between calls (the engine reorders and parallelises).

items.title: Car-following
items.text:
import v2xw
from v2xw.plugins import CarFollowing, card, parameter, source, equation

m = v2xw.math

class Idm(CarFollowing):
    card = card(
        id="mobility/car-following/python-idm", family="mobility", version="1.0.0",
        purpose="Treiber's IDM as a Python plug-in.",
        tier=("abstract",),
        equations=[equation("idm", "a = a_max [1 - (v/v0)^delta - (s*/s)^2]")],
        parameters=[parameter("delta", "-", 4.0,
                              source("paper", "Treiber, Hennecke, Helbing 2000, Eq. 1"))],
    )

    def accel(self, ego, leader, lane, weather):
        # driver parameters arrive on ego: desired_speed_mps, max_accel_mps2,
        # comfort_decel_mps2, time_headway_s, min_gap_m
        ...

model = Idm()
handle = model.attach()                 # a CarFollowingModel: the engine trait object
v2xw.conformance.check(model).raise_for_failures()

card(...) validates immediately, so a bad card fails at its definition. accel is called once per vehicle per mobility step (abstract tier only; one interpreter-lock acquisition per call). A Python exception cannot cross accel's f64 return, so the adapter stores the traceback in last_error and returns NaN, which fails the writer's quantisation check at the first record it reaches. python/examples/python_idm.py is the full example, including a deliberately broken model the kit rejects.

items.title: Detector
items.text:
class SpeedCap(v2xw.plugins.Detector):
    card = v2xw.plugins.card(id="detector/python-speed-cap", family="detector", ...)

    def on_messages(self, ctx, batch):        # ctx: DetectorCtx(t_ns, node)
        # batch: a pyarrow.RecordBatch, one row per received message; read it columnwise
        return [v2xw.plugins.Observation(subject, "speed", confidence, ctx.t_ns), ...]

Called once per window with the whole window, so the per-call cost is amortised. v2xw.plugins.ReferenceDetector is a built-in reference implementation with the same interface.

items.title: MA policy
items.text:
class TwoReports(v2xw.plugins.MaPolicy):
    card = v2xw.plugins.card(id="ma/python-two-reports", family="ma-pipeline", ...)

    def decide(self, ctx, batch):              # ctx: MaCtx(t_ns, ma, provider)
        # batch: MaBatch of this step's accepted reports (MA_BATCH_COLUMNS + observed_ns,
        # reporter_infrastructure); never ground truth
        return [(subject_digest, True)]         # (subject, revoke) or (subject, revoke, row)

run = v2xw.run("scenarios/manhattan-5min.yaml", ma_policy=TwoReports())

It decides for every provider MA that would run the deployment-wide rule; a scenario that already sets detection.ma or security.scms.ma_policy is refused. Define the class in a module file: the manifest pins it as ma_policy:python:<module>.<class> with the SHA-256 of the module's source. Unlike the other families an MA keeps evidence between calls; its state must be a function of the calls it received. Keep separate state per ctx.ma.

items.title: Checking a Python plug-in
items.text:
Call Checks v2xw.conformance.check(model, quantum=1e-3) the whole suite over a car-following plug-in; returns a Report (properties passed, failures, warnings; raise_for_failures() raises DeterminismError) native_checks(model) through the engine's own call path: determinism, thread-count independence, dyn-compatibility, card validation and completeness, quantisation, finiteness purity_guard() replaces random.random, time.time, datetime.now and relatives with functions that raise while the plug-in is called; a call is a failure naming the function scan_source(model) advisory: imports of the banned modules in the plug-in's source (ast) v2xw.run_twice(scenario, build_utc=..., ma_policy_factory=...) two full runs' record digests; the only check for hidden state between calls (rule 5)

Passing the kit is necessary, not sufficient; raise_for_failures() says so.

items.title: Extending: scenarios and cities
items.text: A scenario says what happens (traffic, radio, network, security, attacks, metrics); a city says where. They are chosen separately: any scenario runs on any city of the library. Writing scenarios as a user is covered in Scenarios; this page is about adding files the repository ships and adding cities.

items.title: How a scenario file is loaded
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["bytes (YAML or JSON)"] --> P[parse to an untyped document]
    P --> M["migrate to v2xw/scenario/1<br/>(scenario::migrate)"]
    M --> O["resolve meta.base<br/>(scenario::merge)"]
    O --> D["deserialise<br/>deny_unknown_fields"]
    D --> C["with_city / fill_world_from_city<br/>(city.rs)"]
    C --> V["validate<br/>every error, by dotted field"]

Scenario::load(path) (crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/mod.rs) runs these steps.

items.title: Overlays: meta.base
items.text:
meta.base names another scenario file, relative to the including file's directory. The base is loaded (and migrated on its own), then the overlay is merged onto it on the untyped document, before deserialisation, so "absent" stays distinguishable from "set to the default":

Base Overlay Result mapping mapping merged key by key, recursively anything non-mapping value the overlay replaces the base a list a list the overlay's list replaces the base's (a list is a value, not a set) a key null the key is removed

meta.base is dropped from the merged document. Bases may chain up to MAX_BASE_DEPTH (16) levels; deeper is refused as a likely cycle.

# scenarios/midtown-rain.yaml: four lines of difference from the baseline
schema: v2xw/scenario/1
meta:
  base: midtown-normal.yaml
  name: Heavy rain
  description: >-
    Midday downtown in heavy rain on a wet road ...
  tags: [traffic, weather, rain, scms, dsrc]
weather:
  initial: rain
  intensity: 0.8
  surface: wet

items.title: The scenarios/ layout
items.text: Path Holds scenarios/*.yaml the ready-made scenarios, the study library (sweeps), and the end-to-end slices scenarios/base/ shared deployments the overlays build on: city.yaml (a downtown at midday, the US SCMS, roadside units at the busiest signalised intersections, demand per lane-kilometre), midtown.yaml, radio-faceoff.yaml scenarios/ready-made.txt the Studio picker's list, in order: one file name per line, ## starts a heading, # is a comment; read by the server's scenario.list (crates/v2xw-server/src/live.rs) scenarios/scale/ the wall-clock ladder, each rung an overlay on scale/base.yaml scenarios/sensitivity/ the family files the catalogue sweep routes settings to scenarios/real-world/, interop/, platform/, edge/, benchmark/ scenarios for specific data, SUMO interop, platform and edge cases, benchmarks scenarios/tests/ fixtures that Rust integration tests and the Studio's end-to-end specs load; each named for what it exercises

items.title: Adding a shipped scenario
items.text:
1. Start from the closest file, or write a short overlay on scenarios/base/.
  2. Header comment: what it measures, what it does not measure, and why each non-default number is that number, with its source.

  3. City-independent forms, so it runs on any city:

    Instead of Write The engine (city.rs) a fixed arrival rate actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km multiplies it by the imported network's driving-lane length explicit RSU positions actors.rsu_placement: {count, roles, min_spacing_m} places units at the city's busiest signalised intersections a named street in a closure target: auto closes a side street of whatever city it is a jammer position at: busiest-junction the busiest signalised intersection

  4. meta.name and meta.description are what the picker shows.

  5. For a sweep, set every swept path in the base: a sweep replaces a value already in the serialised scenario, and an optional field left unset is not serialised.
  6. Validate: v2xw validate scenarios/<file>.yaml must report no error.
  7. Offer it in the picker (optional): add its file name to scenarios/ready-made.txt under the right ## heading.
  8. Run the tests that read the folder.
Test What it requires of every scenarios/*.yaml scenario::publish::every_shipped_scenario_is_described (cargo test -p v2xw-engine --lib every_shipped_scenario_is_described) every key of every file that loads is in the published schema v2xw-trafficval invariants/shipped-scenarios (traffic_validation --only invariants) the traffic auditor's classes stay at zero on every shipped scenario that puts traffic on the road v2xw-netval end-to-end checks the shipped scenarios they name load and run under conservation and determinism properties crates/v2xw-engine/tests/scenario.rs, calendar.rs, crates/v2xw-cli/tests/cli.rs named shipped files still load, validate and hash; compressed-calendar files declare it

A scenario that fails to load is skipped by the coverage test

every_shipped_scenario_is_described skips files the loader refuses, so run v2xw validate on every new file yourself.

A fixture for a new test goes in scenarios/tests/, named for what it exercises, with a header saying what it changes.

items.title: Adding a city
items.text:
The city library is worlds/cities.yaml (schema v2xw/cities/1), compiled into the binary so every interface lists the same cities.

  1. Add an entry under cities::

    - id: example-city                  # also the extract's file name: worlds/cache/<id>.osm.xml
  name: "Example City"
  state: XX                         # USPS code
  state_name: "Example State"
  region: west                      # northeast, southeast, south, midwest, southwest, west
  role: largest                     # largest, studied, metro, international
  bbox: [S, W, N, E]                # degrees, WGS 84; the south-west corner is the world origin
  area_km2: 2.24
  utc_offset_h: -8                  # for time.local_start
  highway_preset: urban-us-xx       # crates/v2xw-world/src/jurisdiction.rs (cites each)
  fetched: "YYYY-MM-DD"             # becomes world.imported_at
  description: "Downtown ..."

    Optional drive_lane_km and signals record the network size the city audit measures. With drive_lane_km set, a fixed arrival rate moved to the city is rescaled by the lane-km ratio; without it, the engine uses a reference length until the world is imported, then measures the imported network (city::drive_lane_km). A jurisdiction with no preset needs one in v2xw-world's jurisdiction.rs, with citations.

  2. Fetch the extract: worlds/fetch.sh <id> writes worlds/cache/<id>.osm.xml (git-ignored; OpenStreetMap data under ODbL 1.0). The script queries the Overpass API for the box's nodes, ways, turn restrictions and building multipolygons, retries with backoff, pauses between downloads (FETCH_PAUSE_S, default 15 s), tries mirrors (OVERPASS_URL puts your own first) and checks the answer was not cut short. worlds/fetch.sh --list shows which extracts are present; V2XW_WORLDS_DIR points the engine at another directory.

  3. Audit it:

    cargo run -p v2xw-cli --bin city_audit -- scenarios/base/city.yaml --only example-city \
    [--seconds S] [--json OUT.jsonl]

    The scenario is put on the city as v2xw run --city would (Scenario::with_city), the world imported and fitted (city::adapt_to_world), and the traffic stepped under the auditor. A city passes when it imports, at least one vehicle completes a trip, the roadside units find intersections, no safety-class violation occurs and no vehicle stands past the standstill limit. A city that fails goes under dropped: with the reason.

  4. Rebuild, then v2xw cities lists it and v2xw run <scenario> --city example-city runs on it.

items.title: Other world data
items.text:
Script Produces worlds/fetch-gtfs.sh <name> [YYYYMMDD] worlds/cache/<name>.gtfs/: a GTFS feed clipped to the city's box and one service day (via v2xw-demand gtfs-clip), for the mobility/demand/gtfs demand kind. The scenario names the same date in params.date or has time.t0 on it worlds/fetch-lust.sh [netconvert] rebuilds the committed LuST subsection worlds/sumo/lust-veremi-sub.net.xml (MIT) from a pinned commit and prints its sha256 for comparison with its provenance file worlds/dem/ elevation models draped under the lanes (see each file's provenance note)

See Worlds and maps for the importers and Citation and licence for the data licences.

items.title: Extending: settings
items.text:
A setting is a scenario field. Adding one touches six files under crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/, and the published-surface tests refuse a field that is missing any of them, so the Studio, the assistant and the generated reference cannot fall behind the schema. Background: How settings work, Configuration overview.

flowchart TB
    A["schema.rs<br/>field, doc, default, unit suffix"] --> B["validate.rs<br/>BOUNDS / CHOICES, KEY_STATUS, cross-field rule"]
    B --> C["options.rs<br/>labels, presets, title"]
    C --> D["guide.rs<br/>level, explanation, recommended"]
    D --> E["engine code reads it<br/>+ same-seed test"]
    E --> F["publish tests pass"]
    F --> G["just docs-gen"]

As a running example, a hypothetical numeric field radio.phy.example_margin_db and a closed-set field net.example_mode.

items.title: 1. The field in schema.rs
items.text:
/// The extra link margin the receiver demands, dB. 0 dB (no margin) by default.
#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
pub example_margin_db: Option<f64>,
Rule Why the unit is the name's suffix (_s, _ms, _m, _db, _dbm, _mps, _hz, _veh_per_h, ...) the published surface reads the unit off the name (publish::UNIT_SUFFIXES); a numeric leaf that cannot carry one goes in publish::UNIT_OVERRIDES, or in DIMENSIONLESS if it has none the doc comment's first paragraph says what it is, its unit and its default it is the field's published description (reflected at build time by the crate's build.rs) optional or skip-serialised at its default (#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]) existing scenario hashes and the golden digests must not move structs keep #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] a misspelt key is an error
