A field that selects a model is a ModelChoice { id, params } (or a bare id) and also gets a publish::SLOTS row (Slot { path, label, family, bare_id }); its selectable ids then come from the registry.

items.title: 2. Range or value set in validate.rs
items.text:
A number gets one Bound in validate::BOUNDS:

Bound {
    path: "radio.phy.example_margin_db",
    lo: 0.0,
    hi: 20.0,
    exclusive_lo: false,
    what: "the receiver's extra link margin",   // used in the error message
},

A closed string set gets a row in validate::CHOICES:

choices("net.example_mode", &["off", "basic", "full"]),

A set may narrow on another field (narrowed_by, narrowed_when, narrowed_to), as security.signature narrows under security.crypto_mode: real. Sets whose members come from a registry (model ids, hardware profiles) are slots, not CHOICES rows.

The rules read these tables, so the form and the loader cannot disagree. A cross-field rule goes in validate::validate, and its error is built with the dotted field and the conflict:

e.push(conflict("radio.phy.example_margin_db",
    "is set, and radio.tiers.phy is abstract, which has no SNR to apply it to".into()));

A setting that would change nothing in a context (as above) is refused at load with an error that names it; crates/v2xw-engine/tests/inert_setting_refusals.rs holds such rules, each with a test that the refusal lifts once the setting can act.

items.title: 3. Its status in KEY_STATUS
items.text:
KeyStatus {
    path: "radio.phy.example_margin_db",
    status: Status::Wired,
    note: "Raises the SNR every reception needs by this many dB.",
},

Statuses: Wired, Partial (the note states the conditions), NotImplemented, Refused (only implemented values load), Descriptive. Entries are prefixes and the longest match wins. Keys whose tables live beside the engine module that implements them (for example ma_policy.rs, scms_topology.rs) are reached through scenario/module_keys.rs.

items.title: 4. Words in options.rs
items.text: Need Where a label and one sentence per value of a closed set a match arm in options::words(path, value), returning (label, description, available). Without one, the value falls back to a humanised id and the model card's purpose named values beside a number, each with its source a Preset { path, label, value, note } in PRESETS (or SCMS_PRESETS, MODULE_PRESETS) a plain-language title where the Rust name reads badly options::title a value set that is neither CHOICES nor a reflected enum options::extra_values "only relevant when ..." options::relevant_when (published as x-relevant-when) a numeric step for the form's spinner publish::STEPS

items.title: 5. Level and guidance in guide.rs
items.text:
Every field is advanced unless listed. A field that decides what a run models gets a Basic { path, explain, recommended } row in guide::BASIC: one sentence on what it is in the real world and a recommended range in words, with the source of any number. An advanced field can carry the same row in guide::ADVANCED. A quick setting or a study starting point (guide::quick, guide::studies) is a patch the tests apply to the minimal scenario and validate.

Basic {
    path: "radio.phy.example_margin_db",
    explain: "Extra signal strength a receiver insists on before it trusts a frame.",
    recommended: "0 (default); 3 to 6 to model a conservative receiver.",
},

items.title: 6. Read it in the engine
items.text:
Read the field where the engine builds the affected model (wiring.rs for radio and mobility, phase2.rs for security, threats and detection, run.rs for the loop), and add tests:

  • a same-seed comparison showing that changing the setting changes the run (and that the default leaves the golden digests unchanged);
  • if theory predicts a direction, an expectation row in crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations/<family>.yaml:
- {setting: radio.phy.example_margin_db, change: high, metric: range90_m, expect: down,
   source: "a higher SNR requirement shortens range (cite the text)"}

expect is up, down, same or changes; change is low, high (the ends of the recommended range) or a literal; min_change defaults to 0.01. v2xw sensitivity --expect checks the rows against same-seed runs, and tests/sensitivity_expectations.rs checks that they load and are consistent.

items.title: 7. Migration (only for a breaking change)
items.text: An additive optional field needs no migration. Renaming or restructuring a field means a new schema version: add one single-step Migration to migrate::Chain::shipped() that rewrites the untyped document from the previous version, bump schema::CURRENT_SCHEMA, and update the shipped scenarios. The chain walks one step at a time and fails with ScenarioError::MigrationGap when a step is missing. v2xw/scenario/1 is the only version so far, so the shipped chain is empty.

items.title: 8. The tests that guard the published surface
items.text:
cargo test -p v2xw-engine --lib scenario runs them:

Test File Fails when every_leaf_has_a_status publish.rs a leaf matches no KEY_STATUS row every_number_publishes_a_unit publish.rs a numeric leaf has no suffix, override or DIMENSIONLESS entry the_tables_name_real_fields publish.rs a BOUNDS, CHOICES or KEY_STATUS row names a path the schema does not have the_published_defaults_load publish.rs a document of the published defaults does not load every_shipped_scenario_is_described publish.rs a key in a file under scenarios/ is not in the schema every_section_has_a_group publish.rs a new top-level section has no display group every_model_parameter_publishes_its_provenance publish.rs a model card parameter in the catalogue lacks a unit, default or source module_keys_publish_menus_ranges_and_status publish.rs a module-owned key lacks a title, a menu, a unit, a range or a step every_quick_choice_and_study_loads guide.rs a quick-setting or study patch does not validate every_quick_field_and_basic_path_is_published guide.rs a BASIC row names an unpublished path the_typed_fields_are_choices options.rs a field with a closed set of accepted values is not offered as a menu of exactly those values

items.title: 9. Regenerate the reference
items.text:
just docs-gen       # dump_settings -> tools/docs/gen_config_reference.py
just docs-build     # optional: build the site and check links

Commit the regenerated docs/configuration/reference/ with the change.

items.title: Checklist
items.text:
• field in schema.rs: unit suffix, doc with default, skip-serialised at default
  • BOUNDS or CHOICES row (or a SLOTS row for a model)
  • KEY_STATUS row with a one-line note
  • labels (options::words) and presets with sources
  • guide::BASIC row if it decides what a run models
  • read in the engine; same-seed test; expectation row if theory predicts a direction
  • publish tests green; just docs-gen run

items.title: Command-line tool
items.text:
cargo build --release -p v2xw-cli builds two programs into target/release/:

Program What it is v2xw the command-line tool: every subcommand below v2xw-server the engine server with the assistant's endpoints always on; the same program as v2xw serve, with the server's own flags (below)

The grammar is in crates/v2xw-cli/src/cli.rs; v2xw <command> --help prints the same text. Two conventions hold everywhere: units are in flag names (--keyframe-ms, --duration-s), and a flag that overrides a scenario field changes the scenario hash and is recorded in the run's resolved scenario.

Exit codes. 0 success; 1 the command failed (a scenario error also names the offending key on stderr); 2 the arguments were wrong. Commands that check something (check-traffic, sensitivity) exit 1 when the check fails and still print their table.

Durations. Flags typed DURATION take a number with units: 90s, 15m, 6h, 2d, 1d12h.

items.title: Commands
items.text: Command Does run run a scenario and write its recording, metrics, report and manifest resume carry on a checkpointed run, verified to be the same run validate load and check a scenario without running it info a recording's manifest, channels and verification report cities the city library and which extracts are downloaded import-osm import an OpenStreetMap extract into the three world formats export-sumo write a scenario's network and demand in SUMO formats experiment run, inspect or resume a scenario's sweep compare the settings and headline metrics that differ between two runs compare-signatures one scenario and seed under several signature schemes sensitivity one-at-a-time perturbations checked against expected directions ma-replay replay recorded misbehaviour reports through MA decision rules check-traffic audit a finished run's traffic from its recording energy score a recording for emissions, fuel and EV energy serve the engine server with the assistant's endpoints agent the assistant: build a scenario from a prompt, run it, report

items.title: run
items.text:
v2xw run [OPTIONS] <SCENARIO>. Guide: Running and recording.

Argument or flag Type Default Meaning <SCENARIO> path required the scenario file, YAML or JSON -o, --out path runs/<meta.name> (runs/<meta.name>-<city> with --city) output directory --build-utc ISO 8601 this machine's clock the manifest's build timestamp; pass it to compare two manifests field by field --keyframe-ms integer, ms 1000 the recording's keyframe period; a whole number of mobility steps --node-only flag off record the NODE-only profile, which refuses every ground-truth record --no-recording flag off run into a counting sink with no recording (scaling measurements) --attach-world flag off also attach the world payload to the recording (tens of MB for a city) --no-verify flag off skip reading the recording back (digest and chunk checksums) --digest flag off with --no-recording: stream a SHA-256 of every record and report it as stream_digest --duration-s number, s scenario override time.duration_s --duration DURATION scenario the same in units (15m, 6h); wins over --duration-s --rate-veh-per-h number, veh/h scenario override actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h --veremi veremi-ext, veremi-1 none add the veremi exporter with this attack codebook, or set the codebook of the one the scenario names --city city id scenario's run on this city of the library (v2xw cities) instead of the file's world --progress-every DURATION 15 min for runs of 1 h or more, else none write a progress line (progress.jsonl and stderr): wall clock per simulated hour, memory, fleet; 0 turns it off --quiet flag off keep progress.jsonl, print no progress on stderr --checkpoint-every DURATION none write checkpoint.json this often and record in segments, so v2xw resume can carry the run on --record-level full, receptions, events, metrics full how much reaches the recording (levels) --json flag off print the outcome as JSON

Rate override and per-lane-km demand

A scenario that states rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km recomputes rate_veh_per_h from the world's lane length after import, so --rate-veh-per-h has no effect on it. Change the density in an overlay instead.

A scenario that names exporters refuses --no-recording (every exporter reads the recording) and --checkpoint-every (exporters read one recording.mcap, a checkpointed run records in segments).

v2xw run scenarios/manhattan-day.yaml --out runs/day --record-level metrics --checkpoint-every 1h

items.title: resume
items.text:
v2xw resume [OPTIONS] <CHECKPOINT>: rebuild the run from scenario.resolved.yaml beside the checkpoint, replay it to the checkpoint's instant with outputs off, refuse unless the record digest there matches, then continue writing the outputs.

Argument or flag Type Default Meaning <CHECKPOINT> path required checkpoint.json in the interrupted run's output directory --quiet flag off no progress lines on stderr --json flag off print the outcome as JSON 
v2xw resume runs/day/checkpoint.json

items.title: validate
items.text:
v2xw validate [--json] <SCENARIO>: load, merge overlays, migrate and validate; print every error with its dotted field, and advisory notes. Exit 1 on any error.

v2xw validate scenarios/attack-fake-positions.yaml

items.title: info
items.text:
v2xw info [--json] <RECORDING>: the recording's size, profile, cadence, content digest, channels with their encoding, visibility class and message counts, attachments, the verification walk (frames, records, chunk checksums) and the manifest.

v2xw info runs/highway/recording.mcap

items.title: cities
items.text:
v2xw cities [--json] [FILTER]: the city library (worlds/cities.yaml, compiled into the binary), grouped by state, with each city's id, name, highway preset, description and [not fetched] when its extract is missing. FILTER keeps cities whose name, id, state or state code contains it, ignoring case.

v2xw cities texas

items.title: import-osm
items.text:
v2xw import-osm [OPTIONS] --speed-preset <NAME> <EXTRACT> <OUT>: write world.vwb (the browser's vwp-world/1 payload), world.json, world.v2xw (the engine's native binary) and report.txt (the importer's report) into OUT.

Argument or flag Type Default Meaning <EXTRACT> path required the .osm or .osm.xml extract <OUT> path required output directory --speed-preset name required, no default the highway=* class-default speed table: urban-us-nyc, urban-us-portland, urban-de, sumo-german, or an urban-us-<state> preset --bbox MIN_LON,MIN_LAT,MAX_LON,MAX_LAT the extract's bounds box to keep; its south-west corner is the world origin --imported-at ISO 8601 this machine's clock provenance date; excluded from the world hash --json flag off print the outcome as JSON instead of the report

Box order

import-osm --bbox is longitude first (min_lon,min_lat,max_lon,max_lat); worlds/fetch.sh and worlds/cities.yaml are south, west, north, east. An import with no drivable lane is refused with the box and the argument order in the message.

v2xw import-osm worlds/cache/manhattan.osm.xml out/manhattan --speed-preset urban-us-nyc \
    --bbox -73.9900,40.7440,-73.9680,40.7620

items.title: export-sumo
items.text:
v2xw export-sumo [-o <OUT>] [--json] <SCENARIO>: the scenario's world as SUMO plain XML (.nod.xml, .edg.xml, .con.xml), a .net.xml when netconvert is found, and a .rou.xml of every trip the scenario's demand draws, with this engine's routes. -o/--out defaults to sumo-export. Guide: SUMO co-simulation.

v2xw export-sumo scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml --out out/sumo

items.title: experiment
items.text:
Three subcommands over a scenario's experiment block. Guide: Experiments and sweeps.

Subcommand Does run <SCENARIO> expand the sweep, run every outstanding run, write the results table; finished runs are skipped (the journal decides) status <SCENARIO> how far along the sweep is and which runs are next; runs nothing resume <SCENARIO> as run, but refuse if no journal for this sweep exists in --out

run and resume flags:

Flag Type Default Meaning -o, --out path runs/<meta.name>-sweep the sweep's output directory --build-utc ISO 8601 the clock, read once the manifest timestamp every run shares --concurrency integer 1 simulations at once; each holds its own world and buffers, so k runs cost k times the memory --ci 90, 95, 99 95 confidence level of the aggregate, percent --keyframe-ms integer, ms 1000 recording keyframe period per run --no-recording flag off no recording per run; metrics, report and manifest are written anyway --node-only flag off NODE-only profile in every run --no-verify flag off skip reading each recording back --format parquet, arrow, jsonl none also write the results table in this format beside results.json --json flag off print the outcome as JSON

status takes -o/--out and --json.

v2xw experiment run scenarios/pdr-vs-distance.yaml --out runs/pdr --format parquet

items.title: compare
items.text:
v2xw compare [OPTIONS] <A> <B>. Each side is a v2xw run --out directory, a run digest JSON (v2xw/run-digest/1, the Studio's export or runs.digest), an experiment output directory, or comma-separated replications. Guide: Comparing runs.

Flag Meaning --all show every metric, not only the meaningful changes --json JSON (v2xw/run-comparison/1) --markdown Markdown --csv CSV 
v2xw compare runs/a1,runs/a2,runs/a3 runs/b1,runs/b2,runs/b3 --markdown

items.title: compare-signatures
items.text:
v2xw compare-signatures [OPTIONS] <SCENARIO>: the same scenario and seed under each scheme, with the signing-overhead metrics on; writes comparison.json, .csv and .md.

Flag Type Default Meaning --schemes comma list ecdsa-p256,ml-dsa-44,falcon-512,hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256 scheme ids; ECDSA P-256 is added as the baseline when missing -o, --out path runs/<meta.name>-signatures output directory --duration number, s scenario simulated seconds per run --build-utc ISO 8601 the clock manifest timestamp every run uses --record flag off write a recording per run --json flag off print the comparison as JSON 
v2xw compare-signatures scenarios/compare-signature-schemes.yaml --duration 60

items.title: sensitivity
items.text:
v2xw sensitivity [OPTIONS] [SPEC]. A spec file, or --catalogue, or --expect. Guide: Sensitivity analysis.

Argument or flag Type Default Meaning [SPEC] path required unless --catalogue or --expect a spec file: a base and one-at-a-time rows --catalogue flag off sweep every published numeric and choice setting, low and high end, against a same-seed base --expect flag off run only the expectation rows and the interaction checks; exit 1 on a failed row (conflicts with --catalogue) --families path scenarios/sensitivity/catalogue.yaml families, routes and value overrides --expectations comma list crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations expectation files or directories --interactions comma list crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations/interactions interaction files for --expect --only comma list all keep settings whose path starts with one of these prefixes --jobs integer 2 parallel runs (--catalogue, --expect) --plan flag off print the plan and run nothing --cache path none JSON-lines cache of finished perturbations; a rerun reuses matching entries --strict flag off --catalogue: exit 1 when an expectation is contradicted --markdown path none also write the results as a Markdown table --json flag off print JSON instead of the table --base-only flag off spec mode: run only the base and print every metric it measured 
v2xw sensitivity scenarios/sensitivity/radio-dsrc.yaml
v2xw sensitivity --catalogue --only radio.phy --plan

items.title: ma-replay
items.text:
v2xw ma-replay [--policies <SCENARIO>] <DIR>: replay the run's recorded misbehaviour reports through a family of MA decision rules, without re-simulating; writes ma-replay.csv in the run directory. The run needs security.scms.report_records: true. --policies replays the scenario's MA policy family instead of the built-in rules and writes ma-replay-policies.csv.

v2xw ma-replay runs/attack

items.title: check-traffic
items.text:
v2xw check-traffic [OPTIONS] <DIR>: audit a finished run's traffic from its recording (needs recording.mcap at --record-level full and scenario.resolved.yaml). Exit 1 when an invariant fails.

Flag Type Default Meaning --green-stop-s number, s 6.0 how long a queue head may stand on its own protected green --examples integer 8 examples printed per row --trace actor id none print this actor's every step on stderr --json flag off print the check as JSON 
v2xw check-traffic runs/midtown-normal

items.title: energy
items.text:
v2xw energy [OPTIONS] <RECORDING>: score a full-profile recording (it reads gt.kinematics) for CO2, fuel, NOx, PM and EV energy, with health bands, without re-running it.

Flag Type Default Meaning --spec path the recording's own energy section a JSON or YAML energy: section body that replaces it --emission-model id section's hbefa3, phemlight, moves-opmode, or a full id --ev-model id section's kurczveil, vt-cpem, or a full id --vehicles-csv path none one CSV row per vehicle --opmode-csv path none the MOVES operating-mode distribution per lane --json flag off print the outcome as JSON 
v2xw energy runs/glosa/recording.mcap --emission-model phemlight --vehicles-csv out/veh.csv

items.title: serve
items.text:
v2xw serve [OPTIONS]: the engine server with the assistant's endpoints on the same origin. Guides: Studio tour, Assistant.

Flag Type Default Meaning --scenario path none: the synthetic fixture the scenario to serve --attach URL none serve only the assistant's endpoints in front of an engine already running there --host IP 127.0.0.1 bind address; a non-loopback bind needs --token --port integer 8787 TCP port --token string none bearer token required on every request --paused flag off start paused at t = 0 --speed number 1 multiple of real time; 0 is unthrottled --record path none write the MCAP recording here 
v2xw serve --scenario scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --paused

items.title: agent
items.text:
v2xw agent [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]: the assistant builds a scenario from the prompt, runs it, analyses it and prints a Markdown report on stdout (progress on stderr). Guide: Assistant.

Argument or flag Type Default Meaning [PROMPT] text empty what to simulate and find out --engine URL none: start one in-process a running engine to drive --scenario path scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml the scenario an in-process engine starts with --no-model flag off run without a language model: the scenario runs as shipped and the report is the analyst's alone --analyse flag off only analyse the run the engine is serving --base current or a preset id current the scenario a model-less run uses --token string none the engine's bearer token --json flag off print the report as JSON 
v2xw agent --no-model > report.md

items.title: v2xw-server
items.text:
The server program, with its own flag parser (v2xw-server --help). It runs the real engine with --scenario, or a synthetic fixture stream without one, and serves the assistant unless --no-agent. Endpoints and methods: Engine server and RPC.

Flag Default Meaning --scenario <p> none scenario to run; without it the synthetic fixture runs --record <p> none write the MCAP recording here --build-utc <t> the clock manifest build timestamp --retain <n> 36000 mobility steps of history kept for run.seek --retain-mb <n> 1024 most memory that history may take, MB --lookahead <n> 64 steps the kernel may run ahead of the stream --resume <p> none open a v2xw run --checkpoint-every run at its checkpoint.json, computed to that instant and served paused --actors <n> 120 fixture: actors to drive --grid <n> 8 fixture: junctions per side --block <m> 150 fixture: junction spacing, metres --duration <s> 600 fixture: simulated seconds --seed <n> 20260918 fixture: phase seed --port <n> 8787 TCP port; 0 for an ephemeral one --host <addr> 127.0.0.1 bind address; a non-loopback bind needs --token --token <t> none bearer token on the upgrade and every HTTP request --speed <x> 1 multiple of real time; 0 is unthrottled --paused off start paused at t = 0 --label <s> none human label for the run (Hello.str_run_label) --quiet off no banner --no-agent off serve the engine without the assistant's endpoints and watcher --env-file <p> ./.env when present read the assistant's provider variables from this file 
v2xw-server --actors 200 --port 8787          # a conforming stream with no map, for UI work

items.title: run-sim.sh
items.text:
./run-sim.sh [scenario] [extra v2xw-server flags]: builds target/release/v2xw-server when it is missing (with -j 1), then serves the scenario (default scenarios/manhattan-5min.yaml) on $V2XW_PORT (default 8787), paused and unthrottled, reading the assistant's variables from .env:

./run-sim.sh scenarios/midtown-pedestrians.yaml
# = v2xw-server --scenario scenarios/midtown-pedestrians.yaml --port 8787 --paused --speed 0 --env-file .env

items.title: v2xw-demand
items.text:
The demand and route-choice tool (cargo build --release -p v2xw-demand-cli, binary v2xw-demand). Every command takes --key value pairs; the world is --scenario FILE (exactly the world a run of that scenario builds, so route files match it) or --world grid (the procedural test grid, the default). Every output is deterministic; any error prints v2xw-demand: <message> and exits 2. Guide: Traffic demand.

Command Required Optional (default) Writes od2trips --matrix M, --out F --zones grid:CxR (grid:3x3), --start HH:MM (00:00), --scale (1) trips (v2xw/trips/1) purposes --out F --daily N (20000), --day D (0) trips for one day assign --trips F, --out F --choice gawron\|logit\|msa (gawron), --loader queue\|bpr\|micro (queue), --iterations (25), --gap (0.02), --warm routes.json routes (v2xw/routes/1) and an iteration log on stdout sample --counts F, --out F --method max-entropy\|greedy (max-entropy) routes reproducing link counts, and a GEH check check --counts F, --routes F --loader (queue) GEH per count, share under 5, RMSE, R² gtfs-clip --feed DIR, --bbox S,W,N,E, --date YYYYMMDD, --out DIR a clipped GTFS feed gtfs --feed DIR, --date YYYYMMDD --start HH:MM (08:00), --run S (900) a summary of the transit trips and stops placed 
v2xw-demand gtfs --scenario scenarios/portland-transit.yaml \
    --feed worlds/cache/portland.gtfs --date 20261007 --start 08:00

items.title: Other programs
items.text:
Program Built from Does cross_validate v2xw-cli (just cross-validate) traffic and radio cross-validation against SUMO, Veins and OpenCV2X; needs SUMO city_audit v2xw-cli import a city and run it under the traffic auditor; measures drive_lane_km and signals for worlds/cities.yaml traffic_validation, traffic_calibration v2xw-trafficval the traffic validation and calibration suites

What these suites check: Validation and conformance tools.

items.title: Your first simulation
items.text:
This walk-through runs the honest baseline of the ready-made scenarios, scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml: a weekday midday in Midtown Manhattan with every vehicle signing BSMs ten times a second, the US SCMS in the loop, eight roadside units at the busiest signalised intersections and misbehaviour detection on every vehicle. Then it changes one setting and compares the two runs.

It assumes the tool is built (Install and build); the commands write v2xw for ./target/release/v2xw. Run them from the repository root: relative paths in a scenario are read from the directory the engine was started in.

items.title: 1. Fetch the map
items.text:
The scenario names no world of its own. Its base, scenarios/base/city.yaml, says city: manhattan, so the world is the Manhattan entry of the city library (Worlds and maps), whose OpenStreetMap extract is not in the repository (it is ODbL data and large):

v2xw cities manhattan          # the library entry, and whether its extract is present
worlds/fetch.sh manhattan      # writes worlds/cache/manhattan.osm.xml from the Overpass API

No download

scenarios/highway-congestion.yaml, scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml and scenarios/credential-lifecycle.yaml build a procedural road network and need no extract. Every step below works on them unchanged.

items.title: 2. Read and validate the scenario
items.text:
midtown-normal.yaml is four lines of meta over meta.base: base/city.yaml; open both to see what the run is. The overlay merge, the sections and the timeline are explained in Scenarios.

v2xw validate scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml

ok              Normal traffic
schema          v2xw/scenario/1
scenario hash   e04fe072…
seed            0xc0ffee5eed
world source    osm-xml:worlds/cache/manhattan.osm.xml
time            300.000 s at 100 ms steps
metrics         all
note            security.verification_policy: 'prioritized' sheds the oldest and least relevant messages unverified …

Validation reports every problem at once, each with its dotted field, and exits 1 if any is an error. A note is advice, not an error: here it says that the prioritized verification policy leaves detection nearly blind under load, which matters if you study detection.

items.title: 3. Run it
items.text:
v2xw run scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --out runs/midtown-normal --duration 60s

--duration 60s overrides time.duration_s (300 s in the file) to keep the first run short; like every override it changes the scenario hash and is recorded in the resolved scenario. The command prints a summary:

scenario        Normal traffic
seed            0xc0ffee5eed
scenario hash   …
world hash      …
outputs         runs/midtown-normal

simulated       60.000 s in … s wall (… wall s per simulated s)
  load … s | build … s | run … s | verify … s | total … s

events          …
  MacTimer      …
  MobilityStep  601
  …
actors spawned  …
frames sent     …
receptions      … attempted, … received
records         … written, 0 refused

channels
  gt.kinematics   … records   … json bytes
  node.tx         … records   … json bytes
  …
container       … messages in … chunk(s), largest chunk … uncompressed bytes
recording       … bytes on disk
content digest  …
file sha256     …  (the container's summary section is not reproducible; compare the content digest)
verified        … records, … frames; integrity VERIFIED over … chunk(s)

--json prints the same as one JSON object. After the run the recording is read back and its chunk checksums verified (--no-verify skips that).

items.title: 4. Read the run directory
items.text:
runs/midtown-normal/
├── recording.mcap           every record, the VWP frames, the manifest, the scenario attached
├── scenario.resolved.yaml   the scenario after overlay merge, migration and defaults: what ran
├── metrics.json             every metric.sample the run emitted
├── run-report.json          event, frame and record counts per channel, and content_digest
├── manifest.json            build, models and card hashes, world, scenario and seed, crypto mode
└── progress.jsonl           progress lines: empty unless --progress-every is set or the run is an hour or more
To answer Read is this the same run as another one? content_digest in run-report.json (not the file hash of recording.mcap) what exactly ran? scenario.resolved.yaml and the hashes in manifest.json what did it measure? metrics.json, or v2xw compare and the Studio's Metrics panel what happened, message by message? recording.mcap, through v2xw info, Python or the Studio

What each file and channel holds: Metrics and outputs and Running and recording.

items.title: 5. Inspect the recording
items.text:
v2xw info runs/midtown-normal/recording.mcap

recording       runs/midtown-normal/recording.mcap
size            … bytes
profile         full
cadence         keyframe 1000 ms, mobility step 100 ms
content digest  …

channels
  vwp/keyframe              vwp1  mixed         61 messages
  vwp/delta                 vwp1  mixed        540 messages
  record/metric.sample      json  derived        … messages
  record/node.tx            json  node           … messages
  record/gt.kinematics      json  gt             … messages
  …

attachments
  scenario.yaml             … bytes

verify          601 frames (61 keyframes, 540 deltas, 0 unknown), … records
integrity       VERIFIED — … chunk(s) checksummed and matched

manifest
  { "build_hash": "…", "build_utc": "…", "crypto_mode": "modeled", … }

Each channel carries a visibility class: gt is ground truth no device could know, node is what a device saw, derived is computed from records. A --node-only run refuses every ground-truth record, which is what a blind evaluation hands a detector.

items.title: 6. Watch it in the Studio
items.text:
The Studio is a browser page that drives a live engine. Serve the same scenario and open the page in a second terminal:

./run-sim.sh scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml          # the engine on :8787, paused at t = 0
pnpm --dir ui install
pnpm --dir ui --filter @vwp/studio dev              # http://127.0.0.1:5173

Press play, click a vehicle to follow it, press M for the metrics. The Studio tour covers each panel, including opening a finished recording without an engine.

items.title: 7. Change one setting and compare
items.text:
Write a three-line overlay beside the scenario. It inherits everything from midtown-normal.yaml and raises the arrival rate by half, from 25 to 37.5 vehicles per hour per kilometre of driving lane (actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km):

scenarios/my-midtown-busier.yaml
schema: v2xw/scenario/1
meta:
  base: midtown-normal.yaml          # resolved relative to this file
  name: Normal traffic, busier
actors:
  vehicles:
    demand:
      rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km: 37.5

v2xw validate scenarios/my-midtown-busier.yaml
v2xw run scenarios/my-midtown-busier.yaml --out runs/midtown-busier --duration 60s
v2xw compare runs/midtown-normal runs/midtown-busier

--rate-veh-per-h does not change this scenario

The run flag --rate-veh-per-h sets actors.vehicles.demand.rate_veh_per_h, and a scenario that states rate_veh_per_h_per_lane_km (as every ready-made city scenario does) recomputes the rate from the city's lane length, which wins. Change the density in an overlay, as above.

v2xw compare prints the settings that differ and every headline metric whose change is meaningful, judged by the metric's health direction:

  1 setting changed: … → ….
  … of … metrics changed meaningfully: … better, … worse, … neutral.
  …
  Both runs used seed 828927532781: every random draw the settings did not touch is shared, so the differences are caused by the settings change.

Settings changed:
  …

metric                       A          B       change        %  verdict
offered_load               … bit/s    … bit/s   … bit/s    +… %  changed
…
  (… rows without a meaningful change hidden; --all shows them)

Both runs inherit one seed, so they share every random draw the change did not reach (common random numbers): the differences are the setting's, not noise. How the verdicts are decided, and the JSON, Markdown and CSV forms: Comparing runs.

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Turn the one change into a sweep with replications and confidence intervals: Experiments and sweeps.
  • Run the same scenario on another city: v2xw run scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --city boston after worlds/fetch.sh boston.
  • Every flag of every command: Command-line tool.

items.title: Introduction
items.text: The simulator answers quantitative questions about connected-vehicle security and privacy that need the whole system in one loop: traffic that moves, radios that lose frames, devices that sign and verify under a compute budget, a credential system that provisions, reports and revokes, attackers who lie with valid signatures, and detectors that only see what a fielded device could see. A run is one scenario file and one seed; its recording replays byte for byte.

items.title: Who it is for
items.text: Reader Start with A researcher running studies Your first simulation, Experiments and sweeps, Comparing runs A reviewer checking a result Determinism, the model cards, Metrics and outputs A user exploring a city in the browser Studio tour A developer (human or coding agent) extending the engine Architecture, Crates, Extending

items.title: The layer stack
items.text:
Each model crate owns one domain and reaches no other crate's state; the engine composes them into a run. Dependencies point down.

flowchart TB
  subgraph interfaces[Interfaces]
    CLI["v2xw, v2xw-server (v2xw-cli)"]
    SRV["VWP stream + JSON-RPC (v2xw-server)"]
    PY["Python (v2xw-py)"]
    WASM["replay reader (v2xw-wasm)"]
    UI["Studio (ui/)"]
    AG["assistant (v2xw-copilot)"]
  end
  subgraph orchestration[Orchestration]
    EXP["sweeps (v2xw-experiment)"]
    ENG["scenario, event loop, wiring, manifest (v2xw-engine)"]
  end
  subgraph runtime[Device runtime]
    NODE["OBU / RSU / VRU runtimes (v2xw-node)"]
    PROTO["credential protocols (v2xw-proto)"]
  end
  subgraph models[Models]
    W[v2xw-world] --- MOB[v2xw-mobility] --- DEM[v2xw-demand]
    RAD[v2xw-radio] --- NET[v2xw-net] --- MSG[v2xw-msg]
    SEC[v2xw-sec] --- THR[v2xw-threat] --- EN[v2xw-energy] --- IO[v2xw-interop]
  end
  subgraph measurement[Measurement]
    MET[v2xw-metrics] --- REC[v2xw-record]
  end
  CORE["contract: DES kernel, keyed RNG, registry, model cards, manifest, math (v2xw-core)"]
  interfaces --> orchestration --> runtime --> models --> measurement --> CORE

What each crate owns: Crates. How one run flows through them (load, build, the event loop, finish): Architecture.

items.title: The determinism promise
items.text:
Same scenario file, seed, engine build and plug-in set give byte-identical outputs, on any thread count. The mechanisms are in v2xw-core and are enforced by tests:

Rule Mechanism no shared random generator every draw comes from a stream keyed by SHA-256(master_seed ‖ domain ‖ entity) (v2xw_core::rng), so a draw does not depend on what was drawn before it no platform maths transcendentals go through v2xw_core::math (pure-Rust libm) no wall clock in the engine the manifest timestamp is an argument (Engine::build(scenario, build_utc); --build-utc on the CLI) no hash-order outputs ordered collections wherever iteration reaches an output quantised floats every recorded float is put on its declared grid before it is written or digested one event order events pop in (time, priority, seq) order; parallel phases are pure maps merged in id order

The run's identity is content_digest in run-report.json: SHA-256 over every recorded message's topic, time and bytes. The MCAP file's own SHA-256 is not reproducible (its summary index is written in hash-map order), which is why v2xw run reports both.

What is checked across platforms

CI builds and tests on Linux, macOS and Windows (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and requires the world-import digest of the committed fixture to agree on all three. The conformance kit's golden records (tests/conformance/golden/) pin, per fixed scenario, the scenario hash, world hash, a digest over every record and per-channel counts.

items.title: Modelled versus simplified
items.text:
Every model is registered with a card that lists its assumptions, limitations and what it ignores relative to the next tier up; the full text of every card is in the model parameters reference. A few that shape what a result can claim:

Area Modelled Simplified or left out (from the cards) Car following (mobility/car-following/idm) IDM with Kesting 2010 car and truck parameters, FHWA weather response no driver imperfection (sigma), action-step length or sub-second reaction time Lane change (mobility/lane-change/mobil) MOBIL incentive and safety criteria SUMO's cooperative helping, keep-right rule and speed-gain lookahead Imported worlds (world/source/osm) lanes, junctions, connectors, conflict matrices, synthesised fixed-time signals, buildings no terrain unless a DEM is attached; the source carries no signal timing, so plans are synthesised Cryptography (crypto-backend/modeled) each operation's measured time on the device profile no mathematics at all; security.crypto_mode: real does the arithmetic (P-256 only) Cryptography (crypto-backend/real) ECDSA P-256 (RFC 6979 nonces), SHA-256 and ECQV reconstruction on real bytes post-quantum primitives (cost tables only), side channels, key storage SCMS (protocol/scms/camp) the CAMP entities and their messages over modelled links certificate encryption is modelled by its size and cost, not performed Network layer (net/wsmp/1609-3) exact WSMP v3 header sizes and the WSM payload cap IEEE 1609.4 channel switching is sized, never acted on GeoNetworking (net/gn-btp/en302636) exact GeoNetworking and BTP header sizes and the MTU rule GBC multi-hop forwarding, the location table, duplicate detection and DCC_NET Jammers (attacker/jammer/*) constant, pulsed and reactive wideband jammers subcarrier-selective jamming; the jammer's own antenna pattern Cellular Uu (cellular/uu/*) fixed latency, M/M/1 cell capacity, packet-level proportional fair, handover outage fast fading, frequency-selective scheduling, MIMO and beam management

Where a number has no source it is marked todo-calibrate on its card with a calibration plan, and the generated reference shows it. Settings the engine validates but acts on only partly, or not at all, carry a status in the configuration reference.

items.title: Platforms
items.text:
Target Status Linux, macOS, Windows built and tested in CI on the GitHub-hosted runners of all three Toolchain Rust 1.98.1, pinned in rust-toolchain.toml (edition 2024) WebAssembly (wasm32-unknown-unknown) the replay reader only (crates/v2xw-wasm); its build needs a WebAssembly-capable clang Browser the Studio (Node 22+, pnpm 10 to build) Python 3.9+, built with maturin from crates/v2xw-py

Next: Install and build, then your first simulation.

items.title: Python
items.text: The v2xw package drives the engine from Python: load a scenario, run it, read a metric as an Arrow table, open the recording, and write a model in Python that the engine calls. It is the compiled module crates/v2xw-py (PyO3) plus a thin Python layer in python/v2xw/. Every class and function: Python API.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Python 3.9 or later, in a virtualenv, from the repository:

pip install maturin
cd python && maturin develop            # editable install into the active virtualenv
cd python && maturin build --release    # or a wheel, in ../target/wheels
pip install 'v2xw[arrow]'               # optional: pyarrow, for zero-copy tables

pyarrow is optional. Without it every table still crosses as an Arrow IPC buffer, which polars.read_ipc_stream reads. With it, Metrics.arrow() and Recording.arrow() hand Python the engine's own buffers through the Arrow C data interface, with no copy.

items.title: Run a scenario and read a metric
items.text:
import v2xw

scenario = v2xw.Scenario.load("scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml")   # load, merge overlays, validate
print(scenario.name, hex(scenario.seed), scenario.content_hash[:16])

run = v2xw.run(scenario, recording="run.mcap", metric_window_s=1.0)
print(run.records, "records;", run.report["frames_transmitted"], "frames")

for t_ns, value in run.metrics.series("pdr"):                   # (t_ns, value) pairs
    print(t_ns / 1e9, value)

table = v2xw.read_ipc(run.metrics.ipc())                        # the whole table, via pyarrow

rec = v2xw.Recording.open("run.mcap")
print(rec.verify())                                             # records, frames, integrity
print(rec.records("node.tx", limit=2))                          # one channel's first records
assert rec.manifest["scenario_hash"] == scenario.content_hash
Call What it does Scenario.load(path) parse YAML or JSON, merge meta.base, migrate, validate; raises ScenarioError on the first problem Scenario.problems() every problem as a list of strings, without raising Scenario.from_dict(doc), Scenario.minimal(), as_dict(), to_yaml(), write(path) build or edit a scenario as a document v2xw.run(scenario, *, build_utc=None, recording=None, metrics=True, metric_window_s=1.0, ma_policy=None) run it; scenario may be a path. build_utc defaults to now, read in Python, because the engine reads no clock Run.metrics.series(name) a metric's time series; windows with too few samples for an estimate are left out, not zeroed Run.metrics.arrow() / ipc() / summary() / digest the table zero-copy, as IPC bytes, the manifest's summary, its digest Recording.open(path), verify(), channels, records(channel, limit), arrow(channel), content_digest() read a recording back

python/examples/run_and_read_metric.py is this walk-through as a script. With no argument it runs the built-in minimal scenario with a short Poisson demand, so it works in a fresh checkout:

python python/examples/run_and_read_metric.py                       # built-in minimal scenario
python python/examples/run_and_read_metric.py scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml

Short runs report insufficiency

On a five-second run with two vehicles, pdr has too few receptions to estimate, and the example prints "no point estimate" for it. That is the statistics refusing to report a number it cannot support (Metrics and outputs).

items.title: Check determinism
items.text:
a, b = v2xw.run_twice(scenario, build_utc="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")
assert a == b      # digests over every record's instant, channel, visibility and bytes, in order

items.title: Write a model in Python
items.text:
v2xw.plugins provides base classes to subclass, card() to build a model card that validates, and handles that put a Python object behind the engine's trait.

Base class Called Notes CarFollowing once per vehicle per mobility step: accel(ego, leader, lane, weather) -> m/s² pure; abstract tier only; each call crosses the interpreter lock, so expect a large slowdown Detector once per window: on_messages(ctx, batch) -> [Observation] batch is a pyarrow.RecordBatch of the window's received messages MaPolicy once per MA step with new evidence: decide(ctx, batch) the batch is the ma.received columns, never ground truth

python/examples/python_idm.py writes the Intelligent Driver Model as a plug-in (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000), runs the conformance kit over it, then shows the kit failing a copy that adds random.gauss jitter:

import v2xw
from v2xw.plugins import CarFollowing, card, equation, parameter, source

m = v2xw.math

class Idm(CarFollowing):
    card = card(
        id="mobility/car-following/python-idm", family="mobility", version="1.0.0",
        tier=["abstract"],
        purpose="Treiber's Intelligent Driver Model, as a Python plug-in.",
        sources=[source("paper", "Treiber, Hennecke & Helbing (2000), Phys. Rev. E 62(2) 1805")],
        parameters=[parameter("delta", "-", 4.0, source("paper", "Treiber et al. (2000) §II"))],
        # equations, assumptions, limitations and ignores as in the example file
    )
    DELTA = 4.0

    def accel(self, ego, leader, lane, weather) -> float:
        v0 = min(ego.desired_speed_mps, lane.speed_limit_mps)
        a_max = ego.max_accel_mps2
        free = a_max * (1.0 - m.pow(ego.speed_mps / v0, self.DELTA))
        if leader is None:
            return free
        dv = ego.speed_mps - leader.speed_mps
        s_star = (ego.min_gap_m + ego.speed_mps * ego.time_headway_s
                  + ego.speed_mps * dv / (2.0 * m.sqrt(a_max * ego.comfort_decel_mps2)))
        return free - a_max * m.pow(max(s_star, 0.0) / max(leader.gap_m, 0.01), 2.0)

handle = Idm().attach()                     # the model behind the engine's trait
print(handle.accel(13.888889, gap_m=50.0, leader_speed_mps=13.888889))
v2xw.conformance.check(Idm()).raise_for_failures()

The driver parameters (v0, a, b, T, s0) arrive on ego because the engine draws them per driver; the model holds no state. The equation it implements:

\[ a = a_{max}\left[1 - \left(\frac{v}{v_0}\right)^{\delta} - \left(\frac{s^*}{s}\right)^2\right],\qquad s^* = s_0 + vT + \frac{v\,\Delta v}{2\sqrt{a_{max}\, b}} \]

items.title: The rules a plug-in must keep
items.text:
Rule Why Checked by no random, numpy.random, secrets, os.urandom randomness comes from streams keyed by (domain, entity) purity_guard replaces them with functions that raise, then calls the model no wall clock (time, datetime.now) simulated time arrives as an argument purity_guard no math, no ** on floats the platform libm differs between machines in the low bits; use v2xw.math scan_source (advisory) no iteration over a set or hashed dict where order reaches a result Python randomises string hashing per process scan_source no hidden state between calls the engine reorders and parallelises phases not decidable: v2xw.run_twice over a real scenario catches it

v2xw.conformance.check(model) runs both halves: the Rust-side checks through the engine's call path (determinism, thread-count independence, card validation and completeness, quantisation, finiteness) and the Python-side purity checks. Passing it is necessary, not sufficient.

items.title: A Misbehaviour Authority rule in Python
items.text:
A rule that security.scms.ma_policy cannot express can be a MaPolicy passed to v2xw.run(..., ma_policy=MyRule()) (a scenario file cannot name code). It decides for every provider MA that would run the deployment-wide rule, so the scenario must not set detection.ma or security.scms.ma_policy. A revoke goes through the provider's decision mode and the CRL like a built-in policy's. Define the class in a module file: the manifest pins it as ma_policy:python:<module>.<class> with the SHA-256 of the module's source. run_twice(..., ma_policy_factory=...) takes a factory so each run starts from a fresh rule. A complete example is in python/README.md.

What v2xw.run accepts

In this build v2xw.run takes a Python plug-in only as ma_policy. A CarFollowing or Detector subclass is attached as an engine trait object (attach()), which is what the conformance kit and direct calls such as handle.accel(...) use.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
cd python && maturin develop && python -m pytest
cargo test -p v2xw-py           # the same surface from Rust, without a wheel

items.title: Studio tour
items.text:
The Studio is the browser interface to a running engine. It adds nothing to the wire: every control is a JSON-RPC method of the engine and every picture is decoded from the VWP stream (Engine-UI protocol), so what the page shows is what the engine computed. Package layout and the developer checks: Studio.

flowchart LR
  E["v2xw-server / v2xw serve<br/>:8787"] -- "WebSocket /vwp/v1<br/>Keyframe, Delta, events" --> P[Studio page]
  P -- "JSON-RPC /rpc<br/>run.*, scenario.*, inspect.*, metrics.*" --> E
  E -- "GET /world/{hash}.vwb" --> P
  P -- "/agent/*" --> E
  F[(recording.mcap)] -- "WebAssembly reader, no engine" --> P

items.title: 1. Start the engine and the page
items.text:
Two terminals, from the repository root:

./run-sim.sh scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml    # or any scenario; default scenarios/manhattan-5min.yaml

pnpm --dir ui install
pnpm --dir ui --filter @vwp/studio dev        # http://127.0.0.1:5173

run-sim.sh builds and starts v2xw-server paused at t = 0 and unthrottled. The equivalents, with every flag in the command reference:

v2xw serve --scenario scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --paused --speed 0
v2xw-server --scenario scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml --port 8787 --paused
v2xw-server --actors 200 --port 8787          # synthetic fixture stream, no map needed

The dev server proxies /vwp/v1, /rpc, /world and /agent to VWP_ENGINE (default http://127.0.0.1:8787); VWP_STUDIO_PORT moves the page. A non-loopback --host needs --token.

Fixture or simulator

With no --scenario the server streams a deterministic synthetic fixture whose numbers are fixture values. The header's engine chip says which one answered ("simulator" or "test fixture"); a plot drawn from the fixture is a plot of the fixture.

items.title: 2. Pick a scenario and a city
items.text: The scenario picker is two steps: what happens (the ready-made scenarios of scenarios/ready-made.txt, by their meta.name and meta.description), then where (a city of the library, cities.list, searchable by name and state). Run loads the scenario on the city (scenario.load {path, city}) and starts it: the engine moves the roadside units to that city's busiest signalised intersections, scales demand to its lane length and keeps the local time of day (Worlds and maps).

items.title: 3. The view
items.text:
Control What it does Camera Map (whole area from above; click a vehicle to follow it), Chase, Driver's view, Free, Roadside unit. Chase and Driver's view need a vehicle on the road Layers Radio: transmissions, received messages, channel load, roadside coverage and range rings. Security: attackers, reported and revoked vehicles, detections, claimed versus true position, backend traffic. Map: paths driven, buildings, lane markings, traffic signals, name tags, density, the detailed-simulation area Blind evaluation turns off and locks every layer drawn from ground truth, so the screen shows only what the radios could know. Ground-truth layers carry a GT tag Lighting how street-level views are lit; the map view is always in daylight

Selecting a vehicle subscribes to its telemetry (view.follow). I opens the vehicle overlay: an overview (identity, health, radio, security, queues, neighbours heard), every sent and received message with its decoded contents, and its five queues.

items.title: 4. The timeline
items.text:
The transport bar is play or pause, step, speed, the clock and the timeline. Each control is one RPC (run.resume, run.pause, run.step, run.speed, run.seek, run.start).

  • Certificate changes, detections, revocations and safety warnings are ticks above the track; the scenario's planned events are taller ticks. Click one to jump there; Alt + arrow jumps to the next or previous event.
  • The part of the run already simulated is drawn apart from the part that is not; a seek outside the produced range is refused and the range that would work is shown. --retain and --retain-mb on the server set how much history run.seek can return to.
  • A disabled control says why: which controls the engine accepts depends on its state.

items.title: 5. Settings
items.text:
Ctrl/Cmd + , opens the settings window. Every row is generated from the engine's published settings surface (scenario.get): its label, unit, explanation, default, recommended range, level (Basic or Advanced) and status, the same rows as the configuration reference. Sections follow a research workflow (Run, Traffic, Radio and Channel, Medium Access, Congestion Control, Messages, Networking, Security and Crypto, Certificates and SCMS, Backend and Cellular, Attackers, Output); search looks across all of them. Edits are checked with scenario.validate and applied with scenario.set; Changes lists what differs from the scenario the engine holds, each with an undo.

Quick settings is the short list people change most (published by the engine from crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/guide.rs); it edits the same draft. ?view=settings opens the settings window in a browser window of its own.

items.title: 6. Metrics
items.text: M opens the metrics dashboard: every measurement of the run, grouped by question (channel load, delivery and reliability, latency, security and PKI, misbehaviour detection, privacy, traffic, safety applications), searchable, with favourites pinned first. Click a card to expand it. The dashboard's address is its state (#metrics/<metric>/<dimension>?from=…&to=…), so a link or a reload reopens the same chart. What each metric means and how its interval is computed: Metrics and outputs.

items.title: 7. The other panels
items.text:
Panels open over the view and are mirrored in the URL hash (#settings, #metrics, #runs, …), so the browser's Back button closes them.

Panel Hash What it is for Certificate system #backend the credential system as the engine runs it: entities, flows, vehicles, cases and revocation lists, viewed as ground truth or as one entity ("as RA", "as LA1") sees it. The ETSI CCMS falls back to a single backend diagram Agent #agent the assistant: type a request, it prepares the settings and shows what it changed with undo; the always-on watcher posts alerts while a run moves (Assistant) Runs and recordings #runs the run on screen, recordings opened in this page, the world under them Compare two runs #compare a second run beside this one with a synchronised clock: from a second engine, a local recording or a recording over HTTP; manifest diff and metric differences Commands #commands the engine's own method list (rpc.discover) and a log of every JSON-RPC call the page made Run details #details identifiers, hashes and counters of the run and the world

items.title: 8. Replay a recording without an engine
items.text:
A finished recording.mcap can be scrubbed in the page with no server. The replay reader is the engine's own Rust reader compiled to WebAssembly (crates/v2xw-wasm), and the frames it returns are the recorded Keyframe and Delta frames byte for byte, so the page decodes them with the same code as the live stream. It is a build step, because the recording's zstd codec is C and needs a WebAssembly-capable clang (Apple's has no wasm32 back end; Homebrew's llvm does):

crates/v2xw-wasm/scripts/build-wasm.sh --web ui/apps/studio/public/wasm

That writes v2xw_replay.js and v2xw_replay_bg.wasm where the Studio loads them (/wasm/). Open the recording from the Runs or Compare panel; a recording served over HTTP is fetched a range at a time. Without the module, the panel says how to build it.

Geometry

A recording carries poses and signals but no world payload, so a replay needs the world from elsewhere: a world.vwb beside the recording (v2xw import-osm writes one) or the run it is being compared against. The page says which it used.

items.title: Assistant
items.text:
The built-in assistant (crates/v2xw-copilot) turns a request in plain words into a scenario, runs it, watches it and reports what happened. It is built on one premise: a language model knows nothing about this simulator and is never asked to. Every fact it states comes from something machine-readable the engine already has, and every number in a report comes from a deterministic analyst, not the model. It is optional: a run never depends on it, and nothing it does reaches a recording, a metric, a manifest or a digest.

flowchart LR
  P[prompt] --> A[agent loop]
  A <--> LLM["language model<br/>(Claude or OpenAI)"]
  A --> G["grounding: model cards,<br/>metric definitions (in process)"]
  A --> SC["scenario check: the engine's<br/>own loader and validator"]
  A --> RPC["engine JSON-RPC<br/>(the Studio's methods)"]
  RPC --> E[engine run]
  E --> AN["deterministic analyst:<br/>findings and numbers"]
  AN --> R[report]
  LLM -. overview, checked number by number .-> R

items.title: Three ways to use it
items.text:
Where Command or place What happens Command line v2xw agent "<prompt>" builds a scenario, runs it to the end, prints a Markdown report on stdout (progress on stderr) Studio the Agent panel (#agent) prepares the settings as the settings window's draft, shows each change with undo; the watcher posts alerts while the run moves HTTP /agent/* on v2xw serve or v2xw-server the endpoints the panel uses 
v2xw agent "compare DSRC and LTE-V2X delivery at rush hour" > report.md
v2xw agent --no-model > report.md                 # no language model: run as shipped, analyst's report
v2xw agent --engine http://127.0.0.1:8787 --analyse   # analyse the run an engine is serving
v2xw serve --scenario scenarios/midtown-normal.yaml   # the engine with the assistant's endpoints

Without --engine, v2xw agent starts an engine in-process with --scenario (default scenarios/phase1-grid.yaml) and stops it after the report. v2xw-server serves the endpoints unless --no-agent; v2xw serve --attach <url> serves only the endpoints in front of an engine already running. Every flag: agent, serve.

items.title: Providers and their environment variables
items.text:
The provider is chosen in the server's environment. v2xw-server and run-sim.sh also read these from --env-file (default ./.env) when they are not already set; only these variables are taken from the file.

Variable Meaning V2XW_AGENT_PROVIDER anthropic (default; claude also accepted) or openai ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the Claude key; else a key file named by V2XW_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/v2xw/anthropic.key, else ~/.config/v2xw/anthropic.key. A key file inside the working directory is refused V2XW_AGENT_MODEL overrides the Claude model (default claude-opus-5-5) V2XW_AGENT_EFFORT Claude effort: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max V2XW_AGENT_FALLBACKS off drops the server-side refusal-fallback request field (for a proxy that rejects beta fields) ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL another endpoint (a gateway); /v1/messages is appended OPENAI_API_KEY the OpenAI key OPENAI_MODEL overrides the OpenAI model (default gpt-4o-mini) OPENAI_BASE_URL another endpoint OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT minimal, low, medium, high for a reasoning model OPENAI_API chat (Chat Completions) or responses (the Responses API); unset starts on Chat Completions and moves to Responses when the model says tools need it

When the provider asked for has no key and the other has one, the other is used. With no key at all, everything that needs no model still works: running a scenario and the deterministic analysis. GET /agent/status says whether a model is attached, which one, and where its key comes from, by name, never by value.

Keys stay in the server process

The key goes into the request header written to curl's standard input and nowhere else: not into a log, an argument vector, a transcript, a tool result or anything served to the browser, and everything the API returns is redacted before it is shown. Put keys in the environment or a key file outside the repository; .env is read but should not be committed.

items.title: What it can do
items.text:
The model is given a small set of high-level tools, and each one is carried out through the engine's own JSON-RPC methods, the same ones the Studio calls:

Tool Does list_scenarios, get_scenario the shipped scenarios; a base scenario's document list_cities the city library, with whether each map is downloaded find_settings, setting_help search the published settings by plain words; everything about one setting (label, unit, range, sources) setup, prepare_scenario build the next run from a base (current, a scenario id, or last) with the request's changes, validated by the engine run_prepared, simulate run a prepared scenario, or build, validate, run and analyse one or more variants run_control start, pause, resume, step, seek, change speed, stop the served run live_metrics, query_metric the run's metrics with units; one metric over time or by a dimension inspect a node (telemetry, queues, neighbours), a link, an entity analyse_current_run, finding_detail the analyst's findings on the run on screen; one finding's evidence compare_runs, list_runs, engine_runs compare runs of this conversation (the same comparison as v2xw compare); the runs it made; the runs the engine kept sensitivity how sensitive a metric is to a setting, from the checked-in sweeps (Sensitivity analysis) registry__metric, registry__model_card a metric's definition, a model's card, with citation

The engine methods behind them are scenario.list, scenario.load, scenario.get, scenario.set, scenario.validate, run.start, run.status, run.pause, run.resume, run.step, run.seek, run.speed, run.stop, metrics.query, inspect.entity, inspect.node, inspect.link and explain (Engine server and RPC). Follow-ups ("now double the density", "compare with LTE-V2X") keep the conversation and start from the last run's scenario. A stop is checked before every model call, every tool and every poll, and a run the agent started is paused, not left running.

The Studio's Commands panel (#commands) is the lower-level surface: its tool list is the engine's rpc.discover document, translated to tool definitions (run.start becomes run__start), and it logs every JSON-RPC call the page made.

items.title: How it is grounded
items.text:
Question Where the answer comes from what a model does, its parameters and sources the model cards, each hit cited with model id, version and the SHA-256 of the card the run manifest pins what a metric means, on what grid, missing what the metric definitions what can be set, to what the engine's published settings index and attacker catalogue is this scenario valid the engine's loader and validator itself where a number came from the run's provenance chain joined to the cards where the bottlenecks are the deterministic analyst over the run's metrics and backend view

A lookup that misses returns "not known", with what was asked and what is declared, never a default or a guess. The model plans and writes; a number in its overview that no tool produced is sent back once for a rewrite and, if it survives, listed in the report as unverified.

items.title: The watcher
items.text: While a run moves, the server's watcher reads run.status once a second and the run's evidence every few seconds, and says in plain words when a finding appears, worsens or clears (delivery collapsing, a busy channel, verify-queue drops, no vehicles, gridlock, attacks detected or missed), when a trend crosses the analyst's thresholds, or when the credential backend's counters rise. At the end it writes the run's summary: verdict, layers, problems, overview and analysis (GET /agent/summary). With a model the overview is the model's, checked number by number; without one it is the analyst's. The watcher only reads: it never pauses, steps or changes the run, and the run never waits for it.

items.title: HTTP endpoints
items.text:
Endpoint Does GET /agent/status whether a model is attached, which one, where its key comes from, how to add one POST /agent/ask {prompt} start the agent on a prompt; follow-ups continue the conversation POST /agent/run {base} run a shipped scenario and analyse it, no model needed POST /agent/analyse analyse the run on screen, no model needed GET /agent/events?job=&after= the job's events from after on: plan, changes, progress, analysis, report POST /agent/stop stop the job at its next check, pausing a run it started POST /agent/reset forget the conversation POST /agent/undo restore a setting the agent changed (refused while the agent is busy) GET /agent/watch?after= the watcher's observations since after GET /agent/summary the last finished run's summary POST /agent/compare-signatures {document?, scenario?, schemes?, duration_s?}, GET /agent/compare-signatures run a signature comparison on a thread; its status and result

A server started with --token requires the bearer token on these too.

items.title: Why it cannot change a result
items.text: crates/v2xw-copilot/src/boundary.rs holds the rule and its checks: the crate's only way into a run is the JSON-RPC transport (no context, recorder, scheduler or random stream); every method it can name is one the server publishes for the Studio, so it has a person's authority and no more; a scenario it drafts is text that a run pins by content hash, so a run's outputs are a function of the document and the seed, not of who typed it; and the crate reads no clock, draws no random number and computes no exported float. Each check has a test that injects the forbidden construct and requires it to fail.

items.title: Comparing runs
items.text:
Five commands read finished runs and tell you what differs or what went wrong. None of them changes a run; three re-read a recording, one re-runs a scenario under several schemes.

Command Question Input Output v2xw compare what changed between two runs, and is it the settings or noise? two run directories, digests, experiment directories or replication lists a table (text, JSON, Markdown, CSV) v2xw compare-signatures what does each signature scheme cost against ECDSA P-256? one scenario comparison.json, .csv, .md v2xw ma-replay how would other MA decision rules have done on these reports? a run with report records ma-replay.csv v2xw check-traffic did the traffic break an invariant? a run with a full recording a pass/fail table v2xw energy what did the traffic emit and consume? a full recording a fleet table with health bands

Every flag: Command-line tool.

items.title: v2xw compare
items.text:
v2xw compare runs/base runs/tx23                              # two run directories
v2xw compare prev.json runs/tx23 --markdown                   # a digest saved from the Studio or runs.digest
v2xw compare runs/a1,runs/a2,runs/a3 runs/b1,runs/b2,runs/b3  # replications pooled per side
v2xw compare runs/sweep-a runs/sweep-b --all --json           # experiment directories, every metric

A side is a run directory (scenario.resolved.yaml and metrics.json), a run digest (v2xw/run-digest/1), an experiment output directory (every run under its runs/ pooled as replications), or a comma-separated list of those. The Studio's "compare with previous run", the assistant and v2xw compare all print the same value (v2xw_server::compare::Comparison), so the three cannot disagree.

items.title: How a run becomes one number per metric
items.text: As the experiment runner does: proportions pool their counts, ratios of sums pool their two sums, scalars and distributions are sample-count weighted means of each window's figure (so a p95 is the typical window's p95), counts are summed, and a level metric aggregated by its maximum (a CRL's entries as last published, a memory high-water mark) pools to its largest value.

items.title: When a change is "meaningful"
items.text:
A row is shown (without --all) when its change is meaningful:

  1. it crosses a health band of the metric, or it moves by at least 10 % of the baseline (RELATIVE_FLOOR) and by more than the unit's resolution; and
  2. when the runs used different seeds, or either side has replications, the difference exceeds twice the combined standard error, estimated per run by batch means over its windows (Law, Simulation Modeling and Analysis, 5th ed., §9.5.3; up to 10 batches).

With the same seed and no replications, the runs share every random draw the settings did not touch (common random numbers), so the difference is the settings'; the output says so.

The verdict column reads the metric's health direction (v2xw_metrics::health):

Verdict Meaning better / worse moved in the direction the metric's polarity calls better or worse changed moved, and the metric has no better direction (a density, a flow) same within the unit's resolution missing one side does not have it 
  1 setting changed: Vehicles entering per hour 30.0 veh/h → 600.0 veh/h.
  15 of 36 metrics changed meaningfully: 3 better, 4 worse, 8 neutral.
  …
Settings changed:
  Vehicles entering per hour               30.0 veh/h → 600.0 veh/h

metric                       A              B         change         %  verdict
offered_load       32259 bit/s   130592 bit/s    98332 bit/s  +304.8 %  changed
half_duplex_rate             0        7.80e-3        7.80e-3            worse
…

--json is schema v2xw/run-comparison/1: both sides' identities, the settings that differ, and a row per metric with a, b, delta, pct, better, verdict, health levels, meaningful and beyond_noise.

items.title: v2xw compare-signatures
items.text:
v2xw compare-signatures scenarios/compare-signature-schemes.yaml \
    --schemes ecdsa-p256,ml-dsa-44,falcon-512,hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256 --duration 60

It is the experiment runner with one sweep axis, security.signature, one seed and one replication, and the opt-in signing-overhead metric group (metrics: [all, signing]) on in every run. The run seed does not depend on the cell, so every scheme sees the same traffic, channel draws and credential calendar. A stopped comparison resumes through the runner's journal.

File in --out What comparison.json the schemes' registry facts and every row, value, difference and health level (v2xw/signature-comparison/1); the Studio's comparison view loads it comparison.csv the same, one line per (row, scheme) comparison.md a table for a paper or an issue: differences in brackets, called-out ones in bold runs/… each run's metrics, report and manifest

The rows are the sig_* metrics: signature, signer-identifier and certificate bytes per message and their airtime shares; signing and verification latency per scheme and engine (ml-dsa-44@cpu, ecdsa-p256@hsm); signer and verifier utilisation, verification capacity and headroom, dropped and late verifications; fragments per message and reassembly loss; added end-to-end latency; the CBR the envelope adds; backend bytes and certificate-authority load. A difference is called out when it crosses a health band, or moves by 10 % of the baseline and more than the row's resolution. One realisation: no confidence interval is claimed. Post-quantum schemes are size and cost models (Security and crypto).

items.title: v2xw ma-replay
items.text:
v2xw ma-replay runs/attack                                     # the built-in rule family
v2xw ma-replay runs/attack --policies scenarios/attack-fake-positions.yaml

Replays the misbehaviour reports a finished run recorded through a family of Misbehaviour Authority decision rules, without re-simulating. The run must have security.scms.report_records: true.

A rule reads only the ma.received channel: field for field what the deciding MA read from each report (reporter and accused pseudonym certificates, subtypes, evidence window, claimed position accuracy, issuer, and the Linkage Authorities' "same device" token). Reports the MA set aside are dropped first. Ground truth (gt.device_exposure, pki.report_fate) is joined only to score decisions, and a blindness check renames every identifier in the MA view and requires the decisions to rename the same way.

Rule Revokes pseudonym-k a pseudonym certificate once k distinct reporters accused it (k = 1 is kept as the unsound baseline) device-k a device (by its LA link) once k distinct reporters accused any of its pseudonyms within a window w catch a device when its reporters' accuracy-weighted factors sum to θ within w; a position report counts \(\mathrm{clamp}(1 - 2a/(\text{excess}\cdot\tau), 0, 1)\) with a the claimed accuracy and τ = 1 m (after Kamel et al., "CaTch", IEEE WCNC 2019, re-implemented from the paper) cluster as device-k, but a device in a class (secMark phase, accuracy band, issuer) with c or more accused devices in w needs m·k reporters --policies every preset and named policy of the scenario's security.scms.ma_policy, replayed through the run's own evaluator

A parameterisation is sound when it needs corroboration (k ≥ 2, θ ≥ 2). ma-replay.csv has one row per rule and parameter:

Column Meaning rule, params, sound the rule and its parameters decisions revocation decisions made honest_devices, honest_device_hours, honest_blocked, honest_blocked_per_1e6_dh false revocations, per 10⁶ honest device-hours attackers, attackers_revoked attackers in the run and how many were revoked tta_median_s, tta_max_s, attack_budget_s the attacker's time to act: attack start to revocation decision

ma-replay-attackers.csv has one line per rule, parameter and attacker (attack_start_s, revoked_s, budget_s) for paired comparisons across runs of one seed.

Offline versus in-run

An offline replay shows no feedback: a revoked device keeps sending, the CRL's delays do not apply and reporters' reputations do not change. A sweep over security.scms.ma_policy.preset runs every policy in full and writes ma-policy-family.csv and .md (Experiments and sweeps).

items.title: v2xw check-traffic
items.text:
v2xw check-traffic runs/midtown-normal

Audits the traffic of a finished run from what was recorded (the poses, lanes and signal lamps the Studio replays), not from inside the engine, so a vehicle the engine thinks is lawfully held at a red whose recorded lamp is green is caught. It needs recording.mcap at --record-level full and scenario.resolved.yaml (the world is rebuilt from it), and exits 1 when a row fails.

Row Fails when stopped_on_green a queue head stands at its stop line longer than --green-stop-s (6 s) on its own protected green with room ahead; a hold behind a standing exit queue (keep-clear, NY VTL §1175) is not counted stopped_on_permitted_green, stopped_at_clear_junction the same on a permitted green, or at an empty unsignalised junction phantom_stop, long_stop a vehicle stands mid-lane with nobody within 30 m, or longer than one signal cycle plus a margin (120 s off a signal); kerbside stops are excused red_entry a vehicle enters a junction on a recorded red lamp_phase_unknown a plan's recorded lamps match none of its phases overlap, jump two vehicles closer than the shorter body on one lane; a step longer than the speed explains decel, accel, jerk, speeding over 9 m/s² braking, 6 m/s² accelerating, jerk over 30 m/s³ in more than one step in a thousand, over 1.25 × the limit + 2 m/s ped_jump, ped_speed_jump, ped_heading_flip a pedestrian step no walker makes

It also measures, with no pass mark, the stop-line saturation headway and start-up lost time (HCM 7th ed. ch. 19: base 1,900 pc/h/ln is a 1.89 s headway, start-up lost time 2 s), the longest stop, mean speed per road class against the limit, and gridlock teleports. --trace <actor> prints one vehicle's every step on stderr.

items.title: v2xw energy
items.text:
v2xw energy runs/glosa/recording.mcap
v2xw energy runs/glosa/recording.mcap --emission-model moves-opmode --opmode-csv out/opmode.csv

Scores a recording's traffic for CO2, fuel, NOx, PM and EV energy without re-running it: the energy provider reads only gt.kinematics, so any full recording can be scored, under a different model or fleet than the run used. The energy section the run carried is the starting point (from the recording's scenario attachment); --spec replaces it, and --emission-model (hbefa3, phemlight, moves-opmode) and --ev-model (kurczveil, vt-cpem) override the models. The fleet draw is keyed by the recording's master seed, so a re-score reproduces the run's fleet.

models      energy/emission/hbefa3 (combustion), energy/ev/kurczveil (electric); section from default
scored      12 vehicles from 4531 gt.kinematics records, 0 unmodelled
fleet       … g/km CO2, … L/100km fuel, - EV

class          km     CO2 kg    fuel L   NOx g    PM g   EV kWh  stops
passenger    2.45      1.063     0.457    0.43   0.018    0.000      7

health
  warn         co2_per_km             passenger  … (healthy 90..350)
  ok           nox_per_km             passenger  … (healthy 0..1)
  not-measured ev_energy_per_100km    passenger  - (healthy 9..25)

A warn is a value outside the band a realistic fleet would show, which on a short run with stop-and-go traffic is often the traffic, not the model. The models and their sources: Energy and emissions.

items.title: Datasets and exports
items.text: The recording is the run's complete record. Exporters turn it into files other tools read: columnar tables, VeReMi-style misbehaviour traces and SUMO output files. They run after the run and over the recording, never inside the event loop, so an export cannot disagree with the recording beside it. Code: crates/v2xw-engine/src/export.rs, crates/v2xw-engine/src/sumo_outputs.rs, crates/v2xw-record/src/export/ and crates/v2xw-record/src/dataset/.

items.title: Naming exporters in a scenario
items.text:
exporters:
  - id: parquet
    opts: {profile: node}          # drop every ground-truth channel and column
  - id: veremi
    opts: {codebook: veremi-ext, slice_s: 3600}
  - id: sumo-fcd
    opts: {period_s: 1.0}

Each entry is exporters[].id with its opts, and writes into <out>/<id>/. Naming any exporter makes the run keep recording.mcap; a run that names exporters refuses --no-recording and --checkpoint-every. v2xw run --veremi <codebook> adds the veremi exporter from the command line. An id this build does not have is refused at load with the list of valid ids.

id Writes Options recording keeps the MCAP recording itself parquet one Apache Parquet table per recorded channel, the primary analysis format profile: full (default) or node arrow the same tables as Arrow IPC profile jsonl the same tables as JSON Lines profile veremi VeReMi traces per receiver and a ground-truth log codebook, slice_s sumo-fcd, sumo-tripinfo, sumo-edgedata, sumo-lanedata, sumo-summary, sumo-e1, sumo-e2 SUMO's output files see below

items.title: Tables: Parquet, Arrow, JSON Lines
items.text:
One table per recorded channel (node.tx, node.rx, phy.rx, mac.cbr, metric.sample, ma.report, …; the channel list and each channel's visibility class are in Metrics and outputs). Every float is quantised to the grid its column declares, the grids are written beside the data as schema.json, and a scan reads the files back and fails on any value off its grid.

opts.profile: node is the blind export: it drops the ground-truth channels entirely and projects the ground-truth columns out of mixed (node-and-gt) channels, so a node export and a ground-truth export never share a file. Each file's schema records which it is.
