  • the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

items.title: channel_load
items.text:
Offered load against capacity, as each node sees it: the air time of every frame arriving above the −85 dBm busy threshold plus the node's own offered air time, over the window. One is a channel exactly full; above one, more is being offered than the channel can carry.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation distribution Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, node Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1 Source Torrent-Moreno, Mittag, Santi, Hartenstein, IEEE Trans. Veh. Technol. 58(7), 2009 (paper) Better lower (standard basis) Healthy below 0.50: congestion control has nothing to do Caution 0.5: above 0.50: SAE J2945/1 congestion control is lowering power and message rate Unhealthy 0.68: above the 0.68 ETSI congestion target; vehicles will throttle their messages Band source ETSI TS 102 687 V1.2.1 §5.4 (adaptive DCC CBR_target 0.68); SAE J2945/1 vMinCBP 50 % (Ahmad et al., IEEE TVT 68(3) 2019, Table I)

Does not account for:

  • frames neighbours' MACs refused, which never reached the air
  • the merging of overlaps: overlapping frames are summed

items.title: channel_occupancy
items.text:
The fraction of the window each node's own transmissions occupied the channel — the channel occupancy ratio C-V2X congestion control limits, applied to 802.11p. Distribution across the nodes that transmitted.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1 Source 3GPP TS 36.214 §5.1.31; ETSI TS 103 574 (standard)

Does not account for:

  • nodes that did not transmit in the window
  • inter-frame spacing and backoff, which are not transmitted time

items.title: collision_rate
items.text:
The fraction of resolved reception attempts lost because two transmissions overlapped at the receiver (causes collision, hidden-terminal and resource-collision).

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: attempts lost to a collision / attempts resolved Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • a frame that survived an overlap by capture, which is a success
  • attempts still in flight when the run ended

items.title: crl_bytes
items.text:
The revocation list's size in bytes as last published.

Field Value Unit B Aggregation max Visibility public Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • compression on the distribution path
  • what any individual node holds

items.title: crl_entries
items.text:
The number of entries in the revocation list as last published.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation max Visibility public Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • what any individual node holds, which lags the published list

items.title: delivery_ratio
items.text:
Application-level packet delivery ratio: of the reception attempts at candidate receivers, the fraction that reached the receiver's applications — after the PHY, reassembly, the receive queue, the verification policy and the signature check. With no dimension over every distance; dist_bin in 50 m bins out to 1 km.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: messages delivered to the application / attempts resolved Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, dist_bin, node Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • attempts still in flight when the run ended
  • receivers outside the engine's 1 km candidate range

items.title: density
items.text:
Edie's density over the window: Σ Δt / (L·T), in veh/km per lane — over the whole network's motorised lanes, and per lane where the run reports lanes.

Field Value Unit veh/km Aggregation rate Visibility gt Dimensions t, region Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source L. C. Edie 1963; FHWA Traffic Flow Theory ch. 2 (paper)

Does not account for:

  • lanes whose length the run did not declare
  • vehicle length, so this is a count density, not an occupancy

items.title: det_accuracy
items.text:
Accuracy: (tp + tn) / total.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: correct decisions / subjects Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • class imbalance: with 2 % attackers, calling everyone benign scores 0.98

items.title: det_f1
items.text:
The F1 score, 2·tp / (2·tp + fp + fn). Reported without a confidence interval: see the card's limitations.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation mean Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • a confidence interval, which has no exact binomial form here
  • true negatives, which F1 ignores by construction

items.title: det_fn
items.text:
The fn cell of the detection confusion matrix over the declared subject population.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level, cell Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • subjects the run never declared
  • attackers that never acted, which are not in the population

items.title: det_fp
items.text:
The fp cell of the detection confusion matrix over the declared subject population.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level, cell Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • subjects the run never declared
  • attackers that never acted, which are not in the population

items.title: det_fpr
items.text:
The false-positive rate: fp / (fp + tn).

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: false positives / truly benign subjects Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30 Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy at most 1 % of honest vehicles are wrongly flagged Caution 0.01: above 1 % of honest vehicles are wrongly flagged Unhealthy 0.05: above 5 % of honest vehicles are wrongly flagged: revocation would hit them Band source engineering choice; no standard sets a false-positive rate

Does not account for:

  • the base rate: at a 2 % attacker fraction a 1 % false-positive rate still produces more false than true positives

items.title: det_precision
items.text:
Precision: tp / (tp + fp). At the report level this is the per-report precision of the legacy validate.py; at the vehicle level it is revoked ∩ attacker / revoked.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: true positives / positives Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • the base rate
  • reports about subjects the run never declared

items.title: det_recall
items.text:
Recall, also the true-positive rate: tp / (tp + fn).

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: true positives / truly misbehaving subjects Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30 Better higher (engineering basis) Healthy at least 90 % of attackers are detected Caution 0.9: between half and 90 % of attackers are detected Unhealthy 0.5: fewer than half the attackers are detected Band source engineering choice; no standard sets a detection rate

Does not account for:

  • how many reports each detection took
  • attackers that never acted

items.title: det_tn
items.text:
The tn cell of the detection confusion matrix over the declared subject population.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level, cell Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • subjects the run never declared
  • attackers that never acted, which are not in the population

items.title: det_tp
items.text:
The tp cell of the detection confusion matrix over the declared subject population.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level, cell Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • subjects the run never declared
  • attackers that never acted, which are not in the population

items.title: digest_misses
items.text:
Digest-signed messages per second, all nodes, whose signer certificate the receiver had not cached. Attaching the full certificate more often lowers it. Not a P2PCD request: a missed pseudonym waits for the sender's next certificate (IEEE 1609.2-2022 clause 8). Named p2pcd_requests before 2026-10-25.

Field Value Unit 1/s Aggregation rate Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • what the receiver did next

items.title: drac
items.text:
The deceleration rate required to avoid the crash: (v_follower − v_leader)² / (2·gap) for a closing same-lane pair.

Field Value Unit m/s² Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper) Better lower (literature basis) Healthy p95 braking needed to avoid a crash is gentle Caution 2.0: p95 braking needed is firm Unhealthy 3.35: p95 braking needed is above 3.35 m/s²: critical Band source Archer 2005 (DRAC critical above 3.35 m/s²); 2 m/s² is an engineering choice

Does not account for:

  • the follower's braking capability or the road surface
  • vehicle length, as with ttc_min

items.title: e2e_latency
items.text:
End-to-end delay of each delivered message: from its generation at the sender to its delivery to the receiver's applications, including signing, channel access, air time, propagation, parsing and verification. With no dimension it is every V2V delivery; msg_type narrows it to one message type; flow names a non-V2V flow (a backend exchange, a multi-hop relay).

Field Value Unit ms Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t, flow, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Better lower (standard basis) Healthy p99 latency within half the 100 ms safety budget Caution 50.0: p99 latency within the 100 ms safety budget, but above half of it Unhealthy 100.0: p99 latency above the 100 ms basic-safety requirement Band source 3GPP TS 22.185 §5.1 (maximum latency 100 ms) and 3GPP TR 22.886; SAE J2945/1 (100 ms BSM interval). The 50 ms caution line is half the budget, an engineering choice

Does not account for:

  • messages that were never delivered, which have no latency
  • the application's own processing after delivery

items.title: envelope_overhead
items.text:
Security envelope bytes divided by application payload bytes, over the window. A ratio of two sums, so it carries no confidence interval; both sums are reported.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: envelope bytes / payload bytes Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • network and MAC headers, which are neither envelope nor payload
  • a binomial interval, which does not apply to a ratio of sums

items.title: false_accusations
items.text:
Benign subjects with at least one report (level = report) and benign subjects that were revoked (level = vehicle).

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, level Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • how many times each benign subject was reported
  • a benign subject reported and then cleared, which still counts

items.title: flow
items.text:
Edie's flow over the window: Σ v·Δt / (L·T), in veh/h per lane — over the whole network's motorised lanes (L their summed length; the macroscopic fundamental diagram's production), and per lane where the run reports lanes.

Field Value Unit veh/h Aggregation rate Visibility gt Dimensions t, region Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source L. C. Edie 1963; FHWA Traffic Flow Theory ch. 2 (paper)

Does not account for:

  • lanes whose length the run did not declare
  • the lane's capacity, which is a property of the road

items.title: frag_content_loss
items.text:
The share of the fragmented SDUs' payload that did not reach the receiver, which is what independently interpretable segments lose instead of whole messages.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ payload octets of fragments that did not decode / Σ payload octets of attempted SDUs Visibility gt Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • content a decoded piece carried of an SDU never reassembled

items.title: frag_content_loss_predicted
items.text:
The content loss predicts from each fragment's PHY success probability, weighted by its share of the payload.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ Σ_i w_i p_i / fragmented SDUs attempted Visibility gt Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • correlation between fragments

items.title: frag_fragment_loss
items.text:
The share of the fragments of attempted SDUs that did not decode at the receiver: the per-fragment loss the SDU loss amplifies.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: fragments that did not decode / fragments of attempted SDUs Visibility gt Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • fragments of SDUs no fragment of which reached the receiver

items.title: frag_sdu_loss
items.text:
The share of fragmented SDUs, per receiver that had any of their fragments in range, of which some fragment did not decode — the SDU's loss when the pieces mean nothing alone.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: fragmented SDUs with a fragment that did not decode / fragmented SDUs attempted Visibility gt Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • losses above reassembly (queue, verification), on node.rx

items.title: frag_sdu_loss_independent
items.text:
The SDU loss if every fragment were lost independently at the window's own measured per-fragment loss rate p̂ (frag_fragment_loss): the textbook 1 − (1 − p)^n. Realised SDU loss below it means the fragments of one SDU tend to be lost together.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ (1 − (1 − p̂)^n_g) / fragmented SDUs attempted Visibility gt Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • the per-fragment loss's dependence on distance and size

items.title: frag_sdu_loss_predicted
items.text:
The SDU loss predicts from each fragment's PHY success probability at that receiver, if fragments were lost independently.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ (1 − Π (1 − p_i)) / fragmented SDUs attempted Visibility gt Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • correlation between fragments, which is what the gap shows

items.title: full_cert_share
items.text:
The certificate attachment rate: messages whose signer identifier is a full certificate rather than a digest, divided by all messages.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: messages carrying a full certificate / all messages Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • peer-to-peer certificate distribution responses, which carry certificates outside the ordinary message flow
  • messages whose signer identifier the producer did not record

items.title: goodput
items.text:
Application payload bytes delivered to receivers' applications (node.rx), divided by the window's length.

Field Value Unit B/s Aggregation rate Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • duplicate suppression: one broadcast to ten receivers counts ten times
  • headers and the security envelope, which are in bytes_air

items.title: half_duplex_rate
items.text:
The fraction of resolved reception attempts lost because the receiver was itself transmitting.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: attempts lost to half duplex / attempts resolved Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • attempts still in flight when the run ended
  • receivers outside the engine's candidate range

items.title: headway_distance
items.text:
Distance headway: the difference of lane positions between a follower and its leader.

Field Value Unit m Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • vehicle length, so this is centre-to-centre, not gap
  • vehicles on other lanes

items.title: headway_time
items.text:
Time headway: the gap to the leader divided by the follower's speed.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • a stopped follower, which contributes no sample
  • vehicle length

items.title: latency_stage
items.text:
The time each delivered message spent in one stage of its journey. For V2V: sign_queue, sign (the signer's own time), handoff (the sender's host latency and J2945/1 transmit-time offset between the signature and the MAC), mac_aifs, mac_backoff, mac_defer (deferral to a busy medium, including repeated AIFS), airtime, propagation, reception (parsing and the verification policy), verify_queue, verify. The stages tile the journey, so they sum to e2e_latency message by message.

Field Value Unit ms Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t, flow, msg_type, stage Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • undelivered messages
  • the interleaving of AIFS, backoff and deferral inside the access delay

items.title: latency_stage_share
items.text:
The share of the total end-to-end delay spent in one stage: the stage's summed duration over the summed latency of the same messages. The shares of all stages of one flow sum to one.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ time in this stage / Σ end-to-end latency Visibility node Dimensions t, flow, msg_type, stage Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • undelivered messages
  • per-message variation: it is a ratio of sums, not a mean of ratios

items.title: latency_trace_rejected
items.text:
Traces in the window that were not a valid decomposition of their message's latency (a gap, an overlap or a negative stage). Anything above zero is a producer defect, and those messages are missing from every latency metric.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • delivered messages whose stamps were absent altogether

items.title: link_overhead
items.text:
The share of the octets on the air that are the link layer: LLC/SNAP, the 802.11 QoS Data MAC header and the frame check sequence.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ LLC/SNAP, MAC header and FCS octets / Σ octets on the air Visibility node Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • the 802.11 PLCP header, which is air time and not octets
  • the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

items.title: loss_rate
items.text:
The fraction of all resolved reception attempts that were lost to one cause — a PHY cause (collision, half-duplex, below-sensitivity, fading, …) or one above it (verification overflow, invalid signature, revoked, …). Summed over causes it is one minus the delivery ratio.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: attempts lost with this cause / attempts resolved Visibility node Dimensions t, cause Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • attempts still in flight when the run ended
  • receivers outside the engine's candidate range

items.title: mac_access_delay
items.text:
Channel-access delay per transmitted frame: from the frame reaching the MAC (its signature complete) to its preamble going on the air — AIFS, backoff and deferral to a busy medium.

Field Value Unit ms Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Source IEEE 802.11-2020 §10.23.2 (standard) Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy p95 channel access within 10 ms Caution 10.0: p95 channel access above 10 ms: a tenth of the 100 ms safety budget Unhealthy 20.0: p95 channel access above 20 ms: a fifth of the 100 ms safety budget is spent waiting for the channel Band source engineering choice against the 100 ms budget of 3GPP TS 22.185 §5.1: 20 % is the run analyst's access_budget_fraction

Does not account for:

  • frames the MAC refused, which never got access
  • signing, which happens before the MAC has the frame

items.title: mac_drops
items.text:
Frames the MAC refused in the window: a full access-category queue or a frame over the MSDU cap.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source IEEE 802.11-2020 §10.23.2 (standard)

Does not account for:

  • frames the node itself never generated because DCC held it back

items.title: mac_queue_depth
items.text:
Frames waiting in a node's EDCA access-category queues, at each MAC report, across nodes.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source IEEE 802.11-2020 §10.23.2 (standard) Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy the transmit queue is usually empty Caution 1.0: the transmit queue is rarely empty: frames wait behind each other Unhealthy 5.0: the transmit queue is backing up; frames will be stale or dropped Band source engineering choice: a mean depth above one frame is a queue that is rarely empty (the run analyst's queue_depth_saturated); five frames is half a second of 10 Hz messages

Does not account for:

  • the depth between reports: it is sampled, not time-averaged
  • frames still in the node's signer, which have not reached the MAC

items.title: mean_speed
items.text:
The space-mean speed, q / k — not the time-mean speed, which is 6–12 % higher on a mixed-speed signalised dataset (Wardrop 1952).

Field Value Unit m/s Aggregation mean Visibility gt Dimensions t, region Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source L. C. Edie 1963; FHWA Traffic Flow Theory ch. 2 (paper)

Does not account for:

  • lanes whose length the run did not declare
  • the time-mean speed, which is a different quantity

items.title: nar
items.text:
Neighbourhood awareness ratio: of the vehicles truly within R metres of each equipped vehicle, the fraction it has received a message from in the last second. Pedestrians' and riders' devices are neither receivers nor neighbours: they beacon at their own rates. Reported at R = 100 m and R = 300 m. Sampled at every mobility step and pooled over the window; the 95 % Wilson interval is computed on the number of distinct neighbour pairs, not on the samples, because one pair seen ten times is not ten independent observations — so a sparse run reports an estimate with a wide interval instead of refusing.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: neighbours within R heard within T / neighbours within R Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, radius Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1 Source Boban and d'Orey, IEEE Trans. Veh. Technol. 65(6), 2016; the interval: Brown, Cai, DasGupta, Statistical Science 16(2), 2001 (Wilson for small n) and Kish, Survey Sampling, 1965 (effective sample size of a clustered sample) (paper) Better higher (engineering basis) Healthy vehicles know about at least 95 % of their neighbours within 100 m Caution 0.95: awareness of neighbours within 100 m below 95 % Unhealthy 0.9: vehicles are unaware of more than 1 in 10 neighbours within 100 m Band source engineering choice matching the 0.9 reception level of 3GPP TR 37.885 (the run analyst's awareness_floor)

Does not account for:

  • roadside units, which have no ground-truth kinematics
  • whether the neighbour was reachable at all (it is counted either way)

items.title: net_header_overhead
items.text:
The share of the octets on the air that are the network and transport header: WSMP for the US stack, GeoNetworking plus BTP for the European one.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ network and transport header octets / Σ octets on the air Visibility node Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • the LLC/SNAP octets, which are in link_overhead
  • the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

items.title: offered_load
items.text:
PSDU bits every node handed to its MAC in the window, whatever became of them, per second — network-wide.

Field Value Unit bit/s Aggregation rate Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time and not bits
  • spatial reuse: this is a network total, not one channel's load

items.title: p2pcd_requests
items.text:
Peer-to-peer certificate distribution requests per second, all nodes: signed SPDUs carrying a learning request for a certificate the sender could not resolve, out-of-band (p2pcdLearningRequest) or inline (inlineP2pcdRequest), IEEE 1609.2-2022 clause 8. Before 2026-10-25 this name counted digest misses, which are now digest_misses.

Field Value Unit 1/s Aggregation rate Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • the responses and the certificates learned
  • nodes whose P2PCD entity is off, which send none

items.title: pdr
items.text:
Packet reception ratio (3GPP TR 36.885 §A.2.1.4): of the equipped receivers truly within range of each frame, the fraction that decoded it. The headline is within 300 m; pdr[100m] and pdr[300m] are the two ranges and dist_bin the 20 m curve. Every receiver in range counts, whether or not the radio evaluated a link to it, so the figure does not depend on the engine's candidate range.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: receivers within range that decoded the frame / receivers within range Visibility gt Dimensions t, radius, dist_bin Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30 Source 3GPP TR 36.885 §A.2.1.4: the packet reception ratio of one transmitted packet is X/Y, Y the receivers located in the distance range (a, b) from the transmitter and X those among them that received it; evaluated in 20 m bins (standard) Better higher (standard basis) Healthy at least 95 % of receivers within 100 m decode each message Caution 0.95: below 95 % within 100 m: losses at short range, where a link should be clean Unhealthy 0.9: below 90 % within 100 m: under the reliability V2V evaluations require Band source 3GPP TR 37.885 (V2X evaluation methodology reads range at a 0.9 packet reception ratio); 0.95 within near range is the run analyst's engineering choice

Does not account for:

  • receivers beyond the stated range
  • reception above the PHY: a decoded frame the receiver then dropped or could not verify counts as received here (delivery_ratio is the application-level figure)
  • coverage: a transmitter with no receiver within range contributes no trials

items.title: pdr_all_pairs
items.text:
Received frames divided by every reception the engine evaluated: every pair within its candidate range, however far and whatever stands between them, per 25 m distance bin. Not the literature's delivery ratio — its denominator is set by the engine's candidate range, so pairs behind a building a kilometre apart count as trials. Kept to show what the radio was asked to do; pdr is the figure to quote.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: received frames / evaluated receptions Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, dist_bin Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • receivers outside the engine's candidate range
  • coverage: a transmitter with no candidate receivers contributes no trials

items.title: pdr_by_cause
items.text:
The share of losses attributable to each loss cause. Invariant I-R3 requires every loss to carry exactly one cause, so the shares sum to one by construction — and when they do not, that is an I-R3violation and not a rounding artefact.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: losses with this cause / all losses Visibility node Dimensions t, cause Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • a frame lost for two reasons at once
  • losses the producer recorded without a cause

items.title: ped_conflicts
items.text:
Vehicle-pedestrian approaches whose time to collision fell below 3 s, each approach counted once.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper)

Does not account for:

  • cyclists
  • the pedestrian's own evasive action

items.title: ped_midblock_share
items.text:
The share of pedestrian samples off every lane: time spent crossing mid-block, away from any crosswalk.

Field Value Unit 1 Aggregation mean Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • a crossing at an unmarked junction leg mapped without a crossing way, which is on a lane

items.title: ped_near_misses
items.text:
Of the vehicle-pedestrian conflicts, those whose time to collision fell below 1.5 s.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper)

Does not account for:

  • cyclists

items.title: ped_ttc
items.text:
The time to collision of every vehicle-pedestrian pair-step below 10 s: a pedestrian walking across a moving vehicle's heading inside its swept width.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper)

Does not account for:

  • a turning vehicle's curved path

items.title: ped_wait
items.text:
Pedestrian delay: the length of each standing episode (below 0.2 m/s) that ended in the window — at a kerb waiting for walk or a gap, mostly.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • why the pedestrian stood

items.title: per
items.text:
The complement of the headline pdr, over the same census within 300 m. Reported separately because a loss-oriented reader should not have to subtract.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: receivers within range that did not decode the frame / receivers within range Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30 Source 3GPP TR 36.885 §A.2.1.4: the packet reception ratio of one transmitted packet is X/Y, Y the receivers located in the distance range (a, b) from the transmitter and X those among them that received it; evaluated in 20 m bins (standard)

Does not account for:

  • the same census as pdr
  • bit errors within a received frame (a frame is received or not)

items.title: pet
items.text:
Post-encroachment time: the interval between one actor leaving a position and a different actor arriving at it, resolved to cells of pet_cell_m.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper)

Does not account for:

  • the conflict angle
  • vehicle extent beyond one cell
  • a cell revisited by the same actor, which is not a conflict

items.title: pir
items.text:
Packet inter-reception time: the gap between successive receptions from the same transmitter at the same receiver. Pedestrians' and riders' devices, which beacon at their own lower rates, are the class vru sample rather than the headline.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t, class Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Source Martelli, Elena Renda, Resta, Santi, 'A measurement-based study of beaconing performance in IEEE 802.11p vehicular networks', IEEE INFOCOM 2012 (packet inter-reception time) (paper) Better lower (standard basis) Healthy p95 gap between messages from one sender under 0.3 s Caution 0.3: p95 gap above 0.3 s: three or more 10 Hz messages lost in a row Unhealthy 0.6: p95 gap above 0.6 s: longer than J2945/1 ever schedules; messages are lost Band source SAE J2945/1 vMaxITT 600 ms (Ahmad et al., IEEE TVT 68(3) 2019, Table I); Martelli et al., IEEE INFOCOM 2012 (packet inter-reception time)

Does not account for:

  • the first reception from a transmitter, which has no predecessor
  • a pseudonym change, which a receiver sees as a new transmitter while this metric pairs on the true id

items.title: revocation_latency_stage
items.text:
The time between consecutive emitted stages of one revocation. The stage dimension names the transition, e.g. decision->issued.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility public Dimensions t, stage Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy each revocation stage completes within a minute Caution 60.0: a revocation stage takes over a minute Unhealthy 300.0: a revocation stage takes over five minutes: a misbehaving vehicle stays trusted Band source engineering choice: no standard sets a revocation deadline (IEEE 1609.2.1 and ETSI TS 102 941 leave CRL timing to policy)

Does not account for:

  • stages a protocol does not emit, which invariant I-P4 reports
  • per-node enforcement spread: this is the transition's distribution, not t95

items.title: security_overhead
items.text:
The share of the octets on the air that are the security envelope — headers, signer identifier (certificate or digest) and signature — over the frames whose payload/envelope split is known.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: Σ envelope octets / Σ octets on the air Visibility node Dimensions t, msg_type Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • frames whose envelope was sized from a table rather than built
  • the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

items.title: speed
items.text:
The distribution of sampled actor speeds over the window.

Field Value Unit m/s Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • the sampling bias: this is time-weighted, so a stopped vehicle dominates it

items.title: time_to_decision
items.text:
Attack onset to the authority's decision about the attacker.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • attackers never decided about
  • the decision's propagation, which is revocation_latency_stage

items.title: time_to_detect
items.text:
Attack onset to the first correct report about the attacker at the authority.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility node-and-gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • attackers never reported, which contribute no sample: read it beside det_recall
  • reports about benign subjects, which are false_accusations

items.title: ttc_conflicts
items.text:
Same-lane pair-steps whose time to collision is below the 1.5 s threshold (the one verified threshold). The comparison is made on the quantised value, so a boundary case cannot flip between platforms.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation count Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper)

Does not account for:

  • distinct conflicts: a pair closing for ten steps counts ten times
  • the threshold's own uncertainty

items.title: ttc_min
items.text:
Time to collision for a closing same-lane pair: gap / (v_follower − v_leader), sampled at every mobility step. Reported as a distribution; the minimum of the run is its min.

Field Value Unit s Aggregation distribution Visibility gt Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Source FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM) (paper) Better higher (literature basis) Healthy encounters keep at least 3 s to collision Caution 3.0: encounters come within 3 s of collision Unhealthy 1.5: encounters come within 1.5 s of collision: traffic conflicts Band source 1.5 s: the conflict threshold of surrogate-safety studies (Hayward 1972; FHWA SSAM default, Gettman et al. 2008); 3 s, twice it, is an engineering choice

Does not account for:

  • vehicle length: the gap is between reported lane positions
  • crossing conflicts, which need trajectory intersection
  • a pair that is not closing, which has no time to collision

items.title: unverified_ratio
items.text:
Messages delivered to applications without verification, divided by messages delivered.

Field Value Unit ratio Aggregation ratio: delivered without verification / delivered Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.0001 Min samples 30 Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy almost every delivered message was verified Caution 0.01: above 1 % of delivered messages were not verified Unhealthy 0.05: above 5 % of delivered messages were not verified: verification is a bottleneck Band source engineering choice; 5 % is the run analyst's unverified_ratio threshold

Does not account for:

  • messages that were dropped rather than delivered

items.title: verify_cost
items.text:
The per-task verification cost, from the primitive's cost table for the node's hardware profile (modeled mode) or measured (real mode).

Field Value Unit ms Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t, primitive Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30

Does not account for:

  • the cost of not verifying: a skipping policy records no task, so a low mean may mean less verification rather than cheaper verification
  • time the task spent waiting, which is verify_wait

items.title: verify_queue_depth
items.text:
The verification queue's depth, sampled when a task is enqueued.

Field Value Unit count Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy the verification queue is usually empty Caution 1.0: messages queue for verification: the verifier is busy most of the time Unhealthy 5.0: the verification queue is backing up: the verifier (HSM) is saturated Band source engineering choice: a mean depth above one is a server rarely idle (the run analyst's queue_depth_saturated)

Does not account for:

  • the depth between arrivals: this is arrival-biased, not a time average

items.title: verify_rate
items.text:
Verifications completed per second, per cryptographic primitive.

Field Value Unit 1/s Aggregation rate Visibility node Dimensions t, primitive Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 1

Does not account for:

  • tasks still queued when the window ended
  • tasks dropped by policy or overflow before they ran

items.title: verify_wait
items.text:
Enqueue to start of verification.

Field Value Unit ms Aggregation distribution Visibility node Dimensions t Grid (quantum) 0.001 Min samples 30 Better lower (engineering basis) Healthy p95 verification wait within 10 ms Caution 10.0: p95 verification wait above 10 ms: a tenth of the 100 ms safety budget Unhealthy 50.0: p95 verification wait above 50 ms: the verifier (HSM) cannot keep up Band source engineering choice against the 100 ms budget of 3GPP TS 22.185 §5.1: 10 % queueing is tolerable, half the budget leaves too little for access and air

Does not account for:

  • a task that never started, which contributes no sample

Opt-in: metrics: [all, signing], or any sig_* name. Not part of a bare all.

Metric Unit Aggregation Visibility Definition sig_backend_bytes B/s rate public Credential-system octets to and from devices per second: certificate provisioning, downloads and the requests for them sig_ca_busy ms/s rate public Certificate-authority service time per second of simulated time: what the scheme costs the backend sig_ca_sign_rate 1/s rate public Signatures the certificate authorities made per second sig_cbr_extra ratio ratio: mean CBR × security octet share / 1 node Estimated channel busy ratio the security envelope adds: the measured CBR times the envelope's share of the octets on the air sig_cert_airtime_share ratio ratio: Σ certificate octets / Σ octets on the air node The share of the octets on the air that are attached certificates sig_cert_bytes B/msg ratio: Σ attached-certificate octets / signed messages node Attached-certificate octets per signed message, averaged over messages with and without one sig_e2e_added ms distribution node End-to-end latency added by security on a delivered message: the wait for and time of signing, plus the wait for and time of verification sig_e2e_added_share ratio ratio: Σ latency added by security / Σ end-to-end latency node The share of end-to-end latency that is signing and verification sig_fragmented_share ratio ratio: messages in more than one frame / messages sent node The share of messages that had to be fragmented, which large signatures cause sig_fragments_per_msg frames/msg ratio: frames on the air / messages sent node Fragments on the air per message: 1 when every signed message fits the MTU sig_neighbour_capacity count mean node How many neighbours a device can verify every message from before its queue grows: verification capacity over each sender's message rate sig_reassembly_loss ratio ratio: fragmented SDUs failed or expired / fragmented SDUs resolved node Fragmented messages a receiver could not reassemble: the delivery lost to fragmentation sig_security_airtime_share ratio ratio: Σ envelope octets / Σ octets on the air node The share of the octets on the air that are the security envelope — headers, signer identifier and signature — with certificates sig_security_airtime_share_nocert ratio ratio: Σ envelope octets less what attaching certificates added / Σ octets on the air less what attaching certificates added node The security envelope's share of the air had no certificate been attached, each certificate-signed message carrying the 8-octet digest instead (the certificate and its 2-octet SEQUENCE OF quantity out, the digest in): what signing alone costs sig_sign_latency ms distribution node Time to make one signature (signer start to signature done), labelled scheme@engine with the engine the device's hardware profile signs on sig_sign_wait ms distribution node Time a message waited for the signer, generation to signer start sig_signature_bytes B/msg ratio: Σ signature octets / signed messages node Signature octets per items.title: Models overview
items.text:
Every behaviour the engine simulates (a car-following law, a path-loss model, a codec, a detector, an emission model) is a model: a Rust implementation of a family trait plus a model card that states what it computes, from which parameters, with which sources, and where it is known to be wrong. A model without a card cannot be registered, and a number a model reads without declaring it on its card is a conformance failure.

Code: crates/v2xw-core/src/{model,card,registry}.rs, crates/v2xw-engine/src/scenario/publish.rs (slots(), models()), crates/v2xw-engine/src/wiring.rs (what a run registers). Every card in the published catalogue, with every parameter: Model parameters.

items.title: Families and slots
items.text:
A family (v2xw_core::card::Family) is one seam of the architecture: a trait that extends Model, a conformance suite and a Python base class. The set is closed; adding a family is an engine change.

Area Families world and traffic world, mobility, vru, weather, gnss, clock radio propagation, fading, obstacle, phy, mac, dcc network net, fragmenter, backhaul, cellular, backend-net messages codec, generator security envelope, primitive, crypto-backend, verification-policy, hardware-profile applications and sensing safety-app, perception credential system protocol, service-model, responder threats attacker, detector, ma-pipeline measurement metric, exporter energy emission, energy

A slot is a place in the scenario where a model of one family is chosen. Most slots take a ModelChoice:

net:
  fragmenter:
    id: fragmenter/generic-sdu        # the card id
    params: {}                        # overrides of the card's defaults
energy:
  ev_model: energy/ev/vt-cpem         # a slot that takes a bare id

ModelChoice { id, params } denies unknown fields. Anything not named in params keeps the card's default, so the resolved parameter set is a pure function of the card and the overrides and can be content-addressed. The slot table (path, family, selectable ids and whether the engine acts on it) is generated: Slots.

Some models are chosen by named settings rather than an id slot: the radio stack by radio.rat, radio.tiers and radio.models (Radio and network), the signature scheme by security.signature (Security), the pseudonym policy by security.pseudonym_change.strategy (Privacy).

items.title: Resolving parameters
items.text:
ParamSet::resolve(card, overrides) builds the parameter set a model runs on:

  1. start from every parameter's card default;
  2. null overrides keep the defaults; anything but a JSON object is refused;
  3. each override must name a declared parameter (a typo is an error listing the declared names, never a silent fallback), have the default's JSON type, and lie inside the declared range when there is one.

Resolved sets are interned in a ParamSetStore by SHA-256 of their canonical JSON, so provenance records point at a parameter set by id instead of copying it.

items.title: The registry
items.text:
v2xw_core::Registry holds one registration per model id:

Field Meaning card the card as registered licence Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, MPL-2.0 may be linked in process; GPL, LGPL or an unknown licence must run out of process hosting in-process (Rust trait object, or batched Python via PyO3) or out-of-process (a separate process; its replies are hashed into the run digest instead of its code being linked) content_hash SHA-256 of the card's canonical JSON

A ModelRef is a dense u32 handle in registration order, cheap to copy into provenance. Registering a different card under an existing id is refused. A hosted (out-of-tree) plug-in's card must target the engine's plug-in API version (same major; same minor while the major is 0).

The run's manifest pins every registered model as id@version with its card hash, so a changed default is a different run. A run registers what it composes (wiring::register_all, plus the radio models it builds, wiring::register_radio); the published catalogue (publish::catalogue) registers every crate that offers cards, so the documentation can list what a scenario could name.

items.title: The model card
items.text:
v2xw_core::card::ModelCard:

Field Content id stable id, ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(/[a-z0-9-]+)*$, e.g. mobility/car-following/idm family, version, api_version the seam, the model's semver, the plug-in API it targets tier the fidelity tiers it implements (never empty) purpose what it is for equations each with a name, LaTeX or text, and notes on validity and units parameters every number it reads: name, unit, default, optional range, source, calibration plan assumptions what it assumes of the world or its inputs limitations where it is known to be wrong or inapplicable ignores what this tier leaves out relative to the next one up sources citations for the model as a whole validation status (unvalidated, unit-tested, literature-checked, field-checked), references, test names determinism whether it draws random numbers and from which RNG domains cost optional per-call cost estimate

items.title: Sources and todo: calibrate
items.text:
Every parameter carries a Source of one kind: standard (a clause), paper, datasheet, dataset, code (another implementation), or todo-calibrate: a value the implementer chose that still needs calibration. A todo-calibrate parameter must carry a calibration plan (registry rule R1), and the generated reference lists them.

ModelCard::validate refuses, at registration, a card whose id is malformed, whose todo-calibrate parameter has no plan, whose parameter names repeat, whose default lies outside its own range (otherwise a scenario that never mentions the parameter would run on an impossible value), or whose version, API version, purpose or tier is empty.

items.title: How to read a card
items.text:
On the generated page each card shows its purpose, version, tiers, hosting and whether it draws random numbers, then:

  1. Parameters: the table to override in params. Check the source column: standard and paper values are cited; todo-calibrate values are choices to vary in a sensitivity study.
  2. Equations: what the code computes, to check against the paper.
  3. Assumptions, Limitations, Ignores: what not to conclude from the model.
  4. Sources: what to cite.

items.title: Fidelity tiers
items.text:
Tier Meaning Typical use abstract closed-form or probabilistic stand-ins 10,000-node runs medium the models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail (the default) most studies high frame-level or physically detailed a focus region or a small scenario

A scenario picks one tier per family (radio.tiers for the radio stack); a model that offers several branches on the tier selected. The validator refuses combinations that cannot compose, for example phy: high with mac: medium. At city scale, a microscopic focus region runs inside a mesoscopic network (scale, mobility/tiered/meso-micro).

items.title: Writing a model
items.text:
use v2xw_core::card::{Family, ModelCard, Tier};
use v2xw_core::model::Model;

struct FreeSpace { card: ModelCard }

impl Model for FreeSpace {
    fn card(&self) -> &ModelCard { &self.card }
}

The family trait (pub trait Propagation: Model { … }) supplies the behaviour; Model supplies id(), version(), tiers() and family() from the card. Models reach the engine only through a narrowed context (v2xw_core::ctx::Ctx) that gives the clock, keyed RNG streams and the reads the family is allowed. Walk-through: Extending: models.

items.title: V2X applications
items.text:
The applications are where a communication result becomes a safety or traffic result. Each equipped vehicle runs them on what its radio stack delivered and on its own vehicle bus; the engine then runs the same decision functions on ground truth and labels every warning true, false or missed. A lost BSM becomes a late or missed warning, a ghost vehicle a false one, a stale SPaT a wrong advisory.

Code: crates/v2xw-node/src/apps.rs (the applications), vehicle.rs (the vehicle bus), events.rs (SRM/SSM, DENM triggers), crates/v2xw-engine/src/app_truth.rs (labelling), priority.rs (signal priority), perception.rs (sensors), safety_events.rs (scripted emergencies), crates/v2xw-metrics/src/apps.rs (metrics). Settings: apps, perception, events.

flowchart LR
    rx["verified BSM, CAM, PSM, VAM,<br/>DENM, SPaT, MAP, CPM"] --> apps["v2xw_node::apps<br/>decision functions"]
    bus["own vehicle bus:<br/>speed, accel, yaw rate,<br/>turn signal, next movement, limit"] --> apps
    apps --> warn["app.warning (NODE)"]
    apps --> adv["app.advice (GLOSA)"]
    gt["ground truth<br/>(engine only)"] --> truth["app_truth: same functions<br/>on true states"]
    warn --> truth
    truth --> out["app.outcome:<br/>true / false / missed (GT)"]
    out --> m["app_precision, app_miss_ratio,<br/>app_lead_time_s, app_warnings"]

items.title: What an application may read
items.text:
• the messages its stack delivered and verified, decoded from their own octets: a BSM's or CAM's position, speed, heading, acceleration, event flags and path prediction; a PSM's or VAM's; a DENM's event; a SPaT's signal states and timing; a MAP's lanes;
  • its own GNSS belief and its own vehicle bus (v2xw_node::vehicle): speed, acceleration, yaw rate, turn signal, the navigation's next movement, the speed limit.

A heard road user is a Track. Before a decision, a track is advanced by the message's age at its own speed and acceleration, never reversing:

\[ d(\Delta t) = \max\!\big(0,\; v\,\tau + \tfrac12 a\,\tau^2\big),\qquad \tau = \begin{cases}\min(\Delta t,\, v/(-a)) & a < 0\\ \Delta t & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases} \]

items.title: The applications
items.text:
apps.enabled (default: all eight) lists which run on every equipped vehicle.

Id Application Fires when Default threshold Source fcw forward collision warning a vehicle ahead in the ego's predicted path (heading within 30°, inside a 1.8 m half-corridor on the ego's yaw-rate arc, ≤ 150 m, ego ≥ 2.8 m/s) would be hit within the TTC threshold, and the driver is not already braking as hard as avoiding it requires apps.fcw_ttc_s = 2.4 s NHTSA NCAP FCW confirmation test (2013): alert no later than 2.4 s TTC for a decelerating lead eebl emergency electronic brake light a same-direction vehicle ahead brakes hard (BSM hard-braking flag or accelSet past 0.4 g, or an EEBL DENM) ≤ 300 m ahead, within 5.4 m laterally (the ego's lane and the next) 0.4 g: J2735 event flag; 300 m: CAMP VSC-A EEBL range as recalled, a parameter ima intersection movement assist a crossing vehicle and the ego would reach the conflict point within a short time of each other apps.ima_tti_s = 4 s look-ahead, ΔT ≤ 1.5 s ΔT: FHWA SSAM conflict threshold (FHWA-HRT-08-051); 4 s is this build's choice lta left-turn assist the ego is about to turn left (within 30 m) and an opposing vehicle arrives inside the critical gap apps.lta_gap_s = 4.1 s HCM 6th ed. Exhibit 20-11, base critical headway for a major-street left turn bsw blind spot and lane change warning a same-direction vehicle in the blind zone (0.5 to 3.0 m beside, up to 3 m behind the rear); lcw when the ego signals toward it ISO 17387 (LCDAS) adjacent zone pcw pedestrian collision warning a pedestrian or cyclist would be in the ego's path apps.pcw_ttc_s = 3 s, ±1 m this build's choice: no V2P timing is standardised rlvw red-light violation warning the ego would enter on red and cannot stop comfortably after a 1 s reaction apps.rlvw_decel_mps2 = 3.4 m/s² AASHTO 3.4 m/s² comfortable deceleration; ITE 1.0 s perception-reaction time glosa green-light optimal speed advisory (advisory) the speed that reaches the stop line on green from 300 m, minimum advice 20 km/h, 1 s margin Katsaros et al. 2011; the minimum and margin are this build's choice

A warning is issued once (issue), refreshed at most once a second (update) and cleared when its condition has been gone for 300 ms (clear), on app.warning. GLOSA writes app.advice.

items.title: Decision quantities
items.text:
Time to collision (FCW, PCW): the smallest \(t \le 10\) s on a 50 ms grid at which the ego at constant speed \(v_e\) closes the net gap \(g\) on a lead at \(v_l\) that brakes at \(a_l < 0\) and stops:

\[ v_e\,t \;\ge\; g + x_l(t),\qquad x_l(t) = v_l\,t' + \tfrac12 a_l\,t'^2,\; t' = \min(t,\, v_l/(-a_l)). \]

A non-positive gap from two GNSS errors is an apparent overlap; it counts only once the ego is truly closing.

Required deceleration (FCW suppression):

\[ d_{\text{req}} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{v_e^2}{2\,(g + v_l^2/(2(-a_l)))} & a_l < 0,\ v_l > 0 \\[2mm] \dfrac{v_e^2}{2g} & v_l \le 0 \\[2mm] \dfrac{(v_e - v_l)^2}{2g} & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

FCW stays silent when the driver already brakes at \(-a_e \ge d_{\text{req}}\).

RLVW: with distance \(d\) to the stop line and reaction time \(t_r\),

\[ d_{\text{need}} = \frac{v^2}{2\,(d - v\,t_r)},\qquad \text{warn if } d_{\text{need}} \ge 3.4\ \text{m/s}^2 \text{ and the driver is not braking at } 0.9\,\tfrac{v^2}{2d}. \]

GLOSA: with \(t_{\text{left}}\) the likely change instant of the SPaT (likelyTime, or minEndTime when it is not sent; CTI 4501) and margin \(m\):

  • on green, if \(d / v_{\text{limit}} \le t_{\text{left}} - m\): advise \(\min(v, v_{\text{limit}})\) if the current speed makes it, else \(d/(t_{\text{left}} - m)\); otherwise no speed (it will stop);
  • on red: advise \(d/(t_{\text{left}} + m)\), capped at the limit, or nothing below the 20 km/h minimum.

A driver decides once, with probability apps.glosa_compliance (default 0) on a stream keyed by the actor, whether to follow; a follower's speed is capped at the advice while it stands.

items.title: Labelling against ground truth
items.text:
v2xw_engine::app_truth runs the same decision functions over true states:

Term Rule truth episode for every equipped ego and subject within 300 m (EEBL's reach), each mobility step the decision fires on true states; consecutive steps form one episode true warning an issue whose (ego, subject, application) had an episode open, ended within 1 s before, or opening within 1 s after false warning an issue with no such episode missed an episode of at least 300 ms that ended with no issue for that subject and application lead time the true TTC left at the issue instant (FCW, IMA, LTA, PCW)

Labelled applications: fcw, eebl, ima, lta, pcw, rlvw. bsw and lcw are advisory and neither matched nor counted as missed. RLVW's truth uses the signal the approach truly shows (the controller's plan as it runs now, priority service included).

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
Metric Formula Unit Visibility app_warnings warnings issued (rising edges) count NODE app_precision true / (true + false) ratio, Wilson interval GT app_miss_ratio missed / (true + missed) ratio, Wilson interval GT app_lead_time_s true TTC left when a true warning issued s, distribution GT

All are per application (app dimension). They do not account for whether the driver reacted, for warnings about objects reported only in CPMs, or for EEBL and RLVW lead time (no TTC). See Metrics and outputs.

items.title: Surrogate measures
items.text: v2xw_node::safety computes the surrogate safety family (TTC, PET, DRAC) over what the node believed, quantised to 10⁻³, with the FHWA SSAM 1.5 s conflict threshold; the metric crate's ground-truth ttc_min, pet and drac (metric/safety/surrogates-and-flow) are the truth side. Their difference under attack is the attack's effect on safety. The catalogue's safety-app/fcw-vsca, ima-vsca and eebl-vsca cards describe that module; the applications a run executes are the v2xw_node::apps set above.

items.title: Signal priority for emergency vehicles
items.text:
An emergency-class vehicle with srm in messages.sets sends an SRM to a junction whose MAP it heard, once it is within 300 m, repeated every second. The RSU with the spat role hands it to the controller (v2xw_engine::priority, NTCIP 1211 strategies) and answers with an SSM when ssm is on.

Action Rule Default green extension while the requested green would end before the vehicle's ETA plus a margin, hold the plan clock at most 10 s; margin 2 s early green while the requested movement is red, end a conflicting green that has run its minimum; its amber, all-red and clearances run in full; never cut a pedestrian clearance or a walk below the minimum minimum green 7 s (MUTCD 2009 §4E.06 walk) recovery walk the offset back during greens only, at most a fraction of real time, so a green runs 80 to 120 % of its length rate 0.2 lapse a request not repeated 2 s

NTCIP 1211 leaves the limits to the operator; the defaults are this build's (the 10 s extension from FHWA's TSP handbook range of 5 to 15 s, as recalled). Each action is a signal.priority record. The drivers, the SPaT and the page's lamps all read the moved plan. The NEMA dual-ring controller applies the same strategies to its phases (Traffic).

items.title: Perception
items.text:
v2xw_engine::perception is the one place that reads true positions and hands a vehicle a list of perceived objects: detected with a probability, placed with an error, hidden when something is in the way. It is the input to CPMs (Messages).

Default sensor Range Field of view Source long-range radar 250 m ±9° Continental ARS 408-21 datasheet, far range short-range radar 70 m ±45° the same sensor's near range front camera 80 m ±26° a 52° mono camera (Mobileye EyeQ class); the range is this build's choice Model element Rule Status detection probability linear from pd_near 0.99 at the sensor to pd_far 0.90 at range this build's choice, in the range ETSI TR 103 562 assumes position error Gaussian, σ = 0.10 m + 0.5 % of range (radar), 0.20 m + 2 % (camera), 0.03 m base (lidar) this build's choice, the order of datasheet accuracies occlusion centre-line (default) hidden when the line to the reference point crosses a building or passes within half a body width of another vehicle occlusion outline seen when any silhouette corner is in range and view with a clear 2.5D line past buildings and other vehicles' oriented rectangles Günther, Riebl et al., IEEE VNC 2016 (Artery's visible-corner rule) tracking perfect association; confirmed after 3 hits in the last 5 scans, dropped after 1 s unseen; only confirmed tracks are reported M-of-N rule roadside suite RSUs with the cpm role; default four 80 m cameras, 90° each, facing east, north, west, south TS 103 324 §7.1.3

Suites are configurable per vehicle class (perception.classes), with mount anchor (front, rear, centre), offsets, height, azimuth, range (≤ 409.5 m) and field of view. Draws come from the perception RNG domain.
