items.title: Scripted safety events
items.text:
The calibrated drivers rarely brake past 0.4 g, so the emergency applications need an emergency put there. The timeline (events) offers:

Kind The vehicle Defaults safety.hard-brake brakes at decel_mps2 to a stop, stands hold_s, drives on 0.5 g (4.90 m/s²), 2 s safety.breakdown brakes to a stop, hazard lights on, stands until until 3 m/s² safety.cut-in changes lane to side into the gap ahead of that lane's follower left

0.5 g is above J2945/1's 0.4 g flag; on the ETSI stack an EEBL DENM needs decel_mps2 ≥ 6 (UN R48). target: auto (default) picks the first fitting vehicle in actor-id order and waits up to within_s for one.

events:
  - t: 120
    type: safety.hard-brake
    params: { target: auto, decel_mps2: 4.9, hold_s: 2 }

items.title: Modelled versus simplified
items.text: Modelled Simplified or absent eight applications on verified, decoded messages and the own vehicle bus no driver model of reaction to a warning; a warning is the HMI output per-message age extrapolation of tracks FCW, IMA and PCW geometry is planar; no elevation truth labelling with the same decision functions BSW/LCW are not labelled; CPM-only objects are not used by the applications' labels GLOSA from SPaT likelyTime with per-driver compliance GLOSA advice does not model eco-driving acceleration profiles NTCIP 1211 extension, early green and recovery limits are this build's defaults, not an operator's sensor detection, error, occlusion and M-of-N tracking perfect data association; no false positives from clutter; detection probability and error are uncited choices

items.title: Determinism and time
items.text:
Same scenario file, same seed, same engine build and same plug-in set give the same records, the same metrics and the same digests. This page explains how the engine keeps that promise: what simulated time is, how events are ordered, where random numbers come from, which sources of nondeterminism are banned, and how a run is checked and resumed.

Code: crates/v2xw-core/src/{time,event,rng,hash,math,manifest}.rs, crates/v2xw-engine/src/{event,run}.rs, crates/v2xw-node/src/clock.rs, crates/v2xw-cli/src/checkpoint.rs. Settings: time and seed.

items.title: Simulated time
items.text:
Quantity Type Unit Notes instant SimTime = u64 ns since t0 584 years of range; symbol boundaries (8 µs), slot times (13 µs) and propagation delays (about 1 µs per 300 m) are exact integers span time::Duration(u64) ns a delay, not an instant; arithmetic saturates, and a negative span clamps to zero civil time WallClock s time.t0 (RFC 3339) plus SimTime; a pure function of the scenario IEEE 1609.2 Time32 / Time64 WallClock::time32, time64 TAI s / TAI µs since 2004-01-01T00:00:00Z leap seconds included from the IANA leap-seconds.list table (time::LEAP_SECONDS); a t0 of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z gives Time32 694 310 405

The kernel always counts nanoseconds. time.des_resolution (1ns, 1us default, 1ms) is the resolution promised to models; the loader refuses a resolution the run cannot keep, for example 1ms with a PHY or MAC that times frames in microseconds.

Floats appear only at the edges. time.duration_s is converted once (Time::horizon_ns, rounded to the nanosecond), and ns_to_secs is exact only for the first 2⁵³ ns (about 104 days), so it is used for model inputs and display only.

The wall clock

Nothing in the engine reads the host clock. The civil time of the run is time.t0, which is scenario data (default 2027-03-04T07:00:00Z). The only other real-world instant is the manifest's build_utc, which the caller supplies (v2xw run --build-utc) and which is excluded from every digest.

items.title: Time settings
items.text:
Setting Default Range Meaning time.t0 2027-03-04T07:00:00Z RFC 3339 civil instant of SimTime 0 time.duration_s 60 > 0 s run length time.mobility_step_ms 100 10 to 100 ms mobility period time.des_resolution 1us 1ns, 1us, 1ms resolution promised to models time.metric_period_s 1 s when unset 0.1 to 3600 s metric flush window time.warmup_s none ≥ 0 s no metric sample is recorded for a window that ends inside it time.calendar real real, compressed credential-system calendar time.time_dilation[] none {from_s, to_s} windows in which no radio frame is generated time.fast_forward[] none {from_s, to_s} windows the engine jumps through between credential-system events

Full table with status notes: generated time reference.

items.title: The event queue
items.text:
One binary heap holds every cross-node event, ordered by the total order (time, priority, seq) (v2xw_core::event):

  • time: SimTime;
  • priority: fixed per event class, never chosen by a plug-in;
  • seq: one global monotonic counter stamped when the event is scheduled.

Two events at the same instant therefore run in an order fixed by rule, and two events with the same time and priority run in the order they were scheduled. Because scheduling itself happens in deterministic order (id-sorted merges), the whole run is deterministic.

Priority Class Payload (v2xw_engine::Event) Scheduled by 0 Control a scenario timeline item, start or end the timeline, at load 1 MobilityStep none (period time.mobility_step_ms) itself 2 SignalPhase the signal whose controller advances the mobility phase 3 PhyEnd one frame whose arrival ends (receivers resolved inside the phase) the PHY 4 MacTimer a node and channel whose backoff, AIFS or SPS reservation expires the MAC 5 PhyStart one frame whose transmission begins the MAC 6 NodeTask the batched node phase, or one node's own wake-up mobility and node phases 7 NetDeliver an SDU and the node it reaches the network layer 8 FlowTimer a protocol flow step whose timer expires credential and backend protocols 9 Observe metric flush, UI keyframe, exporter flush, end of run the run

The order encodes causality at one instant: scenario control is visible to everything, kinematics for t are final before any radio event at t reads them, a reception is decided before the MAC reacts, and observation looks at a fully settled instant.

Stable numbers

The priorities, the RNG domain codes and the entity encoding below are part of the determinism contract. Changing any of them changes every golden digest.

items.title: The main loop and phases
items.text:
crates/v2xw-engine/src/run.rs runs one single-threaded loop over the heap. A few event classes are phases: pure maps over actors, receivers or nodes, which may run on a thread pool and are merged in id order. A phase never touches the heap while it maps, so thread count changes wall time and nothing else.

flowchart TD
    pop["pop min (time, priority, seq)"] --> c{"event class"}
    c -->|Control p0| ctl["apply timeline item"]
    c -->|MobilityStep p1| mob["map over actors, merge by ActorId<br/>publish gt.kinematics and VWP frame at t<br/>advance world to t + dt"]
    c -->|PhyEnd p3| rx["map over the frame's receivers<br/>merge by NodeId"]
    c -->|PhyStart p5| tx["frame goes on the air"]
    c -->|NodeTask p6| node["map over nodes, merge by NodeId<br/>node-local queues drained inside the map"]
    c -->|Observe p9| obs["metric flush, keyframe, end sentinel"]
    ctl & mob & rx & tx & node & obs --> sched["schedule follow-ups (seq++)"] --> pop

Node-local work (signing, verification queues, stores, detectors) is drained inside the node map and never reaches the global heap, so the heap grows with traffic between nodes rather than with work inside them.

items.title: The mobility step
items.text:
Mobility is periodic. A step dispatched at t publishes the state at t (the gt.kinematics records and one VWP keyframe or delta), then advances the world to t + dt. Each step is a Jacobi update: every decision reads a frozen start-of-step snapshot, so the order in which actors are visited cannot change the result.

A radio event at \(t'\) strictly inside a step reads positions by the published extrapolation rule (Kinematics::extrapolate, applied only in Engine::position_at):

\[ \mathbf{p}(t') = \mathbf{p}(t) + \mathbf{v}(t)\,(t' - t), \qquad t \le t' < t + \Delta t . \]

items.title: Generation phase
items.text: Every node draws a generation phase \(\varphi \sim U[0, T)\) once, so a fleet's BSMs and CAMs are not synchronised on the engine's step grid. The rules are on the messages page.

items.title: Random numbers
items.text:
There is no shared sequential generator. Every draw comes from an RngStream, a ChaCha12 keystream whose 32-byte key is

\[ \text{key} = \operatorname{SHA\text{-}256}\big(\text{master\_seed}_{\text{le},8} \,\|\, \text{domain\_code}_{\text{le},4} \,\|\, \text{entity\_encoding}\big). \]

The key depends only on who draws and what for, so one entity's sequence is independent of every other entity's activity, of event order and of thread count. seed is the only seed a scenario sets (decimal, 0x… or "0x…"); there is no field for a sub-stream seed.

Domain Code Purpose spawn 1 demand and spawn decisions mobility 2 car-following acceleration noise only lane-change 3 lane-change decisions gnss 4 GNSS position and time error, outages shadow 5 large-scale shadowing fading 6 small-scale fading mac-backoff 7 CSMA/CA contention windows sps-selection 8 sidelink SPS resource selection abstract-rx 9 abstract-tier reception coin flip attack 10 attacker behaviour service-time 11 queueing service times backend 12 backend batching jitter, retries collusion 13 attacker group formation perception 14 detection, position error, false positives report 15 misbehaviour report generation crypto 16 modelled cryptography material (crypto_mode: modeled only) desired-speed 17 driver desired speed reaction-time 18 driver reaction time plug-in high bit set the high bit, then the first four octets of SHA-256(model id) as a little-endian u32, shifted right by one

One domain names one purpose: two models drawing from the same (domain, entity) key would interleave and depend on each other's order. A plug-in's domain is derived from its model id (PluginDomain::for_model), never picked by hand.

Entity Tag Payload Lifetime Global 0x00 cached Actor 0x01 u32 cached Node 0x02 u32 cached Link 0x03 u32 tx, u32 rx cached LinkFrame 0x04 u32 tx, u32 rx, u64 frame single use, never cached Lane 0x05 u32 cached Signal 0x06 u32 cached Custom 0x07 u16 kind, u64 id cached

RngRegistry::checkout(&self) is the one sanctioned accessor and works inside parallel phases: it borrows the stream from a sharded, locked cache and panics if the same key is checked out twice at once. A per-frame scope (LinkFrame) is derived, used and dropped, because caching one generator per frame per link would not fit in memory at scale.

Samplers (uniform, normal, Nakagami and the rest) are implemented in rng.rs with fixed algorithms and documented draw counts, never with the rand crate's distributions.

items.title: Banned sources of nondeterminism
items.text:
The conformance kit (tests/conformance/src/firewall.rs) scans the source tree, recursively and outside comments and tests, and fails on any of these:

Check Forbidden Why Use instead hash order HashMap, HashSet std hash iteration order is randomised per process, so any ordering, id assignment or digest it reaches differs between runs BTreeMap, BTreeSet, a sorted Vec wall clock Instant::now, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH a duration measured on a real clock differs between identical runs SimTime, time.t0 transcendental .sin(, .cos(, .exp(, .powf( and the rest std transcendentals call the platform libm, whose precision varies by platform and version v2xw_core::math (the pure-Rust libm port of musl) ground truth node code reading truth belief and truth separation NodeView

Exemptions are data in the rule table, each with a reason (the CLI's wall.rs, the server's HTTP task, two Arrow metadata maps). sqrt, + − × ÷, abs, floor, ceil, round and trunc are IEEE-754 exact and need no wrapper; mul_add must not be used, because whether it fuses depends on the target.

Every recorded float is quantised on its declared grid at write time (math::quantize_to, v2xw-world/src/quant.rs, v2xw-record/src/grid.rs), and metric digests hash the integer grid index, not the float.

items.title: Node clocks and GNSS time
items.text:
A node does not read simulated time. It reads its own clock (v2xw_node::ClockModel, card clock/gnss-locked-tcxo): GNSS-disciplined while a fix holds, free-running at the oscillator's drift otherwise. Every freshness check a node performs (the 1609.2 generationTime window, CAM age, replay guards) and every generation interval uses the believed time.

\[ \text{offset}(t) = \text{offset}(t_{\text{lost}}) + \varepsilon\,(t - t_{\text{lost}}) \quad\text{(holdover)},\qquad \text{offset} \leftarrow 0 \text{ on reacquisition}. \] What Value in the engine Where node runtime drift 0 ppm: believed time equals true time ObuRuntime, RsuRuntime, VRU device construct ClockModel::new(0.0) deliberate skew security.scms.lifecycle.clock_skew_s steps a share (clock_skew_share) of devices ahead phase2.clock_skew_for; the device signs, rotates and judges on its own clock telemetry clock_offset_ns (the one ground-truth integer in the 208-byte NodeTelemetry record) VWP §3.5.2

The catalogue also registers two clock cards from v2xw-mobility: clock/drift/none (abstract: believed equals true) and clock/drift/tcxo-ocxo, which adds a GNSS time-transfer error \(\mathcal N(0, \sigma)\) with \(\sigma = 30\,\text{ns}/1.96\) (GPS SPS Performance Standard 2020, Table 3.8-3: ≤ 30 ns at 95 %) and a per-unit fractional frequency error drawn once (TCXO 2 ppm, OCXO 0.5 ppb by default).

Library model, not wired

clock/drift/tcxo-ocxo is implemented and carded in v2xw-mobility::clock, but the engine's node runtimes do not use it: their clocks run at zero drift unless a scenario sets clock_skew_s. Clock-drift and holdover studies need that wiring first.

items.title: Real and compressed calendar
items.text:
The credential system runs on a calendar (time.calendar):

  • real (default): one-week i-periods counted from the US SCMS epoch, 2015-01-06 04:00 US Eastern (SCMS Manager IEEE 1609.2.1 Profile §2.1.17, Table 2), with US Eastern daylight-saving time, federal holidays and business days (v2xw_proto::scms::calendar). A run starting 2026-10-16 provisions i = 614.
  • compressed: the only way to set a shorter security.protocol.params.i_period_s. Its i-period numbers and validity windows are not the deployment's, and the manifest and the run report say so.

time.fast_forward windows freeze traffic, generate no radio event and jump from one credential-system event to the next (top-ups, RA shuffles, CRL publication and fetches, re-enrolment, root rollovers) on the mobility-step grid; a backend event lands on the step a full run would have handled it on. time.time_dilation windows only suppress radio frames, counted in the run report. Both are recorded in the manifest. Details of the SCMS calendar: SCMS.

items.title: Digests and replay
items.text:
Digest Over Where scenario hash canonical JSON of the resolved scenario manifest world hash the world's content manifest, /world/{hash}.vwb card hash SHA-256 of each registered card's canonical JSON, pinned as id@version manifest plugins record digest SHA-256 over every record emitted, in order v2xw run --no-recording --digest (stream_digest), checkpoints metric digest integer grid indices, sample counts and keys; runtime diagnostics structurally excluded (DigestSet) metrics/summary.json file digests and data_digest SHA-256 of each output file; aggregate over sorted paths and hex digests manifest

The aggregate data digest is

h = SHA-256()
for rel in sorted(paths):
    h.update(rel)                          # UTF-8 path
    h.update(hex(sha256(file_bytes)))      # 64 lower-case hex characters
data_digest = hex(h)

The manifest also pins the engine version, a build hash over compiler, platform, git commit and dirty state, the master seed and the crypto mode. Wall time and memory use are diagnostics and never enter a digest.

Compare two runs bit for bit without writing recordings:

v2xw run scenarios/connected-intersections.yaml --no-recording --digest

items.title: Checkpoint and resume
items.text:
v2xw run scenarios/manhattan-day.yaml --checkpoint-every 1h
v2xw resume runs/<name>/checkpoint.json

A checkpoint (checkpoint.json, format v2xw-checkpoint/1, method replay) stores the run's inputs (resolved scenario, scenario hash, world hash, build timestamp), the instant t, the record digest at t with the record count, and how much of each output was complete (recording segments, metrics.json bytes and samples, progress.jsonl). The recording is written as segments recording.0000.mcap, recording.0001.mcap, …, each a complete MCAP file, closed at every checkpoint and listed in recording_index.json.

v2xw resume rebuilds the engine, re-runs to t with outputs off, refuses to continue unless the record digest at t equals the checkpoint's, truncates the outputs to what was complete at t and carries on. The finished outputs equal an uninterrupted run's (crates/v2xw-cli/tests/longrun.rs checks this by file digest, with a forged checkpoint that must be refused as its control).

What a checkpoint does not store

It does not serialise the engine's memory. Resuming costs re-simulating the time before t without recording; what it saves is everything already written and the proof that the resumed run is the same run.

items.title: Guarantees and their limits
items.text:
Guarantee Status same inputs on one machine give identical records and digests the contract; checked by the byte-identity and wire-vector tests in v2xw-record and the resume test in v2xw-cli independent of thread count phase-parallel maps merged in id order; the RNG tests pin streams byte for byte for 1 and 8 threads independent of OS and CPU (macOS, Linux, Windows; x86-64, arm64; WebAssembly) the design contract of math, rng and the firewall. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, determinism jobs) imports a committed OSM fixture on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows and fails if the world and payload digests differ or any value is off its quantisation grid same recording replayed gives the same frames the browser replay reader (v2xw-wasm) decodes the recorded VWP stream; it re-runs nothing

Limits, stated:

  • A different engine build, a different card (any parameter, any default) or a different plug-in set is a different run; the manifest records which.
  • Out-of-process plug-ins are outside the Rust firewall; the registry hashes their replies into the run digest instead of linking their code.
  • The cross-platform CI check covers world import and quantisation; full-run digests are compared within one platform.

items.title: Energy and emissions
items.text:
v2xw-energy scores what the traffic burns and emits: tailpipe CO₂, CO, HC, NOx, PM and fuel of combustion vehicles, and the traction-battery energy of battery-electric ones. It reads the recorded ground-truth trajectories (gt.kinematics) and nothing else, so the same numbers come from a live run, from a replayed recording, or from a recording made before the energy section existed, and a recording can be re-scored under another model or fleet without re-simulating.

Code: crates/v2xw-energy/src/ (hbefa3, phemlight, moves, ev, powertrain, provider, bands), crates/v2xw-cli/src/energy.rs (the v2xw energy command). Settings: energy. Card parameters: model parameters, emission and energy families.

Post-hoc, no feedback

Energy does not feed back into driving: an EV that runs out of charge keeps moving and is counted in ev_depleted. There is no charging infrastructure.

items.title: The energy section
items.text:
A scenario without the section computes no energy metrics (and keeps its content hash). energy: {} runs HBEFA 3 over a Euro 4 petrol fleet (diesel for heavy trucks, buses and coaches) with no electric vehicles.

energy:
  emission_model: energy/emission/hbefa3    # or hbefa3 | phemlight | moves-opmode
  emission_model_by_segment:                # optional: another model per segment
    passenger-car: phemlight
  ev_model: energy/ev/kurczveil             # or kurczveil | vt-cpem
  fleet:
    passenger-car: { ev_share: 0.2, diesel_share: 0.3, euro: 6 }
    urban-bus:     { ev_share: 0.5 }
  ev:
    initial_soc: 0.8
    params: { mass_kg: 1600 }               # the EV model's card parameter names
  stop_speed_mps: 0.1
Field Default Range Meaning emission_model energy/emission/hbefa3 id or last segment combustion model emission_model_by_segment.<segment> none id per-segment override ev_model energy/ev/kurczveil id or last segment battery-electric model fleet.<segment>.ev_share 0 0 to 1 share of battery-electric vehicles fleet.<segment>.diesel_share 0 0 to 1 diesel share among combustion vehicles fleet.<segment>.euro 4 0 to 6 Euro emission standard (segment not named) all petrol, Euro 4, no EVs; diesel for heavy-truck, urban-bus, coach HBEFA 3 has no petrol bus or coach class ev.initial_soc 0.8 (todo-calibrate) 0 to 1 starting state of charge ev.params card defaults the EV card's names EV parameter overrides stop_speed_mps 0.1 (0, 5] m/s below this a vehicle is halting (SUMO's threshold)

Segments: passenger-car, light-commercial, heavy-truck, urban-bus, coach, motorcycle. Mobility classes map onto them (passenger, emergency, taxi… are passenger cars; delivery is light commercial; truck, trailer heavy trucks; bus; coach; motorcycle, moped). Pedestrians, bicycles and e-scooters are skipped; an unknown class is counted in energy_unmodelled, never guessed.

items.title: The fleet draw
items.text: Each vehicle draws its powertrain once, from the stream (plugin("energy/fleet/draw"), Actor(id)): one uniform decides electric against combustion, a second diesel against petrol. Both are always drawn, so changing one share never shifts the other. The draw is keyed by the master seed, so a re-score reproduces the run's own fleet.

items.title: The integration interval
items.text:
Between two consecutive gt.kinematics records of one actor, at most 5 s apart, every model sees the same kinematically consistent interval:

\[ \bar v = \frac{v_0 + v_1}{2},\qquad a = \frac{v_1 - v_0}{\Delta t},\qquad s = \bar v\,\Delta t,\qquad \text{grade} = \frac{\Delta z}{s}\ (s \ge 1\,\text{m},\ |\text{grade}| \le 0.3). \]

With these, \(m\,a\,\bar v\,\Delta t = \tfrac12 m (v_1^2 - v_0^2)\) exactly: a power-based model charges the kinetic energy the vehicle actually gained. The interval is charged to the lane the vehicle was on at its start. A stop is counted when $v < $ stop_speed_mps after \(v > 1\) m/s (hysteresis).

items.title: energy/emission/hbefa3: HBEFA 3.1 polynomial fit
items.text:
45 classes (passenger cars and light commercial vehicles, petrol and diesel, Euro 0 to 6; heavy trucks, urban buses, coaches), six quantities each. Tiers abstract, medium.

\[ a' = a + g \sin(\arctan(\text{grade})),\qquad E = \frac{\max\!\big(0,\; c_0 + c_1 a' v + c_2 a'^2 v + c_3 v + c_4 v^2 + c_5 v^3\big)}{3.6}\ \ [\text{mg/s}], \]

with \(v\) in m/s, \(g = 9.80665\) m/s² and one coefficient row per class and quantity (the fuel row is fuel mass). Coefficients: Krajzewicz et al. 2015, transcribed from Eclipse SUMO HelpersHBEFA3.cpp (numeric data only).

High idle

The intercept is the standstill rate and it is high: PC_G_EU4 idles at 2.6 g/s CO₂ and 0.84 g/s fuel, about four times a warm petrol car's measured idle. Traffic that queues a lot reads high, and an application that removes idling reads a larger saving under HBEFA 3 than under PHEMlight. SUMO's HBEFA3 behaves the same.

items.title: energy/emission/phemlight: power-based (TU Graz)
items.text:
The two openly published vehicles, a Euro 4 petrol and a Euro 4 diesel passenger car. Tiers medium, high.

\[ P = \frac{(m{+}L) g (f_0 + f_1 v + f_4 v^4) v + \tfrac{\rho}{2} c_d A v^3 + (m\,k_{\text{rot}}(v) + m_{\text{rot}} + L) a v + (m{+}L) g\,\tfrac{\text{grade}\%}{100} v}{1000\,\eta} + P_{\text{aux}}\ \ [\text{kW}] \] \[ FC = FC_{\text{curve}}(P/P_{\text{rated}})\,P_{\text{rated}},\qquad E_X = E_{X,\text{curve}}(P/P_{\text{drive}}),\ P_{\text{drive}} = P(19.444\,\text{m/s},\ 0.45\,\text{m/s}^2,\ 0), \] \[ \text{CO}_2 = \frac{FC\,f_C - 0.429\,\text{CO} - 0.866\,\text{HC}}{0.273},\quad f_C = 0.865\ \text{(petrol)},\ 0.863\ \text{(diesel)}. \]

Fuel is cut off (every rate 0) when the car decelerates harder than it would coast in gear. Idle rows apply at \(|v| \le 0.5\) m/s. A Euro 0 to 3, 5 or 6 car is computed with the Euro 4 vehicle of its fuel. Parameters: gravity 9.81, air density 1.182 kg/m³, drivetrain efficiency 0.9 (SUMO's PHEMlight data, EPL-2.0; Hausberger et al. 2009).

items.title: energy/emission/moves-opmode: US EPA MOVES operating modes
items.text:
Each interval is binned into one of 23 running operating modes by speed and scaled tractive power, and charged that mode's rate. Light-duty only. Tiers abstract, medium.

\[ \text{STP} = \frac{A v + B v^2 + C v^3 + m v (a + g \sin\theta)}{f}\ \ [\text{kW/tonne}],\qquad E = \frac{\text{rate}[\text{mode}]}{3600}\ \ [\text{g/s}], \]

mode 0 braking (\(a \le -2\) mph/s, or \(a < -1\) mph/s for 3 s), mode 1 idle (\(v < 1\) mph), 11 to 16, 21 to 30, 33 to 40 by speed band and STP bin. Fuel by carbon balance from CO₂.

Source type A (kW s/m) B (kW s²/m²) C (kW s³/m³) m, f (t) passenger car 0.156461 0.002002 0.000493 1.4788 passenger truck 0.22112 0.002838 0.000698 1.86686

Rates: MOVESTAR's light-duty vehicle and truck tables (Wang, Wu & Scora 2020, arXiv:2008.04986), derived from MOVES. v2xw energy --opmode-csv writes the operating-mode distribution per lane (MOVES opModeDistribution).

items.title: energy/ev/kurczveil: SUMO's battery device (default)
items.text:
\[ \Delta E = \tfrac12 (m + m_{\text{rot}})(v_1^2 - v_0^2) + m g \sin\theta\, s + \tfrac12 \rho A c_d \bar v^2 s + c_r m g s + c_{\text{rad}} \frac{m \bar v^2}{r}\Delta t, \] \[ E_{\text{bat}} = \begin{cases} \Delta E / \eta_{\text{prop}} & \Delta E > 0 \\ \Delta E\, \eta_{\text{recup}}\, e^{-\alpha/|a|} & \Delta E \le 0 \end{cases},\qquad P = E_{\text{bat}}/\Delta t + P_{\text{const}}, \]

with \(r = s/|\Delta\psi|\) clamped to \([10^{-4}, 10^4]\) m.

Parameter Default Unit mass_kg 1830 kg front_area_m2 2.6 m² drag_coefficient 0.35 rotating_mass_kg 40 kg roll_coefficient 0.01 radial_coefficient 0.1 constant_power_w 100 W propulsion_efficiency 0.98 recuperation_efficiency 0.96 recuperation_decel_alpha 0 (SUMO); > 0 applies Fiori 2016's regeneration m/s² air_density 1.2041 kg/m³ capacity_wh 35000 Wh

Source: Kurczveil, López & Schnieder 2014 (SUMO 2013, LNCS 8594); defaults from SUMO HelpersEnergy.

items.title: energy/ev/vt-cpem: VT-CPEM (Fiori, Ahn & Rakha 2016)
items.text:
\[ P_w = \Big(m a + m g \cos\theta\,\frac{C_r}{1000}(c_1 v_{\text{km/h}} + c_2) + \tfrac12 \rho A_f C_D v^2 + m g \sin\theta\Big) v, \] \[ P_m = \begin{cases} P_w / (\eta_D \eta_{EM}) & P_w \ge 0 \\ P_w\, \eta_D \eta_{EM} \eta_{rb},\ \ \eta_{rb} = e^{-\alpha/|a|}\ (a<0) & P_w < 0 \end{cases},\qquad P_b = \frac{P_m}{\eta_{\text{bat}}}\ \text{or}\ P_m \eta_{\text{bat}},\ + P_{\text{aux}}. \]

Parameterised for a 2011 to 2013 Nissan Leaf: 1521 kg, \(C_D\) 0.28, \(A_f\) 2.3316 m², \(\eta_D\) 0.92, \(\eta_{EM}\) 0.91, \(\eta_{\text{bat}}\) 0.9 (todo-calibrate), \(P_{\text{aux}}\) 700 W, \(\alpha\) 0.0411, 24 kWh. Rolling resistance from Rakha et al. 2001 (\(C_r\) 1.75, \(c_1\) 0.0328, \(c_2\) 4.575).

Recalled values

The card marks the Fiori 2016 parameter table as recalled, not re-read; check it before citing results.

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
Provider metrics/energy (visibility GT):

items.title: Health bands
items.text:
v2xw_energy::bands grades a run's latest samples: ok inside the band, warn outside it but inside the plausible range, fail outside that (almost certainly a defect), and not-measured when there is no usable sample. A band is a sanity range, not a target.

Metric Class OK Plausible Basis co2_per_km passenger 90 to 350 g/km 40 to 700 EEA 2010 new-car fleet average 140.3 g/km (NEDC); urban stop-and-go well above it fuel_per_100km passenger 4 to 15 2 to 30 the CO₂ band through EPA's 8,887 g CO₂ per gallon ev_energy_per_100km passenger 9 to 25 kWh 3 to 45 2013 Nissan Leaf label, 18 kWh/100 km at the wall nox_per_km passenger 0 to 1 g/km 0 to 3 Directive 98/69/EC Euro 4 limits ev_soc_min all 0.05 to 1 0 to 1 below 5 % an EV would be seeking a charger energy_unmodelled all 0 ≥ 0 every vehicle had a class in the selected model

items.title: The v2xw energy command
items.text:
v2xw energy runs/<name>/recording.mcap
v2xw energy runs/<name>/recording.mcap --emission-model phemlight --ev-model vt-cpem
v2xw energy runs/<name>/recording.mcap --spec fleet-2030.yaml \
    --vehicles-csv vehicles.csv --opmode-csv opmode.csv --json
Argument Meaning RECORDING a full-profile recording (it reads gt.kinematics) --spec FILE a JSON or YAML energy: section body; replaces the scenario's --emission-model ID hbefa3, phemlight, moves-opmode or a full id --ev-model ID kurczveil, vt-cpem or a full id --vehicles-csv FILE one row per vehicle --opmode-csv FILE MOVES operating-mode distribution per lane --json print the outcome as JSON

The starting section is the one the recording's attached scenario carried; the simulation is not repeated, and the same recording scored twice gives the same numbers. A NODE-only recording has no gt.kinematics and cannot be scored.

items.title: Modelled versus simplified
items.text: Modelled Simplified or absent hot running exhaust emissions by three published methods cold start, evaporative emissions, non-exhaust PM (brakes, tyres, road), ambient temperature and air conditioning, deterioration HBEFA 3 for 45 classes no two-wheeler class; polynomial extrapolates outside its driving situations; no SUMO coasting rule PHEMlight with fuel cut-off two vehicles only (Euro 4 petrol and diesel passenger car); PN, NO and NOx corrections ignored MOVES operating modes with MOVESTAR rates light-duty only; one MOVES run's fleet and calendar year; start and hotelling processes ignored EV energy balance with regeneration (two models) constant efficiencies (no motor map), no battery resistance, temperature or ageing; no charging grade from the recorded height change grade clamped to ±0.3; upstream (well-to-tank) emissions ignored

items.title: Messages
items.text:
What a node sends, when it sends it, and how many bytes it weighs. The message layer is built so that every reported size says how real it is: generated from a published ASN.1 module, hand-written and checked against an independent decoder, or a length from a size model.

Code: crates/v2xw-msg (codecs, generators, size models, evidence table), crates/v2xw-node/src/{generate,events,denm_triggers,cpm,bsm_timing,vru,rsu}.rs (which node sends what), crates/v2xw-sec (the security envelope). Settings: messages, actors.vehicles.bsm_timing. The radio and network layers that carry these bytes are on Radio and network.

items.title: Message sets
items.text:
messages.sets (default [bsm]) chooses which services the nodes run. The loader refuses a set no node could send.

Set Standard Sent by Requires bsm SAE J2735 BSM, SAE J2945/1 rules equipped vehicles cam ETSI EN 302 637-2, TS 103 900 equipped vehicles denm ETSI EN 302 637-3, TS 103 831 equipped vehicles, on events net.layer: gn-btp spat, map SAE J2735 SPaT and MAP (SPATEM/MAPEM on the ETSI stack) roadside units with the spat / map role an RSU with that role srm J2735 signal request emergency-class vehicles map in the sets and an emergency class share ssm J2735 signal status RSUs with the spat role srm and a spat RSU cpm ETSI TS 103 324 collective perception vehicles; RSUs with the cpm role net.layer: gn-btp psm, vam SAE J2735 PSM (J2945/9), ETSI TS 103 300-3 VAM VRU devices refused as sets: set actors.vru.device_fraction > 0

A VRU device sends PSMs when the sets include bsm (or psm), VAMs when they include cam (or vam), both when both stacks are present, and PSMs when neither is (v2xw_engine::hosted::vru_services).

items.title: How real the bytes are
items.text:
Every encoded message carries a size_source (uper, coer or size-model), and v2xw_msg::evidence::EVIDENCE states, per message type, what has checked it. A size is byte-exact only when the evidence level says so.

Level Meaning Byte-exact oracle-validated real wire bytes; an independent ASN.1 implementation agreed byte for byte on recorded vectors yes generated-from-module real wire bytes from rasn bindings generated at build time from the committed ASN.1 module; no third-party vectors checked yes real-uper-unvalidated real bytes of a documented subset, checked only by this crate's own tests no size-modelled a fill pattern of exactly the modelled length no not-encoded no codec claims the type Message On the air Evidence Encoder BSM UPER oracle-validated (pycrate compiled from the J2735 modules) hand-written, v2xw_msg::j2735::bsm SPaT, MAP UPER oracle-validated (pycrate, public J2735 2016 and 2020 modules) hand-written, j2735::spat, j2735::map PSM UPER the VRU device's bytes are hand-written UPER checked against pycrate; the generic codec row is a size model j2735::psm CAM, DENM UPER generated from module (TS 103 900, TS 103 831 over TS 102 894-2 Release 2) rasn, v2xw_msg::cam, denm VAM UPER generated from TS 103 300-3 V2.2.1; decoded and re-encoded identically by asn1tools v2xw_msg::vam CPM UPER generated from TS 103 324 V2.1.1; decoded and re-encoded identically by asn1tools v2xw_msg::cpm WSA UPER oracle-validated against asn1tools on the IEEE 1609.3-2016 modules hand-written, v2xw_msg::wsa SRM, SSM size model derived from the ASN.1 structure, todo-calibrate size_model CRL, P2PCD COER encoded by v2xw-sec over the generated IEEE 1609.2 bindings Security ETSI misbehaviour report not encoded through a codec Threats

Why SAE J2735 is hand-written

The SAE J2735 ASN.1 is licensed and not redistributable, so it is not in the repository (it is git-ignored under third_party/asn1/j2735/). rasn-compiler cannot compile it either: the RegionalExtension information-object-class idiom produces compile errors. The BSM, SPaT, MAP and PSM codecs are therefore written by hand against the bit-level UPER engine in j2735::uper, and checked against an independent decoder when a local copy of the modules is present. The ETSI modules are BSD-3-Clause and are committed under third_party/asn1/etsi/ with their provenance.

messages.codec_tier: size-model replaces encoding with the size model for very large runs; the default is uper.

items.title: SAE J2735 BSM
items.text:
BasicSafetyMessage = coreData (14 mandatory fields, 290 bits, every message) plus an optional partII with VehicleSafetyExtensions (container 0). A Part I-only BSM is 37 octets, 40 inside a MessageFrame. Every field holds the wire integer (latitude in 0.1 µdeg, speed in 0.02 m/s, acceleration in 0.01 m/s²) and uses the type's unavailable sentinel for a missing quantity.

Element Status BSMcoreData, every field encoded and decoded VehicleSafetyExtensions: events, pathHistory.crumbData, pathPrediction, lights, currGNSSstatus encoded and decoded PathHistory.initialPosition refused Part II containers 1 (special vehicle) and 2 (supplemental) carried verbatim regional, any extension addition refused

items.title: ETSI CAM, DENM, VAM, CPM
items.text:
Message Containers filled CAM basic and high-frequency every time; low-frequency on the first CAM and then every ≥ 500 ms (EN 302 637-2 §6.1.3). A typical unsecured CAM is about 60 octets of UPER DENM management, situation and location for a new or updated event; neither situation nor location for a termination (the WITH COMPONENTS constraint rasn does not carry is enforced in denm.rs) VAM header (messageId vam(16)), basic container (stationType pedestrian 1 or cyclist 2), VRU high-frequency, VRU low-frequency on its cadence; no cluster or motion-prediction container CPM management (referenceTime, referencePosition), originating vehicle (or RSU), sensor information, perceived objects in an ENU frame centred on the reference position (TS 103 324 §7.1.8.1)

Every input is the sender's belief (its GNSS estimate), never ground truth.

items.title: WSA
items.text: v2xw_msg::wsa encodes the IEEE 1609.3-2016 WAVE Service Advertisement (protocol version 3) as UPER. A roadside unit with the WSA role advertises the SCMS service: WAVE security management (PSID 0x23, the IEEE 1609.2.1 SecurityMgmtPsid; that a US RSU uses exactly this PSID is an assumption the code states) and IPv6 Routing, with a WAVE Routing Advertisement: 84 octets. The default period is 10 Hz (USDOT RSU Specification v4.1 App. D).

items.title: BSM: SAE J2945/1
items.text:
generator/bsm-j2945-1. Part I in every message, 10 Hz nominal.

Parameter Default Source nominal_itt_ms 100 ms SAE J2945/1, 10 Hz min_itt_ms (vMinITT) 100 ms todo-calibrate max_itt_ms (vMaxITT) 600 ms todo-calibrate vTxRand 5 ms J2945/1 (2020) 6.3.8.8, Table 21 vRescheduleTh 25 ms J2945/1 6.3.8.5

On a vehicle the engine runs J2945/1's own schedule (6.3.8.5 to 6.3.8.8) on the unit's clock:

\[ t_{\text{next}} = t_{\text{last tx}} + \text{Max\_ITT} + \text{RandOffset},\qquad \text{RandOffset} \sim U(-v_{\text{TxRand}}, +v_{\text{TxRand}}), \]

with RandOffset drawn from the key (plugin(generator/bsm-j2945-1), LinkFrame((n, n), LastTxTime)). Every vTxRateCntrlInt (100 ms) and at the onset of a critical event, the transmission decision may move the scheduled BSM. Max_ITT comes from the congestion control (dcc/sae/j2945-1-rate-power, network) and is held inside [min_itt, max_itt] and never below the nominal interval.

items.title: CAM: EN 302 637-2
items.text:
generator/cam-en302637-2, the §6.1.3 state machine, checked every T_CheckCamGen:

Parameter Default Clause t_gen_cam_min_ms 100 ms §6.1.3 t_gen_cam_max_ms 1000 ms §6.1.3 t_check_cam_gen_ms 100 ms §6.1.3 n_gen_cam 3 §6.1.3 heading_threshold_deg 4° §6.1.3 position_threshold_m 4 m §6.1.3 speed_threshold_mps 0.5 m/s §6.1.3 low_frequency_interval_ms 500 ms §6.1.4

Trigger 1 (dynamics) fires when \(|\Delta\psi| > 4^\circ \lor |\Delta \mathbf{p}| > 4\,\text{m} \lor |\Delta v| > 0.5\,\text{m/s}\) since the last CAM, and sets \(T_{\text{GenCam}} := \operatorname{clamp}(\text{elapsed}, T_{\text{GenCamMin}}, T_{\text{GenCamMax}})\); trigger 2 is the periodic deadline, and after N_GenCam consecutive trigger-2 CAMs \(T_{\text{GenCam}} := T_{\text{GenCamMax}}\). T_GenCam_Dcc arrives as the DCC's T_off and acts as a floor (C2C-CC RS 2037 RS_BSP_293). The thresholds are evaluated on the GNSS belief, so a noisy fix raises the CAM rate as it does on a road.

messages.rate_hz replaces both rules with a fixed awareness rate (the ns-3 BsmApplication and Veins beaconInterval convention); congestion control may still stretch it.

items.title: Generation timing
items.text:
Each node's generation clock is offset from the engine's step grid by \(\varphi \sim U[0, T)\), drawn once per node from (plugin(generator/timing-phase-jitter), Node(id)), where \(T\) is the generation period. Without this, every node would sign and contend in the same few hundred microseconds of each 100 ms. A per-message hand-off jitter \(j \sim U[0, j_{\max}]\) follows signing; its default is ns-3 BsmApplication's TxMaxDelay (10 ms), a simulator convention rather than a standard's number. A J2945/1 unit on 802.11p uses RandOffset instead and has no hand-off jitter; on a PC5 sidelink there is none either, because SPS schedules rather than contends.

messages:
  generator:
    id: generator/timing-phase-jitter
    params: { phase_window_ms: 0, max_jitter_ms: 0 }   # every node on one grid

items.title: BSM Part II: path history and prediction (J2945/1)
items.text:
v2xw_msg::j2945, from the node's own GNSS fixes:

Rule Value Source path history covers at least 200 m (vMinPHistDistance) J2945/1 §6.3.6.16, Table 21 most points per message 15 (vMaxPHistPoints; J2735 allows 23) Table 21; messages.path_history_points chord perpendicular error below 1 m (vPathPerpendicularDist) Table 21 longest chord 210 m (vMaxChordLength) Table 21 start-up history one point at the newest fix §6.3.1, §6.3.7 path prediction \(R = v/\dot\psi\), straight beyond 2,500 m radius cap recalled, a parameter hard-braking flag > 0.4 g; > 0.2 g for buses and Class 7 to 13 trucks J2735 event flags lights-changed flag held 2 s after a change J2735 on a pseudonym change keep (default for BSM nodes) or clear messages.bsm.path_history_on_change

items.title: BSM timestamp model
items.text: actors.vehicles.bsm_timing (off by default) gives each OBU a timing class drawn once per device: whether its secMark sits on the GNSS fix epoch ("locked") or not ("free"), epoch slips between the reported position and the timestamp, frozen repeats, the jitter of the 1609.2 generationTime against secMark, and (schema v2 and v3) a free-running BSM clock, output noise and a position-error random walk. Classes and shares come from a calibration file (data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot.yaml when present) fitted to public CV-pilot BSMs; the built-in values are provisional. Only the transmitted BSM is affected; ground truth and the GNSS model are not.

items.title: Event and infrastructure messages
items.text:
Message Trigger Source DENM emergencyElectronicBrakeLights the emergency stop signal: deceleration ≥ 6 m/s², off below 2.5 m/s²; update every 100 ms while on; validity 2 s C2C-CC RS 2003 RS_tcDaSi_167; UN R48 / R13-H DENM stationaryVehicle / vehicleBreakdown hazard lights on, standing, Triggering Timer (10 s) elapsed; repeated every 1 s for 15 s; validity 30 s C2C-CC RS 2006 §3.2 DENM sudden speed drop, local slow down off unless messages.denm_traffic_condition C2C-CC RS 2007 §3.1, §3.2 DENM traction loss (adhesion) friction estimate below 0.3 or 0.2 for 5 s; off unless messages.denm_traction_loss C2C-CC RS 2002 §3.3 SPaT / MAP every 100 ms / 1 s (messages.spat_interval_ms, map_interval_ms) CTI 4501 SRM a junction whose MAP was heard within 300 m ahead; repeated every 1 s J2735; range and interval are this build's choice SSM a received request; at most one per 100 ms J2735 PSM 1 Hz, floored at 100 ms todo-calibrate VAM the CAM machine with T_GenVamMin 100 ms, T_GenVamMax 5 s, 4 m / 0.5 m/s / 4°, low-frequency every ≥ 2 s TS 103 300-3 §6.2

The DENM lifecycle (EN 302 637-3 V1.3.1) is implemented in v2xw_msg::denm: unused actionId per new event (§8.2.1.5), updates keep it and advance referenceTime (§6.1.2), repetition only when the application supplies both interval and duration (§6.1.4.2), default validity 600 s, termination by cancellation or negation (§8.3.2.5), and keep-alive forwarding at \(2\,T_{\text{tx}} + U(0, 150\,\text{ms})\) (Annex B). A VRU device's VAM omits the trajectory-interception trigger and redundancy mitigation, so it transmits at least as often as a conformant device.

items.title: CPM: TS 103 324 V2.1.1
items.text:
v2xw_node::cpm, on the objects the perception model reports.

Rule Value Clause generation check T_GenCpm 100 ms (messages.cpm_interval_ms) §6.1.2.1, Table F.1 a CPM at least every T_GenCpmMax 1000 ms Table F.1 Type-B object (vehicle) included first detection, or moved > 4 m, speed change > 0.5 m/s, orientation change ≥ 4°, or last included ≥ 1 s ago §6.1.2.3 rule 2 Type-A object (pedestrian, cyclist, animal) first detection; when any has gone 500 ms unincluded, all are included §6.1.2.3 rule 1 sensor information container first CPM, then every ≥ 1000 ms §6.1.2.2 objects per CPM ≤ 255 (messages.cpm_max_objects) ASN.1 DCC-limited T_GenCpm T_off clamped to [100, 1000] ms (messages.cpm_dcc_limited) §6.1.2.1, Annex D quality threshold objects whose objectPerceptionQuality exceeds it (messages.cpm_quality_threshold, Table F.1 recommends 3) §6.1.2.3, §7.1.8.6

Object perception quality (§7.1.8.6, Table F.4 weights all 1, EMA factor 0.5):

\[ q = \left\lfloor \frac{w_d r_d + w_c r_c + w_{oa} r_{oa}}{w_d + w_c + w_{oa}} \right\rfloor,\quad r = \lfloor \mathrm{EMA}\cdot 15 \rfloor,\quad r_{oa} = \min(\lfloor oa / 100\,\text{ms}\rfloor, 15). \]

Under a budget, objects are ordered by the §6.1.3.2 utility \(p_{\text{conf}} + p_{\text{pos}} + p_{\text{speed}} + p_{\text{orient}} + p_{\text{time}}\) and the lowest are cut. Perception regions, look-ahead inclusion, segmentation by MTU_CPM and multi-channel operation are not modelled.

items.title: The security envelope
items.text:
The IEEE 1609.2 SignedData envelope and its ETSI TS 103 097 profile are encoded for real (COER) by v2xw_sec::envelope, so the overhead is measured, not tabled. With ECDSA P-256 under PSID 0x20:

Component Octets Ieee1609Dot2Data (protocolVersion, content choice) 2 hashId 1 SignedDataPayload preamble and inner Ieee1609Dot2Data 1 + 3 to 4 HeaderInfo preamble, psid, generationTime 1 + 2 + 8 signer = digest (HashedId8) 9 signer = certificate 3 + certificate ECDSA P-256 signature (x-only rSig, sSig) 66 generationLocation (DENM, TS 103 097 §7.1.2) +10

Measured (crates/v2xw-sec/tests/overhead.rs): 93 octets with a digest signer, and 87 octets plus the certificate with a certificate signer (an implicit certificate is about 80 octets, an explicit one about 147). A PSID ≥ 256 adds one octet. How often a full certificate is attached is security.signer_id_policy (Security).

items.title: The size model
items.text:
For the messages no codec encodes (and for codec_tier: size-model), v2xw_msg::size_model and etsi_size give a base plus a per-element increment per content profile, each row checked against its published anchors after converting them to payload scope (removing the 93-octet digest envelope, the 87 + 80 certificate envelope and the 5-octet WSMP header).

Message Profile Base Increment Basis PSM typical 27 B 8 B per path-history point ASN.1 structure; the increment from C2C-CC TR 2052 §3.1 SRM typical 20 B 10 B per request ASN.1 structure, todo-calibrate SSM typical 16 B 12 B per status ASN.1 structure, todo-calibrate SPaT, MAP (retired) 17 B, 40 B per movement / lane superseded by the real encoders, kept as a cross-check CPM typical per object ETSI TR 103 562 Table 3 container sizes, bounded by C2C-CC TR 2050 Fig. 13 VAM typical fitted to four published planning sizes (TR 2050 Fig. 12 and others)

Below the envelope, the network layer adds its own headers (WSMP 5 octets for a BSM; GeoNetworking and BTP 52 octets including LLC/SNAP below a secured CAM); see Radio and network.

items.title: Outputs
items.text: Channel What node.tx every transmission: message type, bytes on air, payload bytes, signer identifier type, pseudonym digest (VWP §3.6.4) node.rx, node.verify receptions and their verification metric.sample message-rate, size and channel metrics (Metrics)

items.title: Modelled versus simplified
items.text: Modelled Simplified or absent real UPER bytes for BSM, SPaT, MAP, PSM, WSA (hand-written, oracle-checked) and CAM, DENM, VAM, CPM (generated) SRM and SSM are sized, not encoded real COER security envelope, measured overhead encrypted SPDUs and countersignatures are not produced J2945/1 BSM schedule with RandOffset and congestion-driven Max_ITT vMinITT and vMaxITT defaults are uncited (todo-calibrate) EN 302 637-2 CAM triggers on the GNSS belief and the believed clock the CAM's ≤ 50 ms generation budget is not a delay; special-vehicle and RSU CAM containers are not filled J2945/1 path history and prediction PathHistory.initialPosition and BSM regional extensions are refused C2C-CC DENM triggering conditions VAM clustering, redundancy mitigation and trajectory interception are absent TS 103 324 CPM inclusion, quality and utility rules CPM segmentation, perception regions and multi-channel operation are absent

items.title: Radio, network and message models
items.text:
Code: crates/v2xw-radio (geometry to decibels to frame outcomes), crates/v2xw-net (headers, routing, fragmentation, byte accounting), crates/v2xw-msg (what is sent and what it weighs). Every cited constant carries its clause in the code and in its model card. Validation of each layer against its reference, with fault injection: crates/v2xw-netval (../testing.md).

Radio access technology is chosen by radio.rat: dsrc-80211p (IEEE 802.11p / ITS-G5), lte-v2x-pc5, nr-v2x-pc5, or hybrid. Each family has abstract, medium and high tiers (radio.tiers), and specific models can be named in radio.models.

items.title: Link budget
items.text: budget.rs composes three terms per link: a deterministic distance law, obstacle loss, and stochastic shadowing and fading. Carrier 5.9 GHz unless a 3GPP model sets its own.

items.title: Path loss (prop.rs, winner.rs)
items.text:
Model id Model Source propagation/free-space Friis propagation/two-ray-ground two-ray ground-reflection asymptote ns-3 TwoRayGroundPropagationLossModel propagation/two-ray-interference phase-exact ground reflection with the Fresnel coefficient of the road Sommer, Joerer & Dressler, IEEE VNC 2012, Eq. 4-6; Rappaport §4.6 propagation/log-distance-shadowing dual-slope log-distance with spatially correlated log-normal shadowing; LOS and OLOS rows Abbas et al. 2015; Kunisch & Pamp and Cheng rows via Karedal 2011 propagation/v2v-urban-geometric NLOS at intersections Mangel, Klemp & Hartenstein, EURASIP JWCN 2011:182 propagation/winner-plus-b1 WINNER+ B1 LOS with effective antenna heights, as adopted for V2V 3GPP TR 36.885 propagation/tr37885 the TR 37.885 V2X channel states (LOS, NLOSv, NLOS) 3GPP TR 37.885 §6.2, Tables 6.2-1, 6.2.1-1

Vehicle antenna patterns: antenna/vehicle/tr37885-option1 (TR 37.885 V15.3.0 §6.1.4).

Received power and the link's decision quantity:

\[ P_r = P_t + G_t + G_r - PL(d) - L_{ ext{obstacle}} - X_\sigma + 10\log_{10} g_{ ext{fading}},\qquad ext{SINR} = rac{P_r}{N + \sum_j I_j}, \]

with interference \(I_j\) from concurrent frames and jammers summed in node-id order.

Model Equation (from the card) two-ray ground (asymptote) crossover \(d_c = 4\pi h_t h_r/\lambda\); above it \(L = 10\log_{10}\! ig(d^4 L_{ ext{sys}}/(h_t^2 h_r^2) ig)\) two-ray interference \(d_{ ext{los}} = \sqrt{d^2 + (h_t - h_r)^2}\), \(d_{ ext{ref}} = \sqrt{d^2 + (h_t + h_r)^2}\), \(\varphi = 2\pi(d_{ ext{los}} - d_{ ext{ref}})/\lambda\), \(\Gamma_\perp = \dfrac{\sin heta - \sqrt{\varepsilon_r - \cos^2 heta}}{\sin heta + \sqrt{\varepsilon_r - \cos^2 heta}}\) dual-slope log-distance \(PL = PL_0 + 10 n_1 \log_{10}(d/d_0)\) for \(d \le d_b\), \(PL(d_b) + 10 n_2 \log_{10}(d/d_b)\) above, \(d_0 = 10\) m; Abbas 2015 urban LOS: \(n_1\) 1.81, \(n_2\) 2.85, \(PL_0\) 63.9 dB, σ 4.15 dB, \(d_b\) 104 m TR 37.885 LOS / NLOSv urban \(38.77 + 16.7\log_{10} d_{3D} + 18.2\log_{10} f_c\); highway \(32.4 + 20\log_{10} d_{3D} + 20\log_{10} f_c\); urban \(P( ext{LOS}) = \min\{1, 1.05\,e^{-0.0114 d}\}\) buildings (Sommer 2011) \(PL_{ ext{LOS}} + 9\,n_{ ext{walls}} + 0.4\,d_{ ext{in}}\) dB knife-edge (ITU-R P.526) \(J( u) = 6.9 + 20\log_{10}\! ig(\sqrt{( u - 0.1)^2 + 1} + u - 0.1 ig)\) dB for \( u > -0.78\) rain (ITU-R P.838-3) \(A = k(f)\,R^{\alpha(f)}\,d_{ ext{km}}\) dB

items.title: Obstacles (obstacle.rs, obstacle/, foliage.rs, terrain.rs)
items.text:
Model id Model Source obstacle/building/sommer-2011 per-wall and per-metre loss through building footprints (9 dB per wall, 0.4 dB/m) Sommer, Eckhoff, German & Dressler 2011 obstacle/vehicle/tr37885-nlosv blockage by vehicles TR 37.885 NLOSv; Boban vehicle heights obstacle/reflection/gemv2-single-bounce single-bounce building reflection Boban et al., GEMV² obstacle/terrain/knife-edge-p526 multiple knife-edge diffraction over the DEM profile ITU-R P.526-14 obstacle/foliage/p833 excess loss through vegetation ITU-R P.833-10 §3.1

Building material properties follow ITU-R P.2040-3. Rain attenuation follows ITU-R P.838-3.

items.title: Fading (fading.rs)
items.text: fading/nakagami-m samples one power gain per directed link per frame from a stream keyed by that link and frame, so a repeated query gives the same sample; distance- dependent m profiles are cited on the card. fading/none disables it.

items.title: 802.11p / ITS-G5
items.text:
Model id What Source phy/80211p/ofdm-10mhz air time from the OFDM symbol structure, noise floor (-104 dBm in 10 MHz plus noise figure), EN 302 663 sensitivity table, CCA thresholds, SINR per overlap window, capture IEEE 802.11-2020 §17; ETSI EN 302 663; EN 302 571 phy/80211p/nist-per NIST OFDM packet-error model Pei & Henderson 2010 mac/80211p/edca-ocb EDCA in OCB mode: four access categories, AIFS and contention windows, backoff that freezes on a busy medium; broadcast frames are never retransmitted and the window never doubles IEEE 802.11; EN 302 663 Annex C mac/80211p/slotted-abstraction slotted medium-tier abstraction alternating channel access (net.channel_access: alternating, wave_schedule.rs) the EDCA MAC gated on the CCH/SCH schedule IEEE 1609.4-2016 §6.2.5

Channel busy ratio is measured by the MAC (radio/mac/cbr-window). Regional channel plans, power limits, spectrum masks and adjacent-channel leakage are in regulation.rs.

items.title: Congestion control (dcc.rs)
items.text:
Model id What Source dcc/etsi/reactive-ts102687 reactive state machine ETSI TS 102 687 dcc/etsi/adaptive-ts102687 adaptive duty-cycle control ETSI TS 102 687; TS 103 175 EN 302 571 floor idle-time bound enforced under any algorithm EN 302 571 §4.2.10.2; TS 103 175 §7.2 Eq. 1 dcc/sae/j2945-1-rate-power (+ /tracking, /inference) BSM rate and power control with tracking-error and channel-quality inference Ahmad et al. (CAMP), IEEE TVT 2019, Table I, Eq. 5-9; FMVSS 150 NPRM 82 FR 3854 dcc/sae/j3161-1-rate LTE-V2X rate control presets SAE J3161/1

Adaptive DCC (TS 102 687), every 200 ms:

\[ \text{CBR} \leftarrow \tfrac12\text{CBR} + \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{\text{CBR}_{L0} + \text{CBR}_{L0,\text{prev}}}{2},\quad \delta \leftarrow (1-\alpha)\,\delta + \operatorname{clip}\big(\beta(\text{CBR}_{\text{target}} - \text{CBR})\big),\quad t_{\text{go}} = t_{pg} + \min\!\big(\max(T_{\text{on}}/\delta,\ 25\,\text{ms}),\ 1\,\text{s}\big), \]

with \(\alpha\) = 0.016 and \(\delta\) clamped to \([\delta_{\min}, \delta_{\max}]\). SAE J2945/1 rate control smooths the vehicle density within 100 m, \(N_s(t) = \lambda N(t) + (1-\lambda)N_s(t - 100\,\text{ms})\), and sets \(\text{Max\_ITT} = 100\) ms for \(N_s \le B\), \(100\,N_s/B\) ms above, capped at vMaxITT; its power control moves the radiated power linearly from vRPMax to vRPMin between vMinCU and vMaxCU of the smoothed channel busy percentage (6.3.8.1, Eq. 2).

items.title: Network layer (crates/v2xw-net)
items.text:
The network layer counts octets exactly but does not synthesise header bytes that no code reads: a NetPdu carries the SDU's real bytes and the header's exact size and decoded fields.

items.title: Fragmentation (frag/)
items.text:
Neither WSMP nor GeoNetworking can fragment, so an SDU over the MTU (a post-quantum certificate, for example) has three fates, chosen by net.fragmenter:

Model id What fragmenter/none refused fragmenter/facilities-segmentation segmented at the facilities layer into independently usable pieces fragmenter/generic-sdu split into pieces useless alone; loss amplifies as P_sdu = 1 - prod(1 - p_i) fragmenter/cert-cycle-partial-hybrid the partially hybrid certificate cycle (NDSS 2024)

Byte accounting (accounting.rs) attributes every octet on the air, the Uu link, the backhaul and the backend to a layer, and the sum is an invariant; frame.rs breaks one PSDU down by payload, envelope, network header, LLC/SNAP, MAC header and FCS.

items.title: Privacy
items.text:
The pseudonym scheme exists to defeat one adversary: someone with receivers by the road who writes down what they hear and tries to follow a vehicle across certificate changes. The engine models the scheme (pseudonym change policies, silent periods, mix zones), the adversary (a passive observer that only listens), and what the backend learns (the separation of SCMS roles), and measures the result.

Code: crates/v2xw-engine/src/pseudonym_policy.rs (strategies and eavesdropper coverage), crates/v2xw-node/src/stores.rs (RotationPolicy, the certificate store), crates/v2xw-threat/src/privacy.rs (the observer), crates/v2xw-engine/src/privacy_metrics.rs (metrics), crates/v2xw-proto/src/scms/pki_view.rs (pki.knowledge), tools/pki_view/aca_blindness.py (ACA blindness check). Settings: security.pseudonym_change, threats.eavesdropper, messages.bsm.path_history_on_change.

flowchart LR
    pol["pseudonym policy<br/>(when to change)"] --> store["certificate store:<br/>certificate, TemporaryID,<br/>link-layer address change together"]
    store --> air["safety frames on the air"]
    air --> cov{"sniffer in range<br/>and not in a mix zone?"}
    cov -->|yes| obs["passive observer<br/>(kinematic tracker)"]
    obs --> claim["privacy.link claims<br/>privacy.track chains (NODE)"]
    gt["sec.pseudonym, node.security<br/>(ground-truth join)"] --> met["linkability,<br/>pseudonym_change_rate"]
    claim --> met

items.title: What changes on a pseudonym change
items.text:
On a change the node replaces, together, the signing certificate, the BSM TemporaryID (the first four octets of the certificate's digest) and the link-layer address derived from it, and restarts the BSM msgCnt at a random value (C2C-CC BSP RS_BSP_182; J2735 allows a restart on a change of identity). The first BSM after start-up also carries a random msgCnt (SAE J2945/1 §6.3.6.2 DATAACC-002). A scheduled change happens in the node's own store; the engine's policy can also ask the store to change now. An expiring certificate always changes.

The path history in a BSM's Part II carries over a change by default (keep: SAE J2945/1 has no clearing rule and asks for 200 m of history); clear restarts it, a research option.

items.title: Change strategies
items.text:
security.pseudonym_change.strategy:

Strategy Rule Source by-region (default) the region's rule: j2945-1 under the US IEEE 1609.2 envelope, time every 5 minutes under etsi103097; a by-region scenario that sets period_s gets the time rule time after period_s of use (300 s unless set) SAE J2945/1 CERTCHG, USDOT SCMS primer j2945-1 after 5 minutes and at least 2,100 m in a straight line from the last change point, never while the BSM carries a critical event flag SAE J2945/1 APR2020 §6.5.3 CERTCHG-001 to -003, Table 21 (vCertChangeInterval, vCertChangeDistance with 100 m tolerance) distance after distance_m in a straight line from the last change point (2 km unless set) NYC CV pilot nyc-pilot at 2 km or after 5 minutes, whichever comes first NYC CV pilot c2c-cc first after a random [800, 1500] m; the second at least 800 m on plus a random [120, 360] s; the third after a random [10, 20] km; then every random [25, 35] km C2C-CC Basic System Profile R1.5.1, RS_BSP_521 to 524 mix-zone inside a zone around each signalised intersection (radius mix_zone_radius_m, 30 m) once the pseudonym is mix_zone_min_age_s old (60 s) Freudiger et al., Mix-zones for location privacy in vehicular networks, WiN-ITS 2007 (CMIX) silent no scheduled change (control arm)

Distances are straight-line displacement from the last change point, not distance driven. The mix-zone radius and minimum age are this build's choices (CMIX fixes neither).

silent_period_s: [min, max] adds, under any strategy, a silent period after every change: no safety message for a uniform draw from the range (Huang et al., IEEE WCNC 2005; PRESERVE's 3 to 13 s). A silent vehicle is invisible to its neighbours' safety applications too.

security:
  pseudonym_change:
    strategy: c2c-cc
    silent_period_s: [3, 13]
threats:
  eavesdropper:
    id: threat/observer/passive-privacy
    params: { sniffer_fraction: 0.25, range_m: 200 }

Draws come from the plug-in domain of security/pseudonym-policy, keyed by the node.

items.title: The eavesdropper
items.text:
threats.eavesdropper (threat/observer/passive-privacy) sets the observer's coverage:

Parameter Default Meaning sniffer_fraction 1.0 share of signalised intersections with a sniffer (all junctions if the world has none signalised), spread deterministically range_m 200 m each sniffer hears every safety frame sent within this disc (a receiver on a pole, not a link budget)

Without the section the observer is global: it hears every safety frame on the air, the worst case. A frame sent inside a mix zone is not readable by the observer: the zone key's encryption is modelled by that rule, not performed.

items.title: The tracker
items.text:
The observer sees receptions and nothing else (ObservedMessage, the detector firewall): it has no credentials, transmits nothing and never learns which vehicle a digest belongs to. It is the constant-velocity, best-hypothesis tracker of Wiedersheim, Ma, Kargl and Papadimitratos (Privacy in inter-vehicular networks: why simple pseudonym change is not enough, WONS 2010).

Prediction over a silence \(\Delta t\), with \(\sigma_0\) the larger of the broadcast confidence and a floor, and \(a\) the plausible-acceleration bound:

\[ \hat{\mathbf p}(t) = \mathbf p + \mathbf v\,\Delta t,\qquad \sigma(\Delta t) = \sqrt{\sigma_0^2 + \big(a\,\Delta t^2/2\big)^2}. \]

A candidate predecessor \(u\) is kept when \(\lVert \text{claim} - \hat{\mathbf p}_u \rVert \le z\,\sigma_u\), and the posterior over the gated set \(\Psi\) is

\[ w_u = \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac12 (r_u/\sigma_u)^2\Big),\qquad p_u = \frac{w_u}{\sum_{k\in\Psi} w_k}. \]

The observer links the best hypothesis, or declines (method unlinked). With link_by_sequence, a successor whose msgCnt continues a predecessor's (the counter can have advanced at most \(\lfloor \Delta t / 0.1\,\text{s} \rfloor + 1\)) is linked by sequence; an honest vehicle restarts its counter at a change, so this catches a sender that does not.

Parameter Default Source z_gate 3.0 a 3σ gate carried from the earlier implementation; not externally cited sigma_floor_m 5.0 m position-consistency threshold carried from the earlier implementation; not externally cited; stops a sender evading by stating zero confidence accel_bound_mps2 3.0 m/s² F2MD MIN_MAX_ACCEL max_silence_s 13 s PRESERVE's longest silent period min_fixes_for_velocity 2 structural track_unverifiable true a passive observer needs no trust anchor link_by_sequence true J2735 MsgCount is on the air in the clear min_message_interval_s 0.1 s J2945/1 100 ms

items.title: Privacy measures
items.text:
Anonymity at a change (ETSI TR 103 415 §5.1.2), on every privacy.link record:

\[ S = -\sum_{u\in\Psi} p_u \log_2 p_u \quad\text{(effective set, bits)},\qquad d = \begin{cases} S/\log_2|\Psi| & |\Psi| > 1\\ 0 & |\Psi| \le 1\end{cases}. \]

\(d = 0\) with one candidate is the honest answer (nobody to hide among); \(d = 1\) means the observer learned nothing.

Record (NODE) Fields privacy.link observer, predecessor and successor digests, posterior, candidates, anonymity_set_size (the size of \(\Psi\), candidates plus target), effective_anonymity_set_bits (\(S\)), degree_of_anonymity (\(d\)), method privacy.track one chain of pseudonyms followed: origin and last digests, links, fixes, duration_s (last minus first reception, the WONS 2010 tracking duration), closed_reason

Metrics (metric/security/pseudonym-privacy):

Metric Formula Unit Not accounted for linkability correct observer links / pseudonym changes, cumulative ratio a declined link counts as a change not bridged; correctness is the ground-truth join from sec.pseudonym and node.security, never the observer's pseudonym_change_rate Σ changes / Σ vehicle-hours observed (fast-forward hours excluded) 1/(veh·h) changes before a vehicle's first node.security row cert_pool_valid distribution of certificates each vehicle holds valid now count certificates for later periods backend_link_up rows whose vehicle's backend access was usable / rows ratio down time between rows

The anonymity-set size, degree of anonymity and tracking duration are record fields to aggregate from the recording; they are not in the metric catalogue.

items.title: What the backend learns
items.text:
The US SCMS separates roles so that no single entity can link a device's pseudonyms (SCMS):

Property Mechanism Where the RA never learns a certified public key butterfly expansion: the PCA adds a secret random value to the RA's cocoon key v2xw_sec::butterfly the PCA cannot link two certificates to one device cocoon keys are pseudorandom without the expansion key; the RA shuffles requests across devices (1,000 requests or 2 days, CAMP 1.2.2) RA shuffle the PCA does not learn the device's enrolment identity the RA strips it before forwarding (IEEE 1609.2.1 §4.1.3) tools/pki_view/aca_blindness.py checks the recorded PDUs neither LA alone can link the linkage value is the XOR of two pre-linkage values from two LAs; the RA cannot open a pre-linkage value v2xw_sec::linkage revocation is forward-only publishing \(ls(i)\) reveals certificates from period \(i\) on, never earlier CrlLinkageEntry::matches the MA must ask the MA needs the PCA and both LAs to resolve a report separation rules in v2xw_proto::scms

pki.knowledge records what each entity holds in its own identifiers, with the ground-truth join kept apart, so a study can audit what each party could link. pki.flow carries each SPDU's bytes and the plaintext its recipient opened by really decrypting it.

items.title: ACA blindness check
items.text:
python -I tools/pki_view/aca_blindness.py runs/<name>            # writes aca-check.json
python -I tools/pki_view/aca_blindness.py runs/<name> --inject   # positive control

It decodes the RA-bound requests (each signed by the device's enrolment certificate, the whole certificate), collects every enrolment certificate and its HashedId8, and searches every ACA-bound PDU, wire bytes and opened plaintext, for any of them. leaks must be 0; --inject appends one enrolment certificate to the first ACA-bound blob, and leaks must then be at least 1, which proves the check can fail. It needs the oracle tooling under tools/oracle and a recording with security.scms.pki_view on.

items.title: Modelled versus simplified
items.text: Modelled Simplified or absent the deployed and proposed change rules, silent periods and mix zones RS_BSP_520 (silence at cold start) has nothing to act on: vehicles enter already driving identifiers changing together (certificate, TemporaryID, link-layer address, msgCnt restart) the path history carries over by default (keep), as J2945/1 asks a passive observer at a share of signalised junctions sniffer reception is a disc, not a link budget; mix-zone encryption is a readability rule kinematic best-hypothesis tracking with cited gate and silence bounds no linking by radio fingerprint or message-timing pattern the SCMS role separations, with recorded per-entity knowledge a backend insider combining several entities' knowledge is not simulated; pki.knowledge lets a study audit what such an insider could link

items.title: SCMS and credential systems
items.text:
Code: crates/v2xw-proto (entities, flows, protocols), with the cryptographic core in crates/v2xw-sec and the run-time wiring in crates/v2xw-engine/src/phase2.rs, scms_topology.rs, credentials.rs, pseudonym_policy.rs and ma_policy.rs. Selected by security.protocol.id (and the same id in actors.backend.protocol).

Two protocols are selectable: the US CAMP SCMS (protocol/scms/camp) and the ETSI ITS PKI (protocol/etsi/ts102941). Settings: security, actors.backend; every default with its source: SCMS constants.

items.title: CAMP SCMS (protocol/scms/camp)
items.text: Implements the US Security Credential Management System as specified by CAMP (SCMS PoC EE Requirements and Specifications, Release 1.2.2), IEEE 1609.2.1 and the SCMS Manager profiles, with Brecht et al., A Security Credential Management System for V2X Communications (IEEE T-ITS 2018) for the design rationale. Modules: crates/v2xw-proto/src/scms/ (run/ holds the behaviour of each flow).

items.title: Components
items.text:
Component Role in the engine End entity (EE) an OBU, RSU or VRU device: holds its enrolment certificate, butterfly keys and pseudonym pool Device Configuration Manager (DCM) proxies the device's enrolment to the ECA Enrolment CA (ECA) issues the enrolment certificate (US profile: crlSeries 4, region USA/Canada/Mexico) Registration Authority (RA) accepts requests, expands cocoon keys, shuffles, routes to the PCA, serves batch downloads, keeps blocklists Pseudonym / Authorization CA (PCA, the 1609.2.1 ACA) issues pseudonym certificates and encrypts each response to the device Linkage Authorities LA1, LA2 each hold a linkage-seed chain and produce pre-linkage values the RA cannot open Location Obscurer Proxy (LOP) hides the device's network identity from the RA Misbehaviour Authority (MA) receives reports, decides, runs linkage resolution and revocation CRL Generator (CRLG), CRL store and broadcast signs CRLs on their cadence; distribution by download through the RA and by RSU broadcast SCMS Manager, five electors, Root CA, Intermediate CA, Policy Generator governance: the elector-signed CTL (any 3 of 5), offline roots, the Global and Local Policy Files

scms/deployment.rs builds the topology from a preset: the default (us-production-2025) models two production providers on one CTL, each with its own roots and online components; a single-SCMS reference topology is kept for comparison. Provider regions and fleet shares are labelled assumptions.

The role separations of Brecht et al. are enforced on the placement: a scenario that co-hosts PCA with RA, PCA with either LA, LA1 with LA2, LOP with RA or MA, or MA with RA, either LA or PCA is refused unless it sets security.protocol.params.relax_separation.

items.title: How the layer measures cost
items.text:
The purpose of this layer is to measure what credential management costs (round trips, queueing delay, bytes) and what each party learns. Every backend role is therefore a node with a service queue on modelled links, never a function call:

  • every message between entities crosses a v2xw_proto::net::Link and pays for its bytes; Kernel::dispatch refuses delivery between nodes without a link;
  • every compute step is charged to the entity's queue (an entity fills an Outbox and the kernel decides when its work finished);
  • every flow declares which credential signs what and the stage timestamps it emits (spec::FlowSpec::stages); tests require the emitted stages to equal the declaration;
  • end entities read no backend state; answers reach them only as messages;
  • every byte count on a link has a provenance (sizes::SizeProvenance): the real encoder, a cited constant, or a model-card parameter with a calibration plan.

items.text:

items.title: Butterfly key expansion (v2xw_sec::butterfly, CAMP SCP1)
items.text:
The device uploads two caterpillar public keys \(A = aG\) and \(P = pG\) and two AES-128 expansion keys \(ck\) and \(ek\). With \(\iota = (i, j)\) packed into a 128-bit block \(x = \text{prefix}^{32} \| i^{32} \| j^{32} \| 0^{32}\) (prefix \(0^{32}\) for signing, \(1^{32}\) for encryption):

\[ f(k, \iota) = \big(\mathrm{AES}_k(x{+}1) \oplus (x{+}1) \,\|\, \mathrm{AES}_k(x{+}2) \oplus (x{+}2) \,\|\, \mathrm{AES}_k(x{+}3) \oplus (x{+}3)\big) \bmod n . \] Party Computes RA cocoon signing key \(B_{ij} = A + f_1(ck, \iota)\,G\); cocoon encryption key \(J_{ij} = P + f_2(ek, \iota)\,G\) PCA, explicit certificate certified key \(B_{ij} + cG\), with \(c\) secret to the PCA PCA, implicit (ECQV) reconstruction value \(P_U = B_{ij} + kG\), \(r = e k + d_{CA}\) device, explicit \(d = a + f_1(ck, \iota) + c \pmod n\), checked \(dG\) = certified key device, implicit \(d = e\,b_{ij} + r\) with \(b_{ij} = a + f_1(ck, \iota)\), checked \(dG = eP_U + Q_{CA}\) device, response opened with \(h_{ij} = p + f_2(ek, \iota)\) (IEEE 1609.2.1-2022 §9.3.4, original variant)

So the RA never learns a certified key, the PCA cannot link two certificates to one device (the cocoon keys are pseudorandom without \(ck\), and the RA shuffles), and the device re-derives every private key itself. Test vectors: CAMP bfkeyexp.txt with every intermediate and the OpenSCMS (Apache-2.0) signing and encryption vectors, plus cocoon keys, explicit and implicit issuance and response encryption per IEEE 1609.2.1-2022 §9.3 (crates/v2xw-sec/tests/official_vectors.rs). Only the original butterfly variant is accepted; the unified and compact unified variants are refused.

items.title: Linkage values (v2xw_sec::linkage, CAMP SCP2)
items.text:
Per Linkage Authority \(x \in \{1, 2\}\) with a 16-bit identifier \(la\_id_x\):

\[ \begin{aligned} ls_x(i) &= \operatorname{trunc}_{128}\big(\operatorname{SHA\text{-}256}(la\_id_x \| ls_x(i{-}1) \| 0^{112})\big)\\ plv_x(i, j) &= \operatorname{trunc}_{72}\big(\mathrm{AES}_{ls_x(i)}(la\_id_x \| j \| 0^{80}) \oplus (la\_id_x \| j \| 0^{80})\big)\\ lv(i, j) &= plv_1(i, j) \oplus plv_2(i, j) \end{aligned} \]

Only the PCA ever computes \(lv\); the 9-byte value is the LinkageValue in each certificate. Revocation publishes \(ls_x(i)\) for the current period, never \(ls_x(0)\), and a CRL entry refuses to match an earlier period, so revocation is forward-only; tests check that certificates from before the revocation period stay unlinkable. Two seeds revoke every future certificate of a device, about 40 bytes per entry (Brecht 2018 §VI-F). Vectors: CAMP lv.txt and glv.txt. Group linkage exists and is off by default.

items.title: Revocation
items.text: Active (a linkage-based series-1 CRL is produced, distributed, installed and enforced) and passive (issuance stops and the device runs out of certificates). Revocation latency is decomposed into the stages of the path, from the detector firing to the receivers that install the CRL (revocation_latency_stage). Hash-based CRLs (series 2, 3, 4, 256) cover non-pseudonym certificates. CRLs are real Ieee1609Dot2Crl encodings with their sizes from the encoder.

items.title: Calendar
items.text: time.calendar: real (default) runs one-week i-periods counted from the US SCMS epoch, 2015-01-06 04:00 US Eastern, with US Eastern daylight-saving time, US federal holidays and business days (scms/calendar.rs) for rules such as CRL publication within one business day. compressed allows a shorter i_period_s; every output labels it. time.fast_forward windows let a run cover weeks of credential activity.

items.title: Parameters
items.text:

items.title: ETSI ITS PKI (protocol/etsi/ts102941)
items.text: crates/v2xw-proto/src/etsi/. Enrolment with the Enrolment Authority, standard and butterfly authorization (TS 102 941 §6.2.3.5) with the Authorization Authority, authorization-ticket batch download, ECTL issuance by the Trust List Manager and publication at the CPOC, CA-only CRLs signed by the Root CA, fetches from the Distribution Centre that return only newer list versions (§6.3, §6.3.3), and TS 103 759 misbehaviour reporting with an EA blocklist. Certificates and cryptographic components are sized by the real COER encoder and cited constants; the TS 102 941 message framing that no clause fixes is a card parameter with a calibration plan.

items.title: Threshold protocols (crates/v2xw-proto/src/threshold/)
items.text: A t-of-n committee replaces one server's private-key operation (security.threshold names which roles). Shipped: FROST (RFC 9591), threshold ECDSA (CGGMP21), a t-of-n umbrella authority, and t-of-n linkage-seed release. The group arithmetic is not executed; the rounds, per-round message sizes, per-round compute from cited anchors, what each party learns, and slow, offline and malicious members (identifiable abort and restart) are. Flows: distributed key generation, signing, proactive refresh.

items.title: Security envelope, cryptography and node security
items.text: Code: crates/v2xw-sec (envelope, certificates, primitives, backends, schemes), crates/v2xw-node (what a device does with them, at what cost). The credential system that issues and revokes certificates is in scms.md.

items.title: The envelope
items.text:
v2xw_sec::envelope builds IEEE 1609.2 SignedData (§5.3.1) and its ETSI TS 103 097 profile (security.envelope: ieee1609.2 | etsi103097) by real COER encoding through the generated ASN.1 bindings, so a SecuredPdu's bytes are bytes a conformant receiver would accept and its size is exact; the overhead equals payload plus envelope as derived from the profile tables, and tests assert equality. v2xw_msg::sec_types is the single inclusion of the generated 1609.2 types.

Module Contents Source hashedid HashedId3/8/10 IEEE 1609.2a-2017 §6.3.25-6.3.26 cert implicit (ECQV) certificates, about 80 octets, and explicit ones, about 147 SEC 4; IEEE 1609.2 credential an implicit certificate with the private key its holder reconstructed SEC 4 §3.4-3.5 chain chain validation to a root on the installed trust list IEEE 1609.2 crl Ieee1609Dot2Crl: linkage-based (series 1) and hash-based lists, signing and verification IEEE 1609.2-2022 ctl the IEEE 1609.2.1 certificate trust list (MultiSignedCtl, fullIeeeCtl), elector-signed, any 3 of 5, ECDSA P-384 IEEE 1609.2.1 sig1609 1609.2 signatures: ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 and P-384/SHA-384 IEEE 1609.2 ecies, kdf, ccm ECIES over P-256 wrapping an AES-128-CCM key; KDF2 and MAC1 IEEE 1609.2a-2017 §5.3.5, Annex D.6.3 vectors p2pcd peer-to-peer certificate distribution wire formats IEEE 1609.2 clause 8 ec, p384, aes128 P-256 arithmetic, P-384, the raw AES-128 permutation FIPS 186-4, SEC 1, FIPS 197 butterfly, linkage butterfly key expansion and linkage values scms.md

items.title: Crypto backends (security.crypto_mode)
items.text:
Mode What runs real (crypto::Real) ECDSA P-256 with RFC 6979 nonces, SHA-256, SEC 4 ECQV reconstruction modeled (crypto::Modeled) a signature is a token derived from the key's secret and the digest; verification compares tokens; sizes from the primitive descriptors

The two produce identical verification outcomes and identical encoded sizes: a modelled token is exactly the descriptor's signature length and a modelled public key has the SEC 1 compressed shape, and nothing in the envelope branches on the mode (crates/v2xw-sec/tests/equivalence.rs). Only the manifest's crypto_mode differs. Both are deterministic, so neither affects run determinism.

In either mode, the compute a node spends signing and verifying comes from its hardware profile, not from the host's wall time.

items.title: Signature and KEM schemes (security.signature, security.kem)
items.text:
v2xw_sec::scheme describes each scheme as a composition of primitives with cited sizes and cost anchors (scheme::SIGNATURE_IDS, scheme::KEM_IDS):

Mode Signature ids classical ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-brainpoolp256r1, ecdsa-p384 hybrid: both signatures concatenated, both made and checked hybrid-falcon512-ecdsa-p256, hybrid-mldsa44-ecdsa-p256, hybrid-mldsa65-ecdsa-p256 post-quantum alone: certificate key and issuer signature are post-quantum ml-dsa-44, ml-dsa-65, ml-dsa-87, falcon-512, falcon-1024, slh-dsa-sha2-128s, slh-dsa-sha2-128f

KEM ids: ecies-p256, ml-kem-512, ml-kem-768, ml-kem-1024, hybrid-ecies-p256-ml-kem-768.

Post-quantum schemes are size and cost models: sizes are the standards' (FIPS 204 Table 2, FIPS 205 Table 2, PQClean's padded Falcon), costs are the catalogue's cited anchors, scaled by cycle ratio where a profile publishes nothing for a parameter set. No post-quantum signature is computed; crypto_mode: real accepts ecdsa-p256 only. Butterfly key expansion is unavailable in the post-quantum modes, which changes provisioning (handled in v2xw_proto::hybrid). Oversized certificates and signatures go through the fragmenters of network.md.
