items.title: Physical layer: 802.11p (radio.phy, radio.devices)
items.text:
radio.phy is refused on a C-V2X run (radio.rat: lte-v2x-pc5 or nr-v2x-pc5): the sidelink's MCS and sensitivity are radio.models.sidelink's.

Path Default Range Source and effect radio.rat dsrc-80211p dsrc-80211p, lte-v2x-pc5, nr-v2x-pc5 Which access layer runs. radio.region us-2016 (802.11p), us (C-V2X) us, us-2016, eu Band plan, deployment channel, EIRP limits (47 CFR 90.377, FCC 24-123, EN 302 571). Sets the carrier frequency. radio.channel region's channel 170-184 Carrier frequency through the band plan: f = 5000 + 5n MHz. 802.11p channels are 10 MHz. radio.devices.obu.tx_power_dbm 20 -20 to 33 dBm Conducted power. DCC may lower it, and the region's EIRP cap applies. radio.devices.{obu,rsu,vru}.antenna_gain_dbi profile -10 to 20 dBi Link budget at both ends. radio.devices.{obu,rsu,vru}.cable_loss_db profile 0 to 20 dB Link budget at both ends. radio.devices.{obu,rsu,vru}.antenna_height_m body class / mast 0.1 to 15 m Two-ray and geometric laws, LOS tracing. radio.phy.data_rate_mbps 6 3, 4.5, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 27 Every safety frame's MCS: its air time and its sensitivity row (IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 17-4; SAE J2945/1 vDataRate 6 Mbit/s). radio.phy.noise_figure_db 6 (PHY card) 0 to 15 dB Noise floor = -104 dBm (10 MHz thermal) + NF. Also sets the candidate range. radio.phy.sensitivity_dbm per-rate table (measured-obu, -92 dBm at 6 Mbit/s) -105 to -60 dBm One flat floor at every rate, as Veins' minPowerLevel (-89 dBm in Veins). radio.phy.cca_threshold_dbm -85 -100 to -50 dBm Carrier sense and the CBR busy threshold (EN 302 571 §4.2.10.1; ns-3 -82, Veins -65). radio.phy.capture_threshold_db unset (SINR trace) 0 to 30 dB A hard capture rule (Torrent-Moreno 2009 Eq. 1) in place of the error model. radio.models.per per/nist-ofdm ideal presets ideal, sjoberg-atheros Implementation loss of the NIST error model. radio.models.phy measured-obu etsi-static, etsi-dynamic, cohda-mk5, measured-obu Per-rate sensitivity table. radio.tiers.phy medium abstract, medium, high Fidelity. radio.tiers.propagation, radio.tiers.mac medium abstract, medium, high Fidelity. abstract is not a cheap large-fleet mode: free space with no buildings lets more links reach, and receptions dominate run cost (all three abstract measured 11 % cheaper than medium). For large fleets cap radio.range.max_m or use city-scale traffic tiers.

items.title: Channel model (radio.channel_model, radio.models)
items.text: Path Default Range Source and effect radio.models.propagation tier: free space (abstract), dual-slope log-distance (medium), geometric urban V2V (high) free-space, two-ray-ground, log-distance-shadowing, tr37885, v2v-urban-geometric The path-loss law (Abbas 2015, 3GPP TR 37.885, Mangel 2011). radio.channel_model.path_loss_exponent unset (measured dual-slope fits) 1.5 to 6 Single-slope PL = PL_FS(10 m) + 10·n·log10(d/10 m) at the run's carrier (Rappaport Eq. 4.68). Setting it runs the log-distance law. It is refused beside another explicitly named law. radio.channel_model.shadowing_sigma_db the law's own sigma (4.15 dB LOS, 6.67 dB OLOS urban, Abbas 2015) 0 to 15 dB Log-normal shadowing spread, applied to every law with shadowing (log-distance, TR 37.885, geometric, WINNER+ B1). radio.channel_model.shadowing_decorrelation_m environment's (about 10 m city) 0 to 500 m (exclusive of 0) Gudmundson 1991 correlation distance. radio.channel_model.fading tier's (Nakagami m = 3 for 802.11p, none for C-V2X curves) none, rayleigh, rice, nakagami Small-scale fading. Refused beside radio.models.fading. radio.channel_model.fading_coherence independent independent, doppler doppler draws one fade per link per coherence block, T_c = 0.423/f_D (Rappaport 2002 Eq. 5.40c) with f_D = (|v_tx|+|v_rx|)·f_c/c (Akki & Haber 1986), floored at 0.05 m/s: queued vehicles fade in bursts, fast ones decorrelate per frame. Refused when the run draws no fading. radio.channel_model.nakagami_shape 3 0.5 to 20 Nakagami m (needs fading: nakagami). radio.channel_model.rice_k_db 6 dB (Cheng 2007 LOS 3-10 dB) -10 to 30 dB Rice K, simulated as Nakagami m = (K+1)²/(2K+1) (Stüber Eq. 2.57). Needs fading: rice. radio.channel_model.nakagami_shape_far, .nakagami_breakpoint_m unset (one m everywhere) 0.5 to 20; (0, 5000] m Distance-dependent Nakagami m (Veins-style 1.5 near, 0.75 far). Need fading: nakagami, and each other. radio.channel_model.building_wall_loss_db, .building_loss_db_per_m 9 dB, 0.4 dB/m (Sommer 2011) 0 to 40 dB; 0 to 10 dB/m Sommer β and γ, wherever buildings are charged. Refused with buildings off or under TR 37.885. radio.channel_model.vehicle_blockage on with the geometric law bool TR 37.885 NLOSv under any law, or vehicles radio-transparent. world.sumo.signal_programmes as-file as-file, static How a SUMO net.xml's <tlLogic> programmes are imported. as-file: an actuated, delay_based or NEMA programme runs as the live controller its type names, with its phases' minDur/maxDur (and NEMA name, vehext, yellow, red) and its <param>s; delay_based runs as actuated, counted (delay-based-as-actuated); every attribute and parameter is counted in the import report's tl_ledger (applied, approximated, not modelled). static: every programme runs its phase list. Static programmes import byte-identically either way. SUMO-network worlds only (refused otherwise). radio.channel_model.foliage off bool Foliage excess on a path through world.vegetation: depth × 0.79·f^0.61 dB/m (GEMV² eq. 4; 2.33 dB/m at 5.9 GHz), capped at the P.526 knife edge over a 15 m canopy (P.833-10 §3.1, used above 1 GHz. Refused without world.vegetation. radio.channel_model.density_sigma off bool GEMV² eq. 10: the log-distance shadowing σ from the vehicles and building footprints inside each link's ellipse, between Table V's bounds (LOS 3.3-5.2 dB, NLOSv 3.8-5.3, NLOSb 4.1-6.8). Normalising densities are assumptions (11,500 veh/km², 60 % built). world.vegetation false bool The OSM import keeps natural=wood, landuse=forest, natural=tree_row (8 m strip) and natural=tree (diameter_crown, else 8 m) as a vegetation layer. A world without it keeps its content hash. radio.channel_model.reflection off bool GEMV² single-bounce building reflection (Boban 2014 §IV-B.3, eqs. 6-8): a building-blocked link also receives the strongest specular ray off a footprint wall whose legs are clear, priced by free-space spreading over the unfolded path (at most Table VI's 300 m) and the TE Fresnel coefficient of the wall material (ITU-R P.2040-3 Table 3; unknown walls are concrete), power-summed with the shadowed path. With density_sigma, NLOSb σ_min becomes 0 dB (Table V). Refused without buildings. world.terrain.drape false bool Lays lanes, junctions, crossings, buildings, sites and signal heads on world.terrain.dem (z += the DEM height), so traffic.vehicle_dynamics.grade has a slope to read. Off, the DEM is only the radio's ground and the geometry stays flat. Refused without world.terrain.dem. A world without it keeps its content hash. world.buildings.enabled true bool Buildings exist, and so obstruct. radio.models.obstacle obstacle/building-shadowing (Sommer 2011) presets Per-wall and per-metre loss. radio.range.margin_db, radio.range.max_m 10 dB, unset 0 to 40 dB; 50 m to 100 km How far a transmission is followed. This changes cost, not physics.

items.title: 802.11p medium access (radio.mac)
items.text:
This applies at radio.tiers.mac: medium or high, and is refused at abstract, which models no access. Broadcast OCB never doubles the window and never retries (EN 302 663 Annex C.4.2), so CWmax and a retry limit would change nothing and are not offered.

Path Default Range Source and effect radio.mac.edca_profile by-region by-region "By region", sae-j2945-1 "SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (BSM at AC_VI, critical BSM at AC_VO)", en-302-663 "ETSI EN 302 663 (OCB defaults)" The EDCA table. by-region is SAE J2945/1 §6.3.4 Table 18 (UPEDCA-003: AC_VI CWmin 15, CWmax 1023, AIFSN 4) for 802.11p under us/us-2016, EN 302 663 (AC_VI 7/15/3) elsewhere; AC_VO, AC_BE and AC_BK are the same in both. An explicit cw_min_*/aifsn_* still wins. Refused at radio.tiers.mac: abstract. Under Table 18 a BSM waits at AC_VI, or at AC_VO when it carries a critical event flag (hard braking, ABS, traction, stability), unless periodic_access_category is set. radio.mac.periodic_access_category vo vo, vi "Video (AC_VI) (SAE J2945/1 UP 5)", be, bk Queue of BSM, CAM, PSM, VAM, CPM, SPaT and MAP. SAE J2945/1 §6.3.4 sends a BSM without a critical event flag at user priority 5 (AC_VI, UPEDCA-001) and one with a flag at 7 (AC_VO, UPEDCA-002); EN 302 663 Annex C puts CAM at video. Unset under SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (edca_profile), a BSM is queued by its flags that way; set, it names the queue of every periodic message, the BSM included. radio.mac.event_access_category vo same Queue of DENM. radio.mac.cw_min_vo / cw_min_vi 3 / 15 (US 802.11p), 3 / 7 (elsewhere) 2^k - 1, from 1 to 1023 Random back-off window (SAE J2945/1 Table 18 under a US region, else EN 302 663 Table C.4; IEEE 802.11-2020 §9.4.2.28). radio.mac.aifsn_vo / aifsn_vi 2 / 4 (US 802.11p), 2 / 3 (elsewhere) 2 to 15 AIFS = AIFSN·13 µs + 32 µs. radio.mac.queue_length 64 1 to 1024 frames Per-category queue. A full queue drops (mac_drops). net.channel_access continuous continuous, alternating IEEE 1609.4 channel switching. alternating gates the EDCA MAC: a one-radio unit sends and hears the safety channel only in the CCH interval and the service channel only in the SCH interval; no frame starts in a 4 ms guard or crosses its interval's end (report mac_gate_deferrals, mac_guard_deferrals, straddling_frames). Two-radio units (radio.devices.*.radios: 2) do not switch. Interval lengths UNVERIFIED.

Refused without that message in sets. messages.cpm_interval_ms 100 ms 100 to 1000 ms T_GenCpm (ETSI TS 103 324 §6.1.2.3). Refused without cpm in sets. messages.cpm_dcc_limited off bool T_GenCpm follows the DCC's minimum gap T_off, clamped to [100, 1000] ms (ETSI TS 103 324 V2.1.1 §6.1.2.1, Annex D; Table F.1). Refused without cpm in sets. messages.cpm_quality_threshold unset (not applied) 0 to 15 (ratio); TS recommends 3 ObjectPerceptionQualityThreshold: a CPM carries only objects whose §7.1.8.6 quality (α 0.5, weights 1, Table F.4) exceeds it, and states that quality. Refused without cpm in sets. messages.cpm_max_objects unset (255, perception order) 1 to 255 objects Objects per CPM, ordered by the §6.1.3.2 utility (Table F.2 thresholds); the lowest-utility objects past it wait for the next event. Refused without cpm in sets. messages.denm_traffic_condition off bool The C2C-CC RS 2007 R1.6.10 sudden-speed-drop (dangerousEndOfQueue 27) and local-slow-down (trafficCondition 1) DENMs, non-urban roads only. Refused without denm in sets. messages.denm_traction_loss off bool The C2C-CC RS 2002 R1.6.10 §3.3 traction-loss DENM (adhesion 6) from the own ABS's friction estimate (< 0.3 or < 0.2 for 5 s). Refused without denm in sets. messages.path_history_points 15 0 to 23 points The most path-history points a BSM Part II (or a CAM) carries: SAE J2945/1 recalls 15, J2735 PathHistoryPointList allows 23, 0 sends none. About 8 to 9 bytes a point. Refused without bsm or cam in sets. messages.bsm.path_history_on_change unset: keep on a node that sends BSMs, clear on a CAM-only (ETSI) station keep "Keep (SAE J2945/1 6.3.6.16)", clear "Clear at each pseudonym change (privacy research)" What a pseudonym change does to the path history. J2945/1 has no clearing rule and asks for 200 m of history (DATAACC-039), so the US device keeps it; clear is a research option. Refused without bsm or cam in sets. An ETSI station without the BSM service clears at a change unless this is set; a set value holds for every node (NodeConfig::path_history_on_change). actors.vehicles.gnss.quality reid-2019 reid-2019 "Production receiver, measured (3.07 m at 68 %)", j2945-1 "SAE J2945/1 open sky (1.5 m / 3 m at 68 %)", rtk "RTK (0.26 m)" The receiver's quality. j2945-1 meets J2945/1's open-sky accuracies (§6.3.6.5-6.3.6.10: 1.5 m horizontal, 3 m vertical, 0.28 m/s, heading 2°/3° and the 1.10/1.38 m/s heading latch); the urban classes degrade every receiver alike (A.7). The measured receiver stays the default (scms-real/09 §5): certified devices meet the limits in open-sky tests, not in city canyons. j2945-1 acts (wiring::gnss_params); a set velocity_noise_mps still wins over its speed noise. Refused beside a contradictory rtk. security.signer_id_policy.full_cert_every_ms unset: per message type, BSM 450 ms (SAE J2945/1 6.5.2 BSMSIGN-003, Table 21 vMaxCertDigestInterval), CAM and every other message 1,000 ms (ETSI TS 103 097 §7.1.1) ms; menu 450 (SAE J2945/1), 1,000 (ETSI TS 103 097), 0 (every message), or any value 0 to 3,600,000 Certificate attach cadence. A digest is sent otherwise (digest_otherwise). A set value overrides both message types; 0 attaches the certificate to every message.

items.title: Security (security, nodes)
items.text: Path Default Range Source and effect security.envelope ieee1609.2 ieee1609.2, etsi103097 Secured-message format. security.signature ecdsa-p256 schemes in v2xw_sec::scheme (ECDSA, ML-DSA, Falcon, ...) See signature-schemes.md. security.crypto_mode modeled modeled, real Priced or real mathematics. security.verification_policy verify-all verify-all, on-demand, prioritized Verify all, verify on demand, or verify the safety-relevant first (verify-before-act). security.pseudonym_change.strategy by-region : j2945-1 under ieee1609.2, time under etsi103097 or when period_s is set by-region, time, distance, j2945-1 (SAE J2945/1 CERTCHG: 5 min unless within 2,100 m straight-line of the last change, never while a critical event flag is set; expiry still changes), nyc-pilot (2 km or 5 min), c2c-cc, mix-zone, silent Pseudonym strategy, with period_s (1 s to 1 day), distance_m (menu 2,100 m J2945/1, 2 km NYC pilot), silent_period_s, mix_zone_radius_m. The 2,100 m is Table 21's vCertChangeDistance; its 100 m tolerance makes any change at 2,000 m or more conformant. security.scms.rx_beacon_max_age_s by profile: 30 s US (SAE J2945/1 Table 11), 2 s ETSI (C2C-CC RS_BSP_168) 0 to 31536000 s; menu 30, 2, Other… Oldest BSM, CAM, PSM or VAM accepted, by the receiver's clock; older ones are discarded unverified (IEEE 1609.2 §5.2). Under the US window a replay up to 30 s old is verified and left to misbehaviour detection. security.scms.rx_max_age_s 600 s (both profiles) 0 to 31536000 s The same for every other application message. security.scms.rx_max_future_s by profile: 30 s US (Table 11, acceptable future data period), 0.04 s ETSI 0 to 31536000 s; menu 30, 0.04, Other… How far ahead of the receiver's clock a generationTime may be. The MA's report-evidence check still uses 40 ms (open). nodes.default_obu, nodes.per_class profile shipped obu/* profiles Crypto hardware profile: signing and verification service times. nodes.compute_tier medium tiers Queueing of crypto work. nodes.verify_queue_depth 64 1 to 4096 Verification queue. A full queue drops (verify_overflow). nodes.peer_cert_cache 128 1 to 65536 Peer certificates each vehicle or roadside unit holds (LRU). An evicted peer's next digest-signed message needs a P2PCD request and cannot be verified until its certificate arrives again. nodes.validated_cert_cache 4096 1 to 1048576 Validated end-entity certificates each device remembers (LRU, rxval::EE_CACHE); a forgotten signer pays first-sight validation again (ee_evictions). security.scms.crl_overdue_tolerance_s 1209600 (two weeks, CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67) 0 to 31536000 s How long past a CRL's nextCrl (a week after issue) a device keeps trusting the certificates it governs; then it refuses them (crl-overdue). See config-inventory-scms.md. security.scms.crl_poll conditional conditional, info-status How a cellular vehicle polls for new lists: the composite CRL with If-Modified-Since (one exchange), or the RA's signed CertificateManagementInformationStatusSpdu first (IEEE 1609.2.1 6.3.5.14, If-Modified-Since per [SMP] 4.4) and the composite only when it holds an older list. Report: phase2.info_status_polls, info_status_sent. security.scms.crl_overdue_scope craca craca, all What an overdue pseudonym CRL refuses: craca, the signers whose CRACA is the overdue list's; all, every message while any held series-1 list is past nextCrl + the tolerance (CAMP 1.2.2 Table 67: the EE is "rejecting all of them"; the sources leave both readings open). They differ only once a device holds a list nobody renews, after a CRACA changeover. nodes.hsm_sign_lower_us unset (every signature at the profile's upper bound, CRATON2 <9 ms) (0, 1e6) us, below the bound Each HSM signature drawn uniformly in [this, bound] from the node's own stream. No typical CRATON2/SECTON value is published. Refused when the default OBU has no upper-bound signing time. security.on_demand_threshold 0.5 (0, 1] Relevance score (1/(1+TTC) from the sender's claimed position, speed and heading against the receiver's own) at or above which an on-demand unit verifies a known signer. No published operating point (Krishnan & Weimerskirch 2011). Refused under any other policy. security.prioritized_horizon_m 300 10 to 2000 m Range over which nearness raises a prioritized unit's verification priority; the queue now serves the highest priority first. Refused under any other policy. security.signer_id_policy.on_new_neighbour false bool Also attach the certificate to the next BSM or CAM after a vehicle hears a station it did not know (ETSI TS 103 097 V1.3.1 §7.1.1), on top of the cadence; a forced certificate does not restart the cadence. Refused when every message already carries one, or with no bsm/cam. security.scms.deployment.providers[].site, .lat_deg, .lon_deg unset (the provider's region) a site of 29: today's six assumed regions, Google's nine US regions (published city), Azure's nine (published state or city), AWS's four (published state), custom; degrees -90..90 and -180..180, step 0.0001, only with site: custom Where a provider's servers run (scms-real/08 §5): every city and inter-provider latency is measured from the site's point. Published-city points are 2024 Census Gazetteer internal points; a state-only listing takes a named metro (ASSUMPTION). Not with region. The manifest names each site's point_source and the 30 km (0.15 ms) bound. security.scms.deployment.providers[].sites.<role> unset (every role at the provider's site or region) role: one the provider runs (root … crl_broadcast); site: the site menu less custom One role's servers at their own site (scms-real/08 §5): each link between that role and the provider's other roles costs the great-circle leg between their points at the fibre fraction plus the per-link overhead. The MA-to-MA link is measured from the MAs' sites, and the city leg from the RA's. Each is listed in the manifest. security.scms.deployment.capacity.<role> unset (4 workers, 1 ms, unlimited queue; ASSUMPTION, no provider publishes its capacity) workers 1..1024; queue_limit 1..1e7 requests; overhead_ms 0..10000 ms, step 0.1; service mmc (workers in parallel) / fifo-1 (one at a time) Server capacity of each named role on every provider (scms-real/08 §6). A device's request that reaches a server with queue_limit requests already waiting is turned away as busy, and the device retries after ee_retry_timeout_s within ee_retry_max_per_hour (SCMS-522/523). The count is refused_busy on the entity's queue in backend.state. Refused with the same role's actors.backend.entities.*.service_model, with fifo-1 and more than one worker, and under nodes.backend_tier: abstract. security.scms.deployment.providers[].capacity.<role> unset (the deployment's block) as above; role: one the provider runs One provider's own capacity per role (scms-real/08 §6). Its fields override the deployment's for that provider's servers only, for example a slower CRL Generator at provider-b. A role the provider does not run is refused. security.scms.ma_policy, security.scms.ma_policies, providers[].ma_policy unset (today's MA) preset cv-pilot-manual (US default), corroborated-auto, legacy-window, pseudonym-k, device-k, catch, cluster, custom, or a name from ma_policies; identity pseudonym/device; evidence.rules.<SM-MBR subtype or detect/<check>>.score 0..100 (0 = not evidence); accuracy_weighting none/catch with tau_m 0.1..10 m; event_window_s 0.1..600 s; event_min_reporters 1..100; threshold.min_events 1..100, min_score 0..1e6, min_reports 0..1e6, min_distinct_reporters 1..1000, window_s 1 s..30 days; decay none/daily-multiplier (factor 0..1, hour_et 0..23)/half-life (1 s..1 year); population_guard off/cluster (c 2..1000, m 1..10); defence trusted reporters on/off, reputation_max, report_budget; decision manual-review (review_s up to 30 days)/automatic The MA's decision rule as one declarative policy (scms-real/08 §7): a preset, with any field written beside it overriding the preset's. The default preset is today's MA, run byte-identically. A provider's own policy decides about the certificates it issued. Refused together with detection.ma; a written decision is refused with ma_review_s, and a provider's written decision with its ma_mode. identity: device takes the LAs' answer at once (no query round trips). experiment.sweep."security.scms.ma_policy.preset" unset a list of presets and ma_policies names Compares MA policies with feedback: one full run per policy per seed, security.scms.report_records turned on for every point, and ma-policy-family.csv/.md beside the results table (per run and per policy with a Student-t 95 % interval: attackers and honest devices revoked, honest blocked per 10⁶ device-hours, attack → decision → CRL → first refusal medians and p90s, reports processed, peak open cases; reads each run's recording, so not with --no-recording). v2xw ma-replay <run> --policies <scenario> previews the same family over one recorded run, without feedback (scms-real/08 §7). security.scms.deployment.providers[].ica_levels 1 (US) 1..5 levels; 6 or more is refused (a receiver accepts at most 8 certificates in a chain: root, the levels, the ACA and the pseudonym) Intermediate CA levels under a provider's root (scms-real/08 §8). n > 1 issues ica-2 … ica-n, each under the level above with exact certIssuePermissions {2 + (n − k), 0}. Every level goes in the chain files and the nodes' certificate pool, so each chain is n − 1 certificates longer. The run is flagged NOT the US system in its manifest and in scenario.validate's us_system, which name the level count. Under chain_file: home-provider a device learns a foreign provider's whole chain (the ACA and every level) from one P2PCD caCerts response and pays one signature verification per certificate it did not hold. actors.backend.failures[].node naming root, ica or ica-k is refused: an offline CA takes no request during a run. security.scms.lifecycle.ee_retry_timeout_s, .ee_retry_max_per_hour 10 s, 10 per hour (CAMP SCMS-522/523) 0 to 3600 s; 0 to 1000 A device's retry of an unanswered RA request; 0 turns it off. Before scms-real/08 A1 these were reachable only as security.protocol.params; the typed field wins where both are written. security.scms.lifecycle.crl_background_entries 0 0 to 1,000,000 revocations Earlier revocations already on the home provider's CRL at the start (a longer list to download and search). security.scms.lifecycle.clock_skew_s, .clock_skew_share 0 s, 1 (every device) 0 to 3600 s; 0 to 1 How far ahead the skewed devices' clocks run, and the share of devices skewed. security.scms.lifecycle.root_rollover_at_s, .root_removal_at_s, .peer_root_removal_at_s never ≥ 0 s into the run Root CA rollover and trust-list removals during the run. actors.backend.availability.model, .mtbf_h, .mttr_min; the same under actors.backend.entities.<role>.availability always-up; 720 h; 30 min always-up ("Always up"), two-state ("Random outages (two-state)"); 24, 168, 720, 8,760 h (range 1 to 87,600, step 1); 5, 30, 60, 240 min (range 1 to 10,080, step 1). A compressed calendar also admits 0.001 h and 0.01 min Whether backend servers fail at random: up times exponential with mean MTBF, down times exponential with mean MTTR, each drawn from a keyed hash of (seed, server, interval). A down interval is an offline failure window (the backend's retry and the device's SCMS-522 retry handle it). An entity's fields are written over the backend-wide ones, on that role in every provider. ASSUMPTION parameters (scms-constants.md §1.6). Report: phase2.backend_outages, backend_downtime_ms per server. actors.backend.service_time.model, .cv; the same under actors.backend.entities.<role>.service_time deterministic; 0.25 deterministic ("Fixed (cost table)"), log-normal ("Variable (log-normal)"); 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 (range 0 to 3, step 0.05) How service times vary: each request's time (its cryptographic cost plus the fixed overhead) times a log-normal multiplier with median 1 and this coefficient of variation, keyed by (seed, server, request). ASSUMPTION parameters. security.scms.lifecycle.component_revoked, .component_revoked_provider, .component_revoked_at_s none; the home provider; unset none ("No component revoked"), ica ("Intermediate CA"; ISS providers only), pca ("Pseudonym CA (ACA)"), ra ("Registration Authority"), eca ("Enrolment CA"), la1, la2 ("Linkage Authority 1/2"), ma ("Misbehaviour Authority"), crlg ("CRL Generator"); a provider of the deployment; 0 s to time.duration_s, step 1 s The SCMS component whose certificate a provider revokes, and when. It goes on the hash CRL of the (cracaId, crlSeries) the certificate names (series 2 for an ICA-issued component, 256 for a root-issued one; [SMP] Table 1), published by the provider's rule and carried in the composite CRL; receivers that install it refuse what the component signed (receiver_validation.refused.issuer-revoked). Report: phase2.component_revocations, component_revocations_refused, crl_component_entries. security.scms.lifecycle.ctl_genesis_sequence (gov C-10) auto auto ("By date, as the production series"), 0, 1 The sequence number of the run's first trust list. auto: 1 when time.t0 is on or after 2025-07-16 00:00 UTC (the live production CTL), 0 before (the 2019-12-12 one); 0 and 1 state it. Later CTLs count on from it. security.scms.lifecycle.eac_review (gov G-2) none none ("The times given are the votes"), elector-policy ("The times given are requests; the board reviews per Elector Policy") Whether the board's review delay comes before an EAC vote. Under elector-policy, root_rollover_at_s, root_removal_at_s and peer_root_removal_at_s are requests: each is logged as eac-request, and the vote is taken 10 Eastern business days later for an addition (the rollover's new root) and 24 h later for a removal (Elector Policy v1.0 §2.4.2, §2.4.4-2.4.5). A removal of the superseded root waits for the rollover's vote. Report: phase2.gov_requests. security.scms.lifecycle.elector_replacement_pq (gov G-11) off off ("Classical keys"), dual ("Dual signatures (classical + ML-DSA-65)") How an elector replacement signs its transition CTL (Elector Technical Specification v1.1 §2.5). Under dual the outgoing elector's P-384 key signs beside the others and the incoming elector's ML-DSA-65 key signs tbsCtl in a sidecar, so a device that knows either key accepts it. ASSUMPTION: the ML-DSA-65 half is the engine's modelled signature (3,309 B). No scenario key replaces an elector yet, so the setting takes effect only when Governance::replace_elector runs. security.scms.lifecycle.root_termination_notice_at_s (gov L-8) unset 0 s to time.duration_s, step 1 s; needs a second provider Provider gives termination notice at: starts the 365-day notice before the provider's root may leave the trust list ([SM-PROV] §3.5.6). The notice is the first peer provider's (the root peer_root_removal_at_s removes); a removal vote before notice + 365 d is refused. A run of a year or more uses time.fast_forward. The Paper 1 gap-limit scenarios (p1-rp-*) set received. detection.local[].params.max_accel_reading (detect/us-sm-mbr) accel-set accel-set (Reported acceleration (SM-MBR): the BSM's own accelSet.long; a BSM without one falls back to the speed difference), speed-difference (From consecutive speeds: |v₂ − v₁| / Δt of two consecutive BSMs, the stricter earlier reading) Which acceleration MaxAcceleration judges against max_accel_mps2 (SM-MBR v1.0 §2.3.1.3.1 and §2.3.1.3.3: the evidence is a single BSM). detection.local[].params.brake_acceleration (detect/us-sm-mbr) on (1) on (1), off (0) ("Brake with positive acceleration") SM-MBR Implausible/BrakeAcceleration (§2.3.1.3.4): a BSM whose brake status has a wheel braked while its accelSet.long is not negative and the vehicle is moving. detection.local[].params.brake_accel_tolerance_mps2 (detect/us-sm-mbr) 0 m/s² 0, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5 m/s² (range 0 to 2, step 0.01) How far above zero accelSet.long must be to count as "not negative" under brakes. 0 is the text: an acute angle with the velocity is a strictly positive component; 0.01 is one J2735 LSB.

items.text:

The vehicle ahead is seen as last seen while the eyes are off; an FCW or EEBL warning from the vehicle's own unit ends the glance. Native engine only. world.signals.coordinate, .progression_speed_mps off 1 to 40 m/s Green-wave signal timing. world.signals.join_m off 0 to 40 m Joins signalised junctions this close into one plan (netconvert --tls.join, 20 m default there). traffic.signals.short_link_clearance_m off 10 to 200 m Downstream green for a link shorter than this starts 2 s before the upstream green that fills it (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2e ch. 6, closely spaced signals). traffic.signals.detector_placement stop-line stop-line, sumo sumo: one loop per approach lane at speed limit x 2 s upstream (SUMO actuated detector-gap); actuated control only. traffic.signals.control: nema, traffic.signals.nema.* (partial) absent rings [1,2,3,4]/[5,6,7,8]; barriers [4,8], [2,6]; lefts lead-lead/lag-lag/lead-lag; left_turn_mode protected-permissive/protected/permissive; permissive_display fya/green-ball; left min/max/passage 4/25/2.5 s (2-60, 5-180, 0.2-10 s); yellow_s 3-6 s and red_clear_s 0-6 s (absent: the plan's own); walk_s 4-30 s, ped_speed_mps 0.8-1.5 (absent: world.signals.*, else 7 s and 1.067 m/s); min_recall [], soft_recall [2,6], max_recall [], ped_recall []; coordination false with coordinate_phases [2,6], force_off floating/fixed, controller_type ts2/type170 NEMA dual-ring eight-phase controller: FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed. (NCHRP 812) Exhibits 5-3, 6-4, 6-9, 6-22; MUTCD 2009 §4D.20, §4D.26, §4E.06; SUMO NEMA parameter names. Off by default: the rings rewrite each plan as composite intervals, unmapped junctions keep the single ring. Lefts follow left_turn_mode and permissive_display (P17.6: FYA window = opposing through, circular green = own approach; a protected-permissive left sharing the through's lane runs permissive). Crosswalks walk on a push-button call from a pedestrian standing at the kerb end, with pedestrian recycle while a green rests, or every cycle under ped_recall. Coordination keeps the plan's cycle and offset (a green wave's when set) with fixed or floating force-offs; under nema a green wave needs coordination: true, and short_link_clearance_m is refused; priority requests are served through the rings (P17.9: green extension up to max + 10 s, early green after 7 s), and SPaT minEndTime is the rings' earliest possible change. world.source.params.ew_green_share 0.5 0.1 to 0.9 East-west share of a generated grid's green (Webster 1958); signalised grids only. traffic.turn_curve_window_m 0 (whole connector) 0 to 30 m Judges a junction turn's radius over its tightest arc of this length instead of its average (SUMO netconvert --junctions.limit-turn-speed averages). At 6 m the 85th-percentile peak lateral acceleration equals turn_lateral_accel_mps2 (5.46 at 5.5, 3.52 at 3.5, AASHTO 0.38 g = 3.73); at 0 it is 7.7 at 5.5. Refused when turn_lateral_accel_mps2 is 0. traffic.vehicle_dynamics.grade false bool Subtracts g·sin θ of the draped lane (10 m chord, clamped at 0.3) from the driver's acceleration, as SUMO KraussPS does; an upper bound only, so braking and downhill speed are unchanged. Flat maps are byte-identical. Native engine only. traffic.vehicle_dynamics.power_limit false bool Caps acceleration at η·P/(m·v) less rolling and air resistance, for passenger cars (PHEMlight PC_D_EU4: 93 kW, 1,500 kg) and trailers (Green Book design truck 120 kg/kW at 36.3 t, C_dA 5.95 m², c_rr 0.0077), the rigid truck (NCHRP 505 Table 30, 82.9 lb/hp), the bus (Altoona 1211-P XD40, η 0.54), the coach (Altoona 1209 X3-45, η 0.84) and the van (EPA MY2020 Transit road load), with a rolling speed term that is zero on the car and trailer rows; emergency vehicles and two-wheelers have no sourced row. With grade the trailer crawls at 12.9 m/s (46 km/h) on 5 %. Binds on flat roads at speed. traffic.emergency_yield.enabled false bool A driver with an emergency vehicle running its beacons within the reaction distance behind, on the same carriageway, yields by the jurisdiction's rule (v2xw_mobility::rules::EmergencyYield): US presets move to the right-hand lane and stop clear of the junction until it has passed (NY VTL §1144(a); UVC §11-405 is the model); one who cannot move right and is in its lane drives on. Native engine only. traffic.emergency_yield.reaction_distance_m 25 m 1 to 500 m Gap from the emergency vehicle's front bumper to the driver's rear at which they react (SUMO bluelight device reactiondist default; calibrate against siren audibility). Needs enabled. traffic.emergency_yield.red_pass_speed_mps 0 m/s 0 to 10 m/s An emergency vehicle at a red stops (0) or slows to this at the line, then passes once nothing is inside on a conflicting path, the exit has room and no conflicting vehicle will reach its line within 4 s (UVC §11-106(b)2: "only after slowing down as may be necessary"; 0 is fire-service practice, NFPA 1451 §7.1.3 as quoted, secondary). Tagged as an intended red entry. Needs enabled. apps.glosa_compliance scenario's 0 to 1 Share of drivers who follow advice. actors.vru.red_crossing_share scenario's 0 to 1 Pedestrian non-compliance. actors.vru.walking_speed_mps 1.51 (observed), 1.34 (document) 0.5 to 2.5 m/s Mean walking speed under 65 (Knoblauch 1996); older walkers scale with it.

Further traffic fields: free-speed factor and spread, start-up reaction, queue start-up delay, per-class drivers (truck, bus, motorcycle, bicycle), junction gaps and turning speed, kerbside stops, OSM signal cycle, all-red and pedestrian timing, and GNSS receiver settings (actors.vehicles.gnss). config-inventory-traffic.md lists them with their defaults, ranges and sources, together with every parameter left hard-coded and the reason.

The IDM delta exponent and the other model internals are parameters of the chosen model: actors.vehicles.driving.car_following.params, published from the model's card. actors.vehicles.drivers is refused with mobility.provider: sumo, since SUMO's vType holds those drivers.

items.title: Not configurable yet
items.text: Knob Why it is not offered 802.11p 20 MHz channels The PHY, the error model and the sensitivity tables are 10 MHz, and 802.11p is refused on a wider channel. A 20 MHz PHY needs its own timing and PER curves. CWmax, retry limit (802.11p) Broadcast OCB has no ACK. CW never doubles and nothing is retried (EN 302 663 Annex C.4.2), so these would change nothing. CWmin/AIFSN for be/bk Safety traffic uses vo/vi. If one of these categories is moved to be/bk, it runs the standard's values. NR numerology other than the profile's Sub-channel and slot structure come from the profile's transcribed link-level curves (Lusvarghi 2024 at µ = 1). Sidelink mode 1 (network-scheduled) No gNB/eNB scheduler is modelled. Sub-channel size and count Fixed by the profile (J3161/1, EN 303 613, EN 303 798), because the BLER curves were computed for those pools. LIMERIC as such The ETSI adaptive approach is TS 102 687's LIMERIC-derived algorithm, and its α, β and target are above. Signal timing plan per junction Fixed-time plans come from the map. Coordination, cycle length, all-red and pedestrian timing are configurable for every junction at once (world.signals), not per junction.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
crates/v2xw-engine/tests/researcher_config.rs runs a baseline and the setting side by side on the same seed for each area:

  • PHY: 27 Mbit/s and a 15 dB noise figure lower delivery.
  • MAC: CWmin 1023 multiplies the access delay.
  • Channel: exponent 3.8, and Rayleigh fading, decode less than free space with no fading.
  • DCC: ETSI α = 0.5 gates frames, and DCC off records no DCC state.
  • Sidelink: random selection changes collisions.
  • Traffic: timid drivers are slower.
  • Messages: 5 Hz halves the frames.
  • Run: the warm-up drops early samples.
  • Loader: it refuses the meaningless settings.

crates/v2xw-engine/tests/network_audit_config.rs does the same for the network fields: sidelink noise figure and CBR threshold, the reactive DCC table, CBF timers, SPaT, MAP and CPM intervals, the verification queue depth, and the loader's refusals. Every number found in the network crates, exposed or kept and why, is listed in config-inventory-network.md.

v2xw sensitivity --catalogue sweeps every published numeric and choice setting at once. It runs each one at both ends of its recommended range, or at each of its choices, against a same-seed base on a small family of scenarios (scenarios/sensitivity/catalogue.yaml). It then lists the settings that move no metric, the effects that contradict crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations/*.yaml, and the values every family refuses. The result is docs/reference/sensitivity-catalogue.md, and crates/v2xw-engine/tests/sensitivity_catalogue.rs is its fast CI subset.

items.title: SCMS constants and their sources
items.text:
Every default the SCMS code runs on, with where it lives and why it has the value it has.

Status is one of four: - CITED: a primary source prints the value. A unit conversion of a printed value, such as 6 years to seconds, still counts as cited. - DERIVED: computed from cited inputs, or produced by the engine's own real encoder and pinned by a test. - MEASURED: measured by a script in this repository that anyone can rerun. - ASSUMPTION: no source prints the value. The row gives the reason for the value chosen, and every such value can be changed in the scenario or the library.

How this file is checked. The tables are machine-read, so a value changed in the code but not here (or here but not in the code) fails a test: - crates/v2xw-proto/tests/model_card.rs (constants_md_matches_the_scms_card) checks every parameter on the protocol/scms/camp model card. Each one must have a row here with the same default. A row is ASSUMPTION exactly when the card marks it todo-calibrate, and each such row carries a plan. - crates/v2xw-engine/tests/scms_constants.rs does the same for the engine, node and security constants the SCMS path uses. - Rows that neither test reads are listed for completeness. Their values are pinned by the tests named in the row.

Sources. Profiles IEEE 1609.2.1-2022. https://www.scmsmanager.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/IEEE1609Dot2Dot1-SCMS_Manager_Profile_1_0_3.pdf - [SM-MBR] SCMS Manager, "Misbehavior Report and Application Specification for Connected Vehicle Pilot Deployment", v1.0, 2019-02-14. https://scmsmanager.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Misbehavior-Report-and-Application-Specification-v1.0.pdf - [PRIMER] USDOT ITS JPO, "SCMS Technical Primer", FHWA-JPO-19-775, 2019. https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/43635 - [SM-PROV] SCMS Manager, "Provider Requirements", v1.1, 2024-08-09. https://www.scmsmanager.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/SCMS-Manager-Provider-Requirements-v1_1.pdf - [CVP-P2] USDOT ITS JPO, "CV Pilot Deployment Program: Driving Towards Deployment — Lessons Learned from the Design/Build/Test Phase", 2018. https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/37681 - [BRECHT] Brecht et al., "A Security Credential Management System for V2X Communications", IEEE T-ITS 2018, arXiv:1802.05323 - [SM-REENR] SCMS Manager, "EE Certificate Rollover (Re-Enrollment) Technical Standard", v1.0, 2020-10-08. https://www.scmsmanager.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/SCMS-Manager-EE-Re-Enrollment-Technical-Specification-v1.0.pdf - [SM-MBR-ASN] SCMS Manager, "ASN.1 for Misbehavior Reporting", v1.1. https://scmsmanager.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/ASN.1-for-Misbehavior-Reporting-v1.1.pdf - [SM-EESEC] SCMS Manager, "End-Entity Security Requirements, Design Guidance, and Validation Approach", v2.04, 2023-10-12. https://www.scmsmanager.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/SCMS-Manager-End-Entity-Security-Requirements-v2_04.pdf - [CVP-LOG] USDOT ITS JPO, "CV Pilot Deployment Lessons Learned Logbook Synthesis", 2022. https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/66286 - [RSU41] USDOT, Specifications for DSRC Roadside Unit v4.1, 2016-10-31 (FHWA-JPO-17-589), §2.1, §2.2 and Appendix C. items.title: 2.2 TLS sessions (backend.rs, measured by tools/scms_constants/tls_handshake_sizes.py)
items.text:
The script runs a real handshake between two OpenSSL 3.0.15 endpoints over memory BIOs, restricted to the US profile: server-only X.509 authentication, ECDHE-ECDSA suites and no session tickets ([SMP] §2.1.18, §3.2; [SM-EESEC] §5.2.3). It counts the bytes of each TLS-record flight. Nothing goes on the network.

The results rest on three assumptions: - The server sends a two-certificate ECDSA P-256 chain: a leaf of 367 B DER and an issuing CA of 323 B. No provider publishes its TLS chain. - The client sends OpenSSL's ClientHello restricted to the profile's suites. No OBU publishes its TLS stack. - The host name is a neutral 26-character one.

Rerun it with python -I tools/scms_constants/tls_handshake_sizes.py. It needs cryptography.

Name Default Unit Status Where Source or reason tls_session_max_s 300 s CITED TLS_SESSION_MAX "The max lifetime of a session shall be 5 minutes", and resumption is not supported. [SMP] §3.2 tls13_client_hello_bytes 256 B MEASURED SCMS_TLS13_FLIGHTS.0 The script above tls13_server_flight_bytes 1066 B MEASURED SCMS_TLS13_FLIGHTS.1 ServerHello through server Finished, with the 2-certificate chain tls13_client_finish_bytes 80 B MEASURED SCMS_TLS13_FLIGHTS.2 Rides with the first request. Not charged separately (open item 4) tls12_client_hello_bytes 173 B MEASURED SCMS_TLS12_FLIGHTS.0 ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 tls12_server_flight_bytes 934 B MEASURED SCMS_TLS12_FLIGHTS.1 ServerHello through ServerHelloDone tls12_client_finish_bytes 43 B MEASURED SCMS_TLS12_FLIGHTS.2 The measured flight is 93 B. The engine adds 50 B for ChangeCipherSpec and record headers. The server's last flight of 51 B matches the transport's fixed 51

The engine's earlier defaults were a 512 B ClientHello and a 4,000 B server flight, both todo-calibrate and sized for an RSA chain. The SCMS carrier no longer uses them. The other transport figures (MSS, CUBIC, RTO, HTTP headers) stay on the generic v2xw-radio card with their own status.

Devices fetch "as often as possible but no later than once a week" ([CAMP122] §3 item 10) and "on every RA connection" ([PRIMER] pp.5, 8), but no interval is printed. One hour is far inside the weekly bound and matches the profile's RA polling granularity (ra-minWait 1 h, [SMP] Table 3) crl_background_entries 0 - ASSUMPTION engine phase2.rs LifecycleParams::background_entries; run/crl.rs ScmsRun::seed_standing_crl The revocations already on the home provider's CRL at t0 (a standing list of earlier years). No deployment publishes its CRL length; 0 keeps the clean-slate run. Set it to size the list a vehicle downloads: every download (cellular, RSU backhaul, MBMS) is charged the encoded CompositeCrlSpdu (ctl::encode_composite_crl_coer), 33.08 B per linkage entry at 10,000 (edge_cases.rs) clock_skew_s 0 s ASSUMPTION engine phase2.rs Phase2::clock_skew_for; node secure.rs NodeSecurity::set_clock_offset A scenario setting; the default is the no-fault case. A vehicle clock's believed-minus-true offset (a GNSS time error held while the fix holds, or a spoofed time source). The node signs (generationTime, IEEE 1609.2 §6.3.9), rotates and judges validity (§5.2) on its own clock. 0 is a true clock clock_skew_share 1 - ASSUMPTION engine phase2.rs A scenario setting; the default is the no-fault case. The share of vehicles that carry clock_skew_s, taken by a fixed hash of the node index so a base and a variant skew the same vehicles peer_root_removal_at_s unset s ASSUMPTION engine phase2.rs governance_due, take_ctl_install A scenario setting; the default is the no-fault case. The EAC removes the second provider's root; the CTL is published 48 h later (Elector Policy v1.0 §2.2.4). Devices install a newer CTL with their next composite CRL download (the file carries the home CTL, IEEE 1609.2.1) and drop the root; RAs stop serving that provider's CRL crl_not_modified_bytes 92 B ASSUMPTION CRL_NOT_MODIFIED_BYTES The RA's HTTP 412 answer to a conditional CRL poll whose copy is current ([SMP] §4.3.1, §4.3.2: If-Modified-Since on 6.3.5.8 composite CRL and 6.3.5.14 information status). A minimal HTTP/1.1 response: status line 34 B, Date: 37 B, Content-Length: 0 19 B, blank line 2 B. Every due poll now sends its request; before, a poll that would find nothing new put nothing on the air http_header_set Host; Content-Type, Content-Length with a body; Date on answers - ASSUMPTION scms/http.rs (post_bytes, download_bytes, conditional_get_bytes, upload_bytes, answer_bytes) Every EE-RA request is charged its request line, Host: ra.<provider>:8892 (the RA certificate's name, which its TLS certificate must match, [SMP] §3.2), and Content-Type: application/octet-stream and Content-Length when it has a body ([CAMP122] §6.1); a GET download carries its SecuredAuthenticatedDownloadRequest Base64 in Download-Req, padded 4·⌈n/3⌉ (RFC 4648 §4), never also as a body; the file check is two conditional GETs with If-None-Match ("local_policy_<g>_<l>.oer", SCMS-544; the LCCF's tag "local_certificate_chain_<v>.oer" is unpublished), answered 200 or 304. Answers carry Date (29 B IMF-fixdate, RFC 9110 §6.6.1) and Content-Length, plus Content-Type with a body; 304 carries Date only; a resumed batch is 206 with Content-Range; refusals are 500 around the modelled refusal body. No User-Agent, Accept, Connection or Server. Paths are [CAMP122] Table 79's; the 1609.2.1 v3 paths are paywalled (UNCONFIRMED). The 412 answer this set gives is crl_not_modified_bytes (92 B) crl_store_path /download-crl/ on ma.<provider>:8894 - CITED phase2::CRL_STORE_PATH, Phase2::crl_poll_request_bytes CAMP; the IEEE 1609.2.1 path string is UNCONFIRMED. A vehicle's composite CRL poll is an unauthenticated conditional GET ([CAMP122] §6.2.1, §6.2.3; [SMP] §4.3.2 If-Modified-Since), no body: 107 B with the 29 B IMF-fixdate. Before B9b it was charged the size model's signed request (crl_request, 97 B). The answer is http::answer_bytes: 200 with the composite, or the 92 B 412. The roadside unit's download answer is framed the same way; its request is still not charged. info_status_path /download/info-status on ra.<provider>:8892 - ASSUMPTION phase2::INFO_STATUS_PATH, Phase2::info_status_request_bytes The information-status poll (1609.2.1 §6.3.5.14, If-Modified-Since). A US RSU repeats back-office content as Store and Repeat, whose TxInterval "1 to 5" seconds ([RSU41] Appendix C, p.117) bounds this. 5 s is the longest allowed and costs the least channel time report_bytes 1119 B DERIVED report_bytes(); mbr.rs REFERENCE_UPLOAD_BYTES The upload of the reference report: 804 B signed and encrypted plus a 315 B Download-Req header, from the real encoder (tests/mbr.rs). The forwarding MA re-encrypts the reporter-signed inner SPDU it opened, byte for byte, to the receiving provider's MA certificate as a device encrypts its report ([SM-MBR] §3, without the signing step and with no Download-Req header), so the receiving MA verifies the reporter's signature and the evidence itself, and the link carries the real ciphertext length. Draws come from the run's own ma-share stream

items.title: 4. Known limitations
items.text:
1. Real artefacts would replace these assumptions. A provider's TLS chain, an RA acknowledgement and a batch .zip would turn repo_url_bytes, batch_container_bytes and the TLS chain into measurements. The SCMS Manager publications carry no such samples.
  2. MA review time and capacity. No public figure exists. They stay ASSUMPTIONs that can be swept.
  3. TLS 1.3 client Finished. These 80 B ride with the first request and are not counted in the handshake bytes. The undercount is small and known.
  4. Report sizes for other evidence. report_bytes assumes two BSMs. An Implausible report with one BSM is 918 B as measured (603 + 315), and a real report is always charged its own length.

items.title: Catalogue-wide sensitivity sweep
items.text:
This sweep moves every numeric or choice setting the engine publishes, one at a time. The settings come from scenario::publish::fields(), the same index the Studio settings window and the agent read. Each setting goes to the low and high end of its recommended range, or to each of its choices, on a small scenario family run with the same seed. The sweep then records which metrics changed and by how much.

  • Command: v2xw sensitivity --catalogue [--only PREFIXES] [--jobs N] [--cache FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--strict]. Use --plan to list the perturbations without running them.
  • Code: crates/v2xw-engine/src/sensitivity/sweep.rs.
  • Families, routing, prerequisites and value overrides: scenarios/sensitivity/catalogue.yaml.
  • Expectation table: crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations/*.yaml. Each row gives a setting, a change, a metric, a direction and the theory it comes from.
  • Fast CI subset: crates/v2xw-engine/tests/sensitivity_catalogue.rs, about 4 s. It checks that every expectation names a setting and end the sweep plans, and that the plan covers at least 150 settings. It also checks that four link-budget, rate and frame settings on the DSRC family move the way the table says and are not dead. An injected wrong-direction row turns this check red.

What a run measures. Each run produces a fingerprint of about 250 to 300 metrics:

  • the radio harness's metrics: PDR, PRR, the range edges, CBR, the latency stages, age of information and the inter-packet gap;
  • every numeric leaf of the RunReport (report.*);
  • the sample-weighted mean of every metric.sample (metric.*, with metrics: [all]);
  • the ground-truth kinematics of vehicles and of VRUs (traffic.*, vru.*).

Both runs use the same seed. A setting the run never reads therefore gives a bit-identical run, and "dead" needs no tolerance.

Cost. A full sweep from an empty cache takes about 47 minutes on two threads. The saturated family dominates: 250 vehicles for 90 s is about 5 minutes a run. A rerun with --cache re-measures only the family bases and the entries whose setting, value or family changed, which takes about 8 minutes.

items.title: Reading the tables
items.text:
• Dead settings are wired fields whose fingerprint did not change on the family the setting was routed to. Read one as "either a wiring bug or a family that does not exercise it": a setting can be quiet because of the family (low load, a single DENM, a car-only fleet, a run too short for a vehicle to leave its segment). To judge it, extend catalogue.yaml with a context, a route or a family.
  • Contradictions are effects whose direction or size disagrees with the expectation table; docs/reference/sensitivity-expectations.md explains each.
  • Refusals are perturbations every family's loader rejects, usually by design (a setting that needs a partner setting, or a signature scheme the OBU publishes no cost for).

items.title: Expectation checks across the settings catalogue
items.text:
What the engine should do when a setting moves, written down before the run with its theory or source, and checked against same-seed runs. Two kinds of row:

  • Single-setting rows (crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations/*.yaml, 274 rows over 129 settings). Each row moves one published setting to an end of its recommended range, or to a literal value. It names a fingerprint metric, a direction, and optionally a magnitude band (changed / base) and a minimum relative change. It runs on the family scenarios/sensitivity/catalogue.yaml routes the setting to.
  • Interaction checks (crates/v2xw-engine/tests/expectations/interactions/*.yaml, 47 checks). Each is a 2 × 2 on one family, with all four runs on the same seed: the base, factor A alone, condition B alone, and both. A's effect without B (A − base) is compared with its effect under B (AB − B), in the metric's own units (Montgomery, Design and Analysis of Experiments 9e, 5.2). The verdict is dampens, amplifies, holds (same sign) or reverses, and A's own direction is checked too. Examples: density × DCC, message rate × signature size, data rate × frame size, demand × signal control, trucks × NLOSv blockage.

Run it:

  • v2xw sensitivity --expect [--only PREFIXES] [--cache FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--json]. It prints one PASS / FAIL / DEAD / REFUSED line per row, failures first, and exits non-zero on any failure. It plans only the perturbations the table names. That is about 7 minutes from an empty cache on two threads, and about 1 minute with the cache.
  • cargo test -p v2xw-engine --test sensitivity_expectations, the fast part:
  • every interaction's four scenarios pass the loader;
  • every row is planned;
  • the interaction judge goes red on a wrong expectation;
  • one interaction runs end to end.
  • -- --ignored runs the whole table.

items.title: Reading the results
items.text:
A row that fails or is dead is either a family that does not exercise the setting (too little load, too few vehicles, a car-only fleet) or an open modelling question. Each row's source gives the theory the expectation comes from, and a corrected expectation keeps the measured value and the reason in its source.
